# OPTIMAL BRAIN: FILE 03. EXERCISE LIBRARY

Every exercise in the Optimal movement library (all 19 categories from the coaches' wall sheets) plus the signature exercises from the coach research, 1069 unique exercises in total. Every exercise carries the same information so the AI and every coach work from the same playbook. Built 11 October 2026.

## HOW THE AI SHOULD USE THIS FILE

1. Pick exercises by PATTERN first (File 02 Section 4), then choose the GRADE that matches the member's grade for that pattern.
2. Use exercise names exactly as written here so the app can match them.
3. Every exercise lists named progressions (Progress to), named regressions (Regress to) and Same level swaps. If no named option exists, use the 'progress by' / 'regress by' levers.
4. GROUP sessions (BURN, STRONG, HYBRID): only use exercises marked Group: Yes. Optimal groups have a no jumping / no high impact rule. Exercises marked Group: No list a group swap.
5. Check the Cautions line against the member's flags (knee, low back, shoulder, osteoporosis/osteopenia, pelvic floor, blood pressure). A caution means: choose a regression or a different exercise unless the coach has cleared it.
6. Equipment is tagged on every exercise. Optimal's equipment rules already in the brain take priority. Kit marked 'confirm' is not on the confirmed list (benches, barbells, safety squat bar, kettlebells, rig, TRX, cable machine, sled, ski erg, rower, assault bike, wall balls, ab mats, mats).
7. Default prescriptions are starting points; File 02 Section 7 overrides them by goal and phase.

## GRADES (matches Optimal's existing G1 to G4 system)

- **G1 Foundation**: beginner or modified version, supported or assisted, lowest load or range. Seniors, rehab, new members, flare up days.
- **G2 Standard**: the standard version with moderate load. Most members in their first 3 to 6 months.
- **G3 Advanced**: increased load, range or complexity (single arm, single leg, paused, barbell, unstable). Experienced members.
- **G4 Maximum**: maximum challenge version (heavy barbell, advanced single leg, high skill). Mostly Teams, coach approved.

Move a member up a grade when they complete all target reps with good form at RPE 7 or less for 2 sessions in a row, pain free, and the coach signs off technique. Move down a grade on amber/red readiness days or if pain goes above 3/10.

## FIELDS ON EVERY EXERCISE

ID · Grade · Pattern · Equipment · Session fit (BURN / STRONG / HYBRID) · Group OK · Impact · Teams only · Seniors OK · Why we use it · Variation notes · Muscles · 3 coaching cues · Common faults · Progress to (named, with grade) · Progress by (levers) · Regress to (named, with grade) · Regress by (levers) · Same level swaps · Cautions · Joint notes · Default prescription · Coach sources · Also listed in

# 01. SQUAT PATTERN: BILATERAL

*Knee dominant, both feet*

**Grade ladder at a glance** (use this to slot every member into the same session at their level):

- **G1**: Bodyweight Squat, Prisoner Squat, Box Squat, Plate Front Raise Squat, TRX Assisted Squat, Wall Sit, Wall Sit with Plate Hold, Swiss Ball Wall Squat, Goblet Box Squat, Spanish Squat (Band), Mini Band Squat, Isometric Squat Hold, Squat with Heel Raise, Frog Squat, KB Deadstop Squat, Squat to Box Stand Up (Bodyweight)
- **G2**: Landmine Squat, Landmine Hack Squat, Goblet Squat (KB), Goblet Squat (DB), Barbell Box Squat, Heels Elevated Goblet Squat, Tempo Goblet Squat, Goblet Squat Pulses, Bottoms Up KB Goblet Squat, Cyclist Squat, Banded Barbell Box Squat, Band Resisted Squat, Cable Goblet Squat, Sissy Squat (Assisted), Cable Squat to Row, DB Suitcase Squat, Heels Elevated DB Squat, DB Sumo Squat, Narrow Stance Goblet Squat, KB Sumo Squat, Goblet Squat with Rotation
- **G3**: DB Squat to Overhead Press, DB Overhead Squat, Landmine Squat to Press, Paused Goblet Squat, 1.5 Rep Goblet Squat, Zercher Squat, DB Front Squat, KB Goblet Squat to Press
- **G4**: Barbell Back Squat ✱, Barbell Front Squat ✱, Paused Back Squat ✱, Tempo Back Squat ✱, 1.25 Rep Back Squat ✱, Paused Front Squat ✱, Barbell Pin Squat ✱, Anderson Squat ✱, Barbell Overhead Squat ✱, Barbell Hack Squat ✱, Trap Bar Squat (High Handles), Wide Stance Barbell Squat ✱, Double KB Front Rack Squat, Double KB Front Squat to Press ✱, Barbell Front Rack Squat to Press ✱

✱ = not for group sessions (impact).

## Bodyweight Squat

`SQB-001 | G1 | Squat: knee dominant bilateral | BURN, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Bodyweight
- **Why we use it:** The foundation squat pattern. Builds the movement before load and is useful for warm ups, high rep BURN work and beginners. Band and pause variations add a twist: mini bands cue the knees out, pulses keep tension, dead stops kill the bounce.
- **Muscles:** Quads, glutes, adductors
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Feet shoulder width, toes slightly out, tripod foot. 2) Sit down between the hips, knees track over the toes. 3) Stand tall and squeeze the glutes.
- **Common faults:** Heels lifting; Knees caving; Folding forward at the hips.
- **Progress to:** Goblet Squat (KB) (G2); Goblet Squat (DB) (G2); Barbell Box Squat (G2). **Or progress by:** Add a pause, tempo, then load (goblet squat).
- **Regress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or regress by:** Squat to a box, TRX assisted squat.
- **Same level swaps:** Frog Squat; Prisoner Squat; Mini Band Squat
- **Cautions:** None specific. Generally joint friendly. Use a box with knee pain, heel elevation with stiff ankles.
- **Default prescription:** 2 to 3 sets x 12 to 20 reps (or 30 to 40s)
- **Coach sources:** Squat University, Paul Chek (Primal Pattern), Dan John

## DB Squat to Overhead Press

`SQB-002 | G3 | Squat + vertical push (combination) | BURN, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Dumbbells (confirm)
- **Why we use it:** Links a squat and an overhead press into one total body movement. Very metabolic, great for BURN and HYBRID sessions, and the legs help drive the weight overhead so people can press more.
- **This variation:** Combination move: trains two qualities at once, efficient for HYBRID and BURN; keep technique of both parts clean before speeding up.
- **Muscles:** Quads, glutes, shoulders, triceps, core
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Squat with the weight in the rack. 2) Drive up hard and use that momentum to press overhead. 3) Lock out with biceps by the ears, ribs down, then lower back to the rack.
- **Common faults:** Pressing before the legs finish the drive; Arching the low back at the top; Losing the rack position and squatting with the elbows dropped.
- **Progress to:** Barbell Thruster (G4); Double KB Front Squat to Press (G4); Barbell Front Rack Squat to Press (G4). **Or progress by:** Add load, double KBs, barbell, more rounds or density.
- **Regress to:** DB Sumo Squat (G2); Goblet Squat (DB) (G2); DB Suitcase Squat (G2). **Or regress by:** Goblet squat to press, landmine squat to press, split into separate squat and press.
- **Same level swaps:** DB Thruster; DB Thrusters; KB Thruster
- **Cautions:** Shoulder. Needs pain free overhead range. With shoulder pain swap to squat to landmine press. Watch technique as fatigue builds in circuits.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 4 sets x 8 to 12 reps, or 30 to 40s in circuits
- **Coach sources:** Cosgrove (MRT), DeFranco

## DB Overhead Squat

`SQB-004 | G3 | Squat: bilateral overhead (mobility/stability test) | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Dumbbells (confirm)
- **Why we use it:** The overhead squat exposes stiffness at the ankles, hips, T spine and shoulders all at once, which is why Squat University and the FMS use it as a screen. With a dowel it is an excellent mobility drill; loaded it is a high skill G4 lift.
- **Muscles:** Quads, glutes, upper back, shoulders, core
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Arms locked overhead, biceps by the ears, push up into the dowel or weight. 2) Sit down between the hips with the chest proud. 3) Keep the bar over the middle of the foot throughout.
- **Common faults:** Arms drifting forward; Lower back rounding at the bottom; Heels lifting.
- **Progress to:** Anderson Squat (G4); Tempo Back Squat (G4); Paused Back Squat (G4). **Or progress by:** Dowel → light DB/plate → barbell overhead squat.
- **Regress to:** DB Sumo Squat (G2); Goblet Squat (DB) (G2); DB Suitcase Squat (G2). **Or regress by:** Dowel only, squat to a box, heels elevated, arms in a Y position.
- **Same level swaps:** Dowel Overhead Squat
- **Cautions:** Shoulder. Shoulder demanding: avoid loading with shoulder pain or impingement. Use a dowel as a warm up screen instead.
- **Default prescription:** 2 to 3 sets x 5 to 8 reps, light, slow
- **Coach sources:** Squat University, Gray Cook (FMS), Poliquin

## Box Squat

`SQB-005 | G1 | Squat: knee dominant bilateral (depth controlled) | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Box / bench / step
- **Why we use it:** The box sets a consistent, safe depth and teaches people to sit back and control the descent. It is the best teaching squat for beginners and painful knees and, with a barbell or SSB, a classic DeFranco/Westside strength builder.
- **Muscles:** Quads, glutes, adductors, hamstrings
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Box at a height where the spine stays neutral. 2) Sit back and down with control, touch the box lightly (don't crash). 3) Stay braced, drive up through the whole foot.
- **Common faults:** Plonking down and relaxing on the box; Rocking back to get up; Knees caving as they stand.
- **Progress to:** Barbell Box Squat (G2); Banded Barbell Box Squat (G2). **Or progress by:** Lower the box, add load (goblet then SSB/barbell), pause on the box without relaxing, remove the box.
- **Regress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or regress by:** Raise the box, TRX assisted box squat, sit to stand.
- **Same level swaps:** Goblet Box Squat; Box Squat (High Box)
- **Cautions:** None specific. Excellent for knee pain and older members: adjust height to the pain free range. Lower the box as mobility and control improve.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8
- **Coach sources:** DeFranco (Westside), Squat University, Cosgrove
- **Also listed in:** Rehab: Hip

## Plate Front Raise Squat

`SQB-006 | G1 | Pull: scapular / lower trap raises | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Plate
- **Why we use it:** Small raises in Y, T, W and I shapes strengthen the muscles that control the shoulder blade, especially the lower traps that are often weak in rounded posture. Poliquin's structural balance and Cressey's shoulder programmes rely on them.
- **Muscles:** Lower and middle traps, rear shoulders, rotator cuff
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Chest supported on an incline bench or lying face down. 2) Thumbs up, lift the arms into the shape using the shoulder blades. 3) Pause 1 to 2s at the top, lower slowly.
- **Common faults:** Shrugging up to the ears; Using heavy weights and swinging; Arching the low back.
- **Progress to:** Cyclist Squat (G2); DB Sumo Squat (G2); KB Sumo Squat (G2). **Or progress by:** Light DBs, longer pauses.
- **Regress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or regress by:** Bodyweight, smaller range.
- **Same level swaps:** Plate Front Raise; TRX Y Raise; TRX T Raise
- **Cautions:** None specific. Shoulder rehab friendly. Use 1 to 3kg or bodyweight.
- **Default prescription:** 2 to 3 sets x 8 to 12 per shape, pause at the top
- **Coach sources:** Poliquin, Cressey, Squat University

## TRX Assisted Squat

`SQB-007 | G1 | Squat: assisted | STRONG, HYBRID, BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** TRX
- **Why we use it:** Holding the TRX lets people counterbalance, so they can sit deeper and more upright than they could alone. It is the go to G1 squat for beginners, seniors, heavy members and anyone with knee or hip pain, and it builds confidence fast.
- **This variation:** Assisted version: support lets members practise the full pattern safely while strength builds (Cosgrove: regress to progress).
- **Muscles:** Quads, glutes
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Hold the handles at chest height with arms straight. 2) Sit back and down, letting the straps take a little weight. 3) Use the legs to stand, the arms only steady you.
- **Common faults:** Pulling with the arms to stand up; Leaning back so far the feet slide; Squatting deeper than the pain free range.
- **Progress to:** Barbell Box Squat (G2); Goblet Squat (KB) (G2); Goblet Squat (DB) (G2). **Or progress by:** Use the straps less, slower tempo, add a pause, progress to goblet box squat.
- **Regress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or regress by:** Squat to a high box with the TRX, reduce depth.
- **Same level swaps:** TRX Pull Up Assisted Squat; Box Squat; Goblet Box Squat
- **Cautions:** None specific. Very joint friendly. Ideal first squat after injury or replacement surgery (within surgeon's limits).
- **Default prescription:** 3 sets x 10 to 15 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0
- **Coach sources:** Cosgrove (regress to progress), Boyle, Squat University
- **Also listed in:** Rehab: Knee

## Landmine Squat

`SQB-008 | G2 | Squat: knee dominant bilateral | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Landmine (confirm)
- **Why we use it:** The landmine's arc lets people lean into the bar and squat with an upright torso and a guided path. It is very back and shoulder friendly and a great bridge between goblet and barbell squatting.
- **This variation:** Landmine: the arc path is shoulder and back friendly and very easy to learn.
- **Muscles:** Quads, glutes, core
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Hold the end of the bar at the chest, lean slightly into it. 2) Feet slightly in front of the body, sit down and back. 3) Drive up into the bar, finish tall.
- **Common faults:** Feet too close to the bar so the knees jam; Rounding the back; Pushing the bar away with the arms.
- **Progress to:** Landmine Squat to Press (G3); Zercher Squat (G3); DB Front Squat (G3). **Or progress by:** Add plates, add a press at the top, pause reps.
- **Regress to:** Wall Sit (G1); Box Squat (G1); Frog Squat (G1). **Or regress by:** Lighter load, reduce depth, goblet box squat.
- **Same level swaps:** Landmine Hack Squat
- **Cautions:** None specific. Shoulder friendly (no bar on the back). Hack squat version loads knees more: control depth with knee pain.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8
- **Coach sources:** DeFranco, Cosgrove

## Wall Sit

`SQB-009 | G1 | Squat: isometric | STRONG, HYBRID, BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Bodyweight
- **Why we use it:** A simple, joint friendly way to build quad strength and endurance with zero technique demand. Isometrics can reduce knee pain and are ideal for beginners, seniors and anyone who cannot yet squat through full range. The Swiss ball version lets people practise the squat path with support.
- **Muscles:** Quads, glutes, adductors
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Back flat against the wall, feet hip width and slightly in front. 2) Slide down until the knees are at a pain free angle (aim 90 degrees over time). 3) Weight through the whole foot, breathe slowly, knees in line with toes.
- **Common faults:** Hands pushing on the thighs; Knees caving in; Going too deep too soon and aggravating knees.
- **Progress to:** Cyclist Squat (G2); DB Sumo Squat (G2); KB Sumo Squat (G2). **Or progress by:** Lower the position, hold longer, hold a plate, progress to single leg wall sit or tempo goblet squats.
- **Regress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or regress by:** Higher position, shorter holds, hands on thighs for the first few sessions.
- **Same level swaps:** Isometric Wall Sit; Isometric Squat Hold; Swiss Ball Wall Squat
- **Cautions:** None specific. Very knee friendly at higher positions. Adjust depth to stay at or below 3/10 pain. Avoid long holds with breath holding for members with high blood pressure.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 5 x 20 to 45s holds, rest 60s, about 70% effort
- **Coach sources:** Squat University, Rehab research (isometrics), Ben Patrick
- **Also listed in:** Rehab: Lower Back

## Barbell Back Squat

`SQB-014 | G4 | Squat: knee dominant bilateral (barbell) | STRONG | Group: No | Impact: none | Teams only: Yes | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Barbell
- **Why we use it:** The classic heavy squat. Builds strength, muscle and bone density (LIFTMOR used heavy squats). Pin and Anderson squats start from the bottom, removing the bounce and building strength out of the hole. At Optimal it is a G4 lift for members with good mobility and no back or shoulder restriction; the SSB is the default alternative.
- **This variation:** Barbell: allows the heaviest loading for maximum strength and bone stimulus; earn it with technique (usually G3 to G4, Teams).
- **Muscles:** Quads, glutes, adductors, spinal erectors
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Bar on the upper back, hands tight, elbows under the bar. 2) Big breath and brace, sit between the hips with knees tracking the toes. 3) Drive up keeping the chest and hips rising together.
- **Common faults:** Hips shooting up first (good morning squat); Losing the brace and rounding at the bottom; Knees caving under load.
- **Progress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or progress by:** Add load, pause reps, tempo, 1.25 reps, rep maxes (Teams G4 only).
- **Regress to:** Zercher Squat (G3); DB Front Squat (G3); SSB Squat (G3). **Or regress by:** SSB squat, box squat, goblet or double KB front squat.
- **Same level swaps:** Anderson Squat; Tempo Back Squat; Paused Back Squat
- **Cautions:** Knee, Low back, Pelvic floor. High spinal load. Not for active back pain. Needs shoulder external rotation to hold the bar: use SSB or trap bar squat if shoulders are cranky.
- **Group swap:** Teams only (heavy or high skill): in groups use a G3 regression from the Regress to list
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8
- **Coach sources:** DeFranco, Squat University, LIFTMOR research, Poliquin

## Goblet Squat (KB)

`SQB-015 | G2 | Squat: knee dominant bilateral | STRONG, HYBRID, BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Kettlebell
- **Why we use it:** Holding the weight at the chest counterbalances the body, so people naturally squat more upright and deeper with better form. Dan John and Squat University both use it as THE teaching squat, and it is strong enough to stay useful for years. Fits groups perfectly because load scales from a 4kg KB to a 40kg+ DB.
- **Muscles:** Quads, glutes, adductors, upper back, core
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Hold the bell tight to the chest, elbows pointing down. 2) Push the knees out and sit between the hips, chest proud. 3) Drive up through the whole foot, squeeze the glutes at the top.
- **Common faults:** Rounding the upper back and letting the weight pull you forward; Heels lifting; Knees caving inward on the way up.
- **Progress to:** Paused Goblet Squat (G3); 1.5 Rep Goblet Squat (G3). **Or progress by:** Add load, tempo (4-1-1-0), pause at the bottom, 1.5 reps, move to double KB front squat or SSB squat.
- **Regress to:** Goblet Box Squat (G1); Box Squat (G1); TRX Assisted Squat (G1). **Or regress by:** Goblet squat to a box, TRX assisted squat, lighter bell.
- **Same level swaps:** Goblet Squat (DB); Tempo Goblet Squat; Cable Goblet Squat
- **Cautions:** None specific. Knee and back friendly. Heels elevated version helps stiff ankles. Use a box for depth control with knee pain. Upper back can fatigue first as loads get heavy.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8
- **Coach sources:** Dan John, Squat University, Cosgrove, Boyle

## Barbell Front Squat

`SQB-016 | G4 | Squat: knee dominant bilateral (front loaded) | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: No | Impact: none | Teams only: Yes | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Barbell
- **Why we use it:** Front loading keeps the torso upright, puts more work on the quads and core, and puts less shear on the low back than back squatting. The double KB front squat is a great G3 group squat; the barbell front squat is a G4 strength lift for those with the wrist and thoracic mobility.
- **This variation:** Barbell: allows the heaviest loading for maximum strength and bone stimulus; earn it with technique (usually G3 to G4, Teams).
- **Muscles:** Quads, glutes, upper back, core
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Bells or bar in a tight rack, elbows high and forward. 2) Brace, sit straight down between the hips. 3) Keep the elbows up as you drive up.
- **Common faults:** Elbows dropping and the chest falling forward; Wrists bent back painfully (barbell); Losing tension at the bottom.
- **Progress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or progress by:** Add load, pause at the bottom, tempo, progress DB → double KB → barbell front squat.
- **Regress to:** Zercher Squat (G3); DB Front Squat (G3). **Or regress by:** Goblet squat, box to control depth, lighter load.
- **Same level swaps:** Paused Front Squat; Double KB Front Rack Squat
- **Cautions:** None specific. Low back friendlier than back squats. Barbell front rack needs wrist, lat and T spine mobility. Zercher loads the elbows: use padding.
- **Group swap:** Teams only (heavy or high skill): in groups use a G3 regression from the Regress to list
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8
- **Coach sources:** Squat University, Boyle, Dan John

## Barbell Box Squat

`SQB-018 | G2 | Squat: knee dominant bilateral (depth controlled) | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Barbell, Box / bench / step
- **Why we use it:** The box sets a consistent, safe depth and teaches people to sit back and control the descent. It is the best teaching squat for beginners and painful knees and, with a barbell or SSB, a classic DeFranco/Westside strength builder.
- **This variation:** Barbell: allows the heaviest loading for maximum strength and bone stimulus; earn it with technique (usually G3 to G4, Teams).
- **Muscles:** Quads, glutes, adductors, hamstrings
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Box at a height where the spine stays neutral. 2) Sit back and down with control, touch the box lightly (don't crash). 3) Stay braced, drive up through the whole foot.
- **Common faults:** Plonking down and relaxing on the box; Rocking back to get up; Knees caving as they stand.
- **Progress to:** SSB Squat (G3); SSB Box Squat (G3); Paused Goblet Squat (G3). **Or progress by:** Lower the box, add load (goblet then SSB/barbell), pause on the box without relaxing, remove the box.
- **Regress to:** Box Squat (G1); Goblet Box Squat (G1); Box Squat (High Box) (G1). **Or regress by:** Raise the box, TRX assisted box squat, sit to stand.
- **Same level swaps:** Banded Barbell Box Squat; Goblet Squat (KB); Goblet Squat (DB)
- **Cautions:** None specific. Excellent for knee pain and older members: adjust height to the pain free range. Lower the box as mobility and control improve.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8
- **Coach sources:** DeFranco (Westside), Squat University, Cosgrove

## Paused Back Squat

`SQB-020 | G4 | Squat: knee dominant bilateral (barbell) | STRONG | Group: No | Impact: none | Teams only: Yes | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Barbell
- **Why we use it:** The classic heavy squat. Builds strength, muscle and bone density (LIFTMOR used heavy squats). Pin and Anderson squats start from the bottom, removing the bounce and building strength out of the hole. At Optimal it is a G4 lift for members with good mobility and no back or shoulder restriction; the SSB is the default alternative.
- **This variation:** Paused version: holding the hardest position removes the bounce and builds strength exactly where people usually fail.
- **Muscles:** Quads, glutes, adductors, spinal erectors
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Bar on the upper back, hands tight, elbows under the bar. 2) Big breath and brace, sit between the hips with knees tracking the toes. 3) Drive up keeping the chest and hips rising together.
- **Common faults:** Hips shooting up first (good morning squat); Losing the brace and rounding at the bottom; Knees caving under load.
- **Progress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or progress by:** Add load, pause reps, tempo, 1.25 reps, rep maxes (Teams G4 only).
- **Regress to:** Zercher Squat (G3); DB Front Squat (G3); SSB Squat (G3). **Or regress by:** SSB squat, box squat, goblet or double KB front squat.
- **Same level swaps:** Anderson Squat; Tempo Back Squat; Barbell Pin Squat
- **Cautions:** Knee, Low back, Pelvic floor. High spinal load. Not for active back pain. Needs shoulder external rotation to hold the bar: use SSB or trap bar squat if shoulders are cranky.
- **Group swap:** Teams only (heavy or high skill): in groups use a G3 regression from the Regress to list
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8
- **Coach sources:** DeFranco, Squat University, LIFTMOR research, Poliquin

- **Default prescription:** 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8
- **Coach sources:** DeFranco, Squat University, LIFTMOR research, Poliquin

## Bottoms Up KB Goblet Squat

`SQB-031 | G2 | Squat: knee dominant bilateral | STRONG, HYBRID, BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Kettlebell
- **Why we use it:** Holding the weight at the chest counterbalances the body, so people naturally squat more upright and deeper with better form. Dan John and Squat University both use it as THE teaching squat, and it is strong enough to stay useful for years. Fits groups perfectly because load scales from a 4kg KB to a 40kg+ DB.
- **This variation:** Bottoms up kettlebell forces the grip and rotator cuff to stabilise; a brilliant (light) shoulder rehab tool.
- **Muscles:** Quads, glutes, adductors, upper back, core
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Hold the bell tight to the chest, elbows pointing down. 2) Push the knees out and sit between the hips, chest proud. 3) Drive up through the whole foot, squeeze the glutes at the top.
- **Common faults:** Rounding the upper back and letting the weight pull you forward; Heels lifting; Knees caving inward on the way up.
- **Progress to:** Paused Goblet Squat (G3); 1.5 Rep Goblet Squat (G3). **Or progress by:** Add load, tempo (4-1-1-0), pause at the bottom, 1.5 reps, move to double KB front squat or SSB squat.
- **Regress to:** Goblet Box Squat (G1); Box Squat (G1); TRX Assisted Squat (G1). **Or regress by:** Goblet squat to a box, TRX assisted squat, lighter bell.
- **Same level swaps:** Goblet Squat (KB); Goblet Squat (DB); Tempo Goblet Squat
- **Cautions:** None specific. Knee and back friendly. Heels elevated version helps stiff ankles. Use a box for depth control with knee pain. Upper back can fatigue first as loads get heavy.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8
- **Coach sources:** Dan John, Squat University, Cosgrove, Boyle

## Zercher Squat

`SQB-032 | G3 | Squat: knee dominant bilateral (front loaded) | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Barbell
- **Why we use it:** Front loading keeps the torso upright, puts more work on the quads and core, and puts less shear on the low back than back squatting. The double KB front squat is a great G3 group squat; the barbell front squat is a G4 strength lift for those with the wrist and thoracic mobility.
- **Muscles:** Quads, glutes, upper back, core
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Bells or bar in a tight rack, elbows high and forward. 2) Brace, sit straight down between the hips. 3) Keep the elbows up as you drive up.
- **Common faults:** Elbows dropping and the chest falling forward; Wrists bent back painfully (barbell); Losing tension at the bottom.
- **Progress to:** Paused Front Squat (G4); Barbell Front Squat (G4); Double KB Front Rack Squat (G4). **Or progress by:** Add load, pause at the bottom, tempo, progress DB → double KB → barbell front squat.
- **Regress to:** Goblet Squat (KB) (G2); Goblet Squat (DB) (G2); Tempo Goblet Squat (G2). **Or regress by:** Goblet squat, box to control depth, lighter load.
- **Same level swaps:** DB Front Squat; SSB Squat; SSB Box Squat
- **Cautions:** None specific. Low back friendlier than back squats. Barbell front rack needs wrist, lat and T spine mobility. Zercher loads the elbows: use padding.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8
- **Coach sources:** Squat University, Boyle, Dan John

## Cyclist Squat

`SQB-033 | G2 | Squat: quad biased (heels elevated, narrow) | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Bodyweight
- **Why we use it:** A narrow stance, heels elevated squat that lets the knees travel well forward. It biases the quads (especially the inner quad) with an upright torso, so it is easy on the low back and great for knee health and quad size. A Poliquin and Squat University favourite.
- **Muscles:** Quads (VMO emphasis), glutes
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Heels on a wedge or plate, feet close together. 2) Hold a weight at the chest, stay tall. 3) Knees travel forward over the toes, sit straight down, control the bottom.
- **Common faults:** Bouncing out of the bottom; Heels rolling off the wedge; Leaning the chest forward.
- **Progress to:** Zercher Squat (G3); DB Front Squat (G3); DB Overhead Squat (G3). **Or progress by:** Add load (DB/KB then SSB), slower tempo (4-1-1-0), pause at the bottom, 1.5 reps.
- **Regress to:** Wall Sit (G1); Box Squat (G1); Frog Squat (G1). **Or regress by:** Lower heel height, squat to a box, bodyweight with TRX support.
- **Cautions:** Knee. Very low back friendly. Knees work hard in deep flexion, so build depth gradually for sensitive knees.
- **Default prescription:** 3 sets x 8 to 12 reps, tempo 3-0-1-1, rest 60 to 90s, RPE 7 to 9
- **Coach sources:** Poliquin, Squat University, Ben Patrick
- **Also listed in:** Rehab: Knee

## Barbell Overhead Squat

`SQB-034 | G4 | Squat: bilateral overhead (mobility/stability test) | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: No | Impact: none | Teams only: Yes | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Barbell
- **Why we use it:** The overhead squat exposes stiffness at the ankles, hips, T spine and shoulders all at once, which is why Squat University and the FMS use it as a screen. With a dowel it is an excellent mobility drill; loaded it is a high skill G4 lift.
- **This variation:** Barbell: allows the heaviest loading for maximum strength and bone stimulus; earn it with technique (usually G3 to G4, Teams).
- **Muscles:** Quads, glutes, upper back, shoulders, core
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Arms locked overhead, biceps by the ears, push up into the dowel or weight. 2) Sit down between the hips with the chest proud. 3) Keep the bar over the middle of the foot throughout.
- **Common faults:** Arms drifting forward; Lower back rounding at the bottom; Heels lifting.
- **Progress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or progress by:** Dowel → light DB/plate → barbell overhead squat.
- **Regress to:** DB Overhead Squat (G3); Dowel Overhead Squat (G3). **Or regress by:** Dowel only, squat to a box, heels elevated, arms in a Y position.
- **Cautions:** Shoulder. Shoulder demanding: avoid loading with shoulder pain or impingement. Use a dowel as a warm up screen instead.
- **Group swap:** Teams only (heavy or high skill): in groups use a G3 regression from the Regress to list
- **Default prescription:** 2 to 3 sets x 5 to 8 reps, light, slow
- **Coach sources:** Squat University, Gray Cook (FMS), Poliquin

## Spanish Squat (Band)

`SQB-035 | G1 | Squat: knee dominant isometric | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Resistance band (confirm)
- **Why we use it:** A band behind the knees lets the shins stay vertical while the hips sit back, so the quads work hard with very little compressive stress on the front of the knee. Isometric holds like this are one of the best known tools for calming irritable knees (patellar tendon and kneecap pain) while still loading the quads. A Squat University and physio favourite.
- **Muscles:** Quads (especially patellar tendon loading), glutes
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Heavy band behind both knees anchored to the rig, walk back until it is tight. 2) Sit back and down until thighs are around 60 to 90 degrees, shins vertical. 3) Keep chest proud, push knees back into the band and hold.
- **Common faults:** Letting the knees drift forward off the band; Holding the breath for the whole set; Going so deep that pain rises above 3/10.
- **Progress to:** Band Resisted Squat (G2); Banded Barbell Box Squat (G2); Cyclist Squat (G2). **Or progress by:** Hold longer (45s), sit deeper, add a weight held at the chest, progress to tempo goblet squats and Poliquin step ups.
- **Regress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or regress by:** Shorten the hold, sit less deep, lighter band, switch to a wall sit with a higher position.
- **Same level swaps:** Spanish Squat Isometric
- **Cautions:** None specific. Knee friendly by design. Often reduces knee pain for several hours afterwards, which makes it a great warm up before squatting for sore knees. Back is upright so low back load is minimal.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 5 x 20 to 45s holds, rest 60s, about 70% effort (5 x 45s is a classic tendon dose)
- **Coach sources:** Squat University, Ben Patrick (knee resilience), Rehab research (tendon isometrics)

## Barbell Hack Squat

`SQB-036 | G4 | Squat: knee dominant bilateral (barbell) | STRONG | Group: No | Impact: none | Teams only: Yes | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Barbell
- **Why we use it:** The classic heavy squat. Builds strength, muscle and bone density (LIFTMOR used heavy squats). Pin and Anderson squats start from the bottom, removing the bounce and building strength out of the hole. At Optimal it is a G4 lift for members with good mobility and no back or shoulder restriction; the SSB is the default alternative.
- **This variation:** Barbell: allows the heaviest loading for maximum strength and bone stimulus; earn it with technique (usually G3 to G4, Teams).
- **Muscles:** Quads, glutes, adductors, spinal erectors
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Bar on the upper back, hands tight, elbows under the bar. 2) Big breath and brace, sit between the hips with knees tracking the toes. 3) Drive up keeping the chest and hips rising together.
- **Common faults:** Hips shooting up first (good morning squat); Losing the brace and rounding at the bottom; Knees caving under load.
- **Progress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or progress by:** Add load, pause reps, tempo, 1.25 reps, rep maxes (Teams G4 only).
- **Regress to:** Zercher Squat (G3); DB Front Squat (G3); SSB Squat (G3). **Or regress by:** SSB squat, box squat, goblet or double KB front squat.
- **Same level swaps:** Anderson Squat; Tempo Back Squat; Paused Back Squat
- **Cautions:** Knee, Low back, Pelvic floor. High spinal load. Not for active back pain. Needs shoulder external rotation to hold the bar: use SSB or trap bar squat if shoulders are cranky.
- **Group swap:** Teams only (heavy or high skill): in groups use a G3 regression from the Regress to list
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8
- **Coach sources:** DeFranco, Squat University, LIFTMOR research, Poliquin

## Mini Band Squat

`SQB-037 | G1 | Squat: knee dominant bilateral | BURN, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Mini band (confirm)
- **Why we use it:** The foundation squat pattern. Builds the movement before load and is useful for warm ups, high rep BURN work and beginners. Band and pause variations add a twist: mini bands cue the knees out, pulses keep tension, dead stops kill the bounce.
- **This variation:** The mini band cues the knees out and switches on the glute med.
- **Muscles:** Quads, glutes, adductors
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Feet shoulder width, toes slightly out, tripod foot. 2) Sit down between the hips, knees track over the toes. 3) Stand tall and squeeze the glutes.
- **Common faults:** Heels lifting; Knees caving; Folding forward at the hips.
- **Progress to:** Goblet Squat (KB) (G2); Goblet Squat (DB) (G2); Barbell Box Squat (G2). **Or progress by:** Add a pause, tempo, then load (goblet squat).
- **Regress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or regress by:** Squat to a box, TRX assisted squat.
- **Same level swaps:** Frog Squat; Prisoner Squat; Bodyweight Squat
- **Cautions:** None specific. Generally joint friendly. Use a box with knee pain, heel elevation with stiff ankles.
- **Default prescription:** 2 to 3 sets x 12 to 20 reps (or 30 to 40s)
- **Coach sources:** Squat University, Paul Chek (Primal Pattern), Dan John
- **Also listed in:** Rehab: Knee

## Banded Barbell Box Squat

`SQB-038 | G2 | Squat: knee dominant bilateral (depth controlled) | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Barbell, Resistance band (confirm), Box / bench / step
- **Why we use it:** The box sets a consistent, safe depth and teaches people to sit back and control the descent. It is the best teaching squat for beginners and painful knees and, with a barbell or SSB, a classic DeFranco/Westside strength builder.
- **This variation:** Band resistance gets harder at the top (accommodating resistance) and can cue better positions such as knees out. Barbell: allows the heaviest loading for maximum strength and bone stimulus; earn it with technique (usually G3 to G4, Teams).
- **Muscles:** Quads, glutes, adductors, hamstrings
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Box at a height where the spine stays neutral. 2) Sit back and down with control, touch the box lightly (don't crash). 3) Stay braced, drive up through the whole foot.
- **Common faults:** Plonking down and relaxing on the box; Rocking back to get up; Knees caving as they stand.
- **Progress to:** SSB Squat (G3); SSB Box Squat (G3); Paused Goblet Squat (G3). **Or progress by:** Lower the box, add load (goblet then SSB/barbell), pause on the box without relaxing, remove the box.
- **Regress to:** Box Squat (G1); Goblet Box Squat (G1); Box Squat (High Box) (G1). **Or regress by:** Raise the box, TRX assisted box squat, sit to stand.
- **Same level swaps:** Barbell Box Squat; Goblet Squat (KB); Goblet Squat (DB)
- **Cautions:** None specific. Excellent for knee pain and older members: adjust height to the pain free range. Lower the box as mobility and control improve.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8
- **Coach sources:** DeFranco (Westside), Squat University, Cosgrove

## Cable Goblet Squat

`SQB-041 | G2 | Squat: knee dominant bilateral | STRONG, HYBRID, BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Kettlebell, Cable machine
- **Why we use it:** Holding the weight at the chest counterbalances the body, so people naturally squat more upright and deeper with better form. Dan John and Squat University both use it as THE teaching squat, and it is strong enough to stay useful for years. Fits groups perfectly because load scales from a 4kg KB to a 40kg+ DB.
- **This variation:** Cable: constant tension through the whole range with smooth, joint friendly resistance.
- **Muscles:** Quads, glutes, adductors, upper back, core
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Hold the bell tight to the chest, elbows pointing down. 2) Push the knees out and sit between the hips, chest proud. 3) Drive up through the whole foot, squeeze the glutes at the top.
- **Common faults:** Rounding the upper back and letting the weight pull you forward; Heels lifting; Knees caving inward on the way up.
- **Progress to:** Paused Goblet Squat (G3); 1.5 Rep Goblet Squat (G3). **Or progress by:** Add load, tempo (4-1-1-0), pause at the bottom, 1.5 reps, move to double KB front squat or SSB squat.
- **Regress to:** Goblet Box Squat (G1); Box Squat (G1); TRX Assisted Squat (G1). **Or regress by:** Goblet squat to a box, TRX assisted squat, lighter bell.
- **Same level swaps:** Goblet Squat (KB); Goblet Squat (DB); Tempo Goblet Squat
- **Cautions:** None specific. Knee and back friendly. Heels elevated version helps stiff ankles. Use a box for depth control with knee pain. Upper back can fatigue first as loads get heavy.

## Sissy Squat (Assisted)

`SQB-042 | G2 | Squat: knee dominant (quad lengthening) | STRONG | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Bodyweight
- **Why we use it:** Trains the quads with the knees travelling far over the toes and the hips extended. Builds strength in the end range of knee bending, which Ben Patrick uses to bulletproof knees. Assisted versions are surprisingly accessible.
- **This variation:** Assisted version: support lets members practise the full pattern safely while strength builds (Cosgrove: regress to progress).
- **Muscles:** Quads (rectus femoris in a lengthened position), hip flexors
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Hold a post or TRX for support. 2) Rise onto the toes, push the knees forward and lean the body back as one straight line from knee to shoulder. 3) Lower only as far as pain free, drive back up through the quads.
- **Common faults:** Bending at the hips (turns it into a normal squat); Dropping too deep too early; Letting go of the support before ready.
- **Progress to:** Zercher Squat (G3); DB Front Squat (G3); DB Overhead Squat (G3). **Or progress by:** Increase range, reduce hand assistance, add a plate at the chest, progress towards reverse Nordic.
- **Regress to:** Wall Sit (G1); Box Squat (G1); Frog Squat (G1). **Or regress by:** Short range only, more hand support, swap to Spanish squat or heels elevated goblet squat.
- **Same level swaps:** Reverse Nordic (Assisted); Sissy Squat (Assisted, Short Range)
- **Cautions:** Knee. Earn it. Start short range with hand support. Avoid with acute knee pain, recent knee surgery or knee replacements unless cleared.
- **Default prescription:** 2 to 3 sets x 6 to 12 reps, slow lowering, hand support
- **Coach sources:** Ben Patrick (ATG), Poliquin (VMO work)

## Cable Squat to Row

`SQB-043 | G2 | Horizontal pull: row | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Cable machine
- **Why we use it:** Rows build the upper back that holds posture upright and balances pressing. Chest supported rows remove the low back from the equation; single arm rows allow heavier loading and fix imbalances; bent over rows add hinge endurance. Aim for about 2 pulls for every push in desk based members.
- **This variation:** Cable: constant tension through the whole range with smooth, joint friendly resistance. Combination move: trains two qualities at once, efficient for HYBRID and BURN; keep technique of both parts clean before speeding up.
- **Muscles:** Upper back, lats, rear shoulders, biceps, grip
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Brace, shoulder blade pulls first, then the elbow. 2) Row towards the hip (lats) or lower ribs (upper back). 3) Pause, lower slowly to a full stretch.
- **Common faults:** Jerking and twisting the torso; Shrugging; Shortening the range.
- **Progress to:** Single Arm Cable Row (G3); Split Stance Single Arm Cable Row (G3); Single Arm Cable Row with Rotation (G3). **Or progress by:** Heavier, pause at the top, tempo, single arm, 1.5 reps.
- **Regress to:** Chest Supported DB Row (G1); Chest Supported DB Row (Neutral) (G1). **Or regress by:** Chest supported row, cable row, TRX row.
- **Same level swaps:** Cable High Row; Seated Cable Row; Standing Cable Row
- **Cautions:** None specific. Chest supported and cable versions are the most back friendly. Bent over versions load the low back: avoid pairing with RDLs for 40+.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8
- **Coach sources:** DeFranco, Cressey, Poliquin, Boyle

## Isometric Squat Hold

`SQB-044 | G1 | Squat: isometric | STRONG, HYBRID, BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Bodyweight
- **Why we use it:** A simple, joint friendly way to build quad strength and endurance with zero technique demand. Isometrics can reduce knee pain and are ideal for beginners, seniors and anyone who cannot yet squat through full range. The Swiss ball version lets people practise the squat path with support.
- **This variation:** Isometric: builds strength and tendon tolerance in a fixed position with minimal joint irritation.
- **Muscles:** Quads, glutes, adductors
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Back flat against the wall, feet hip width and slightly in front. 2) Slide down until the knees are at a pain free angle (aim 90 degrees over time). 3) Weight through the whole foot, breathe slowly, knees in line with toes.
- **Common faults:** Hands pushing on the thighs; Knees caving in; Going too deep too soon and aggravating knees.
- **Progress to:** Cyclist Squat (G2); DB Sumo Squat (G2); KB Sumo Squat (G2). **Or progress by:** Lower the position, hold longer, hold a plate, progress to single leg wall sit or tempo goblet squats.
- **Regress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or regress by:** Higher position, shorter holds, hands on thighs for the first few sessions.
- **Same level swaps:** Wall Sit; Isometric Wall Sit; Swiss Ball Wall Squat
- **Cautions:** None specific. Very knee friendly at higher positions. Adjust depth to stay at or below 3/10 pain. Avoid long holds with breath holding for members with high blood pressure.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 5 x 20 to 45s holds, rest 60s, about 70% effort
- **Coach sources:** Squat University, Rehab research (isometrics), Ben Patrick

- **Cautions:** None specific. Low back friendlier than back squats. Barbell front rack needs wrist, lat and T spine mobility. Zercher loads the elbows: use padding.

## DB Suitcase Squat

`SQB-047 | G2 | Squat: bilateral with offset load | STRONG, HYBRID, BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Dumbbells (confirm)
- **Why we use it:** Weights at the sides lower the centre of mass and make it a hybrid of squat and deadlift. Single side loading adds an anti lateral flexion core challenge. Easy to teach and very back friendly.
- **This variation:** One sided loading adds an anti rotation / anti lateral flexion core challenge and exposes left/right differences.
- **Muscles:** Quads, glutes, obliques (anti lateral flexion)
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Weights by the sides, arms long. 2) Sit down between the heels keeping the chest tall. 3) Stand up without leaning to the loaded side.
- **Common faults:** Rounding the back to reach lower; Leaning toward the weight; Shrugging the shoulders.
- **Progress to:** DB Front Squat (G3); DB Overhead Squat (G3); DB Squat to Overhead Press (G3). **Or progress by:** Heavier, single side only, tempo.
- **Regress to:** Wall Sit (G1); Box Squat (G1); Frog Squat (G1). **Or regress by:** Lighter weights, squat to a box.
- **Cautions:** None specific. Back friendly. Grip may limit load.
- **Default prescription:** 3 sets x 8 to 12 reps, tempo 3-0-1-1, rest 60 to 90s, RPE 7 to 9
- **Coach sources:** Dan John, Cosgrove

## Frog Squat

`SQB-048 | G1 | Squat: knee dominant bilateral | BURN, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Bodyweight
- **Why we use it:** The foundation squat pattern. Builds the movement before load and is useful for warm ups, high rep BURN work and beginners. Band and pause variations add a twist: mini bands cue the knees out, pulses keep tension, dead stops kill the bounce.
- **Muscles:** Quads, glutes, adductors
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Feet shoulder width, toes slightly out, tripod foot. 2) Sit down between the hips, knees track over the toes. 3) Stand tall and squeeze the glutes.
- **Common faults:** Heels lifting; Knees caving; Folding forward at the hips.
- **Progress to:** Goblet Squat (KB) (G2); Goblet Squat (DB) (G2); Barbell Box Squat (G2). **Or progress by:** Add a pause, tempo, then load (goblet squat).
- **Regress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or regress by:** Squat to a box, TRX assisted squat.
- **Same level swaps:** Prisoner Squat; Mini Band Squat; Bodyweight Squat
- **Cautions:** None specific. Generally joint friendly. Use a box with knee pain, heel elevation with stiff ankles.
- **Default prescription:** 2 to 3 sets x 12 to 20 reps (or 30 to 40s)
- **Coach sources:** Squat University, Paul Chek (Primal Pattern), Dan John

## Heels Elevated DB Squat

`SQB-049 | G2 | Squat: knee dominant bilateral | STRONG, HYBRID, BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Dumbbells (confirm), Box / bench / step
- **Why we use it:** Holding the weight at the chest counterbalances the body, so people naturally squat more upright and deeper with better form. Dan John and Squat University both use it as THE teaching squat, and it is strong enough to stay useful for years. Fits groups perfectly because load scales from a 4kg KB to a 40kg+ DB.
- **This variation:** Heels elevated: compensates for stiff ankles, keeps the torso upright and biases the quads (Squat University).
- **Muscles:** Quads, glutes, adductors, upper back, core
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Hold the bell tight to the chest, elbows pointing down. 2) Push the knees out and sit between the hips, chest proud. 3) Drive up through the whole foot, squeeze the glutes at the top.
- **Common faults:** Rounding the upper back and letting the weight pull you forward; Heels lifting; Knees caving inward on the way up.
- **Progress to:** Paused Goblet Squat (G3); 1.5 Rep Goblet Squat (G3). **Or progress by:** Add load, tempo (4-1-1-0), pause at the bottom, 1.5 reps, move to double KB front squat or SSB squat.
- **Regress to:** Box Squat (G1); Goblet Box Squat (G1); TRX Assisted Squat (G1). **Or regress by:** Goblet squat to a box, TRX assisted squat, lighter bell.
- **Same level swaps:** Goblet Squat (DB); Goblet Squat (KB); Tempo Goblet Squat
- **Cautions:** None specific. Knee and back friendly. Heels elevated version helps stiff ankles. Use a box for depth control with knee pain. Upper back can fatigue first as loads get heavy.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8
- **Coach sources:** Dan John, Squat University, Cosgrove, Boyle

## KB Deadstop Squat

`SQB-050 | G1 | Squat: knee dominant bilateral | BURN, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Kettlebell
- **Why we use it:** The foundation squat pattern. Builds the movement before load and is useful for warm ups, high rep BURN work and beginners. Band and pause variations add a twist: mini bands cue the knees out, pulses keep tension, dead stops kill the bounce.
- **Muscles:** Quads, glutes, adductors
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Feet shoulder width, toes slightly out, tripod foot. 2) Sit down between the hips, knees track over the toes. 3) Stand tall and squeeze the glutes.
- **Common faults:** Heels lifting; Knees caving; Folding forward at the hips.
- **Progress to:** Goblet Squat (KB) (G2); Goblet Squat (DB) (G2); Tempo Goblet Squat (G2). **Or progress by:** Add a pause, tempo, then load (goblet squat).
- **Regress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or regress by:** Squat to a box, TRX assisted squat.
- **Same level swaps:** Frog Squat; Prisoner Squat; Mini Band Squat
- **Cautions:** None specific. Generally joint friendly. Use a box with knee pain, heel elevation with stiff ankles.
- **Default prescription:** 2 to 3 sets x 12 to 20 reps (or 30 to 40s)
- **Coach sources:** Squat University, Paul Chek (Primal Pattern), Dan John

## DB Sumo Squat

`SQB-051 | G2 | Squat: wide stance bilateral | STRONG, HYBRID, BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Dumbbells (confirm)
- **Why we use it:** A wide stance with toes turned out shifts work towards the inner thighs and glutes and lets people with limited ankle mobility squat deeper with an upright chest. Useful variety and a gentler squat for some knees and hips.
- **Muscles:** Adductors, glutes, quads
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Feet wide, toes turned out about 30 degrees. 2) Knees push out over the toes, sit straight down. 3) Squeeze the glutes and inner thighs to stand.
- **Common faults:** Knees collapsing inward; Going wider than the hips allow; Rounding to reach the weight to the floor.
- **Progress to:** DB Front Squat (G3); DB Overhead Squat (G3); DB Squat to Overhead Press (G3). **Or progress by:** Add load, stand on two boxes for a deficit, pause at the bottom.
- **Regress to:** Wall Sit (G1); Box Squat (G1); Frog Squat (G1). **Or regress by:** Bodyweight, reduce depth, squat to a box.
- **Same level swaps:** KB Sumo Squat
- **Cautions:** None specific. Avoid very wide stances with hip pain or groin strains. Good for members whose ankles limit a normal squat.
- **Default prescription:** 3 sets x 8 to 12 reps, tempo 3-0-1-1, rest 60 to 90s, RPE 7 to 9
- **Coach sources:** Cosgrove, Squat University

## Narrow Stance Goblet Squat

`SQB-052 | G2 | Squat: knee dominant bilateral | STRONG, HYBRID, BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Progress to:** Paused Goblet Squat (G3); 1.5 Rep Goblet Squat (G3). **Or progress by:** Add load, tempo (4-1-1-0), pause at the bottom, 1.5 reps, move to double KB front squat or SSB squat.
- **Regress to:** Goblet Box Squat (G1); Box Squat (G1); TRX Assisted Squat (G1). **Or regress by:** Goblet squat to a box, TRX assisted squat, lighter bell.
- **Same level swaps:** Goblet Squat (KB); Goblet Squat (DB); Tempo Goblet Squat
- **Cautions:** None specific. Knee and back friendly. Heels elevated version helps stiff ankles. Use a box for depth control with knee pain. Upper back can fatigue first as loads get heavy.

- **Coach sources:** Dan John, Squat University, Cosgrove, Boyle

## KB Sumo Squat

`SQB-053 | G2 | Squat: wide stance bilateral | STRONG, HYBRID, BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Kettlebell
- **Why we use it:** A wide stance with toes turned out shifts work towards the inner thighs and glutes and lets people with limited ankle mobility squat deeper with an upright chest. Useful variety and a gentler squat for some knees and hips.
- **Muscles:** Adductors, glutes, quads

## Wide Stance Barbell Squat

`SQB-054 | G4 | Squat: knee dominant bilateral (barbell) | STRONG | Group: No | Impact: none | Teams only: Yes | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Barbell
- **Why we use it:** The classic heavy squat. Builds strength, muscle and bone density (LIFTMOR used heavy squats). Pin and Anderson squats start from the bottom, removing the bounce and building strength out of the hole. At Optimal it is a G4 lift for members with good mobility and no back or shoulder restriction; the SSB is the default alternative.
- **This variation:** Barbell: allows the heaviest loading for maximum strength and bone stimulus; earn it with technique (usually G3 to G4, Teams). Wide grip/stance shifts emphasis (chest/upper back or adductors) and can be less friendly for some shoulders and hips.
- **Muscles:** Quads, glutes, adductors, spinal erectors
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Bar on the upper back, hands tight, elbows under the bar. 2) Big breath and brace, sit between the hips with knees tracking the toes. 3) Drive up keeping the chest and hips rising together.
- **Common faults:** Hips shooting up first (good morning squat); Losing the brace and rounding at the bottom; Knees caving under load.
- **Progress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or progress by:** Add load, pause reps, tempo, 1.25 reps, rep maxes (Teams G4 only).
- **Regress to:** Zercher Squat (G3); DB Front Squat (G3); SSB Squat (G3). **Or regress by:** SSB squat, box squat, goblet or double KB front squat.
- **Same level swaps:** Anderson Squat; Tempo Back Squat; Paused Back Squat
- **Cautions:** Knee, Low back, Pelvic floor. High spinal load. Not for active back pain. Needs shoulder external rotation to hold the bar: use SSB or trap bar squat if shoulders are cranky.
- **Group swap:** Teams only (heavy or high skill): in groups use a G3 regression from the Regress to list
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8
- **Coach sources:** DeFranco, Squat University, LIFTMOR research, Poliquin

## Double KB Front Rack Squat

`SQB-055 | G4 | Squat: knee dominant bilateral (front loaded) | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Kettlebell
- **Why we use it:** Front loading keeps the torso upright, puts more work on the quads and core, and puts less shear on the low back than back squatting. The double KB front squat is a great G3 group squat; the barbell front squat is a G4 strength lift for those with the wrist and thoracic mobility.
- **This variation:** Double KB: heavier total load plus a front rack or bilateral grip demand.
- **Muscles:** Quads, glutes, upper back, core
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Bells or bar in a tight rack, elbows high and forward. 2) Brace, sit straight down between the hips. 3) Keep the elbows up as you drive up.
- **Common faults:** Elbows dropping and the chest falling forward; Wrists bent back painfully (barbell); Losing tension at the bottom.
- **Progress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or progress by:** Add load, pause at the bottom, tempo, progress DB → double KB → barbell front squat.
- **Regress to:** Zercher Squat (G3); DB Front Squat (G3). **Or regress by:** Goblet squat, box to control depth, lighter load.
- **Same level swaps:** Paused Front Squat; Barbell Front Squat
- **Cautions:** None specific. Low back friendlier than back squats. Barbell front rack needs wrist, lat and T spine mobility. Zercher loads the elbows: use padding.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8
- **Coach sources:** Squat University, Boyle, Dan John

## Goblet Squat with Rotation

`SQB-056 | G2 | Squat: knee dominant bilateral | STRONG, HYBRID, BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Kettlebell
- **Why we use it:** Holding the weight at the chest counterbalances the body, so people naturally squat more upright and deeper with better form. Dan John and Squat University both use it as THE teaching squat, and it is strong enough to stay useful for years. Fits groups perfectly because load scales from a 4kg KB to a 40kg+ DB.
- **This variation:** Combination move: trains two qualities at once, efficient for HYBRID and BURN; keep technique of both parts clean before speeding up.
- **Muscles:** Quads, glutes, adductors, upper back, core
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Hold the bell tight to the chest, elbows pointing down. 2) Push the knees out and sit between the hips, chest proud. 3) Drive up through the whole foot, squeeze the glutes at the top.
- **Common faults:** Rounding the upper back and letting the weight pull you forward; Heels lifting; Knees caving inward on the way up.
- **Progress to:** Paused Goblet Squat (G3); 1.5 Rep Goblet Squat (G3). **Or progress by:** Add load, tempo (4-1-1-0), pause at the bottom, 1.5 reps, move to double KB front squat or SSB squat.
- **Regress to:** Goblet Box Squat (G1); Box Squat (G1); TRX Assisted Squat (G1). **Or regress by:** Goblet squat to a box, TRX assisted squat, lighter bell.
- **Same level swaps:** Goblet Squat (KB); Goblet Squat (DB); Tempo Goblet Squat
- **Cautions:** None specific. Knee and back friendly. Heels elevated version helps stiff ankles. Use a box for depth control with knee pain. Upper back can fatigue first as loads get heavy.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8
- **Coach sources:** Dan John, Squat University, Cosgrove, Boyle

## Double KB Front Squat to Press

`SQB-057 | G4 | Squat + vertical push (combination) | BURN, HYBRID | Group: No | Impact: none | Teams only: Yes | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Barbell, Kettlebell
- **Why we use it:** Links a squat and an overhead press into one total body movement. Very metabolic, great for BURN and HYBRID sessions, and the legs help drive the weight overhead so people can press more.
- **This variation:** Double KB: heavier total load plus a front rack or bilateral grip demand. Combination move: trains two qualities at once, efficient for HYBRID and BURN; keep technique of both parts clean before speeding up.
- **Muscles:** Quads, glutes, shoulders, triceps, core
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Squat with the weight in the rack. 2) Drive up hard and use that momentum to press overhead. 3) Lock out with biceps by the ears, ribs down, then lower back to the rack.
- **Common faults:** Pressing before the legs finish the drive; Arching the low back at the top; Losing the rack position and squatting with the elbows dropped.
- **Progress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or progress by:** Add load, double KBs, barbell, more rounds or density.
- **Regress to:** KB Thruster (G3); KB Goblet Squat to Press (G3); DB Thruster (G3). **Or regress by:** Goblet squat to press, landmine squat to press, split into separate squat and press.
- **Same level swaps:** Barbell Thruster; Barbell Front Rack Squat to Press
- **Cautions:** Shoulder. Needs pain free overhead range. With shoulder pain swap to squat to landmine press. Watch technique as fatigue builds in circuits.
- **Group swap:** Teams only (heavy or high skill): in groups use a G3 regression from the Regress to list
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 4 sets x 8 to 12 reps, or 30 to 40s in circuits
- **Coach sources:** Cosgrove (MRT), DeFranco

## Squat to Box Stand Up (Bodyweight)

`SQB-058 | G1 | Squat: functional (sit to stand) | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Box / bench / step
- **Why we use it:** The most important real life squat: getting up from a chair or toilet. A key longevity skill and a core test for seniors (30 second sit to stand). Done fast on the way up, it trains power, which declines faster than strength with age.
- **This variation:** Combination move: trains two qualities at once, efficient for HYBRID and BURN; keep technique of both parts clean before speeding up.
- **Muscles:** Quads, glutes, balance
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Sit tall on a box or chair, feet slightly back under the knees. 2) Lean the chest forward, push the floor away and stand up tall. 3) Sit back down slowly with control, don't flop.
- **Common faults:** Using the hands to push off; Feet too far forward; Collapsing back down onto the seat.
- **Progress to:** Cyclist Squat (G2); DB Sumo Squat (G2); KB Sumo Squat (G2). **Or progress by:** Lower the box, hold a weight at the chest, stand up as fast as possible (power), single leg sit to stand.
- **Regress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or regress by:** Raise the seat, use hands on thighs or a TRX for help, reduce reps.
- **Same level swaps:** Sit to Stand (Chair); Fast Sit to Stand (Power)
- **Cautions:** None specific. Suitable for almost everyone. Raise the seat height for painful knees or hips. Single leg version needs good knee control.
- **Default prescription:** 3 sets x 8 to 12 reps (or max reps in 30s for testing), stand up fast, lower slowly
- **Coach sources:** Seniors research (functional testing), Gambetta (fundamental movement), Attia (centenarian decathlon)

- **Regress to:** KB Sumo Squat (G2); Goblet Squat (KB) (G2); Goblet Squat (DB) (G2). **Or regress by:** Goblet squat to press, landmine squat to press, split into separate squat and press.

# 02. SQUAT PATTERN: UNILATERAL

*Knee dominant, single leg and split stance*

**Grade ladder at a glance** (use this to slot every member into the same session at their level):

- **G1**: Split Squat (Bodyweight), TRX Assisted Split Squat, Box Step Up (Bodyweight), Poliquin Step Up, Petersen Step Up, Isometric Split Squat Hold, Reverse Lunge (Bodyweight)
- **G2**: Lunge Pulses, Split Squat (DB), TRX Lunge, Goblet Split Squat, Front Foot Elevated Split Squat, Rear Foot Elevated Split Squat (Bodyweight), DB Step Up, Goblet Step Up, Lateral Step Up, Crossover Step Up, Step Up with Knee Drive, Low Box Step Down, Heel Tap Step Down, Landmine Split Squat, Cable Split Squat, Reverse Lunge (DB), Goblet Reverse Lunge, Bulgarian Split Squat Jump (Light) ✱, Curtsy Lunge, Landmine Reverse Lunge, Split Squat with Overhead Reach, Reverse Lunge to Knee Drive, Forward Lunge (DB), Single Leg Sissy Squat (Assisted), Walking Lunge (DB), Walking Lunge Front Rack (KB), Cable Reverse Lunge
- **G3**: Barbell Walking Lunge, Slider Reverse Lunge, Rear Foot Elevated Split Squat (DB), Goblet RFESS, Barbell Step Up, Landmine RFESS, Barbell Split Squat, Box Pistol Squat, TRX Pistol Squat, Band Resisted Split Squat, Pistol Squat, Skater Squat, Deficit Reverse Lunge, Barbell Reverse Lunge, Offset Single Arm Split Squat, Single Leg Wall Sit, Front Rack Reverse Lunge (Barbell), Shrimp Squat, Overhead Walking Lunge (Plate)
- **G4**: Double KB Front Rack RFESS, Barbell RFESS ✱, Offset KB RFESS, Paused RFESS, 1.5 Rep RFESS, Single Leg Box Squat, Single Leg Squat to Bench

✱ = not for group sessions (impact).

## Split Squat (Bodyweight)

`SQU-001 | G1 | Single leg: split squat | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Bodyweight
- **Why we use it:** The entry point of the single leg ladder. A static split stance gives a stable base, so people learn to load one leg at a time safely. It builds balance, fixes imbalances and is far easier on the back than heavy bilateral squats. Front foot elevated adds knee travel (ATG style); cable and landmine versions add stability.
- **Muscles:** Quads, glutes, adductors
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Long split stance, both feet pointing forward, hip width apart. 2) Lower the back knee straight down towards the floor. 3) Push through the front foot to stand, keep the torso tall.
- **Common faults:** Stance too narrow (tightrope), losing balance; Front heel lifting; Lunging forward instead of dropping down.
- **Progress to:** ATG Split Squat (G2); SSB Split Squat (G2); Split Squat (DB) (G2). **Or progress by:** Add load, elevate the front foot (ATG style), then elevate the back foot (RFESS).
- **Regress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or regress by:** TRX or rig assisted split squat, shorter range, isometric split squat hold.
- **Same level swaps:** Split Squat (Supported); TRX Assisted Split Squat; Split Squat (Short Range)
- **Cautions:** None specific. Knee friendly when depth is controlled. Use a pad under the back knee. Hold a support for balance in seniors.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8 (each leg)
- **Coach sources:** Boyle, Squat University, Ben Patrick (front foot elevated)

## Barbell Walking Lunge

`SQU-002 | G3 | Single leg: forward / walking lunge | BURN, HYBRID, STRONG | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Barbell
- **Why we use it:** Forward and walking lunges add deceleration and balance: you have to control the body moving forward over the front leg. Very functional and very metabolic, so they suit BURN and HYBRID sessions. Loaded carry lunges add grip and core.
- **This variation:** Barbell: allows the heaviest loading for maximum strength and bone stimulus; earn it with technique (usually G3 to G4, Teams).
- **Muscles:** Quads, glutes, hamstrings, balance, grip when loaded
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Long step forward, land heel first. 2) Drop the back knee down, front knee over the middle of the foot. 3) Push through the front foot and step through to the next rep.
- **Common faults:** Short choppy steps that load the front knee; Front knee caving; Torso collapsing forward.
- **Progress to:** Barbell RFESS (G4); Paused RFESS (G4); 1.5 Rep RFESS (G4). **Or progress by:** Add load (DB, KB rack, overhead), pulses, longer distance.
- **Regress to:** TRX Lunge (G2); Lunge Pulses (G2); Forward Lunge (DB) (G2). **Or regress by:** Reverse lunge, split squat, hand support.
- **Same level swaps:** Overhead Walking Lunge (KB); Overhead Walking Lunge (Plate)
- **Cautions:** Knee. More knee stress than reverse lunges. Swap to reverse lunges or split squats with knee pain. Needs space in groups.
- **Default prescription:** 3 sets x 8 to 12 reps, tempo 3-0-1-1, rest 60 to 90s, RPE 7 to 9 (each leg) or 20 to 30m
- **Coach sources:** Gambetta (lunge matrix), Cosgrove, Paul Chek (lunge pattern)

## TRX Assisted Split Squat

`SQU-003 | G1 | Single leg: split squat | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** TRX
- **Why we use it:** The entry point of the single leg ladder. A static split stance gives a stable base, so people learn to load one leg at a time safely. It builds balance, fixes imbalances and is far easier on the back than heavy bilateral squats. Front foot elevated adds knee travel (ATG style); cable and landmine versions add stability.
- **This variation:** Assisted version: support lets members practise the full pattern safely while strength builds (Cosgrove: regress to progress).
- **Muscles:** Quads, glutes, adductors
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Long split stance, both feet pointing forward, hip width apart. 2) Lower the back knee straight down towards the floor. 3) Push through the front foot to stand, keep the torso tall.
- **Common faults:** Stance too narrow (tightrope), losing balance; Front heel lifting; Lunging forward instead of dropping down.
- **Progress to:** ATG Split Squat (G2); SSB Split Squat (G2); Split Squat (DB) (G2). **Or progress by:** Add load, elevate the front foot (ATG style), then elevate the back foot (RFESS).
- **Regress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or regress by:** TRX or rig assisted split squat, shorter range, isometric split squat hold.
- **Same level swaps:** Split Squat (Supported); Split Squat (Bodyweight); Split Squat (Short Range)
- **Cautions:** None specific. Knee friendly when depth is controlled. Use a pad under the back knee. Hold a support for balance in seniors.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8 (each leg)
- **Coach sources:** Boyle, Squat University, Ben Patrick (front foot elevated)

## Lunge Pulses

`SQU-004 | G2 | Single leg: forward / walking lunge | BURN, HYBRID, STRONG | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Bodyweight
- **Why we use it:** Forward and walking lunges add deceleration and balance: you have to control the body moving forward over the front leg. Very functional and very metabolic, so they suit BURN and HYBRID sessions. Loaded carry lunges add grip and core.
- **This variation:** Pulses keep constant tension in the bottom range: metabolic and BURN friendly.
- **Muscles:** Quads, glutes, hamstrings, balance, grip when loaded
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Long step forward, land heel first. 2) Drop the back knee down, front knee over the middle of the foot. 3) Push through the front foot and step through to the next rep.
- **Common faults:** Short choppy steps that load the front knee; Front knee caving; Torso collapsing forward.
- **Progress to:** Barbell Walking Lunge (G3); Overhead Walking Lunge (KB) (G3); Overhead Walking Lunge (Plate) (G3). **Or progress by:** Add load (DB, KB rack, overhead), pulses, longer distance.
- **Regress to:** Split Squat (Supported) (G1); Split Squat (Bodyweight) (G1); TRX Assisted Split Squat (G1). **Or regress by:** Reverse lunge, split squat, hand support.
- **Same level swaps:** TRX Lunge; Forward Lunge (DB); Walking Lunge (DB)
- **Cautions:** Knee. More knee stress than reverse lunges. Swap to reverse lunges or split squats with knee pain. Needs space in groups.
- **Default prescription:** 3 sets x 8 to 12 reps, tempo 3-0-1-1, rest 60 to 90s, RPE 7 to 9 (each leg) or 20 to 30m
- **Coach sources:** Gambetta (lunge matrix), Cosgrove, Paul Chek (lunge pattern)

## Slider Reverse Lunge

`SQU-008 | G3 | Single leg: reverse lunge | STRONG, HYBRID, BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Sliders (confirm)
- **Why we use it:** Stepping backwards keeps the shin more vertical, so it is far kinder to the knees than forward lunges while still training single leg strength and balance. The default lunge at Optimal. Deficit and slider versions increase range and control.
- **This variation:** Sliders add a friction based eccentric control challenge.
- **Muscles:** Quads, glutes, hamstrings
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Stand tall, step one foot back. 2) Drop the back knee towards the floor, front shin fairly vertical. 3) Drive through the front heel to stand back up.
- **Common faults:** Stepping too short; Front knee collapsing; Leaning forward and rounding.
- **Progress to:** Paused RFESS (G4); Barbell RFESS (G4); 1.5 Rep RFESS (G4). **Or progress by:** Add load, deficit (front foot on a plate), knee drive at the top, barbell/landmine.
- **Regress to:** SSB Reverse Lunge (G2); Reverse Lunge (DB) (G2); Cable Reverse Lunge (G2). **Or regress by:** Split squat (static), hand support, shorter range.
- **Same level swaps:** Reverse Lunge (Slider); Deficit Reverse Lunge; Barbell Reverse Lunge
- **Cautions:** None specific. Most knee friendly lunge. Use a pad and hand support for beginners.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8 (each leg)
- **Coach sources:** Boyle, Cosgrove, Squat University

- **Why we use it:** The entry point of the single leg ladder. A static split stance gives a stable base, so people learn to load one leg at a time safely. ## Box Step Up (Bodyweight)

`SQU-010 | G1 | Single leg: step up | STRONG, HYBRID, BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Box / bench / step
- **Why we use it:** A real life movement (stairs, kerbs, climbing). Very back friendly, easy to scale by box height, and the concentric emphasis means little soreness. Knee drive and crossover versions add balance and hip work.
- **Muscles:** Quads, glutes, hamstrings, balance
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Whole foot on the box, knee over the middle of the foot. 2) Lean forward slightly and drive through the box leg to stand tall. 3) Step down with control, don't push off the bottom leg.
- **Common faults:** Pushing off the floor leg; Knee caving as you stand; Box too high so the hip hikes.
- **Progress to:** DB Step Up (G2); Goblet Step Up (G2); Lateral Step Up (G2). **Or progress by:** Higher box, add DBs/goblet/barbell, add a knee drive, slower lowering.
- **Regress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or regress by:** Lower box, hand support, bodyweight.
- **Same level swaps:** Patrick Step; Poliquin Step Up; Petersen Step Up
- **Cautions:** None specific. Knee friendly at lower heights. Use a low box and hand support for seniors and knee pain. Faster 'step ups' in BURN keep impact low.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8 (each leg)
- **Coach sources:** Boyle, Cosgrove, Gambetta

## Rear Foot Elevated Split Squat (Bodyweight)

`SQU-011 | G2 | Single leg: split squat (rear foot elevated) | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Box / bench / step
- **Why we use it:** Mike Boyle's signature lower body lift. Huge leg strength with far less spinal load than heavy bilateral squats, fixes left/right differences, and stretches the back leg's hip flexor (great for desk workers). Lean forward slightly for more glutes, stay upright for more quads.
- **Muscles:** Quads, glutes, adductors, hip flexor stretch on the back leg
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Back foot laces down on a bench, front foot far enough forward that the front heel stays down. 2) Drop the back knee straight down, front knee tracks over the toes. 3) Drive through the front foot, keep the hips square.
- **Common faults:** Front foot too close so the heel lifts; Pushing off the back foot; Hips twisting or knee caving.
- **Progress to:** Goblet RFESS (G3); Landmine RFESS (G3); Rear Foot Elevated Split Squat (DB) (G3). **Or progress by:** Add load (DBs, then double KB rack, landmine, SSB/barbell), pause, 1.5 reps, deficit (front foot on a plate).
- **Regress to:** Split Squat (Supported) (G1); Split Squat (Bodyweight) (G1); TRX Assisted Split Squat (G1). **Or regress by:** Split squat with back foot on the floor, hand support, reduce depth.
- **Same level swaps:** ATG Split Squat; SSB Split Squat; Split Squat (DB)
- **Cautions:** None specific. Knee friendly when the depth is controlled. A lower bench helps tight hip flexors. Balance can limit beginners: hold the rig with one hand.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8 (each leg)
- **Coach sources:** Boyle, DeFranco, Cosgrove

- **Why we use it:** A real life movement (stairs, kerbs, climbing). Very back friendly, easy to scale by box height, and the concentric emphasis means little soreness. Knee drive and crossover versions add balance and hip work.

- **Coaching cues:** 1) Whole foot on the box, knee over the middle of the foot. 2) Lean forward slightly and drive through the box leg to stand tall. 3) Step down with control, don't push off the bottom leg.

## Landmine RFESS

`SQU-021 | G3 | Single leg: split squat (rear foot elevated) | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Landmine (confirm), Box / bench / step

## Low Box Step Down

`SQU-024 | G2 | Single leg: eccentric step down | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Box / bench / step
- **Why we use it:** Controlled lowering from a step builds knee control and eccentric quad strength, the exact quality needed for walking downstairs. Also a key screening test for knee valgus and hip control.
- **Muscles:** Quads, glutes, hip stabilisers
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Stand on a box, other leg hanging off the front or side. 2) Lower slowly by bending the standing knee, hips back slightly. 3) Tap the heel lightly and return without pushing off the floor.
- **Common faults:** Knee diving in; Hip dropping on the free side; Crashing down to the floor.
- **Progress to:** Pistol Squat (G3); Skater Squat (G3); Shrimp Squat (G3). **Or progress by:** Higher box, hold weight, slower lowering.
- **Regress to:** Patrick Step (G1); Poliquin Step Up (G1); Petersen Step Up (G1). **Or regress by:** Lower box, hand support, Poliquin step up.
- **Same level swaps:** Lateral Step Down; Forward Step Down; Heel Tap Step Down
- **Cautions:** None specific. Excellent for knee rehab when the box is low. Raise the height as control improves.
- **Default prescription:** 2 to 3 sets x 8 to 12 each leg, 3s lowering
- **Coach sources:** Squat University, Poliquin, Boyle
