- **Coach sources:** Boyle, Cosgrove, Gambetta

## Bulgarian Split Squat (Forward Lean)

`HGU-020 | G3 | Single leg: split squat (rear foot elevated) | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Box / bench / step
- **Why we use it:** Mike Boyle's signature lower body lift. Huge leg strength with far less spinal load than heavy bilateral squats, fixes left/right differences, and stretches the back leg's hip flexor (great for desk workers). Lean forward slightly for more glutes, stay upright for more quads.
- **Muscles:** Quads, glutes, adductors, hip flexor stretch on the back leg
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Back foot laces down on a bench, front foot far enough forward that the front heel stays down. 2) Drop the back knee straight down, front knee tracks over the toes. 3) Drive through the front foot, keep the hips square.
- **Common faults:** Front foot too close so the heel lifts; Pushing off the back foot; Hips twisting or knee caving.
- **Progress to:** Paused RFESS (G4); Barbell RFESS (G4); 1.5 Rep RFESS (G4). **Or progress by:** Add load (DBs, then double KB rack, landmine, SSB/barbell), pause, 1.5 reps, deficit (front foot on a plate).
- **Regress to:** ATG Split Squat (G2); SSB Split Squat (G2); Split Squat (DB) (G2). **Or regress by:** Split squat with back foot on the floor, hand support, reduce depth.
- **Same level swaps:** Goblet RFESS; Landmine RFESS; Rear Foot Elevated Split Squat (DB)
- **Cautions:** None specific. Knee friendly when the depth is controlled. A lower bench helps tight hip flexors. Balance can limit beginners: hold the rig with one hand.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8 (each leg)
- **Coach sources:** Boyle, DeFranco, Cosgrove

## Landmine Single Leg RDL

`HGU-021 | G3 | Hinge: single leg / staggered | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Landmine (confirm)
- **Why we use it:** Single leg hinges build hamstring and glute strength, balance and hip stability one side at a time, and they spare the spine because loads are lighter. Kickstand and B stance versions give a stepping stone with the back foot for support. Hip airplanes train hip rotation control (great for golf).
- **This variation:** Landmine: the arc path is shoulder and back friendly and very easy to learn.
- **Muscles:** Hamstrings, glutes (incl. glute med), foot and ankle stability
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Stand on one leg with a soft knee, other leg reaching back. 2) Hinge forward as one straight line from head to heel, hips square. 3) Drive the standing heel into the floor and squeeze the glute to stand.
- **Common faults:** Hips opening up (rotating) towards the ceiling; Rounding the back to reach the floor; Standing knee locked straight.
- **Progress to:** Single Leg Slider Curl (G4); Offset KB Single Leg RDL (G4). **Or progress by:** Kickstand → full single leg, add load (DB/KB, double KB, landmine), slower tempo, add a row or reach.
- **Regress to:** Kickstand RDL (G2); Banded Airplane (G2); Kickstand RDL (DB) (G2). **Or regress by:** Supported single leg RDL (hand on rig), kickstand RDL, bodyweight.
- **Same level swaps:** TRX Single Leg RDL; Single Leg RDL (DB); Single Leg RDL (KB)
- **Cautions:** None specific. Back friendly. Balance limits load: use a support or kickstand first. Excellent for golfers and runners.
- **Default prescription:** 3 sets x 8 to 12 reps, tempo 3-0-1-1, rest 60 to 90s, RPE 7 to 9 (each leg)
- **Coach sources:** Boyle, Cosgrove, Gambetta

## Reverse Lunge to RDL

`HGU-022 | G2 | Single leg: reverse lunge | STRONG, HYBRID, BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Barbell
- **Why we use it:** Stepping backwards keeps the shin more vertical, so it is far kinder to the knees than forward lunges while still training single leg strength and balance. The default lunge at Optimal. Deficit and slider versions increase range and control.
- **This variation:** Combination move: trains two qualities at once, efficient for HYBRID and BURN; keep technique of both parts clean before speeding up.
- **Muscles:** Quads, glutes, hamstrings
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Stand tall, step one foot back. 2) Drop the back knee towards the floor, front shin fairly vertical. 3) Drive through the front heel to stand back up.
- **Common faults:** Stepping too short; Front knee collapsing; Leaning forward and rounding.
- **Progress to:** Barbell Reverse Lunge (G3); Front Rack Reverse Lunge (Barbell) (G3); Slider Reverse Lunge (G3). **Or progress by:** Add load, deficit (front foot on a plate), knee drive at the top, barbell/landmine.
- **Regress to:** Split Squat (Supported) (G1); Split Squat (Bodyweight) (G1); TRX Assisted Split Squat (G1). **Or regress by:** Split squat (static), hand support, shorter range.
- **Same level swaps:** SSB Reverse Lunge; Reverse Lunge (DB); Cable Reverse Lunge
- **Cautions:** None specific. Most knee friendly lunge. Use a pad and hand support for beginners.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8 (each leg)
- **Coach sources:** Boyle, Cosgrove, Squat University

## Step Up to Single Leg RDL

`HGU-024 | G3 | Single leg: step up | STRONG, HYBRID, BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Box / bench / step
- **Why we use it:** A real life movement (stairs, kerbs, climbing). Very back friendly, easy to scale by box height, and the concentric emphasis means little soreness. Knee drive and crossover versions add balance and hip work.
- **Muscles:** Quads, glutes, hamstrings, balance
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Whole foot on the box, knee over the middle of the foot. 2) Lean forward slightly and drive through the box leg to stand tall. 3) Step down with control, don't push off the bottom leg.
- **Common faults:** Pushing off the floor leg; Knee caving as you stand; Box too high so the hip hikes.
- **Progress to:** Single Leg Slider Curl (G4); Offset KB Single Leg RDL (G4). **Or progress by:** Higher box, add DBs/goblet/barbell, add a knee drive, slower lowering.
- **Regress to:** DB Step Up (G2); Goblet Step Up (G2); Lateral Step Up (G2). **Or regress by:** Lower box, hand support, bodyweight.
- **Same level swaps:** Barbell Step Up
- **Cautions:** None specific. Knee friendly at lower heights. Use a low box and hand support for seniors and knee pain. Faster 'step ups' in BURN keep impact low.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8 (each leg)
- **Coach sources:** Boyle, Cosgrove, Gambetta

## Single Leg Good Morning

`HGU-029 | G2 | Hinge: good morning | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Barbell
- **Why we use it:** Load sits on the upper back while the hips hinge, which strengthens the hamstrings and back extensors. Bodyweight and banded versions are great hinge teaching tools; barbell versions are advanced. ATG style seated good mornings build hamstring and back mobility.
- **Muscles:** Hamstrings, glutes, spinal erectors
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Soft knees, brace, push the hips back. 2) Keep the spine long and neutral. 3) Stand up by driving the hips forward.
- **Common faults:** Rounding the spine; Bending the knees too much; Going deeper than hamstring length allows.
- **Progress to:** Barbell Good Morning (G3); Barbell Romanian Deadlift (G3); Paused DB RDL (G3). **Or progress by:** Band → light barbell → SSB good morning, tempo, pause.
- **Regress to:** Bodyweight Good Morning (G1); Hip Hinge to Wall (G1); Hip Hinge Dowel Drill (G1). **Or regress by:** Bodyweight, dowel hinge drill.
- **Same level swaps:** SSB Good Morning; Seated Good Morning; Banded Good Morning
- **Cautions:** Low back. Loaded good mornings are not for low back pain. Keep loads light and range controlled for 40+.
- **Default prescription:** 3 sets x 8 to 12 reps, tempo 3-0-1-1, rest 60 to 90s, RPE 7 to 9
- **Coach sources:** Westside/DeFranco, Ben Patrick (seated), Poliquin

## Offset KB Single Leg RDL

`HGU-038 | G4 | Hinge: single leg / staggered | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Kettlebell
- **Why we use it:** Single leg hinges build hamstring and glute strength, balance and hip stability one side at a time, and they spare the spine because loads are lighter. Kickstand and B stance versions give a stepping stone with the back foot for support. Hip airplanes train hip rotation control (great for golf).
- **This variation:** One sided loading adds an anti rotation / anti lateral flexion core challenge and exposes left/right differences.
- **Muscles:** Hamstrings, glutes (incl. glute med), foot and ankle stability
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Stand on one leg with a soft knee, other leg reaching back. 2) Hinge forward as one straight line from head to heel, hips square. 3) Drive the standing heel into the floor and squeeze the glute to stand.
- **Common faults:** Hips opening up (rotating) towards the ceiling; Rounding the back to reach the floor; Standing knee locked straight.
- **Progress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or progress by:** Kickstand → full single leg, add load (DB/KB, double KB, landmine), slower tempo, add a row or reach.
- **Regress to:** Single Leg RDL (KB) (G3); Single Leg RDL (Double KB) (G3); TRX Single Leg RDL (G3). **Or regress by:** Supported single leg RDL (hand on rig), kickstand RDL, bodyweight.
- **Cautions:** None specific. Back friendly. Balance limits load: use a support or kickstand first. Excellent for golfers and runners.
- **Default prescription:** 3 sets x 8 to 12 reps, tempo 3-0-1-1, rest 60 to 90s, RPE 7 to 9 (each leg)
- **Coach sources:** Boyle, Cosgrove, Gambetta

## Lateral Lunge to RDL

`HGU-046 | G2 | Single leg: lateral (frontal plane) | HYBRID, STRONG, BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Barbell
- **Why we use it:** Most training is forwards and backwards; lateral lunges train the side to side plane, building adductor strength and hip mobility that protect against groin strains and help golf, tennis and walking on uneven ground. Cossack squats are a great mobility and strength hybrid (Squat University and DeFranco's Limber 11).
- **This variation:** Combination move: trains two qualities at once, efficient for HYBRID and BURN; keep technique of both parts clean before speeding up.
- **Muscles:** Adductors, glutes, quads, hip mobility
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Step wide to the side, toes forward or slightly out. 2) Sit back into one hip, keeping the other leg straight. 3) Push back to the start through the bent leg.
- **Common faults:** Knee caving on the bent leg; Rounding the back to get lower; Heel lifting.
- **Progress to:** Slider Lateral Lunge (G3); Offset Lateral Lunge (G3); Speed Skater (Slider) (G3). **Or progress by:** Add load (goblet, DB, landmine), slider, deeper cossack.
- **Regress to:** Cossack Squat (Assisted) (G1); Lateral Lunge (Bodyweight) (G1). **Or regress by:** Shorter range, hand support, lateral lunge rock (mobility).
- **Same level swaps:** Cossack Squat; Lateral Lunge (DB); Cable Lateral Lunge
- **Cautions:** None specific. Groin and hip sensitive members: reduce range. Assisted versions (holding the rig) for seniors.
- **Default prescription:** 3 sets x 8 to 12 reps, tempo 3-0-1-1, rest 60 to 90s, RPE 7 to 9 (each side)
- **Coach sources:** Gambetta (multi plane), DeFranco (Limber 11), Squat University

## Curtsy to Single Leg RDL

`HGU-048 | G3 | Single leg: lunge (rotational/adductor bias) | HYBRID, BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Bodyweight
- **Why we use it:** Stepping back and across challenges the hips in a different plane, hitting the side glutes and inner thighs. Good variety and good for hip stability and golf.
- **Muscles:** Glutes (especially glute med), adductors, quads
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Step one foot back and across behind the other. 2) Lower straight down with the front knee tracking the toes. 3) Push through the front foot to return.
- **Common faults:** Twisting the hips excessively; Front knee caving; Losing balance from too narrow a step.
- **Progress to:** Single Leg Slider Curl (G4); Offset KB Single Leg RDL (G4). **Or progress by:** Add load, deficit, pair with a single leg RDL.
- **Regress to:** Curtsy Lunge (G2); Curtsy Lunge (DB) (G2). **Or regress by:** Shorter range, hand support, reverse lunge.
- **Cautions:** Knee. Can irritate knees and hips if the range is forced. Keep it pain free.
- **Default prescription:** 3 sets x 8 to 12 reps, tempo 3-0-1-1, rest 60 to 90s, RPE 7 to 9 (each side)
- **Coach sources:** Gambetta (multi plane), Cosgrove

## Single Leg Swiss Ball Curl

`HGU-051 | G3 | Hinge: knee flexion (hamstring curl) | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Swiss ball (confirm)
- **Why we use it:** Hamstrings both extend the hip and bend the knee; curls train the knee bending role that RDLs miss. Strong hamstrings protect knees and reduce hamstring strain risk. Nordic curls are among the best researched injury prevention exercises.
- **This variation:** Swiss ball adds instability for core control (Paul Chek); keep loads modest.
- **Muscles:** Hamstrings (knee flexion function), glutes
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Lie on your back, heels on the ball/sliders/TRX, lift the hips. 2) Curl the heels towards the bum keeping the hips high. 3) Extend slowly back out (control is the exercise).
- **Common faults:** Hips dropping during the curl; Rushing the lowering; Cramping (start with fewer reps).
- **Progress to:** Single Leg Slider Curl (G4); Offset KB Single Leg RDL (G4). **Or progress by:** Hips stay up throughout, single leg, slower lowering, Nordic progression.
- **Regress to:** Swiss Ball Hamstring Curl (G2); Hamstring Curl (Swiss Ball) (G2); TRX Hamstring Curl (G2). **Or regress by:** Hips on the floor curl, eccentric only, double leg.
- **Same level swaps:** Nordic Curl (Full); Slider Hamstring Curl; Hamstring Curl (Slider)
- **Cautions:** None specific. Knee friendly. Nordics are demanding: use band assistance and partial range, expect soreness at first.
- **Default prescription:** 3 sets x 8 to 12 reps, tempo 3-0-1-1, rest 60 to 90s, RPE 7 to 9
- **Coach sources:** Squat University, Ben Patrick (Nordic), Poliquin

- **Default prescription:** 3 sets x 8 to 12 reps, tempo 3-0-1-1, rest 60 to 90s, RPE 7 to 9 (pause 1 to 2s at the top)
- **Coach sources:** Cosgrove, McGill, Boyle

## Single Leg Slider Curl

`HGU-053 | G4 | Hinge: knee flexion (hamstring curl) | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Sliders (confirm)
- **Why we use it:** Hamstrings both extend the hip and bend the knee; curls train the knee bending role that RDLs miss. Strong hamstrings protect knees and reduce hamstring strain risk. Nordic curls are among the best researched injury prevention exercises.
- **This variation:** Sliders add a friction based eccentric control challenge.
- **Muscles:** Hamstrings (knee flexion function), glutes
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Lie on your back, heels on the ball/sliders/TRX, lift the hips. 2) Curl the heels towards the bum keeping the hips high. 3) Extend slowly back out (control is the exercise).
- **Common faults:** Hips dropping during the curl; Rushing the lowering; Cramping (start with fewer reps).
- **Progress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or progress by:** Hips stay up throughout, single leg, slower lowering, Nordic progression.
- **Regress to:** Slider Hamstring Curl (G3); Hamstring Curl (Slider) (G3); Nordic Curl (Full) (G3). **Or regress by:** Hips on the floor curl, eccentric only, double leg.
- **Cautions:** None specific. Knee friendly. Nordics are demanding: use band assistance and partial range, expect soreness at first.
- **Default prescription:** 3 sets x 8 to 12 reps, tempo 3-0-1-1, rest 60 to 90s, RPE 7 to 9
- **Coach sources:** Squat University, Ben Patrick (Nordic), Poliquin

## Split Stance Cable RDL

`HGU-054 | G2 | Hinge: single leg / staggered | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Cable machine
- **Why we use it:** Single leg hinges build hamstring and glute strength, balance and hip stability one side at a time, and they spare the spine because loads are lighter. Kickstand and B stance versions give a stepping stone with the back foot for support. Hip airplanes train hip rotation control (great for golf).
- **This variation:** Cable: constant tension through the whole range with smooth, joint friendly resistance. Split stance adds a stability and anti rotation demand closer to real life movement.
- **Muscles:** Hamstrings, glutes (incl. glute med), foot and ankle stability
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Stand on one leg with a soft knee, other leg reaching back. 2) Hinge forward as one straight line from head to heel, hips square. 3) Drive the standing heel into the floor and squeeze the glute to stand.
- **Common faults:** Hips opening up (rotating) towards the ceiling; Rounding the back to reach the floor; Standing knee locked straight.
- **Progress to:** Cable Single Leg RDL (G3); TRX Single Leg RDL (G3); Single Leg RDL (DB) (G3). **Or progress by:** Kickstand → full single leg, add load (DB/KB, double KB, landmine), slower tempo, add a row or reach.
- **Regress to:** KB Deadlift (G1); DB Deadlift (G1); Sumo KB Deadlift (G1). **Or regress by:** Supported single leg RDL (hand on rig), kickstand RDL, bodyweight.
- **Same level swaps:** Kickstand RDL; Banded Airplane; Kickstand RDL (DB)
- **Cautions:** None specific. Back friendly. Balance limits load: use a support or kickstand first. Excellent for golfers and runners.
- **Default prescription:** 3 sets x 8 to 12 reps, tempo 3-0-1-1, rest 60 to 90s, RPE 7 to 9 (each leg)
- **Coach sources:** Boyle, Cosgrove, Gambetta

- **Regress to:** TRX Hamstring Curl (G2); Swiss Ball Hamstring Curl (G2); Hamstring Curl (Swiss Ball) (G2). **Or regress by:** Hips on the floor curl, eccentric only, double leg.

## Single Leg RDL to Press

Kickstand and B stance versions give a stepping stone with the back foot for support. Hip airplanes train hip rotation control (great for golf).
- **This variation:** Combination move: trains two qualities at once, efficient for HYBRID and BURN; keep technique of both parts clean before speeding up.
- **Muscles:** Hamstrings, glutes (incl. glute med), foot and ankle stability
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Stand on one leg with a soft knee, other leg reaching back. 2) Hinge forward as one straight line from head to heel, hips square. 3) Drive the standing heel into the floor and squeeze the glute to stand.
- **Common faults:** Hips opening up (rotating) towards the ceiling; Rounding the back to reach the floor; Standing knee locked straight.

## Single Leg Back Extension

`HGU-057 | G3 | Hinge: back extension | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Bodyweight
- **Why we use it:** Strengthens the back extensors and glutes, improving posture and back resilience. Reverse hypers decompress the spine as they train. Extend to neutral only: the goal is a strong, straight spine, not arching.
- **Muscles:** Spinal erectors, glutes, hamstrings
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Hinge at the hips, keep the spine long. 2) Lift to a straight line from head to heels using the glutes. 3) Lower with control.
- **Common faults:** Hyperextending at the top; Swinging/using momentum; Rounding heavily at the bottom under load.
- **Progress to:** Single Leg Slider Curl (G4); Offset KB Single Leg RDL (G4). **Or progress by:** Hold a plate, single leg, pause at the top.
- **Regress to:** Prone Cobra (Chek) (G2); Reverse Hyper (Bench) (G2); Superman (Alternating) (G2). **Or regress by:** Superman, bird dog, shorter range.
- **Cautions:** None specific. Good for most back pain when kept to neutral. Avoid loaded flexion at the bottom for osteoporosis.
- **Default prescription:** 2 to 3 sets x 10 to 15 reps, tempo 2-1-1-1, rest 45 to 60s, RPE 8
- **Coach sources:** DeFranco (reverse hyper), McGill, Paul Chek (prone cobra)

## Single Arm KB Swing

`HGU-059 | G3 | Hinge: ballistic (power) | BURN, HYBRID, STRONG | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Kettlebell
- **Why we use it:** The king of hinge conditioning (Dan John, Pavel). Trains explosive hip extension (power) and heart rate at the same time with no impact on the knees. Excellent for fat loss, posture and glute strength. Dead stop versions teach control; single arm versions add anti rotation.
- **This variation:** One sided loading adds an anti rotation / anti lateral flexion core challenge and exposes left/right differences.
- **Muscles:** Glutes, hamstrings, core, grip, cardiovascular system
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Hike the bell back high between the thighs. 2) Snap the hips forward, squeeze the glutes, let the bell float to chest height. 3) Let it fall, hinge late, keep the spine neutral.
- **Common faults:** Squatting the swing instead of hinging; Lifting with the arms; Leaning back at the top.
- **Progress to:** Double KB Clean (G4); KB High Pull (Single Arm) (G4); Barbell Push Jerk (G4). **Or progress by:** Heavier bell, single arm, alternating, swings EMOM, heavier with fewer reps for power.
- **Regress to:** KB Swings (G2); KB Swing (Power) (G2); American KB Swing (G2). **Or regress by:** KB deadlift, dead stop swing, lighter bell, cable pull through.
- **Same level swaps:** Double KB Swing; Single Arm KB Swing to Catch; Single Arm KB Swing (Anti Rotation)
- **Cautions:** Low back. Back friendly when the hinge is good. Teach the KB deadlift first. Not for acute low back pain. American (overhead) swings stress shoulders and low back: use hip height swings instead.
- **Default prescription:** 4 to 10 sets x 10 to 20 reps, or EMOM; 'hike, snap, float'
- **Coach sources:** Dan John, Pavel Tsatsouline, Cosgrove

## Standing Cable Hip Extension

`HGU-060 | G1 | Hinge: hip extension accessory | STRONG, HYBRID, BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Cable machine
- **Why we use it:** Cable/band pull throughs teach the hip hinge with the load pulling from behind, so people naturally sit the hips back and finish with the glutes. Kickbacks and quadruped hip extensions isolate the glutes for activation and rehab.
- **This variation:** Cable: constant tension through the whole range with smooth, joint friendly resistance.
- **Muscles:** Glutes, hamstrings
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Face away from the cable, rope between the legs. 2) Hinge back letting the rope pull the hips back. 3) Drive the hips through and squeeze the glutes, stand tall.
- **Common faults:** Pulling with the arms; Squatting instead of hinging; Leaning back at the top.
- **Progress to:** Single Arm Cable Pull Through (G2); KB Swings (G2); KB Swing (Power) (G2). **Or progress by:** Heavier, pause at the top, progress to KB swing.
- **Regress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or regress by:** Band version, shorter range.
- **Same level swaps:** Cable Kickback; Band Pull Through; Cable Pull Through
- **Cautions:** None specific. Very back friendly. A great swing and deadlift regression.
- **Default prescription:** 2 to 3 sets x 10 to 15 reps, tempo 2-1-1-1, rest 45 to 60s, RPE 8
- **Coach sources:** Cosgrove, McGill, Boyle
- **Also listed in:** Rehab: Hip

# 05. HORIZONTAL PUSH

*Chest, front of shoulder, triceps*

**Grade ladder at a glance** (use this to slot every member into the same session at their level):

- **G1**: Wall Press Up, Incline Press Up (Bench), Box Press Up, Knee Press Up, Press Up Plus
- **G2**: DB Squeeze Press, DB Low Incline Press, DB Fly, Incline DB Fly, Press Up, Tempo Press Up, Close Grip Press Up, Wide Press Up, TRX Press Up, TRX Chest Fly, Landmine Press (Half Kneeling), Landmine Chest Press, Press Up to Shoulder Tap, Cable Chest Press, Split Stance Cable Press, Cable Fly, Low to High Cable Fly, Single Arm Incline Press Up, High to Low Cable Fly, Band Chest Press, DB Incline Press, Band Chest Fly, Swiss Ball DB Press, Neutral Grip DB Press, Plate Squeeze Press (Svend), Ring Dip (Assisted)
- **G3**: KB Floor Press, Bottoms Up KB Floor Press, Paused Press Up, Hand Release Press Up, Decline Press Up, Close Grip Bench Press, Deficit Press Up (DB Handles), Spoto Press, Pin Press, Band Resisted Press Up, Weighted Press Up (Plate), Single Arm Landmine Press (Standing), Archer Press Up, Single Arm Cable Chest Press, Spiderman Press Up, Swiss Ball Press Up, DB Bench Press, DB Floor Press, Alternating DB Bench Press, Bench Dip, Parallel Bar Dip
- **G4**: Double KB Floor Press ✱, Barbell Bench Press ✱, Barbell Floor Press ✱, Incline Barbell Press ✱, Paused Bench Press ✱, Plyo Press Up ✱, Single Arm DB Bench Press ✱, Single Arm DB Floor Press ✱

✱ = not for group sessions (impact).

## Wall Press Up

`HPU-001 | G1 | Horizontal push: push up | STRONG, HYBRID, BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Bodyweight
- **Why we use it:** A moving plank: chest and arm strength plus core control. The shoulder blades move freely, which is healthier for shoulders than bench pressing. Easy to scale by hand height so every level in a group can do the same exercise. Push up plus adds serratus work for shoulder health.
- **Muscles:** Chest, shoulders, triceps, serratus, core (anti extension)
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Hands just outside shoulders, body in a straight line, glutes and abs tight. 2) Lower the chest between the hands, elbows about 45 degrees from the body. 3) Push the floor away until arms are straight and the upper back is spread.
- **Common faults:** Hips sagging; Elbows flaring to 90 degrees; Head poking forward / half reps.
- **Progress to:** Press Up (G2); TRX Press Up (G2); Wide Press Up (G2). **Or progress by:** Lower the hand height (wall → bench → box → floor), tempo, pause, feet elevated, add a weighted vest/plate.
- **Regress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or regress by:** Higher incline (bench or wall), knee push up, shorter range.
- **Same level swaps:** Box Press Up; Knee Press Up; Incline Press Up (Bench)
- **Cautions:** None specific. Wrist pain: use DB handles or fists. Shoulder pain: elevate the hands and keep elbows tucked.
- **Default prescription:** 3 sets x 6 to 15 reps (or total reps progression)
- **Coach sources:** Cosgrove, Boyle, Dan John

## DB Squeeze Press

`HPU-002 | G2 | Horizontal push: DB/KB press | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Dumbbells (confirm)
- **Why we use it:** Dumbbells let each arm move freely and the shoulders find their own path, so they are friendlier for 40+ shoulders than a straight bar. Neutral grip (palms facing) is the most shoulder friendly; squeeze presses bias the chest with lighter loads; single arm versions add core.
- **Muscles:** Chest, front shoulders, triceps
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Shoulder blades back and down. 2) Lower with elbows about 45 degrees, forearms vertical. 3) Press up together without clanking the bells.
- **Common faults:** Flaring elbows; Dropping too deep with tight shoulders; Arching the low back off the bench.
- **Progress to:** DB Bench Press (G3); DB Floor Press (G3); Alternating DB Bench Press (G3). **Or progress by:** Heavier, single arm, alternating, tempo, incline angle changes.
- **Regress to:** Box Press Up (G1); Wall Press Up (G1); Knee Press Up (G1). **Or regress by:** Floor press, lighter weight, push up variation.
- **Same level swaps:** DB Incline Press; Swiss Ball DB Press; DB Low Incline Press
- **Cautions:** None specific. Neutral grip and floor presses protect shoulders. Single arm versions: brace hard.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8
- **Coach sources:** Poliquin, Cosgrove, Cressey

## DB Fly

`HPU-006 | G2 | Horizontal push: fly (isolation) | STRONG | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Dumbbells (confirm)
- **Why we use it:** Flys isolate the chest by moving the arm across the body with the elbow fixed. Useful for muscle building and variety at lighter loads.
- **Muscles:** Chest, front shoulders
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Slight bend in the elbows, kept fixed. 2) Open the arms with control until a stretch across the chest. 3) Hug back together, squeezing the chest.
- **Common faults:** Going too deep and stressing the shoulder; Bending and straightening the elbows (turns into a press); Going too heavy.
- **Progress to:** DB Bench Press (G3); DB Floor Press (G3); Alternating DB Bench Press (G3). **Or progress by:** Cable, slower tempo, pauses.
- **Regress to:** Box Press Up (G1); Wall Press Up (G1); Knee Press Up (G1). **Or regress by:** Lighter, shorter range, band fly.
- **Same level swaps:** Incline DB Fly; Cable Fly; TRX Chest Fly
- **Cautions:** Shoulder. Limit range for shoulder pain. Cables are smoother than DBs.
- **Default prescription:** 2 to 3 sets x 10 to 15 reps, tempo 2-1-1-1, rest 45 to 60s, RPE 8
- **Coach sources:** Poliquin, Schoenfeld (hypertrophy)

## Tempo Press Up

`HPU-011 | G2 | Horizontal push: push up | STRONG, HYBRID, BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Bodyweight
- **Why we use it:** A moving plank: chest and arm strength plus core control. The shoulder blades move freely, which is healthier for shoulders than bench pressing. Easy to scale by hand height so every level in a group can do the same exercise. Push up plus adds serratus work for shoulder health.
- **This variation:** Tempo version: a slow 3 to 5 second lowering builds control, tendon strength and muscle at lighter loads (Poliquin), ideal for joint sensitive members.
- **Muscles:** Chest, shoulders, triceps, serratus, core (anti extension)
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Hands just outside shoulders, body in a straight line, glutes and abs tight. 2) Lower the chest between the hands, elbows about 45 degrees from the body. 3) Push the floor away until arms are straight and the upper back is spread.
- **Common faults:** Hips sagging; Elbows flaring to 90 degrees; Head poking forward / half reps.
- **Progress to:** Paused Press Up (G3); Archer Press Up (G3); Decline Press Up (G3). **Or progress by:** Lower the hand height (wall → bench → box → floor), tempo, pause, feet elevated, add a weighted vest/plate.
- **Regress to:** Box Press Up (G1); Wall Press Up (G1); Knee Press Up (G1). **Or regress by:** Higher incline (bench or wall), knee push up, shorter range.
- **Same level swaps:** Press Up; TRX Press Up; Wide Press Up
- **Cautions:** None specific. Wrist pain: use DB handles or fists. Shoulder pain: elevate the hands and keep elbows tucked.
- **Default prescription:** 3 sets x 6 to 15 reps (or total reps progression)
- **Coach sources:** Cosgrove, Boyle, Dan John

## TRX Chest Fly

`HPU-027 | G2 | Horizontal push: fly (isolation) | STRONG | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** TRX
- **Why we use it:** Flys isolate the chest by moving the arm across the body with the elbow fixed. Useful for muscle building and variety at lighter loads.
- **Muscles:** Chest, front shoulders
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Slight bend in the elbows, kept fixed. 2) Open the arms with control until a stretch across the chest. 3) Hug back together, squeezing the chest.
- **Common faults:** Going too deep and stressing the shoulder; Bending and straightening the elbows (turns into a press); Going too heavy.
- **Progress to:** Pin Press (G3); Bench Dip (G3); Spoto Press (G3). **Or progress by:** Cable, slower tempo, pauses.
- **Regress to:** Box Press Up (G1); Wall Press Up (G1); Knee Press Up (G1). **Or regress by:** Lighter, shorter range, band fly.
- **Same level swaps:** DB Fly; Cable Fly; Incline DB Fly
- **Cautions:** Shoulder. Limit range for shoulder pain. Cables are smoother than DBs.
- **Default prescription:** 2 to 3 sets x 10 to 15 reps, tempo 2-1-1-1, rest 45 to 60s, RPE 8
- **Coach sources:** Poliquin, Schoenfeld (hypertrophy)

## Pin Press

`HPU-028 | G3 | Horizontal push: press (bench / floor) | STRONG | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Barbell
- **Why we use it:** Pressing builds upper body strength and muscle. DB versions allow a natural path for the shoulders; floor presses limit range, which protects shoulders (a DeFranco favourite for cranky shoulders). Barbell bench is a G4 strength option.
- **Muscles:** Chest, front shoulders, triceps
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Shoulder blades pulled back and down, feet planted. 2) Lower with control to the chest (or until elbows touch the floor). 3) Press up and slightly back, keep the wrists stacked over the elbows.
- **Common faults:** Flared elbows at 90 degrees; Bouncing off the chest; Losing the shoulder blade position.
- **Progress to:** Paused Bench Press (G4); Barbell Bench Press (G4); Barbell Floor Press (G4). **Or progress by:** Add load, pause on the chest, rep max on rotating variations (Teams G4).
- **Regress to:** Press Up (G2); TRX Press Up (G2); Wide Press Up (G2). **Or regress by:** DB floor press, neutral grip DB press, push up.
- **Same level swaps:** Spoto Press; KB Floor Press; DB Bench Press
- **Cautions:** Shoulder. Shoulder pain: floor press, neutral grip DBs, or landmine press. Wrists stacked.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8
- **Coach sources:** DeFranco, Poliquin, Cosgrove

## Band Resisted Press Up

`HPU-029 | G3 | Horizontal push: push up | STRONG, HYBRID, BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Resistance band (confirm)
- **Why we use it:** A moving plank: chest and arm strength plus core control. The shoulder blades move freely, which is healthier for shoulders than bench pressing. Easy to scale by hand height so every level in a group can do the same exercise. Push up plus adds serratus work for shoulder health.
- **This variation:** Band resistance gets harder at the top (accommodating resistance) and can cue better positions such as knees out.
- **Muscles:** Chest, shoulders, triceps, serratus, core (anti extension)
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Hands just outside shoulders, body in a straight line, glutes and abs tight. 2) Lower the chest between the hands, elbows about 45 degrees from the body. 3) Push the floor away until arms are straight and the upper back is spread.
- **Common faults:** Hips sagging; Elbows flaring to 90 degrees; Head poking forward / half reps.
- **Progress to:** Paused Bench Press (G4); Barbell Bench Press (G4); Barbell Floor Press (G4). **Or progress by:** Lower the hand height (wall → bench → box → floor), tempo, pause, feet elevated, add a weighted vest/plate.
- **Regress to:** Press Up (G2); TRX Press Up (G2); Wide Press Up (G2). **Or regress by:** Higher incline (bench or wall), knee push up, shorter range.
- **Same level swaps:** Paused Press Up; Archer Press Up; Decline Press Up
- **Cautions:** None specific. Wrist pain: use DB handles or fists. Shoulder pain: elevate the hands and keep elbows tucked.
- **Default prescription:** 3 sets x 6 to 15 reps (or total reps progression)
- **Coach sources:** Cosgrove, Boyle, Dan John

## Landmine Press (Half Kneeling)

`HPU-030 | G2 | Push: landmine press | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Landmine (confirm)
- **Why we use it:** The landmine press moves on an arc between a horizontal and vertical press, letting the shoulder blade move freely. It is the most shoulder friendly way to press overhead and the go to for members who can't press straight overhead (Cressey). Half kneeling adds core and hip stability.
- **This variation:** Landmine: the arc path is shoulder and back friendly and very easy to learn. Kneeling position locks the hips so the core has to control the trunk and stops the legs cheating.
- **Muscles:** Shoulders, chest, triceps, serratus, core
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Hold the end of the bar at the shoulder, ribs down, glutes tight. 2) Press up and forward, letting the shoulder blade reach around. 3) Lower with control back to the shoulder.
- **Common faults:** Arching the low back; Shrugging; Twisting the torso to press.
- **Progress to:** Single Arm Landmine Push Press (G3); Single Arm Landmine Press (Standing) (G3). **Or progress by:** Half kneeling → tall kneeling → split stance → standing → push press; add plates.
- **Regress to:** Landmine Press (Light) (G1); Seated DB Shoulder Press (G1). **Or regress by:** Lighter, two hands, half kneeling.
- **Same level swaps:** Landmine Press; Landmine Push Press; Landmine Chest Press
- **Cautions:** None specific. Best press for shoulder pain and limited overhead range.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8 (each arm)
- **Coach sources:** Cressey, Boyle, DeFranco

- **Coaching cues:** 1) Hold the end of the bar at the shoulder, ribs down, glutes tight. 2) Press up and forward, letting the shoulder blade reach around. 3) Lower with control back to the shoulder.

- **Same level swaps:** Single Arm Landmine Push Press; Z Press (DB); Offset DB Press

## Press Up Plus

`HPU-035 | G1 | Shoulder: serratus anterior | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Bodyweight
- **Why we use it:** The serratus holds the shoulder blade against the ribcage and rotates it upward for overhead reaching. Weak serratus = winging and shoulder pain.
- **Muscles:** Serratus anterior
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Arms straight. 2) Push the floor or weight away, spreading the shoulder blades. 3) Return slowly.
- **Common faults:** Bending the elbows; Shrugging; Sagging hips (push up plus).
- **Progress to:** DB Fly (G2); Press Up (G2); Cable Fly (G2). **Or progress by:** Push up plus, band punch, heavier.
- **Regress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or regress by:** Wall version.
- **Same level swaps:** Scapula Push Up; Serratus Punch (Band); Bear Plank Protraction
- **Cautions:** None specific. Very shoulder friendly.
- **Default prescription:** 2 to 3 sets x 10 to 15 reps, tempo 2-1-1-1, rest 45 to 60s, RPE 8
- **Coach sources:** Cressey, Squat University
- **Also listed in:** Rehab: Shoulder

## Cable Chest Press

`HPU-036 | G2 | Horizontal push: cable / band press | STRONG, HYBRID, BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Cable machine
- **Why we use it:** Standing presses with cables or bands train pushing while the core resists rotation and extension, closer to real life pushing. Smooth, joint friendly resistance.
- **This variation:** Cable: constant tension through the whole range with smooth, joint friendly resistance.
- **Muscles:** Chest, shoulders, triceps, core (standing)
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Split or athletic stance, brace. 2) Press forward until arms are straight, keep the ribs down. 3) Return with control.
- **Common faults:** Leaning into the press; Rotating the torso; Shrugging.
- **Progress to:** Single Arm Cable Chest Press (G3); Paused Press Up (G3); Archer Press Up (G3). **Or progress by:** Single arm, heavier, slower, split stance to parallel stance.
- **Regress to:** Box Press Up (G1); Wall Press Up (G1); Knee Press Up (G1). **Or regress by:** Two arms, lighter, wider stance.
- **Same level swaps:** Split Stance Cable Press; Band Chest Press
- **Cautions:** None specific. Very shoulder friendly.
- **Default prescription:** 3 sets x 8 to 12 reps, tempo 3-0-1-1, rest 60 to 90s, RPE 7 to 9
- **Coach sources:** Boyle, Cosgrove

## Plyo Press Up

`HPU-041 | G4 | Power: upper body plyometric | HYBRID | Group: No | Impact: high | Teams only: Yes | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Bodyweight
- **Why we use it:** Explosive push ups train upper body power. Advanced and higher joint stress, so Teams only for members with healthy wrists and shoulders.
- **Muscles:** Chest, shoulders, triceps
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Lower under control, push explosively so the hands leave the floor. 2) Land softly with bent elbows. 3) Reset each rep.
- **Common faults:** Sagging hips; Landing on locked elbows; Doing them fatigued.
- **Progress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or progress by:** Higher, then clap.
- **Regress to:** Pin Press (G3); Bench Dip (G3); Spoto Press (G3). **Or regress by:** Incline plyo push up, med ball chest pass.
- **Same level swaps:** Clap Press Up
- **Cautions:** Pelvic floor, Shoulder. Wrist and shoulder stress. Not for groups or anyone with shoulder pain. Med ball chest pass is the safer option.
- **Group swap:** Group swap: med ball chest pass or explosive band press
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 5 sets x 3 to 6 reps, full recovery (60 to 120s), stop when speed drops
- **Coach sources:** DeFranco, Gambetta
- **Also listed in:** Power And Plyometrics

## Cable Fly

`HPU-042 | G2 | Horizontal push: fly (isolation) | STRONG | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Cable machine
- **Why we use it:** Flys isolate the chest by moving the arm across the body with the elbow fixed. Useful for muscle building and variety at lighter loads.
- **This variation:** Cable: constant tension through the whole range with smooth, joint friendly resistance.
- **Muscles:** Chest, front shoulders
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Slight bend in the elbows, kept fixed. 2) Open the arms with control until a stretch across the chest. 3) Hug back together, squeezing the chest.
- **Common faults:** Going too deep and stressing the shoulder; Bending and straightening the elbows (turns into a press); Going too heavy.
- **Progress to:** Single Arm Cable Chest Press (G3); Pin Press (G3); Bench Dip (G3). **Or progress by:** Cable, slower tempo, pauses.
- **Regress to:** Box Press Up (G1); Wall Press Up (G1); Knee Press Up (G1). **Or regress by:** Lighter, shorter range, band fly.
- **Same level swaps:** Low to High Cable Fly; High to Low Cable Fly; DB Fly
- **Cautions:** Shoulder. Limit range for shoulder pain. Cables are smoother than DBs.
- **Default prescription:** 2 to 3 sets x 10 to 15 reps, tempo 2-1-1-1, rest 45 to 60s, RPE 8
- **Coach sources:** Poliquin, Schoenfeld (hypertrophy)

## DB Bench Press

`HPU-047 | G3 | Horizontal push: press (bench / floor) | STRONG | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Barbell, Dumbbells (confirm), Box / bench / step
- **Why we use it:** Pressing builds upper body strength and muscle. DB versions allow a natural path for the shoulders; floor presses limit range, which protects shoulders (a DeFranco favourite for cranky shoulders). Barbell bench is a G4 strength option.
- **Muscles:** Chest, front shoulders, triceps
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Shoulder blades pulled back and down, feet planted. 2) Lower with control to the chest (or until elbows touch the floor). 3) Press up and slightly back, keep the wrists stacked over the elbows.
- **Common faults:** Flared elbows at 90 degrees; Bouncing off the chest; Losing the shoulder blade position.
- **Progress to:** Single Arm DB Bench Press (G4); Single Arm DB Floor Press (G4); Paused Bench Press (G4). **Or progress by:** Add load, pause on the chest, rep max on rotating variations (Teams G4).
- **Regress to:** DB Squeeze Press (G2); DB Incline Press (G2); Swiss Ball DB Press (G2). **Or regress by:** DB floor press, neutral grip DB press, push up.
- **Same level swaps:** DB Floor Press; Alternating DB Bench Press; Pin Press
- **Cautions:** Shoulder. Shoulder pain: floor press, neutral grip DBs, or landmine press. Wrists stacked.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8
- **Coach sources:** DeFranco, Poliquin, Cosgrove

## Band Chest Press

`HPU-048 | G2 | Horizontal push: cable / band press | STRONG, HYBRID, BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Resistance band (confirm)
- **Why we use it:** Standing presses with cables or bands train pushing while the core resists rotation and extension, closer to real life pushing. Smooth, joint friendly resistance.
- **Muscles:** Chest, shoulders, triceps, core (standing)
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Split or athletic stance, brace. 2) Press forward until arms are straight, keep the ribs down. 3) Return with control.
- **Common faults:** Leaning into the press; Rotating the torso; Shrugging.
- **Progress to:** Band Resisted Press Up (G3); Paused Press Up (G3); Archer Press Up (G3). **Or progress by:** Single arm, heavier, slower, split stance to parallel stance.
- **Regress to:** Box Press Up (G1); Wall Press Up (G1); Knee Press Up (G1). **Or regress by:** Two arms, lighter, wider stance.
- **Same level swaps:** Cable Chest Press; Split Stance Cable Press
- **Cautions:** None specific. Very shoulder friendly.
- **Default prescription:** 3 sets x 8 to 12 reps, tempo 3-0-1-1, rest 60 to 90s, RPE 7 to 9
- **Coach sources:** Boyle, Cosgrove

## DB Incline Press

`HPU-049 | G2 | Horizontal push: DB/KB press | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Dumbbells (confirm), Box / bench / step
- **Why we use it:** Dumbbells let each arm move freely and the shoulders find their own path, so they are friendlier for 40+ shoulders than a straight bar. Neutral grip (palms facing) is the most shoulder friendly; squeeze presses bias the chest with lighter loads; single arm versions add core.
- **Muscles:** Chest, front shoulders, triceps
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Shoulder blades back and down. 2) Lower with elbows about 45 degrees, forearms vertical. 3) Press up together without clanking the bells.
- **Common faults:** Flaring elbows; Dropping too deep with tight shoulders; Arching the low back off the bench.
- **Progress to:** DB Bench Press (G3); DB Floor Press (G3); Alternating DB Bench Press (G3). **Or progress by:** Heavier, single arm, alternating, tempo, incline angle changes.
- **Regress to:** Box Press Up (G1); Wall Press Up (G1); Knee Press Up (G1). **Or regress by:** Floor press, lighter weight, push up variation.
- **Same level swaps:** DB Squeeze Press; Swiss Ball DB Press; DB Low Incline Press
- **Cautions:** None specific. Neutral grip and floor presses protect shoulders. Single arm versions: brace hard.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8
- **Coach sources:** Poliquin, Cosgrove, Cressey

## Band Chest Fly

`HPU-050 | G2 | Horizontal push: fly (isolation) | STRONG | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Resistance band (confirm)
- **Why we use it:** Flys isolate the chest by moving the arm across the body with the elbow fixed. Useful for muscle building and variety at lighter loads.
- **Muscles:** Chest, front shoulders
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Slight bend in the elbows, kept fixed. 2) Open the arms with control until a stretch across the chest. 3) Hug back together, squeezing the chest.
- **Common faults:** Going too deep and stressing the shoulder; Bending and straightening the elbows (turns into a press); Going too heavy.
- **Progress to:** Band Resisted Press Up (G3); Pin Press (G3); Bench Dip (G3). **Or progress by:** Cable, slower tempo, pauses.
- **Regress to:** Box Press Up (G1); Wall Press Up (G1); Knee Press Up (G1). **Or regress by:** Lighter, shorter range, band fly.
- **Same level swaps:** DB Fly; Cable Fly; TRX Chest Fly
- **Cautions:** Shoulder. Limit range for shoulder pain. Cables are smoother than DBs.
- **Default prescription:** 2 to 3 sets x 10 to 15 reps, tempo 2-1-1-1, rest 45 to 60s, RPE 8
- **Coach sources:** Poliquin, Schoenfeld (hypertrophy)

## Bench Dip

`HPU-056 | G3 | Horizontal/vertical push: dip | STRONG | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Box / bench / step
- **Why we use it:** Strong triceps and chest builder, but the bottom position stretches the front of the shoulder under load. Use selectively in the 40+ population.
- **Muscles:** Triceps, chest, front shoulders
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Shoulders down and back, lean slightly forward. 2) Lower until upper arms are about parallel (or less if painful). 3) Press up to straight arms.
- **Common faults:** Going too deep; Shoulders rolling forward; Bench dips with the shoulder internally rotated.
- **Progress to:** Paused Bench Press (G4); Barbell Bench Press (G4); Barbell Floor Press (G4). **Or progress by:** Assisted → bodyweight → weighted.
- **Regress to:** DB Fly (G2); Press Up (G2); Cable Fly (G2). **Or regress by:** Band assisted, close grip press up, tricep extensions.
- **Same level swaps:** Parallel Bar Dip
- **Cautions:** Shoulder. Bench dips and deep dips often irritate shoulders. Avoid with any shoulder pain. Assisted versions first.
- **Default prescription:** 3 sets x 8 to 12 reps, tempo 3-0-1-1, rest 60 to 90s, RPE 7 to 9
- **Coach sources:** DeFranco, Poliquin

# 06. HORIZONTAL PULL

*Upper back, rear shoulder, biceps*

**Grade ladder at a glance** (use this to slot every member into the same session at their level):

- **G1**: TRX Face Pull, TRX Y Raise, TRX T Raise, TRX W Raise, Cable Face Pull, Kneeling Face Pull, Cable Rear Delt Fly, Band Face Pull, Chest Supported DB Row, Band Pull Apart, Chest Supported DB Row (Neutral), Band Pull Apart (Overhand), Band Pull Apart (Underhand), Band Diagonal Pull Apart, Prone Y T W (DB), Incline Rear Delt Fly (DB), Bent Over Rear Delt Fly, Reverse Fly (Swiss Ball), Sled Row (Rope)
- **G2**: TRX Row, Wide Grip Cable Row, Half Kneeling Cable Row, Cable Row with Rotation, Standing Cable Row, Band Row, Incline Bench DB Row, Seal Row (DB), Bent Over DB Row, Alternating Bent Over DB Row, KB Gorilla Row, Bench Supported Barbell Row, Pendlay Row, Meadows Row (Landmine), Isometric Row Hold (TRX), T Bar Row (Landmine), Kroc Row, Tempo Seated Cable Row, Seated Cable Row, Cable High Row
- **G3**: TRX Row (Feet Elevated), Single Arm Cable Row, Single Arm TRX Row, Split Stance Single Arm Cable Row, Inverted Row (Barbell in Rack), Inverted Row (Feet Elevated), Single Arm DB Row, Single Arm DB Row (Tripod), Seal Row (Barbell), Renegade Row, DB Row (Bench Paused), Single Arm KB Row, Plank Row, Double KB Bent Over Row, Bear Plank Row, KB High Pull, Barbell Bent Over Row, Single Arm Landmine Row, Underhand Barbell Row, Band Resisted Inverted Row, 1.5 Rep Single Arm DB Row

✱ = not for group sessions (impact).

## TRX Row

`HPL-001 | G2 | Horizontal pull: inverted / suspension row | STRONG, HYBRID, BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** TRX
- **Why we use it:** Pulling your own bodyweight in a plank position. The angle sets the difficulty, so it scales from total beginner (standing upright) to advanced (feet elevated) in the same station. A core Optimal group exercise and part of Ed's screening (TRX row at 45 degrees).
- **Muscles:** Upper back, lats, rear shoulders, biceps, core
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Body in a straight line, heels down. 2) Pull the chest to the handles, shoulder blades back and down. 3) Lower slowly to straight arms.
- **Common faults:** Hips sagging; Shrugging or poking the chin forward; Half reps.
- **Progress to:** Single Arm TRX Row (G3); TRX Row (Feet Elevated) (G3); Band Resisted Inverted Row (G3). **Or progress by:** Walk the feet forward (more horizontal), feet elevated, single arm, pause/tempo.
- **Regress to:** Chest Supported DB Row (G1); Chest Supported DB Row (Neutral) (G1). **Or regress by:** Stand more upright, step back, scapular retraction only (G1 of the Optimal screen).
- **Same level swaps:** TRX Row (Fast Tempo); Isometric Row Hold (TRX); Inverted Row to Pull Up Progression
- **Cautions:** None specific. Shoulder friendly. Neutral grip TRX handles are easiest on elbows.
- **Default prescription:** 3 sets x 8 to 15 reps (or total reps progression), pause at the top
- **Coach sources:** Cosgrove, Boyle, Dan John

## Wide Grip Cable Row

`HPL-002 | G2 | Horizontal pull: row | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Cable machine
- **Why we use it:** Rows build the upper back that holds posture upright and balances pressing. Chest supported rows remove the low back from the equation; single arm rows allow heavier loading and fix imbalances; bent over rows add hinge endurance. Aim for about 2 pulls for every push in desk based members.
- **This variation:** Cable: constant tension through the whole range with smooth, joint friendly resistance. Wide grip/stance shifts emphasis (chest/upper back or adductors) and can be less friendly for some shoulders and hips.
- **Muscles:** Upper back, lats, rear shoulders, biceps, grip
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Brace, shoulder blade pulls first, then the elbow. 2) Row towards the hip (lats) or lower ribs (upper back). 3) Pause, lower slowly to a full stretch.
- **Common faults:** Jerking and twisting the torso; Shrugging; Shortening the range.
- **Progress to:** Single Arm Cable Row (G3); Split Stance Single Arm Cable Row (G3); Single Arm Cable Row with Rotation (G3). **Or progress by:** Heavier, pause at the top, tempo, single arm, 1.5 reps.
- **Regress to:** Chest Supported DB Row (G1); Chest Supported DB Row (Neutral) (G1). **Or regress by:** Chest supported row, cable row, TRX row.
- **Same level swaps:** Cable High Row; Seated Cable Row; Cable Squat to Row
- **Cautions:** None specific. Chest supported and cable versions are the most back friendly. Bent over versions load the low back: avoid pairing with RDLs for 40+.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8
- **Coach sources:** DeFranco, Cressey, Poliquin, Boyle

- **This variation:** Feet elevated: more bodyweight on the arms for a harder variation.
- **Muscles:** Upper back, lats, rear shoulders, biceps, core

- **Common faults:** Hips sagging; Shrugging or poking the chin forward; Half reps.

- **Regress to:** TRX Row (G2); TRX Row (Fast Tempo) (G2); Isometric Row Hold (TRX) (G2). **Or regress by:** Stand more upright, step back, scapular retraction only (G1 of the Optimal screen).
- **Same level swaps:** Single Arm TRX Row; Band Resisted Inverted Row; Inverted Row (Feet Elevated)
- **Cautions:** None specific. Shoulder friendly. Neutral grip TRX handles are easiest on elbows.

## Single Arm TRX Row

`HPL-005 | G3 | Horizontal pull: inverted / suspension row | STRONG, HYBRID, BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** TRX
- **Why we use it:** Pulling your own bodyweight in a plank position. The angle sets the difficulty, so it scales from total beginner (standing upright) to advanced (feet elevated) in the same station. A core Optimal group exercise and part of Ed's screening (TRX row at 45 degrees).
- **This variation:** One sided loading adds an anti rotation / anti lateral flexion core challenge and exposes left/right differences.
- **Muscles:** Upper back, lats, rear shoulders, biceps, core
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Body in a straight line, heels down. 2) Pull the chest to the handles, shoulder blades back and down. 3) Lower slowly to straight arms.
- **Common faults:** Hips sagging; Shrugging or poking the chin forward; Half reps.
- **Progress to:** Weighted Pull Up (G4); Weighted Chin Up (G4); Commando Pull Up (G4). **Or progress by:** Walk the feet forward (more horizontal), feet elevated, single arm, pause/tempo.
- **Regress to:** TRX Row (G2); TRX Row (Fast Tempo) (G2); Isometric Row Hold (TRX) (G2). **Or regress by:** Stand more upright, step back, scapular retraction only (G1 of the Optimal screen).
- **Same level swaps:** TRX Row (Feet Elevated); Band Resisted Inverted Row; Inverted Row (Feet Elevated)
- **Cautions:** None specific. Shoulder friendly. Neutral grip TRX handles are easiest on elbows.
- **Default prescription:** 3 sets x 8 to 15 reps (or total reps progression), pause at the top
- **Coach sources:** Cosgrove, Boyle, Dan John

## Half Kneeling Cable Row

`HPL-006 | G2 | Horizontal pull: row | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Cable machine
- **Why we use it:** Rows build the upper back that holds posture upright and balances pressing. Chest supported rows remove the low back from the equation; single arm rows allow heavier loading and fix imbalances; bent over rows add hinge endurance. Aim for about 2 pulls for every push in desk based members.
- **This variation:** Cable: constant tension through the whole range with smooth, joint friendly resistance. Kneeling position locks the hips so the core has to control the trunk and stops the legs cheating.
- **Muscles:** Upper back, lats, rear shoulders, biceps, grip
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Brace, shoulder blade pulls first, then the elbow. 2) Row towards the hip (lats) or lower ribs (upper back). 3) Pause, lower slowly to a full stretch.
- **Common faults:** Jerking and twisting the torso; Shrugging; Shortening the range.
- **Progress to:** Single Arm Cable Row (G3); Split Stance Single Arm Cable Row (G3); Single Arm Cable Row with Rotation (G3). **Or progress by:** Heavier, pause at the top, tempo, single arm, 1.5 reps.
- **Regress to:** Chest Supported DB Row (G1); Chest Supported DB Row (Neutral) (G1). **Or regress by:** Chest supported row, cable row, TRX row.
- **Same level swaps:** Cable High Row; Seated Cable Row; Cable Squat to Row
- **Cautions:** None specific. Chest supported and cable versions are the most back friendly. Bent over versions load the low back: avoid pairing with RDLs for 40+.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8
- **Coach sources:** DeFranco, Cressey, Poliquin, Boyle

## TRX Face Pull

`HPL-007 | G1 | Pull: face pull (shoulder health) | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Cable machine, TRX
- **Why we use it:** Face pulls combine a high row with external rotation, strengthening the muscles that keep shoulders healthy and posture upright. Cressey and DeFranco use them in almost every programme to balance all the pressing. Optimal: at least 2x per week for desk workers.
- **Muscles:** Rear shoulders, rotator cuff (external rotators), mid traps
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Rope at forehead height, thumbs pointing back. 2) Pull towards the face, elbows high, separate the rope. 3) Finish with the knuckles beside the ears (like a double bicep pose), pause.
- **Common faults:** Leaning back and using bodyweight; Elbows dropping; Shrugging.
- **Progress to:** TRX Row (G2); Cable High Row (G2); Seated Cable Row (G2). **Or progress by:** Heavier, slower, add external rotation emphasis.
- **Regress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or regress by:** Band face pull, lighter.
- **Same level swaps:** Band Face Pull; Cable Face Pull; Kneeling Face Pull
- **Cautions:** None specific. Shoulder friendly and often therapeutic.
- **Default prescription:** 2 to 3 sets x 12 to 20 reps, pause 1s
- **Coach sources:** DeFranco, Cressey, Poliquin (structural balance)

## TRX Y Raise

`HPL-009 | G1 | Pull: scapular / lower trap raises | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** TRX
- **Why we use it:** Small raises in Y, T, W and I shapes strengthen the muscles that control the shoulder blade, especially the lower traps that are often weak in rounded posture. Poliquin's structural balance and Cressey's shoulder programmes rely on them.
- **Muscles:** Lower and middle traps, rear shoulders, rotator cuff
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Chest supported on an incline bench or lying face down. 2) Thumbs up, lift the arms into the shape using the shoulder blades. 3) Pause 1 to 2s at the top, lower slowly.
- **Common faults:** Shrugging up to the ears; Using heavy weights and swinging; Arching the low back.
- **Progress to:** TRX Row (G2); Isometric Row Hold (TRX) (G2); Band Row (G2). **Or progress by:** Light DBs, longer pauses.
- **Regress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or regress by:** Bodyweight, smaller range.
- **Same level swaps:** TRX T Raise; TRX W Raise; Prone Y Raise
- **Cautions:** None specific. Shoulder rehab friendly. Use 1 to 3kg or bodyweight.
- **Default prescription:** 2 to 3 sets x 8 to 12 per shape, pause at the top
- **Coach sources:** Poliquin, Cressey, Squat University

## Prone Y T W (DB)

`HPL-032 | G1 | Pull: scapular / lower trap raises | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Dumbbells (confirm)
- **Why we use it:** Small raises in Y, T, W and I shapes strengthen the muscles that control the shoulder blade, especially the lower traps that are often weak in rounded posture. Poliquin's structural balance and Cressey's shoulder programmes rely on them.
- **Muscles:** Lower and middle traps, rear shoulders, rotator cuff
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Chest supported on an incline bench or lying face down. 2) Thumbs up, lift the arms into the shape using the shoulder blades. 3) Pause 1 to 2s at the top, lower slowly.
- **Common faults:** Shrugging up to the ears; Using heavy weights and swinging; Arching the low back.
- **Progress to:** Seal Row (DB) (G2); Bent Over DB Row (G2); Incline Bench DB Row (G2). **Or progress by:** Light DBs, longer pauses.
- **Regress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or regress by:** Bodyweight, smaller range.
- **Same level swaps:** DB Front Raise; TRX Y Raise; TRX T Raise
- **Cautions:** None specific. Shoulder rehab friendly. Use 1 to 3kg or bodyweight.
- **Default prescription:** 2 to 3 sets x 8 to 12 per shape, pause at the top
- **Coach sources:** Poliquin, Cressey, Squat University

## Renegade Row

`HPL-037 | G3 | Pull + core: plank row | HYBRID, BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Dumbbells (confirm)
- **Why we use it:** Rowing from a plank or bear position adds a strong anti rotation challenge: the core must stop the hips twisting. Great for HYBRID and BURN sessions.
- **Muscles:** Upper back, lats, core (anti rotation), shoulders
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Wide feet, strong plank or bear position. 2) Row one weight to the hip without the hips rotating. 3) Place it down with control, alternate.
- **Common faults:** Hips rotating; Feet too narrow; Rushing reps.
- **Progress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or progress by:** Narrower feet, heavier, add a push up.
- **Regress to:** Seal Row (DB) (G2); Bent Over DB Row (G2); Incline Bench DB Row (G2). **Or regress by:** Knees down, bird dog row, chest supported row.
- **Same level swaps:** Renegade Row (Anti Rotation); Plank Row; Bird Dog Row
- **Cautions:** Shoulder. Wrist load: use hex DBs. Shoulder pain: use bird dog row or chest supported row instead.
- **Default prescription:** 2 to 3 sets x 6 to 10 reps each side (or 20 to 40s), slow and controlled
- **Coach sources:** Cosgrove, McGill (anti rotation)

`HPL-043 | G3 | Horizontal pull: row | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Kettlebell
- **Why we use it:** Rows build the upper back that holds posture upright and balances pressing. Chest supported rows remove the low back from the equation; single arm rows allow heavier loading and fix imbalances; bent over rows add hinge endurance. Aim for about 2 pulls for every push in desk based members.
- **This variation:** Double KB: heavier total load plus a front rack or bilateral grip demand.
- **Muscles:** Upper back, lats, rear shoulders, biceps, grip
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Brace, shoulder blade pulls first, then the elbow. 2) Row towards the hip (lats) or lower ribs (upper back). 3) Pause, lower slowly to a full stretch.
- **Common faults:** Jerking and twisting the torso; Shrugging; Shortening the range.
- **Progress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or progress by:** Heavier, pause at the top, tempo, single arm, 1.5 reps.
- **Regress to:** KB Gorilla Row (G2); Band Row (G2); Kroc Row (G2). **Or regress by:** Chest supported row, cable row, TRX row.
- **Same level swaps:** Single Arm KB Row; Single Arm DB Row; Seal Row (Barbell)
- **Cautions:** Low back. Chest supported and cable versions are the most back friendly. Bent over versions load the low back: avoid pairing with RDLs for 40+.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8
- **Coach sources:** DeFranco, Cressey, Poliquin, Boyle

## Bear Plank Row

`HPL-044 | G3 | Pull + core: plank row | HYBRID, BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Bodyweight
- **Why we use it:** Rowing from a plank or bear position adds a strong anti rotation challenge: the core must stop the hips twisting. Great for HYBRID and BURN sessions.
- **Muscles:** Upper back, lats, core (anti rotation), shoulders
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Wide feet, strong plank or bear position. 2) Row one weight to the hip without the hips rotating. 3) Place it down with control, alternate.
- **Common faults:** Hips rotating; Feet too narrow; Rushing reps.
- **Progress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or progress by:** Narrower feet, heavier, add a push up.
- **Regress to:** TRX Row (G2); Band Row (G2); Kroc Row (G2). **Or regress by:** Knees down, bird dog row, chest supported row.
- **Same level swaps:** Plank Row; Renegade Row; Bird Dog Row
- **Cautions:** Shoulder. Wrist load: use hex DBs. Shoulder pain: use bird dog row or chest supported row instead.
- **Default prescription:** 2 to 3 sets x 6 to 10 reps each side (or 20 to 40s), slow and controlled
- **Coach sources:** Cosgrove, McGill (anti rotation)

## KB High Pull

`HPL-045 | G3 | Power: Olympic lift / derivative | HYBRID, STRONG | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Kettlebell
- **Why we use it:** Explosive triple extension (ankles, knees, hips) trains power and rate of force development. Power declines faster than strength with age, so it must be trained, but the skill demand is high. DB, KB and landmine versions are far easier to learn and safer for groups than barbell versions.
- **Muscles:** Whole body: glutes, quads, hamstrings, traps, shoulders
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Start in a strong hinge with the weight close. 2) Explode up through the legs and hips, shrug and pull the elbows high. 3) Catch softly in a strong rack position (or overhead), stand tall.
- **Common faults:** Pulling early with the arms; Weight swinging away from the body; Catching with the back arched.
- **Progress to:** Double KB Clean (G4); KB High Pull (Single Arm) (G4); Barbell Push Jerk (G4). **Or progress by:** Pull → hang version → from the floor; DB → KB → barbell.
- **Regress to:** KB Gorilla Row (G2); TRX Row (G2); Band Row (G2). **Or regress by:** Pull only (no catch), KB swing, med ball scoop toss, landmine clean.
- **Same level swaps:** KB Clean; KB Snatch; KB Clean and Press
- **Cautions:** Low back, Osteoporosis/osteopenia, Shoulder. Wrists, shoulders and low back need to be healthy. Barbell versions: Teams G4 only. Not for osteoporosis without careful progression.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 5 sets x 3 to 6 reps, full recovery (60 to 120s), stop when speed drops
- **Coach sources:** DeFranco, Cosgrove (power block), Gambetta

## Sled Row (Rope)

`HPL-050 | G1 | Carry / gait: sled push, pull and drag | BURN, HYBRID, STRONG | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Sled
- **Why we use it:** The sled is the most joint friendly strength and conditioning tool in the gym: concentric only, so almost no soreness, no impact and no technique to fail. Ben Patrick uses backward drags for knee health; DeFranco uses pushes for conditioning. Every member at every level can use it.
- **Muscles:** Quads, glutes, calves, whole body conditioning
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Push: arms extended or bent, body at 45 degrees, drive through the balls of the feet. 2) Drag backward: lean back, small steps, push through the front of the foot (knees over toes). 3) Keep steady steps and a neutral spine.
- **Common faults:** Hips too high or too low; Rounding the back; Taking huge steps that slow the sled.
- **Progress to:** Prowler Push (G3); Sled Sprint (Push) (G3); Sled Sprint (Pull) (G3). **Or progress by:** More weight, faster (sprints), longer distance, less rest.
- **Regress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or regress by:** Lighter, slower, shorter distance.
- **Same level swaps:** Sled Push; Sled Pull; Sled Pull (Rope)
- **Cautions:** None specific. Almost universally safe. Backward drag is a knee pain staple. Heavy pushes raise blood pressure: keep breathing.
- **Default prescription:** 6 to 10 x 15 to 25m, walk back recovery; or 3 to 5 min backward drag in warm up
- **Coach sources:** Ben Patrick (ATG), DeFranco, Boyle

## Band Resisted Inverted Row

`HPL-052 | G3 | Horizontal pull: inverted / suspension row | STRONG, HYBRID, BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Resistance band (confirm)
- **Why we use it:** Pulling your own bodyweight in a plank position. The angle sets the difficulty, so it scales from total beginner (standing upright) to advanced (feet elevated) in the same station. A core Optimal group exercise and part of Ed's screening (TRX row at 45 degrees).
- **This variation:** Band resistance gets harder at the top (accommodating resistance) and can cue better positions such as knees out.
- **Muscles:** Upper back, lats, rear shoulders, biceps, core
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Body in a straight line, heels down. 2) Pull the chest to the handles, shoulder blades back and down. 3) Lower slowly to straight arms.
- **Common faults:** Hips sagging; Shrugging or poking the chin forward; Half reps.
- **Progress to:** Weighted Pull Up (G4); Weighted Chin Up (G4); Commando Pull Up (G4). **Or progress by:** Walk the feet forward (more horizontal), feet elevated, single arm, pause/tempo.
- **Regress to:** TRX Row (G2); TRX Row (Fast Tempo) (G2); Isometric Row Hold (TRX) (G2). **Or regress by:** Stand more upright, step back, scapular retraction only (G1 of the Optimal screen).
- **Same level swaps:** Single Arm TRX Row; TRX Row (Feet Elevated); Inverted Row (Feet Elevated)
- **Cautions:** None specific. Shoulder friendly. Neutral grip TRX handles are easiest on elbows.
- **Default prescription:** 3 sets x 8 to 15 reps (or total reps progression), pause at the top
- **Coach sources:** Cosgrove, Boyle, Dan John

- **Progress to:** Single Arm Cable Row (G3); Split Stance Single Arm Cable Row (G3); Single Arm Cable Row with Rotation (G3). **Or progress by:** Heavier, pause at the top, tempo, single arm, 1.5 reps.
- **Regress to:** Chest Supported DB Row (G1); Chest Supported DB Row (Neutral) (G1). **Or regress by:** Chest supported row, cable row, TRX row.
- **Same level swaps:** Seated Cable Row; Cable Squat to Row; Standing Cable Row
- **Cautions:** None specific. Chest supported and cable versions are the most back friendly. Bent over versions load the low back: avoid pairing with RDLs for 40+.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8
- **Coach sources:** DeFranco, Cressey, Poliquin, Boyle

# 07. VERTICAL PUSH

*Shoulders and triceps, pressing overhead*

**Grade ladder at a glance** (use this to slot every member into the same session at their level):

- **G1**: Wall Slide, Seated DB Shoulder Press, Plate Front Raise, DB Front Raise, DB Lateral Raise, Leaning Lateral Raise, Cable Lateral Raise, Band Lateral Raise, Lu Raise, Y Raise (Incline Bench), Scaption Raise, Half Turkish Get Up, Overhead Tricep Extension (DB), Behind the Neck Press (Light), Overhead Cable Tricep Extension, Overhead Band Tricep Extension
- **G2**: Tall Kneeling Landmine Press, Landmine Press to Rotation, Landmine Push Press, Tall Kneeling DB Press, Half Kneeling Cable Overhead Press, Band Overhead Press, Standing DB Shoulder Press, Plate Overhead Press, Alternating DB Shoulder Press, Neutral Grip DB Press, Arnold Press, DB Push Press, Split Stance DB Press, Overhead Hold (DB), Overhead Hold (Plate), KB Push Press, KB Windmill, Turkish Get Up, Seated Barbell Press, Landmine Press, Half Kneeling Landmine Press
- **G3**: Pike Press Up, Elevated Pike Press Up, Half Kneeling Single Arm DB Press, Single Arm Cable Press (Overhead), Single Arm DB Press (Standing), Z Press (DB), Offset DB Press, Single Arm KB Press, Bottoms Up KB Carry Overhead, Bottoms Up KB Press, Double KB Press, DB Thruster, KB Thruster, Handstand Hold (Wall), Barbell Overhead Press, Wall Walk, Bear Crawl to Pike, Barbell Push Press, Paused Overhead Press, Single Arm Landmine Push Press, KB Clean and Press
- **G4**: Z Press (Barbell) ✱, Barbell Thruster ✱

✱ = not for group sessions (impact).

## Wall Slide

`VPU-001 | G1 | Shoulder: scapular control (wall slides) | STRONG, HYBRID, BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Bodyweight
- **Why we use it:** Sliding the arms up the wall trains the shoulder blade to rotate upward properly, which is key for pain free overhead movement. Part of the Simple 6 style warm up.
- **Muscles:** Lower traps, serratus, T spine extension
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Back or forearms against the wall, ribs down. 2) Slide the arms up keeping contact, shoulders down. 3) Slide back down, squeezing the shoulder blades.
- **Common faults:** Arching the low back; Shrugging; Forcing range.
- **Progress to:** KB Windmill (G2); Arnold Press (G2); DB Push Press (G2). **Or progress by:** Add a band or lift off at the top.
- **Regress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or regress by:** Smaller range, floor angels.
- **Same level swaps:** Wall Slides; Wall Angels; Floor Angels
- **Cautions:** None specific. Very shoulder friendly.
- **Default prescription:** 1 to 2 sets x 5 to 10 slow reps (or 30 to 60s), in warm up or cool down
- **Coach sources:** Cressey, DeFranco (Simple 6), Squat University

## Tall Kneeling Landmine Press

`VPU-002 | G2 | Push: landmine press | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Landmine (confirm)
- **Why we use it:** The landmine press moves on an arc between a horizontal and vertical press, letting the shoulder blade move freely. It is the most shoulder friendly way to press overhead and the go to for members who can't press straight overhead (Cressey). Half kneeling adds core and hip stability.
- **This variation:** Landmine: the arc path is shoulder and back friendly and very easy to learn. Kneeling position locks the hips so the core has to control the trunk and stops the legs cheating.
- **Muscles:** Shoulders, chest, triceps, serratus, core
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Hold the end of the bar at the shoulder, ribs down, glutes tight. 2) Press up and forward, letting the shoulder blade reach around. 3) Lower with control back to the shoulder.
- **Common faults:** Arching the low back; Shrugging; Twisting the torso to press.
- **Progress to:** Single Arm Landmine Push Press (G3); Single Arm Landmine Press (Standing) (G3). **Or progress by:** Half kneeling → tall kneeling → split stance → standing → push press; add plates.
- **Regress to:** Landmine Press (Light) (G1); Seated DB Shoulder Press (G1). **Or regress by:** Lighter, two hands, half kneeling.
- **Same level swaps:** Landmine Press; Landmine Push Press; Landmine Chest Press
- **Cautions:** None specific. Best press for shoulder pain and limited overhead range.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8 (each arm)
- **Coach sources:** Cressey, Boyle, DeFranco

## Pike Press Up

`VPU-003 | G3 | Vertical push: bodyweight overhead (pike/handstand) | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Bodyweight
- **Why we use it:** Bodyweight overhead pressing progressions. High skill and high shoulder load; good for strong, healthy shoulders only.
- **Muscles:** Shoulders, triceps, core
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Hips high, hands shoulder width. 2) Lower the head between the hands. 3) Press back up, keep the core tight.
- **Common faults:** Flared elbows; Arching the back; Head crashing to the floor.
- **Progress to:** Barbell Thruster (G4); Z Press (Barbell) (G4). **Or progress by:** Elevate the feet, wall handstand holds.
- **Regress to:** KB Windmill (G2); Arnold Press (G2); DB Push Press (G2). **Or regress by:** Pike from knees, DB overhead press.
- **Same level swaps:** Wall Walk; Bear Crawl to Pike; Handstand Hold (Wall)
- **Cautions:** Blood pressure (inverted), Shoulder. Avoid with shoulder pain, high blood pressure (inverted), glaucoma.
- **Default prescription:** 3 sets x 5 to 10
- **Coach sources:** DeFranco

## Half Kneeling Single Arm DB Press

`VPU-007 | G3 | Vertical push: overhead press | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Dumbbells (confirm)
- **Why we use it:** Pressing overhead builds shoulder strength and the ability to put things on high shelves (a real life task). LIFTMOR used overhead presses for spinal bone density. Requires overhead mobility; half kneeling and single arm versions add core demand and are often easier on the low back.
- **This variation:** One sided loading adds an anti rotation / anti lateral flexion core challenge and exposes left/right differences. Kneeling position locks the hips so the core has to control the trunk and stops the legs cheating.
- **Muscles:** Shoulders, triceps, upper back, core
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Ribs down, glutes tight, wrist stacked over the elbow. 2) Press up and slightly back so the biceps finish by the ears. 3) Lower with control to the shoulder.
- **Common faults:** Arching the low back to get the weight up; Pressing forward; Shrugging at the top.
- **Progress to:** Barbell Thruster (G4); Z Press (Barbell) (G4). **Or progress by:** Seated → half kneeling → standing → push press; heavier, single arm, bottoms up.
- **Regress to:** Arnold Press (G2); DB Push Press (G2); Split Stance DB Press (G2). **Or regress by:** Landmine press, high incline DB press, lighter weights.
- **Same level swaps:** Z Press (DB); Offset DB Press; Single Arm DB Press (Standing)
- **Cautions:** Shoulder. Needs pain free overhead range (wall test). Shoulder pain: landmine press. Behind the neck pressing: avoid for 40+.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8
- **Coach sources:** Cressey, Poliquin, LIFTMOR research, Dan John
