## Plate Front Raise

`VPU-016 | G1 | Pull: scapular / lower trap raises | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Plate
- **Why we use it:** Small raises in Y, T, W and I shapes strengthen the muscles that control the shoulder blade, especially the lower traps that are often weak in rounded posture. Poliquin's structural balance and Cressey's shoulder programmes rely on them.
- **Muscles:** Lower and middle traps, rear shoulders, rotator cuff
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Chest supported on an incline bench or lying face down. 2) Thumbs up, lift the arms into the shape using the shoulder blades. 3) Pause 1 to 2s at the top, lower slowly.
- **Common faults:** Shrugging up to the ears; Using heavy weights and swinging; Arching the low back.
- **Progress to:** Plate Overhead Press (G2); Overhead Hold (Plate) (G2); KB Windmill (G2). **Or progress by:** Light DBs, longer pauses.
- **Regress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or regress by:** Bodyweight, smaller range.
- **Same level swaps:** Plate Front Raise Squat; TRX Y Raise; TRX T Raise
- **Cautions:** None specific. Shoulder rehab friendly. Use 1 to 3kg or bodyweight.
- **Default prescription:** 2 to 3 sets x 8 to 12 per shape, pause at the top
- **Coach sources:** Poliquin, Cressey, Squat University

**Neutral Grip DB Press** (G2): full entry under Horizontal Push, ID HPU-053.

## Y Raise (Incline Bench)

`VPU-029 | G1 | Pull: scapular / lower trap raises | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Box / bench / step
- **Why we use it:** Small raises in Y, T, W and I shapes strengthen the muscles that control the shoulder blade, especially the lower traps that are often weak in rounded posture. Poliquin's structural balance and Cressey's shoulder programmes rely on them.
- **Muscles:** Lower and middle traps, rear shoulders, rotator cuff
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Chest supported on an incline bench or lying face down. 2) Thumbs up, lift the arms into the shape using the shoulder blades. 3) Pause 1 to 2s at the top, lower slowly.
- **Common faults:** Shrugging up to the ears; Using heavy weights and swinging; Arching the low back.
- **Progress to:** KB Windmill (G2); Arnold Press (G2); DB Push Press (G2). **Or progress by:** Light DBs, longer pauses.
- **Regress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or regress by:** Bodyweight, smaller range.
- **Same level swaps:** TRX Y Raise; TRX T Raise; TRX W Raise
- **Cautions:** None specific. Shoulder rehab friendly. Use 1 to 3kg or bodyweight.
- **Default prescription:** 2 to 3 sets x 8 to 12 per shape, pause at the top
- **Coach sources:** Poliquin, Cressey, Squat University

## Bottoms Up KB Carry Overhead

`VPU-033 | G3 | Carry: overhead / waiter | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Kettlebell
- **Why we use it:** Holding weight overhead while walking trains shoulder stability and core in one. Bottoms up holds make the rotator cuff work hard with light weight: brilliant for shoulder rehab.
- **This variation:** Bottoms up kettlebell forces the grip and rotator cuff to stabilise; a brilliant (light) shoulder rehab tool.
- **Muscles:** Shoulder stability, rotator cuff, core
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Arm locked, biceps by the ear, shoulder packed. 2) Ribs down, walk slowly. 3) Keep the weight stacked over the shoulder.
- **Common faults:** Arching the back; Arm drifting forward; Going too heavy.
- **Progress to:** Barbell Thruster (G4); Z Press (Barbell) (G4); Single Arm Overhead Carry (DB) (G4). **Or progress by:** Heavier, double, bottoms up.
- **Regress to:** Bottoms Up KB Hold (G2); Overhead Hold (KB) (G2); Overhead March (KB) (G2). **Or regress by:** Waiter's carry, lighter, static hold.
- **Same level swaps:** Bottoms Up KB Carry; Overhead Carry (Double KB); Overhead Carry (Plate)
- **Cautions:** Shoulder. Needs pain free overhead range. Waiter's carry (arm at 90 degrees) is an easier option.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 5 x 20 to 40m (or 30 to 45s), rest 60 to 90s
- **Coach sources:** Dan John, Cressey

- **Cautions:** Shoulder. Needs pain free overhead range. Waiter's carry (arm at 90 degrees) is an easier option.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 5 x 20 to 40m (or 30 to 45s), rest 60 to 90s
- **Coach sources:** Dan John, Cressey

## KB Push Press

`VPU-038 | G2 | Vertical push: overhead press | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Kettlebell
- **Why we use it:** Pressing overhead builds shoulder strength and the ability to put things on high shelves (a real life task). LIFTMOR used overhead presses for spinal bone density. Requires overhead mobility; half kneeling and single arm versions add core demand and are often easier on the low back.
- **Muscles:** Shoulders, triceps, upper back, core
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Ribs down, glutes tight, wrist stacked over the elbow. 2) Press up and slightly back so the biceps finish by the ears. 3) Lower with control to the shoulder.
- **Common faults:** Arching the low back to get the weight up; Pressing forward; Shrugging at the top.
- **Progress to:** Double KB Press (G3); Single Arm KB Press (G3); Bottoms Up KB Press (G3). **Or progress by:** Seated → half kneeling → standing → push press; heavier, single arm, bottoms up.
- **Regress to:** Landmine Press (Light) (G1); Seated DB Shoulder Press (G1). **Or regress by:** Landmine press, high incline DB press, lighter weights.
- **Same level swaps:** Arnold Press; DB Push Press; Band Overhead Press
- **Cautions:** Shoulder. Needs pain free overhead range (wall test). Shoulder pain: landmine press. Behind the neck pressing: avoid for 40+.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8
- **Coach sources:** Cressey, Poliquin, LIFTMOR research, Dan John

## DB Thruster

`VPU-039 | G3 | Squat + vertical push (combination) | BURN, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Dumbbells (confirm)
- **Why we use it:** Links a squat and an overhead press into one total body movement. Very metabolic, great for BURN and HYBRID sessions, and the legs help drive the weight overhead so people can press more.
- **Muscles:** Quads, glutes, shoulders, triceps, core
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Squat with the weight in the rack. 2) Drive up hard and use that momentum to press overhead. 3) Lock out with biceps by the ears, ribs down, then lower back to the rack.
- **Common faults:** Pressing before the legs finish the drive; Arching the low back at the top; Losing the rack position and squatting with the elbows dropped.
- **Progress to:** Barbell Thruster (G4); Double KB Front Squat to Press (G4); Barbell Front Rack Squat to Press (G4). **Or progress by:** Add load, double KBs, barbell, more rounds or density.
- **Regress to:** Arnold Press (G2); DB Push Press (G2); Overhead Hold (DB) (G2). **Or regress by:** Goblet squat to press, landmine squat to press, split into separate squat and press.
- **Same level swaps:** DB Thrusters; DB Squat to Overhead Press; KB Thruster
- **Cautions:** Shoulder. Needs pain free overhead range. With shoulder pain swap to squat to landmine press. Watch technique as fatigue builds in circuits.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 4 sets x 8 to 12 reps, or 30 to 40s in circuits
- **Coach sources:** Cosgrove (MRT), DeFranco

## KB Windmill

`VPU-040 | G2 | Total body: Turkish get up / windmill | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Kettlebell
- **Why we use it:** The get up teaches you to get up from the floor while holding a weight overhead: shoulder stability, hip mobility and confidence in one. Getting off the floor is a key longevity skill (Attia, Dan John, Pavel). Windmills and arm bars build shoulder stability and hip hinge mobility.
- **Muscles:** Shoulder stability, core, hips, whole body
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Eyes on the bell, arm locked. 2) Move through each step slowly: roll to elbow, hand, high bridge, sweep the leg, kneel, stand. 3) Reverse every step with control.
- **Common faults:** Rushing; Bent arm; Losing sight of the bell.
- **Progress to:** KB Thruster (G3); Double KB Press (G3); KB Clean and Press (G3). **Or progress by:** Heavier bell, full get up.
- **Regress to:** Half Turkish Get Up (G1); Turkish Get Up (Light) (G1). **Or regress by:** Half get up, shoe on the fist, no weight.
- **Same level swaps:** Arm Bar (KB); Turkish Get Up; Half Kneeling to Stand
- **Cautions:** Shoulder. Learn with a shoe or no weight first. Shoulder pain: half get up with no load only.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 5 reps each side, slow
- **Coach sources:** Dan John, Pavel Tsatsouline, Gray Cook
- **Also listed in:** Rotational And Anti Rotation

## Handstand Hold (Wall)

`VPU-045 | G3 | Vertical push: bodyweight overhead (pike/handstand) | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Bodyweight
- **Why we use it:** Bodyweight overhead pressing progressions. High skill and high shoulder load; good for strong, healthy shoulders only.
- **Muscles:** Shoulders, triceps, core
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Hips high, hands shoulder width. 2) Lower the head between the hands. 3) Press back up, keep the core tight.
- **Common faults:** Flared elbows; Arching the back; Head crashing to the floor.
- **Progress to:** Barbell Thruster (G4); Z Press (Barbell) (G4). **Or progress by:** Elevate the feet, wall handstand holds.
- **Regress to:** KB Windmill (G2); Arnold Press (G2); DB Push Press (G2). **Or regress by:** Pike from knees, DB overhead press.
- **Same level swaps:** Wall Walk; Pike Press Up; Bear Crawl to Pike
- **Cautions:** Blood pressure (inverted), Shoulder. Avoid with shoulder pain, high blood pressure (inverted), glaucoma.
- **Default prescription:** 3 sets x 5 to 10
- **Coach sources:** DeFranco

## Overhead Tricep Extension (DB)

`VPU-051 | G1 | Arms: triceps extension | STRONG | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

## Behind the Neck Press (Light)

`VPU-052 | G1 | Warm up: dynamic mobility | STRONG, HYBRID, BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Bodyweight
- **Why we use it:** Dynamic drills raise temperature, take joints through range and rehearse patterns (RAMP warm up). The World's Greatest Stretch hits hip flexors, hamstrings, adductors and T spine in one move. 40+ members need a full 8 to 10 minute warm up every session.
- **This variation:** Reduced range/load version: used for rehab, beginners, warm ups or flare up days.
- **Muscles:** Whole body
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Move through big comfortable ranges. 2) Increase range each rep. 3) Breathe and stay controlled.
- **Common faults:** Rushing; Bouncing into range; Skipping the warm up.
- **Progress to:** KB Windmill (G2); Arnold Press (G2); DB Push Press (G2). **Or progress by:** Bigger range, add reaches.
- **Regress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or regress by:** Smaller range, hand support.
- **Same level swaps:** A March; Inchworm; Crab Reach
- **Cautions:** Shoulder. Safe for almost everyone.
- **Default prescription:** 1 to 2 x 5 to 10 each side (or 20 to 30m)
- **Coach sources:** DeFranco (Limber 11, Simple 6), Gambetta, Squat University

## Landmine Press

`VPU-056 | G2 | Push: landmine press | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Landmine (confirm)
- **Why we use it:** The landmine press moves on an arc between a horizontal and vertical press, letting the shoulder blade move freely. It is the most shoulder friendly way to press overhead and the go to for members who can't press straight overhead (Cressey). Half kneeling adds core and hip stability.
- **This variation:** Landmine: the arc path is shoulder and back friendly and very easy to learn.
- **Muscles:** Shoulders, chest, triceps, serratus, core
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Hold the end of the bar at the shoulder, ribs down, glutes tight. 2) Press up and forward, letting the shoulder blade reach around. 3) Lower with control back to the shoulder.
- **Common faults:** Arching the low back; Shrugging; Twisting the torso to press.
- **Progress to:** Single Arm Landmine Push Press (G3); Single Arm Landmine Press (Standing) (G3). **Or progress by:** Half kneeling → tall kneeling → split stance → standing → push press; add plates.
- **Regress to:** Landmine Press (Light) (G1); Seated DB Shoulder Press (G1). **Or regress by:** Lighter, two hands, half kneeling.
- **Same level swaps:** Landmine Push Press; Landmine Chest Press; Landmine Press to Rotation
- **Cautions:** None specific. Best press for shoulder pain and limited overhead range.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8 (each arm)
- **Coach sources:** Cressey, Boyle, DeFranco

- **Progress to:** Z Press (Barbell) (G4). **Or progress by:** Half kneeling → tall kneeling → split stance → standing → push press; add plates.
- **Regress to:** Landmine Press (G2); Landmine Push Press (G2); Landmine Chest Press (G2). **Or regress by:** Lighter, two hands, half kneeling.
- **Same level swaps:** Single Arm Landmine Press (Standing); Z Press (DB); Offset DB Press
- **Cautions:** None specific. Best press for shoulder pain and limited overhead range.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8 (each arm)
- **Coach sources:** Cressey, Boyle, DeFranco

## Half Kneeling Landmine Press

`VPU-058 | G2 | Push: landmine press | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Landmine (confirm)
- **Why we use it:** The landmine press moves on an arc between a horizontal and vertical press, letting the shoulder blade move freely. It is the most shoulder friendly way to press overhead and the go to for members who can't press straight overhead (Cressey). Half kneeling adds core and hip stability.
- **This variation:** Landmine: the arc path is shoulder and back friendly and very easy to learn. Kneeling position locks the hips so the core has to control the trunk and stops the legs cheating.
- **Muscles:** Shoulders, chest, triceps, serratus, core
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Hold the end of the bar at the shoulder, ribs down, glutes tight. 2) Press up and forward, letting the shoulder blade reach around. 3) Lower with control back to the shoulder.
- **Common faults:** Arching the low back; Shrugging; Twisting the torso to press.
- **Progress to:** Single Arm Landmine Push Press (G3); Single Arm Landmine Press (Standing) (G3). **Or progress by:** Half kneeling → tall kneeling → split stance → standing → push press; add plates.
- **Regress to:** Landmine Press (Light) (G1); Seated DB Shoulder Press (G1). **Or regress by:** Lighter, two hands, half kneeling.
- **Same level swaps:** Landmine Press; Landmine Push Press; Landmine Chest Press
- **Cautions:** None specific. Best press for shoulder pain and limited overhead range.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8 (each arm)
- **Coach sources:** Cressey, Boyle, DeFranco
- **Also listed in:** Rehab: Shoulder

## KB Clean and Press

`VPU-059 | G3 | Power: Olympic lift / derivative | HYBRID, STRONG | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Kettlebell
- **Why we use it:** Explosive triple extension (ankles, knees, hips) trains power and rate of force development. Power declines faster than strength with age, so it must be trained, but the skill demand is high. DB, KB and landmine versions are far easier to learn and safer for groups than barbell versions.
- **This variation:** Combination move: trains two qualities at once, efficient for HYBRID and BURN; keep technique of both parts clean before speeding up.
- **Muscles:** Whole body: glutes, quads, hamstrings, traps, shoulders
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Start in a strong hinge with the weight close. 2) Explode up through the legs and hips, shrug and pull the elbows high. 3) Catch softly in a strong rack position (or overhead), stand tall.
- **Common faults:** Pulling early with the arms; Weight swinging away from the body; Catching with the back arched.
- **Progress to:** Double KB Clean (G4); KB High Pull (Single Arm) (G4); Barbell Push Jerk (G4). **Or progress by:** Pull → hang version → from the floor; DB → KB → barbell.
- **Regress to:** KB Windmill (G2); KB Push Press (G2); Turkish Get Up (G2). **Or regress by:** Pull only (no catch), KB swing, med ball scoop toss, landmine clean.
- **Same level swaps:** KB Clean; KB Snatch; KB High Pull
- **Cautions:** Low back, Osteoporosis/osteopenia, Shoulder. Wrists, shoulders and low back need to be healthy. Barbell versions: Teams G4 only. Not for osteoporosis without careful progression.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 5 sets x 3 to 6 reps, full recovery (60 to 120s), stop when speed drops
- **Coach sources:** DeFranco, Cosgrove (power block), Gambetta
- **Also listed in:** Conditioning

# 08. VERTICAL PULL

*Lats, upper back, biceps, pulling from overhead*

**Grade ladder at a glance** (use this to slot every member into the same session at their level):

- **G1**: Scapula Pull Up, TRX Pull Up Assisted Squat, Behind the Neck Pulldown (Light), Rope Face Pull High, Plate Halo
- **G2**: Band Assisted Pull Up, Swiss Ball DB Pullover, KB Pullover, Half Kneeling Cable High Row, Cable Y Pull, Band Y Pull, High to Low Cable Row, Lat Prayer (Cable), Cable Lat Pull with Rotation, Landmine Pulldown, TRX High Row, Inverted Row to Pull Up Progression, Seated Band Pulldown, TRX Assisted Pull Up, Wide Grip Pulldown, Lat Pulldown (Cable), Close Grip Pulldown, Tempo Lat Pulldown, Neutral Grip Pulldown, Underhand Pulldown, Cable Upright Row, Tall Kneeling Cable Pulldown, DB Upright Row, Kneeling Lat Pulldown (Band), Band Pulldown, Band Upright Row, Straight Arm Pulldown (Cable), Straight Arm Pulldown (Band), DB Shrug, Rope Straight Arm Pulldown, Cable Pullover, Cable Shrug, DB Pullover, Trap Bar Shrug
- **G3**: Pull Up, Chin Up, Barbell Pullover, Neutral Grip Pull Up, Negative Pull Up, Negative Chin Up, Isometric Chin Up Hold, Active Hang, Dead Hang, Flexed Arm Hang, Paused Lat Pulldown, 1.5 Rep Lat Pulldown, Single Arm Cable Pulldown, Half Kneeling Single Arm Pulldown, Barbell Upright Row, Single Arm Band Pulldown, Barbell Shrug
- **G4**: Weighted Pull Up, Weighted Chin Up, Commando Pull Up, KB High Pull (Single Arm)

✱ = not for group sessions (impact).

## Band Assisted Pull Up

`VPL-001 | G2 | Vertical pull: pull up / chin up / hangs | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Resistance band (confirm), Rig / pull up bar
- **Why we use it:** The ultimate upper body bodyweight strength test. Hangs build grip (a strong predictor of longevity) and decompress the spine; negatives and isometrics build strength for the first pull up. LIFTMOR used jumping chin ups with drop landings for bone.
- **This variation:** Assisted version: support lets members practise the full pattern safely while strength builds (Cosgrove: regress to progress).
- **Muscles:** Lats, upper back, biceps, grip, core
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Grip slightly wider than shoulders (chin up: palms facing you). 2) Pull the shoulder blades down first, then drive the elbows to the ribs. 3) Chin over the bar, lower slowly to straight arms.
- **Common faults:** Kipping or swinging; Half reps; Shrugging at the bottom.
- **Progress to:** Pull Up (G3); Chin Up (G3); Dead Hang (G3). **Or progress by:** Band assisted → negatives → bodyweight → weighted.
- **Regress to:** Scapula Pull Up (G1); Shrug to Retraction (G1); Scapula Retraction (TRX) (G1). **Or regress by:** Lat pulldown, TRX assisted pull up, scapula pull up, dead hang.
- **Same level swaps:** Hanging (Supported); TRX Assisted Pull Up
- **Cautions:** Shoulder. Shoulder pain: neutral grip, band assistance. Hanging can irritate some shoulders: build up gradually.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8 or total reps
- **Coach sources:** DeFranco, Dan John, Attia (grip), Boyle

## Swiss Ball DB Pullover

`VPL-002 | G2 | Vertical pull: pulldown / pullover | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Dumbbells (confirm), Swiss ball (confirm)
- **Why we use it:** Pulldowns train the pull up pattern at any load, essential for members who can't yet do pull ups. Straight arm pulldowns and pullovers isolate the lats, which also helps overhead mobility.
- **This variation:** Swiss ball adds instability for core control (Paul Chek); keep loads modest.
- **Muscles:** Lats, upper back, biceps
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Lean back slightly, chest up. 2) Pull the shoulder blades down then the elbows to the ribs. 3) Return slowly to a full stretch.
- **Common faults:** Leaning way back and rowing; Pulling behind the neck (shoulder risk); Shortening the range.
- **Progress to:** Barbell Pullover (G3); Paused Lat Pulldown (G3); 1.5 Rep Lat Pulldown (G3). **Or progress by:** Heavier, single arm, tempo, progress to band assisted pull ups.
- **Regress to:** Chest Supported DB Row (G1); Chest Supported DB Row (Neutral) (G1); Lat Pulldown (Light, Full Range) (G1). **Or regress by:** Lighter, band pulldown, kneeling.
- **Same level swaps:** DB Pullover; KB Pullover; Band Y Pull
- **Cautions:** None specific. Shoulder friendly with neutral grip. Behind the neck versions: avoid for 40+.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8
- **Coach sources:** Boyle, Poliquin

## Half Kneeling Cable High Row

`VPL-008 | G2 | Horizontal pull: row | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Cable machine
- **Why we use it:** Rows build the upper back that holds posture upright and balances pressing. Chest supported rows remove the low back from the equation; single arm rows allow heavier loading and fix imbalances; bent over rows add hinge endurance. Aim for about 2 pulls for every push in desk based members.
- **This variation:** Cable: constant tension through the whole range with smooth, joint friendly resistance. Kneeling position locks the hips so the core has to control the trunk and stops the legs cheating.
- **Muscles:** Upper back, lats, rear shoulders, biceps, grip
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Brace, shoulder blade pulls first, then the elbow. 2) Row towards the hip (lats) or lower ribs (upper back). 3) Pause, lower slowly to a full stretch.
- **Common faults:** Jerking and twisting the torso; Shrugging; Shortening the range.
- **Progress to:** Single Arm Cable Row (G3); Split Stance Single Arm Cable Row (G3); Single Arm Cable Row with Rotation (G3). **Or progress by:** Heavier, pause at the top, tempo, single arm, 1.5 reps.
- **Regress to:** Chest Supported DB Row (G1); Chest Supported DB Row (Neutral) (G1). **Or regress by:** Chest supported row, cable row, TRX row.
- **Same level swaps:** Cable High Row; Seated Cable Row; Cable Squat to Row
- **Cautions:** None specific. Chest supported and cable versions are the most back friendly. Bent over versions load the low back: avoid pairing with RDLs for 40+.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8
- **Coach sources:** DeFranco, Cressey, Poliquin, Boyle

## Scapula Pull Up

`VPL-015 | G1 | Shoulder: scapular control | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Rig / pull up bar
- **Why we use it:** Training the shoulder blade to move (down, back, up) before the arm pulls. Scapula pull ups and retractions are the first step towards rows and pull ups (G1 of the Optimal row screen).
- **Muscles:** Mid and lower traps, rhomboids, lats
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Arms straight. 2) Move only the shoulder blades. 3) Pause and return.
- **Common faults:** Bending the elbows; Shrugging; Rushing.
- **Progress to:** TRX Assisted Pull Up (G2); Band Assisted Pull Up (G2); Inverted Row to Pull Up Progression (G2). **Or progress by:** Full rows/pull ups.
- **Regress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or regress by:** Smaller range.
- **Same level swaps:** Shrug to Retraction; Scapula Retraction (TRX)
- **Cautions:** None specific. Rehab friendly.
- **Default prescription:** 2 to 3 sets x 10 to 15 reps, tempo 2-1-1-1, rest 45 to 60s, RPE 8
- **Coach sources:** Squat University, Cressey
- **Also listed in:** Rehab: Shoulder

## Lat Prayer (Cable)

`VPL-016 | G2 | Vertical pull: pulldown / pullover | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Cable machine
- **Why we use it:** Pulldowns train the pull up pattern at any load, essential for members who can't yet do pull ups. Straight arm pulldowns and pullovers isolate the lats, which also helps overhead mobility.

- **Cautions:** None specific. Shoulder friendly with neutral grip. Behind the neck versions: avoid for 40+.

## TRX High Row

`VPL-022 | G2 | Horizontal pull: row | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** TRX
- **Why we use it:** Rows build the upper back that holds posture upright and balances pressing. Chest supported rows remove the low back from the equation; single arm rows allow heavier loading and fix imbalances; bent over rows add hinge endurance. Aim for about 2 pulls for every push in desk based members.
- **Muscles:** Upper back, lats, rear shoulders, biceps, grip
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Brace, shoulder blade pulls first, then the elbow. 2) Row towards the hip (lats) or lower ribs (upper back). 3) Pause, lower slowly to a full stretch.
- **Common faults:** Jerking and twisting the torso; Shrugging; Shortening the range.
- **Progress to:** Single Arm DB Row (G3); Single Arm KB Row (G3); Seal Row (Barbell) (G3). **Or progress by:** Heavier, pause at the top, tempo, single arm, 1.5 reps.
- **Regress to:** Chest Supported DB Row (G1); Chest Supported DB Row (Neutral) (G1). **Or regress by:** Chest supported row, cable row, TRX row.
- **Same level swaps:** Band Row; Kroc Row; Pendlay Row
- **Cautions:** None specific. Chest supported and cable versions are the most back friendly. Bent over versions load the low back: avoid pairing with RDLs for 40+.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8
- **Coach sources:** DeFranco, Cressey, Poliquin, Boyle

## TRX Pull Up Assisted Squat

`VPL-024 | G1 | Squat: assisted | STRONG, HYBRID, BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** TRX, Rig / pull up bar
- **Why we use it:** Holding the TRX lets people counterbalance, so they can sit deeper and more upright than they could alone. It is the go to G1 squat for beginners, seniors, heavy members and anyone with knee or hip pain, and it builds confidence fast.
- **This variation:** Assisted version: support lets members practise the full pattern safely while strength builds (Cosgrove: regress to progress).
- **Muscles:** Quads, glutes
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Hold the handles at chest height with arms straight. 2) Sit back and down, letting the straps take a little weight. 3) Use the legs to stand, the arms only steady you.
- **Common faults:** Pulling with the arms to stand up; Leaning back so far the feet slide; Squatting deeper than the pain free range.
- **Progress to:** Barbell Box Squat (G2); Goblet Squat (KB) (G2); Goblet Squat (DB) (G2). **Or progress by:** Use the straps less, slower tempo, add a pause, progress to goblet box squat.
- **Regress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or regress by:** Squat to a high box with the TRX, reduce depth.
- **Same level swaps:** TRX Assisted Squat; Box Squat; Goblet Box Squat
- **Cautions:** None specific. Very joint friendly. Ideal first squat after injury or replacement surgery (within surgeon's limits).
- **Default prescription:** 3 sets x 10 to 15 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0
- **Coach sources:** Cosgrove (regress to progress), Boyle, Squat University

## Inverted Row to Pull Up Progression

`VPL-026 | G2 | Horizontal pull: inverted / suspension row | STRONG, HYBRID, BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Rig / pull up bar
- **Why we use it:** Pulling your own bodyweight in a plank position. The angle sets the difficulty, so it scales from total beginner (standing upright) to advanced (feet elevated) in the same station. A core Optimal group exercise and part of Ed's screening (TRX row at 45 degrees).
- **This variation:** Combination move: trains two qualities at once, efficient for HYBRID and BURN; keep technique of both parts clean before speeding up.
- **Muscles:** Upper back, lats, rear shoulders, biceps, core
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Body in a straight line, heels down. 2) Pull the chest to the handles, shoulder blades back and down. 3) Lower slowly to straight arms.
- **Common faults:** Hips sagging; Shrugging or poking the chin forward; Half reps.
- **Progress to:** Inverted Row (Barbell in Rack) (G3); Single Arm TRX Row (G3); TRX Row (Feet Elevated) (G3). **Or progress by:** Walk the feet forward (more horizontal), feet elevated, single arm, pause/tempo.
- **Regress to:** Chest Supported DB Row (G1); Chest Supported DB Row (Neutral) (G1). **Or regress by:** Stand more upright, step back, scapular retraction only (G1 of the Optimal screen).
- **Same level swaps:** TRX Row; TRX Row (Fast Tempo); Isometric Row Hold (TRX)
- **Cautions:** None specific. Shoulder friendly. Neutral grip TRX handles are easiest on elbows.
- **Default prescription:** 3 sets x 8 to 15 reps (or total reps progression), pause at the top
- **Coach sources:** Cosgrove, Boyle, Dan John

- **Cautions:** None specific. Shoulder friendly with neutral grip. Behind the neck versions: avoid for 40+.

## Behind the Neck Pulldown (Light)

`VPL-038 | G1 | Warm up: dynamic mobility | STRONG, HYBRID, BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Cable machine
- **Why we use it:** Dynamic drills raise temperature, take joints through range and rehearse patterns (RAMP warm up). The World's Greatest Stretch hits hip flexors, hamstrings, adductors and T spine in one move. 40+ members need a full 8 to 10 minute warm up every session.
- **This variation:** Reduced range/load version: used for rehab, beginners, warm ups or flare up days.
- **Muscles:** Whole body
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Move through big comfortable ranges. 2) Increase range each rep. 3) Breathe and stay controlled.
- **Common faults:** Rushing; Bouncing into range; Skipping the warm up.
- **Progress to:** Band Y Pull (G2); Cable Shrug (G2); Cable Y Pull (G2). **Or progress by:** Bigger range, add reaches.
- **Regress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or regress by:** Smaller range, hand support.
- **Same level swaps:** A March; Inchworm; Crab Reach
- **Cautions:** Shoulder. Safe for almost everyone.
- **Default prescription:** 1 to 2 x 5 to 10 each side (or 20 to 30m)
- **Coach sources:** DeFranco (Limber 11, Simple 6), Gambetta, Squat University

## Rope Face Pull High

`VPL-040 | G1 | Pull: face pull (shoulder health) | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Cable machine
- **Why we use it:** Face pulls combine a high row with external rotation, strengthening the muscles that keep shoulders healthy and posture upright. Cressey and DeFranco use them in almost every programme to balance all the pressing. Optimal: at least 2x per week for desk workers.
- **Muscles:** Rear shoulders, rotator cuff (external rotators), mid traps
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Rope at forehead height, thumbs pointing back. 2) Pull towards the face, elbows high, separate the rope. 3) Finish with the knuckles beside the ears (like a double bicep pose), pause.
- **Common faults:** Leaning back and using bodyweight; Elbows dropping; Shrugging.
- **Progress to:** Band Y Pull (G2); Cable Shrug (G2); Cable Y Pull (G2). **Or progress by:** Heavier, slower, add external rotation emphasis.
- **Regress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or regress by:** Band face pull, lighter.
- **Same level swaps:** TRX Face Pull; Band Face Pull; Cable Face Pull
- **Cautions:** None specific. Shoulder friendly and often therapeutic.
- **Default prescription:** 2 to 3 sets x 12 to 20 reps, pause 1s
- **Coach sources:** DeFranco, Cressey, Poliquin (structural balance)

## Half Kneeling Single Arm Pulldown

`VPL-041 | G3 | Vertical pull: pulldown / pullover | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Cable machine
- **Why we use it:** Pulldowns train the pull up pattern at any load, essential for members who can't yet do pull ups. Straight arm pulldowns and pullovers isolate the lats, which also helps overhead mobility.

## Cable Upright Row

`VPL-042 | G2 | Pull: shrug / upright row | STRONG | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Cable machine
- **Why we use it:** Traps support the neck and shoulders and carry heavy loads. Upright rows build shoulders but can pinch the shoulder joint: keep them below shoulder height or use cables/bands.
- **This variation:** Cable: constant tension through the whole range with smooth, joint friendly resistance.
- **Muscles:** Upper traps, shoulders
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Stand tall, arms straight. 2) Lift the shoulders straight up to the ears (shrug) or elbows to chest height (upright row). 3) Pause, lower slowly.
- **Common faults:** Rolling the shoulders; Pulling too high in upright rows; Using momentum.
- **Progress to:** Barbell Shrug (G3); Barbell Upright Row (G3). **Or progress by:** Heavier, pause at the top.
- **Regress to:** Rope Face Pull High (G1); Behind the Neck Pulldown (Light) (G1); Plate Halo (G1). **Or regress by:** Lighter, cable/band.
- **Same level swaps:** Cable Shrug; DB Shrug; DB Upright Row
- **Cautions:** Shoulder. Upright rows: avoid with shoulder impingement. Shrugs are safe.
- **Default prescription:** 2 to 3 sets x 10 to 15 reps, tempo 2-1-1-1, rest 45 to 60s, RPE 8
- **Coach sources:** Poliquin, DeFranco

## KB High Pull (Single Arm)

`VPL-046 | G4 | Power: Olympic lift / derivative | HYBRID, STRONG | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Kettlebell
- **Why we use it:** Explosive triple extension (ankles, knees, hips) trains power and rate of force development. Power declines faster than strength with age, so it must be trained, but the skill demand is high. DB, KB and landmine versions are far easier to learn and safer for groups than barbell versions.
- **This variation:** One sided loading adds an anti rotation / anti lateral flexion core challenge and exposes left/right differences.
- **Muscles:** Whole body: glutes, quads, hamstrings, traps, shoulders
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Start in a strong hinge with the weight close. 2) Explode up through the legs and hips, shrug and pull the elbows high. 3) Catch softly in a strong rack position (or overhead), stand tall.
- **Common faults:** Pulling early with the arms; Weight swinging away from the body; Catching with the back arched.
- **Progress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or progress by:** Pull → hang version → from the floor; DB → KB → barbell.
- **Regress to:** KB Clean (G3); KB Snatch (G3); KB High Pull (G3). **Or regress by:** Pull only (no catch), KB swing, med ball scoop toss, landmine clean.
- **Same level swaps:** Double KB Clean; Barbell Push Jerk; Clean Pull (Barbell)
- **Cautions:** Low back, Osteoporosis/osteopenia, Shoulder. Wrists, shoulders and low back need to be healthy. Barbell versions: Teams G4 only. Not for osteoporosis without careful progression.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 5 sets x 3 to 6 reps, full recovery (60 to 120s), stop when speed drops
- **Coach sources:** DeFranco, Cosgrove (power block), Gambetta

## Plate Halo

`VPL-052 | G1 | Shoulder / core: halo | HYBRID, STRONG | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Kettlebell, Plate
- **Why we use it:** Circling a weight around the head builds shoulder mobility and core control. Great warm up tool.
- **Muscles:** Shoulders, upper back, core
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Hold the bell upside down by the horns. 2) Circle it close around the head. 3) Keep ribs down, don't move the hips.
- **Common faults:** Arching the back; Bell too far from the head; Going too heavy.
- **Progress to:** KB Pullover (G2); DB Shrug (G2); Band Y Pull (G2). **Or progress by:** Heavier, half kneeling.
- **Regress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or regress by:** Lighter, plate.
- **Same level swaps:** KB Halo; KB Around the World
- **Cautions:** None specific. Gentle for most shoulders.
- **Default prescription:** 2 sets x 5 to 8 each way
- **Coach sources:** Dan John
- **Also listed in:** Rotational And Anti Rotation

## Straight Arm Pulldown (Band)

`VPL-053 | G2 | Vertical pull: pulldown / pullover | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Resistance band (confirm)
- **Why we use it:** Pulldowns train the pull up pattern at any load, essential for members who can't yet do pull ups. Straight arm pulldowns and pullovers isolate the lats, which also helps overhead mobility.
- **Muscles:** Lats, upper back, biceps
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Lean back slightly, chest up. 2) Pull the shoulder blades down then the elbows to the ribs. 3) Return slowly to a full stretch.
- **Common faults:** Leaning way back and rowing; Pulling behind the neck (shoulder risk); Shortening the range.
- **Progress to:** Single Arm Band Pulldown (G3); Barbell Pullover (G3); Paused Lat Pulldown (G3). **Or progress by:** Heavier, single arm, tempo, progress to band assisted pull ups.
- **Regress to:** Chest Supported DB Row (G1); Lat Pulldown (Light, Full Range) (G1); Chest Supported DB Row (Neutral) (G1). **Or regress by:** Lighter, band pulldown, kneeling.
- **Same level swaps:** Band Y Pull; Band Pulldown; Seated Band Pulldown
- **Cautions:** None specific. Shoulder friendly with neutral grip. Behind the neck versions: avoid for 40+.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8
- **Coach sources:** Boyle, Poliquin

## DB Shrug

`VPL-054 | G2 | Pull: shrug / upright row | STRONG | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Dumbbells (confirm)
- **Why we use it:** Traps support the neck and shoulders and carry heavy loads. Upright rows build shoulders but can pinch the shoulder joint: keep them below shoulder height or use cables/bands.
- **Muscles:** Upper traps, shoulders
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Stand tall, arms straight. 2) Lift the shoulders straight up to the ears (shrug) or elbows to chest height (upright row). 3) Pause, lower slowly.
- **Common faults:** Rolling the shoulders; Pulling too high in upright rows; Using momentum.
- **Progress to:** Barbell Shrug (G3); Barbell Upright Row (G3). **Or progress by:** Heavier, pause at the top.
- **Regress to:** Plate Halo (G1); Scapula Pull Up (G1); Rope Face Pull High (G1). **Or regress by:** Lighter, cable/band.
- **Same level swaps:** DB Upright Row; Cable Shrug; Trap Bar Shrug
- **Cautions:** None specific. Upright rows: avoid with shoulder impingement. Shrugs are safe.
- **Default prescription:** 2 to 3 sets x 10 to 15 reps, tempo 2-1-1-1, rest 45 to 60s, RPE 8
- **Coach sources:** Poliquin, DeFranco

# 09. LATERAL MOVEMENTS

*Side to side, frontal plane*

**Grade ladder at a glance** (use this to slot every member into the same session at their level):

- **G1**: Lateral Lunge (Bodyweight), Sled Lateral Drag, Lateral Sled Push, Lateral Band Walk, Monster Walk, Lateral Squat Walk, Crab Walk (Mini Band), Side Lying Hip Abduction, Lateral Sled Pull, Copenhagen Plank (Short Lever), Lateral Mini Band Squat Walk, Clam Shell (Mini Band), Standing Cable Hip Abduction, Banded Standing Hip Abduction, Side Lying Leg Raise (Ankle Weight)
- **G2**: Lateral Lunge (DB), Goblet Lateral Lunge, Lateral Lunge to Balance, Cossack Squat, Goblet Cossack Squat, Landmine Lateral Lunge, Lateral Lunge with Overhead Reach, Side Step Over Hurdles, Curtsy Lunge (DB), Lateral Plank Walk, Lateral Step Up (DB), Lateral Bear Crawl, Lateral Step Down, Lateral Crab Walk (Hands and Feet), Lateral Box Step Over, Lateral Med Ball Throw, Lateral Lunge to Press, Suitcase Lateral Lunge, Side Lying Hip Adduction, Side Plank, Cable Lateral Lunge, Side Plank with Hip Abduction, Side Plank Clam, Standing Cable Hip Adduction, Lateral Raise to Lateral Lunge, Adductor Squeeze (Ball), Lateral Step Up to Knee Drive
- **G3**: Lateral Hop (Single Leg) ✱, Lateral Line Hops ✱, Lateral Box Jump ✱, Lateral Shuffle, Slider Lateral Lunge, Carioca, Offset Lateral Lunge, Shuffle and Sprint, Copenhagen Plank (Long Lever), Lateral Plyo Step ✱, Lateral Ladder Drill (In and Out), Ickey Shuffle, Speed Skater (Slider), Lateral Bound ✱, Lateral Bound and Stick ✱, Adductor Slide (Slider), Skater Jumps ✱
- **G4**: Lateral Shuffle (Band Resisted)

✱ = not for group sessions (impact).

## Lateral Lunge (Bodyweight)

`LAT-001 | G1 | Single leg: lateral (frontal plane) | HYBRID, STRONG, BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Bodyweight
- **Why we use it:** Most training is forwards and backwards; lateral lunges train the side to side plane, building adductor strength and hip mobility that protect against groin strains and help golf, tennis and walking on uneven ground. Cossack squats are a great mobility and strength hybrid (Squat University and DeFranco's Limber 11).
- **Muscles:** Adductors, glutes, quads, hip mobility
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Step wide to the side, toes forward or slightly out. 2) Sit back into one hip, keeping the other leg straight. 3) Push back to the start through the bent leg.
- **Common faults:** Knee caving on the bent leg; Rounding the back to get lower; Heel lifting.
- **Progress to:** Cossack Squat (G2); Lateral Lunge (DB) (G2); Cable Lateral Lunge (G2). **Or progress by:** Add load (goblet, DB, landmine), slider, deeper cossack.
- **Regress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or regress by:** Shorter range, hand support, lateral lunge rock (mobility).
- **Same level swaps:** Clam Shell; Monster Walk; Reverse Clam
- **Cautions:** None specific. Groin and hip sensitive members: reduce range. Assisted versions (holding the rig) for seniors.
- **Default prescription:** 3 sets x 8 to 12 reps, tempo 3-0-1-1, rest 60 to 90s, RPE 7 to 9 (each side)
- **Coach sources:** Gambetta (multi plane), DeFranco (Limber 11), Squat University

## Lateral Hop (Single Leg)

`LAT-002 | G3 | Power: jumps, hops and landings (plyometric) | HYBRID | Group: No | Impact: high | Teams only: Yes | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Bodyweight
- **Why we use it:** Jumps and hops train power, tendon stiffness and bone (impact is a key bone stimulus in LIFTMOR). Landings (snap downs, drop squats, jump and stick) teach the body to absorb force, the foundation of injury prevention. Progress carefully: landing before jumping, low before high, two legs before one.
- **Muscles:** Whole lower body, tendons, nervous system
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Land softly and quietly, hips back, knees over toes. 2) Stick the landing for a second before the next rep. 3) Quality over quantity: stop when height or control drops.
- **Common faults:** Landing stiff legged or with knees caving; Too many reps (plyos are not cardio); Progressing too fast.
- **Progress to:** Single Leg Box Jump (G4); Alternating Lunge Jump (G4). **Or progress by:** Landings → small jumps → box jumps → broad jumps → single leg hops → depth jumps.
- **Regress to:** Snap Downs (G2); Drop Squat (G2); Pogo Hops (Low) (G2). **Or regress by:** Snap downs/drop squat and stick, step ups, sled push, med ball throws.
- **Same level swaps:** A Skip; Box Jump; Bounding
- **Cautions:** Knee, Low back, Osteoporosis/osteopenia, Pelvic floor. IMPACT: excluded from Optimal GROUP sessions (no jumping rule). Teams only after screening. Avoid with pelvic floor symptoms, osteoporosis with fracture history, joint replacements, acute knee/Achilles pain.
- **Group swap:** Group swap (no jumping): sled push, fast step ups, med ball chest pass or slam, KB swing, fast sit to stand
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 5 sets x 3 to 6 reps, full recovery (60 to 120s), stop when speed drops; 2 to 3 sessions/week max, low total contacts (20 to 60)
- **Coach sources:** Gambetta, DeFranco (dynamic effort), LIFTMOR research (impact for bone)

## Lateral Shuffle

`LAT-008 | G3 | Agility / locomotion | HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: moderate | Teams only: No | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Bodyweight
- **Why we use it:** Change of direction, rhythm and footwork. Builds coordination and reaction (Gambetta), useful for sport and falls prevention, but most variations involve running or hopping.
- **Muscles:** Whole lower body, coordination, conditioning
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Stay low and light on the feet. 2) Short quick steps, eyes up. 3) Control each change of direction.
- **Common faults:** Crossing feet on shuffles; Standing tall and slow; Doing too much volume.
- **Progress to:** Lateral Shuffle (Band Resisted) (G4). **Or progress by:** Faster, more complex patterns.
- **Regress to:** Side Plank (G2); Cossack Squat (G2); Side Plank Clam (G2). **Or regress by:** Walking footwork patterns, lateral band walk, sled lateral drag.
- **Same level swaps:** Carioca; Ickey Shuffle; Shuffle and Sprint
- **Cautions:** Knee, Osteoporosis/osteopenia. IMPACT (running/hopping): excluded from group sessions. Teams only after screening.
- **Default prescription:** 4 to 8 x 10 to 20s, full recovery
- **Coach sources:** Gambetta

- **Why we use it:** Change of direction, rhythm and footwork. Builds coordination and reaction (Gambetta), useful for sport and falls prevention, but most variations involve running or hopping.
- **This variation:** Band resistance gets harder at the top (accommodating resistance) and can cue better positions such as knees out.
- **Muscles:** Whole lower body, coordination, conditioning
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Stay low and light on the feet. 2) Short quick steps, eyes up. 3) Control each change of direction.
- **Common faults:** Crossing feet on shuffles; Standing tall and slow; Doing too much volume.
- **Progress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or progress by:** Faster, more complex patterns.
- **Regress to:** Carioca (G3); Ickey Shuffle (G3); Lateral Shuffle (G3). **Or regress by:** Walking footwork patterns, lateral band walk, sled lateral drag.
- **Cautions:** Knee, Osteoporosis/osteopenia. IMPACT (running/hopping): excluded from group sessions. Teams only after screening.
- **Default prescription:** 4 to 8 x 10 to 20s, full recovery
- **Coach sources:** Gambetta

## Cossack Squat

`LAT-011 | G2 | Single leg: lateral (frontal plane) | HYBRID, STRONG, BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Bodyweight
- **Why we use it:** Most training is forwards and backwards; lateral lunges train the side to side plane, building adductor strength and hip mobility that protect against groin strains and help golf, tennis and walking on uneven ground. Cossack squats are a great mobility and strength hybrid (Squat University and DeFranco's Limber 11).
- **Muscles:** Adductors, glutes, quads, hip mobility
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Step wide to the side, toes forward or slightly out. 2) Sit back into one hip, keeping the other leg straight. 3) Push back to the start through the bent leg.
- **Common faults:** Knee caving on the bent leg; Rounding the back to get lower; Heel lifting.
- **Progress to:** Slider Lateral Lunge (G3); Offset Lateral Lunge (G3); Speed Skater (Slider) (G3). **Or progress by:** Add load (goblet, DB, landmine), slider, deeper cossack.
- **Regress to:** Cossack Squat (Assisted) (G1); Lateral Lunge (Bodyweight) (G1). **Or regress by:** Shorter range, hand support, lateral lunge rock (mobility).
- **Same level swaps:** Lateral Lunge (DB); Cable Lateral Lunge; Lateral Lunge to RDL
- **Cautions:** None specific. Groin and hip sensitive members: reduce range. Assisted versions (holding the rig) for seniors.
- **Default prescription:** 3 sets x 8 to 12 reps, tempo 3-0-1-1, rest 60 to 90s, RPE 7 to 9 (each side)
- **Coach sources:** Gambetta (multi plane), DeFranco (Limber 11), Squat University

## Sled Lateral Drag

`LAT-012 | G1 | Carry / gait: sled push, pull and drag | BURN, HYBRID, STRONG | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Sled
- **Why we use it:** The sled is the most joint friendly strength and conditioning tool in the gym: concentric only, so almost no soreness, no impact and no technique to fail. Ben Patrick uses backward drags for knee health; DeFranco uses pushes for conditioning. Every member at every level can use it.
- **Muscles:** Quads, glutes, calves, whole body conditioning
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Push: arms extended or bent, body at 45 degrees, drive through the balls of the feet. 2) Drag backward: lean back, small steps, push through the front of the foot (knees over toes). 3) Keep steady steps and a neutral spine.
- **Common faults:** Hips too high or too low; Rounding the back; Taking huge steps that slow the sled.
- **Progress to:** Prowler Push (G3); Sled Sprint (Push) (G3); Sled Sprint (Pull) (G3). **Or progress by:** More weight, faster (sprints), longer distance, less rest.
- **Regress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or regress by:** Lighter, slower, shorter distance.
- **Same level swaps:** Sled Push; Sled Pull; Sled Row (Rope)
- **Cautions:** None specific. Almost universally safe. Backward drag is a knee pain staple. Heavy pushes raise blood pressure: keep breathing.
- **Default prescription:** 6 to 10 x 15 to 25m, walk back recovery; or 3 to 5 min backward drag in warm up
- **Coach sources:** Ben Patrick (ATG), DeFranco, Boyle
- **Also listed in:** Loaded Carries

## Side Step Over Hurdles

`LAT-018 | G2 | Lateral: step up / step over | STRONG, HYBRID, BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Bodyweight
- **Why we use it:** Lateral step ups train single leg strength in the frontal plane, great for knee control and balance.
- **Muscles:** Glutes, quads, adductors
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Side on to the box, foot fully on. 2) Drive up through the box leg. 3) Lower with control.
- **Common faults:** Pushing off the floor leg; Knee caving; Box too high.
- **Progress to:** Slider Lateral Lunge (G3); Offset Lateral Lunge (G3); Speed Skater (Slider) (G3). **Or progress by:** Higher box, add load, knee drive.
- **Regress to:** Monster Walk (G1); Sled Lateral Drag (G1); Lateral Sled Push (G1). **Or regress by:** Lower box, hand support.
- **Cautions:** None specific. Knee friendly at low heights.
- **Default prescription:** 3 sets x 8 to 12 reps, tempo 3-0-1-1, rest 60 to 90s, RPE 7 to 9 each side
- **Coach sources:** Gambetta, Boyle

## Curtsy Lunge (DB)

`LAT-019 | G2 | Single leg: lunge (rotational/adductor bias) | HYBRID, BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Dumbbells (confirm)
- **Why we use it:** Stepping back and across challenges the hips in a different plane, hitting the side glutes and inner thighs. Good variety and good for hip stability and golf.
- **Muscles:** Glutes (especially glute med), adductors, quads
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Step one foot back and across behind the other. 2) Lower straight down with the front knee tracking the toes. 3) Push through the front foot to return.
- **Common faults:** Twisting the hips excessively; Front knee caving; Losing balance from too narrow a step.
- **Progress to:** Slider Lateral Lunge (G3); Offset Lateral Lunge (G3); Speed Skater (Slider) (G3). **Or progress by:** Add load, deficit, pair with a single leg RDL.
- **Regress to:** Monster Walk (G1); Sled Lateral Drag (G1); Lateral Sled Push (G1). **Or regress by:** Shorter range, hand support, reverse lunge.
- **Same level swaps:** Curtsy Lunge
- **Cautions:** Knee. Can irritate knees and hips if the range is forced. Keep it pain free.
- **Default prescription:** 3 sets x 8 to 12 reps, tempo 3-0-1-1, rest 60 to 90s, RPE 7 to 9 (each side)
- **Coach sources:** Gambetta (multi plane), Cosgrove

## Lateral Plank Walk

`LAT-020 | G2 | Core: anti extension (plank) | STRONG, HYBRID, BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Bodyweight
- **Why we use it:** The plank trains the core to resist extension. Useful foundation, part of the Optimal screen (30s kneeling → full plank → plank with full tension). Long lever and RKC versions dramatically increase difficulty without longer holds.
- **Muscles:** Abs, shoulders, glutes
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Elbows under shoulders, straight line head to heels. 2) Squeeze glutes, pull the ribs down, push the floor away. 3) Breathe, hold with full tension.
- **Common faults:** Sagging hips; Bum in the air; Holding for minutes with poor form.
- **Progress to:** Single Arm Plank (G3); Long Lever Plank (G3). **Or progress by:** Long lever, RKC plank, leg lift, body saw.
- **Regress to:** Dead Bug (G1); Plank on Knees (G1); Dead Bug Heel Taps (G1). **Or regress by:** Plank on knees, incline plank on a bench.
- **Same level swaps:** Plank Saw; RKC Plank; Front Plank
- **Cautions:** None specific. Shoulder or wrist pain: dead bug or Pallof press instead. Prefer 20 to 30s high tension holds over long sloppy ones.
- **Default prescription:** 3 sets x 20 to 40s (high tension)
- **Coach sources:** McGill, Boyle, Cosgrove

## Lateral Step Up (DB)

`LAT-021 | G2 | Single leg: step up | STRONG, HYBRID, BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Dumbbells (confirm), Box / bench / step
- **Why we use it:** A real life movement (stairs, kerbs, climbing). Very back friendly, easy to scale by box height, and the concentric emphasis means little soreness. Knee drive and crossover versions add balance and hip work.
- **Muscles:** Quads, glutes, hamstrings, balance
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Whole foot on the box, knee over the middle of the foot. 2) Lean forward slightly and drive through the box leg to stand tall. 3) Step down with control, don't push off the bottom leg.
- **Common faults:** Pushing off the floor leg; Knee caving as you stand; Box too high so the hip hikes.
- **Progress to:** Barbell Step Up (G3); Step Up to Single Leg RDL (G3). **Or progress by:** Higher box, add DBs/goblet/barbell, add a knee drive, slower lowering.
- **Regress to:** Patrick Step (G1); Poliquin Step Up (G1); Petersen Step Up (G1). **Or regress by:** Lower box, hand support, bodyweight.
- **Same level swaps:** DB Step Up; Goblet Step Up; Lateral Step Up
- **Cautions:** None specific. Knee friendly at lower heights. Use a low box and hand support for seniors and knee pain. Faster 'step ups' in BURN keep impact low.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8 (each leg)
- **Coach sources:** Boyle, Cosgrove, Gambetta

## Lateral Bear Crawl

`LAT-022 | G2 | Core: quadruped (bear hold / crawl) | HYBRID, BURN, STRONG | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Bodyweight
- **Why we use it:** Bear holds and crawls train the core and shoulders together and build coordination (Gambetta, Chek). Getting down to and moving on the floor is also a longevity skill.
- **Muscles:** Core, shoulders, quads, coordination
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Hands under shoulders, knees under hips, knees hover 2 to 3cm. 2) Back flat, move opposite hand and foot together. 3) Small steps, keep the hips still.
- **Common faults:** Hips high; Back rounding; Moving too fast.
- **Progress to:** Slider Lateral Lunge (G3); Offset Lateral Lunge (G3); Speed Skater (Slider) (G3). **Or progress by:** Longer, add drag/load, reverse and lateral.
- **Regress to:** Monster Walk (G1); Sled Lateral Drag (G1); Lateral Sled Push (G1). **Or regress by:** Static bear hold, knees down.
- **Same level swaps:** Crab Walk; Bear Crawl; KB Bear Crawl Drag
- **Cautions:** None specific. Wrist pain: use fists or DB handles.
- **Default prescription:** 3 x 20 to 40s or 10 to 20m
- **Coach sources:** Gambetta, Paul Chek

## Lateral Step Down

`LAT-023 | G2 | Single leg: eccentric step down | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Box / bench / step
- **Why we use it:** Controlled lowering from a step builds knee control and eccentric quad strength, the exact quality needed for walking downstairs. Also a key screening test for knee valgus and hip control.
- **Muscles:** Quads, glutes, hip stabilisers
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Stand on a box, other leg hanging off the front or side. 2) Lower slowly by bending the standing knee, hips back slightly. 3) Tap the heel lightly and return without pushing off the floor.
- **Common faults:** Knee diving in; Hip dropping on the free side; Crashing down to the floor.
- **Progress to:** Pistol Squat (G3); Skater Squat (G3); Shrimp Squat (G3). **Or progress by:** Higher box, hold weight, slower lowering.
- **Regress to:** Patrick Step (G1); Poliquin Step Up (G1); Petersen Step Up (G1). **Or regress by:** Lower box, hand support, Poliquin step up.
- **Same level swaps:** Low Box Step Down; Forward Step Down; Heel Tap Step Down
- **Cautions:** None specific. Excellent for knee rehab when the box is low. Raise the height as control improves.
- **Default prescription:** 2 to 3 sets x 8 to 12 each leg, 3s lowering
- **Coach sources:** Squat University, Poliquin, Boyle
- **Also listed in:** Rehab: Hip, Rehab: Knee

- **Why we use it:** A real life movement (stairs, kerbs, climbing). Very back friendly, easy to scale by box height, and the concentric emphasis means little soreness. Knee drive and crossover versions add balance and hip work.

## Lateral Med Ball Throw

`LAT-026 | G2 | Power: medicine ball throws and slams | HYBRID, BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Med ball / wall ball
- **Why we use it:** Med ball throws are the safest way to train power for 40+ members: no catching heavy loads, no landing impact, and you can throw as hard as possible. Rotational throws (scoop toss, shot put) are THE golf power exercise (Gambetta, Chek). Wall balls combine a squat with a throw for conditioning.
- **Muscles:** Whole body power, rotational core (rotational throws), shoulders
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Load the hips (or rotate back through the hips for rotational throws). 2) Explode from the ground up: legs, hips, then arms. 3) Throw with intent every rep, reset between reps.
- **Common faults:** Throwing with arms only; Rounding the back on slams; Doing so many reps that it becomes slow cardio.
- **Progress to:** DB Clean (G3); KB Clean (G3); DB Snatch (G3). **Or progress by:** Heavier ball, more distance/speed, step into the throw, single leg stance.
- **Regress to:** Monster Walk (G1); Sled Lateral Drag (G1); Lateral Sled Push (G1). **Or regress by:** Lighter ball, half kneeling throw, slower controlled chops.
- **Same level swaps:** Wall Balls; Med Ball Slam; Med Ball Side Slam
- **Cautions:** None specific. Low impact and joint friendly. Use a soft ball for slams. Rotational throws: avoid with acute back pain. Wall balls need shoulder overhead range.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 5 sets x 3 to 6 reps, full recovery (60 to 120s), stop when speed drops (each side for rotational)
- **Coach sources:** Gambetta, Cosgrove (power block), Paul Chek (twist)

## Lateral Band Walk

`LAT-027 | G1 | Hip: abduction / glute med | STRONG, HYBRID, BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Mini band (confirm)
- **Why we use it:** The side glutes stop the knee caving and the pelvis dropping when on one leg. Weak glute meds are linked to knee pain, hip pain and back pain. Simple band work fixes it and works brilliantly as a warm up (Squat University, Boyle).
- **Muscles:** Glute medius and minimus, hip stabilisers
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Athletic stance, band around the knees or ankles. 2) Push the knees out, step sideways (or lift the leg) leading with the heel. 3) Stay low and keep the pelvis level.
- **Common faults:** Rocking the torso side to side; Feet turning out; Letting the band pull the knees in.
- **Progress to:** Single Leg Glute Bridge (Mini Band) (G2); Cossack Squat (G2); Paused Hip Thrust (G2). **Or progress by:** Heavier band, band lower on the leg, side plank abduction.
- **Regress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or regress by:** Side lying with no band, smaller range.
- **Same level swaps:** Monster Walk; Crab Walk (Mini Band); Clam Shell (Mini Band)
- **Cautions:** None specific. Very joint friendly, ideal for hip and knee rehab.
- **Default prescription:** 2 to 3 sets x 10 to 20 each side
- **Coach sources:** Squat University, Boyle, Paul Chek
- **Also listed in:** Rehab: Hip, Rehab: Knee

## Monster Walk

`LAT-029 | G1 | Hip: abduction / glute med | STRONG, HYBRID, BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Mini band (confirm)
- **Why we use it:** The side glutes stop the knee caving and the pelvis dropping when on one leg. Weak glute meds are linked to knee pain, hip pain and back pain. Simple band work fixes it and works brilliantly as a warm up (Squat University, Boyle).
- **Muscles:** Glute medius and minimus, hip stabilisers
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Athletic stance, band around the knees or ankles. 2) Push the knees out, step sideways (or lift the leg) leading with the heel. 3) Stay low and keep the pelvis level.
- **Common faults:** Rocking the torso side to side; Feet turning out; Letting the band pull the knees in.
- **Progress to:** Single Leg Glute Bridge (Mini Band) (G2); Cossack Squat (G2); Paused Hip Thrust (G2). **Or progress by:** Heavier band, band lower on the leg, side plank abduction.
- **Regress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or regress by:** Side lying with no band, smaller range.
- **Same level swaps:** Lateral Band Walk; Crab Walk (Mini Band); Clam Shell (Mini Band)
- **Cautions:** None specific. Very joint friendly, ideal for hip and knee rehab.
- **Default prescription:** 2 to 3 sets x 10 to 20 each side
- **Coach sources:** Squat University, Boyle, Paul Chek
- **Also listed in:** Rehab: Hip

## Suitcase Lateral Lunge

`LAT-032 | G2 | Single leg: lateral (frontal plane) | HYBRID, STRONG, BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Bodyweight
- **Why we use it:** Most training is forwards and backwards; lateral lunges train the side to side plane, building adductor strength and hip mobility that protect against groin strains and help golf, tennis and walking on uneven ground. Cossack squats are a great mobility and strength hybrid (Squat University and DeFranco's Limber 11).
- **This variation:** One sided loading adds an anti rotation / anti lateral flexion core challenge and exposes left/right differences.
- **Muscles:** Adductors, glutes, quads, hip mobility
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Step wide to the side, toes forward or slightly out. 2) Sit back into one hip, keeping the other leg straight. 3) Push back to the start through the bent leg.
- **Common faults:** Knee caving on the bent leg; Rounding the back to get lower; Heel lifting.
- **Progress to:** Slider Lateral Lunge (G3); Offset Lateral Lunge (G3); Speed Skater (Slider) (G3). **Or progress by:** Add load (goblet, DB, landmine), slider, deeper cossack.
- **Regress to:** Cossack Squat (Assisted) (G1); Lateral Lunge (Bodyweight) (G1). **Or regress by:** Shorter range, hand support, lateral lunge rock (mobility).
- **Same level swaps:** Cossack Squat; Lateral Lunge (DB); Cable Lateral Lunge
- **Cautions:** None specific. Groin and hip sensitive members: reduce range. Assisted versions (holding the rig) for seniors.
- **Default prescription:** 3 sets x 8 to 12 reps, tempo 3-0-1-1, rest 60 to 90s, RPE 7 to 9 (each side)
- **Coach sources:** Gambetta (multi plane), DeFranco (Limber 11), Squat University

## Side Lying Hip Adduction

`LAT-035 | G2 | Hip: adductor strength | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Bodyweight
- **Why we use it:** Copenhagen planks are among the best researched ways to prevent groin injury, and adductor strength supports knee and hip health. Ball squeezes are a gentle entry point.
- **Muscles:** Adductors (inner thigh), core
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Side plank with the top leg on a bench (inside of the knee for short lever, ankle for long lever). 2) Lift the hips into a straight line by squeezing the top leg down. 3) Hold or lift and lower.
- **Common faults:** Hips sagging; Rolling forward; Starting with the long lever.
- **Progress to:** Adductor Slide (Slider) (G3); Copenhagen Plank (Long Lever) (G3). **Or progress by:** Short → long lever, add leg raises.
- **Regress to:** Monster Walk (G1); Sled Lateral Drag (G1); Lateral Sled Push (G1). **Or regress by:** Ball squeeze, side lying adduction.
- **Same level swaps:** Copenhagen Side Plank; Adductor Squeeze (Ball); Standing Cable Hip Adduction
- **Cautions:** None specific. Short lever first. Groin pain: ball squeeze isometrics.
- **Default prescription:** 2 to 3 sets x 15 to 30s each side
- **Coach sources:** Research (groin injury prevention), Boyle
- **Also listed in:** Rehab: Hip

## Lateral Sled Pull

`LAT-036 | G1 | Carry / gait: sled push, pull and drag | BURN, HYBRID, STRONG | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Sled
- **Why we use it:** The sled is the most joint friendly strength and conditioning tool in the gym: concentric only, so almost no soreness, no impact and no technique to fail. Ben Patrick uses backward drags for knee health; DeFranco uses pushes for conditioning. Every member at every level can use it.
- **Muscles:** Quads, glutes, calves, whole body conditioning
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Push: arms extended or bent, body at 45 degrees, drive through the balls of the feet. 2) Drag backward: lean back, small steps, push through the front of the foot (knees over toes). 3) Keep steady steps and a neutral spine.
- **Common faults:** Hips too high or too low; Rounding the back; Taking huge steps that slow the sled.
- **Progress to:** Prowler Push (G3); Sled Sprint (Push) (G3); Sled Sprint (Pull) (G3). **Or progress by:** More weight, faster (sprints), longer distance, less rest.
- **Regress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or regress by:** Lighter, slower, shorter distance.
- **Same level swaps:** Sled Push; Sled Pull; Sled Row (Rope)
- **Cautions:** None specific. Almost universally safe. Backward drag is a knee pain staple. Heavy pushes raise blood pressure: keep breathing.
- **Default prescription:** 6 to 10 x 15 to 25m, walk back recovery; or 3 to 5 min backward drag in warm up
- **Coach sources:** Ben Patrick (ATG), DeFranco, Boyle

## Shuffle and Sprint

`LAT-038 | G3 | Agility / locomotion | HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: moderate | Teams only: No | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Bodyweight
- **Why we use it:** Change of direction, rhythm and footwork. Builds coordination and reaction (Gambetta), useful for sport and falls prevention, but most variations involve running or hopping.
- **This variation:** Fast/power version: move with intent, stop when speed drops.
- **Muscles:** Whole lower body, coordination, conditioning
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Stay low and light on the feet. 2) Short quick steps, eyes up. 3) Control each change of direction.
- **Common faults:** Crossing feet on shuffles; Standing tall and slow; Doing too much volume.
- **Progress to:** Lateral Shuffle (Band Resisted) (G4). **Or progress by:** Faster, more complex patterns.
- **Regress to:** Side Plank (G2); Cossack Squat (G2); Side Plank Clam (G2). **Or regress by:** Walking footwork patterns, lateral band walk, sled lateral drag.
- **Same level swaps:** Carioca; Ickey Shuffle; Lateral Shuffle
- **Cautions:** Knee, Osteoporosis/osteopenia. IMPACT (running/hopping): excluded from group sessions. Teams only after screening.
- **Default prescription:** 4 to 8 x 10 to 20s, full recovery
- **Coach sources:** Gambetta

## Side Plank

`LAT-041 | G2 | Core: anti lateral flexion (side plank) | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Bodyweight
- **Why we use it:** Part of the McGill Big 3. Builds the side core that stabilises the spine when carrying or standing on one leg. Hip abduction versions also train the glute med.
- **Muscles:** Obliques, quadratus lumborum, glute med
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Elbow under the shoulder, body in a straight line. 2) Push the hips up and forward. 3) Breathe and hold.
- **Common faults:** Hips sagging or piking back; Rolling forward; Shoulder shrugging.
- **Progress to:** Adductor Slide (Slider) (G3); Uneven Front Rack Carry (G3); Copenhagen Plank (Long Lever) (G3). **Or progress by:** Feet stacked, add hip abduction, Copenhagen.
- **Regress to:** Side Plank (Knees) (G1); Copenhagen Plank (Short Lever) (G1). **Or regress by:** Knees bent side plank.
- **Same level swaps:** Side Plank Clam; Side Plank Hip Dips; Side Plank Hip Abduction
- **Cautions:** None specific. Shoulder pain: kneeling version or suitcase carry instead.
- **Default prescription:** 3 sets x 15 to 45s each side (or 6/4/2 x 10s)
- **Coach sources:** McGill, Squat University
- **Also listed in:** Rehab: Lower Back

## Lateral Plyo Step

`LAT-044 | G3 | Power: jumps, hops and landings (plyometric) | HYBRID | Group: No | Impact: high | Teams only: Yes | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Bodyweight
- **Why we use it:** Jumps and hops train power, tendon stiffness and bone (impact is a key bone stimulus in LIFTMOR). Landings (snap downs, drop squats, jump and stick) teach the body to absorb force, the foundation of injury prevention. Progress carefully: landing before jumping, low before high, two legs before one.
- **Muscles:** Whole lower body, tendons, nervous system
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Land softly and quietly, hips back, knees over toes. 2) Stick the landing for a second before the next rep. 3) Quality over quantity: stop when height or control drops.
- **Common faults:** Landing stiff legged or with knees caving; Too many reps (plyos are not cardio); Progressing too fast.
- **Progress to:** Single Leg Box Jump (G4); Alternating Lunge Jump (G4). **Or progress by:** Landings → small jumps → box jumps → broad jumps → single leg hops → depth jumps.
- **Regress to:** Snap Downs (G2); Drop Squat (G2); Pogo Hops (Low) (G2). **Or regress by:** Snap downs/drop squat and stick, step ups, sled push, med ball throws.
- **Same level swaps:** A Skip; Box Jump; Bounding
- **Cautions:** Knee, Low back, Osteoporosis/osteopenia, Pelvic floor. IMPACT: excluded from Optimal GROUP sessions (no jumping rule). Teams only after screening. Avoid with pelvic floor symptoms, osteoporosis with fracture history, joint replacements, acute knee/Achilles pain.
- **Group swap:** Group swap (no jumping): sled push, fast step ups, med ball chest pass or slam, KB swing, fast sit to stand
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 5 sets x 3 to 6 reps, full recovery (60 to 120s), stop when speed drops; 2 to 3 sessions/week max, low total contacts (20 to 60)
- **Coach sources:** Gambetta, DeFranco (dynamic effort), LIFTMOR research (impact for bone)

- **Muscles:** Whole lower body, coordination, conditioning
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Stay low and light on the feet. 2) Short quick steps, eyes up. 3) Control each change of direction.
- **Common faults:** Crossing feet on shuffles; Standing tall and slow; Doing too much volume.
- **Progress to:** Lateral Shuffle (Band Resisted) (G4). **Or progress by:** Faster, more complex patterns.
- **Regress to:** Side Plank (G2); Cossack Squat (G2); Side Plank Clam (G2). **Or regress by:** Walking footwork patterns, lateral band walk, sled lateral drag.
- **Same level swaps:** Carioca; Lateral Shuffle; Shuffle and Sprint
- **Cautions:** Knee, Osteoporosis/osteopenia. IMPACT (running/hopping): excluded from group sessions. Teams only after screening.
- **Default prescription:** 4 to 8 x 10 to 20s, full recovery
- **Coach sources:** Gambetta

## Standing Cable Hip Abduction

`LAT-049 | G1 | Hip: abduction / glute med | STRONG, HYBRID, BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Cable machine
- **Why we use it:** The side glutes stop the knee caving and the pelvis dropping when on one leg. Weak glute meds are linked to knee pain, hip pain and back pain. Simple band work fixes it and works brilliantly as a warm up (Squat University, Boyle).
- **This variation:** Cable: constant tension through the whole range with smooth, joint friendly resistance.
- **Muscles:** Glute medius and minimus, hip stabilisers
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Athletic stance, band around the knees or ankles. 2) Push the knees out, step sideways (or lift the leg) leading with the heel. 3) Stay low and keep the pelvis level.
- **Common faults:** Rocking the torso side to side; Feet turning out; Letting the band pull the knees in.
- **Progress to:** Cable Lateral Lunge (G2); Cossack Squat (G2); Paused Hip Thrust (G2). **Or progress by:** Heavier band, band lower on the leg, side plank abduction.
- **Regress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or regress by:** Side lying with no band, smaller range.
- **Same level swaps:** Clam Shell; Monster Walk; Reverse Clam
- **Cautions:** None specific. Very joint friendly, ideal for hip and knee rehab.
- **Default prescription:** 2 to 3 sets x 10 to 20 each side
- **Coach sources:** Squat University, Boyle, Paul Chek
- **Also listed in:** Rehab: Hip

## Speed Skater (Slider)

`LAT-050 | G3 | Single leg: lateral (frontal plane) | HYBRID, STRONG, BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Sliders (confirm)
- **Why we use it:** Most training is forwards and backwards; lateral lunges train the side to side plane, building adductor strength and hip mobility that protect against groin strains and help golf, tennis and walking on uneven ground. Cossack squats are a great mobility and strength hybrid (Squat University and DeFranco's Limber 11).
- **This variation:** Sliders add a friction based eccentric control challenge.
- **Muscles:** Adductors, glutes, quads, hip mobility
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Step wide to the side, toes forward or slightly out. 2) Sit back into one hip, keeping the other leg straight. 3) Push back to the start through the bent leg.
- **Common faults:** Knee caving on the bent leg; Rounding the back to get lower; Heel lifting.
- **Progress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or progress by:** Add load (goblet, DB, landmine), slider, deeper cossack.
- **Regress to:** Cossack Squat (G2); Lateral Lunge (DB) (G2); Cable Lateral Lunge (G2). **Or regress by:** Shorter range, hand support, lateral lunge rock (mobility).
- **Same level swaps:** Slider Lateral Lunge; Offset Lateral Lunge
- **Cautions:** None specific. Groin and hip sensitive members: reduce range. Assisted versions (holding the rig) for seniors.
- **Default prescription:** 3 sets x 8 to 12 reps, tempo 3-0-1-1, rest 60 to 90s, RPE 7 to 9 (each side)
- **Coach sources:** Gambetta (multi plane), DeFranco (Limber 11), Squat University

## Standing Cable Hip Adduction

`LAT-051 | G2 | Hip: adductor strength | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Cable machine
- **Why we use it:** Copenhagen planks are among the best researched ways to prevent groin injury, and adductor strength supports knee and hip health. Ball squeezes are a gentle entry point.
- **This variation:** Cable: constant tension through the whole range with smooth, joint friendly resistance.
- **Muscles:** Adductors (inner thigh), core
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Side plank with the top leg on a bench (inside of the knee for short lever, ankle for long lever). 2) Lift the hips into a straight line by squeezing the top leg down. 3) Hold or lift and lower.
- **Common faults:** Hips sagging; Rolling forward; Starting with the long lever.
- **Progress to:** Adductor Slide (Slider) (G3); Copenhagen Plank (Long Lever) (G3). **Or progress by:** Short → long lever, add leg raises.
- **Regress to:** Standing Cable Hip Abduction (G1); Monster Walk (G1); Sled Lateral Drag (G1). **Or regress by:** Ball squeeze, side lying adduction.
- **Same level swaps:** Copenhagen Side Plank; Adductor Squeeze (Ball); Side Lying Hip Adduction
- **Cautions:** None specific. Short lever first. Groin pain: ball squeeze isometrics.
- **Default prescription:** 2 to 3 sets x 15 to 30s each side
- **Coach sources:** Research (groin injury prevention), Boyle

## Lateral Bound

`LAT-055 | G3 | Power: jumps, hops and landings (plyometric) | HYBRID | Group: No | Impact: high | Teams only: Yes | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Bodyweight
- **Why we use it:** Jumps and hops train power, tendon stiffness and bone (impact is a key bone stimulus in LIFTMOR). Landings (snap downs, drop squats, jump and stick) teach the body to absorb force, the foundation of injury prevention. Progress carefully: landing before jumping, low before high, two legs before one.
- **Muscles:** Whole lower body, tendons, nervous system
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Land softly and quietly, hips back, knees over toes. 2) Stick the landing for a second before the next rep. 3) Quality over quantity: stop when height or control drops.
- **Common faults:** Landing stiff legged or with knees caving; Too many reps (plyos are not cardio); Progressing too fast.
- **Progress to:** Single Leg Box Jump (G4); Alternating Lunge Jump (G4). **Or progress by:** Landings → small jumps → box jumps → broad jumps → single leg hops → depth jumps.
- **Regress to:** Snap Downs (G2); Drop Squat (G2); Pogo Hops (Low) (G2). **Or regress by:** Snap downs/drop squat and stick, step ups, sled push, med ball throws.
- **Same level swaps:** A Skip; Box Jump; Bounding
- **Cautions:** Knee, Low back, Osteoporosis/osteopenia, Pelvic floor. IMPACT: excluded from Optimal GROUP sessions (no jumping rule). Teams only after screening. Avoid with pelvic floor symptoms, osteoporosis with fracture history, joint replacements, acute knee/Achilles pain.
- **Group swap:** Group swap (no jumping): sled push, fast step ups, med ball chest pass or slam, KB swing, fast sit to stand
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 5 sets x 3 to 6 reps, full recovery (60 to 120s), stop when speed drops; 2 to 3 sessions/week max, low total contacts (20 to 60)
- **Coach sources:** Gambetta, DeFranco (dynamic effort), LIFTMOR research (impact for bone)
- **Also listed in:** Power And Plyometrics
