## Lateral Step Up to Knee Drive

`LAT-060 | G2 | Single leg: step up | STRONG, HYBRID, BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Box / bench / step
- **Why we use it:** A real life movement (stairs, kerbs, climbing). Very back friendly, easy to scale by box height, and the concentric emphasis means little soreness. Knee drive and crossover versions add balance and hip work.
- **This variation:** Combination move: trains two qualities at once, efficient for HYBRID and BURN; keep technique of both parts clean before speeding up. Knee drive adds hip flexor strength and single leg balance at the top.
- **Muscles:** Quads, glutes, hamstrings, balance
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Whole foot on the box, knee over the middle of the foot. 2) Lean forward slightly and drive through the box leg to stand tall. 3) Step down with control, don't push off the bottom leg.
- **Common faults:** Pushing off the floor leg; Knee caving as you stand; Box too high so the hip hikes.
- **Progress to:** Barbell Step Up (G3); Step Up to Single Leg RDL (G3). **Or progress by:** Higher box, add DBs/goblet/barbell, add a knee drive, slower lowering.
- **Regress to:** Patrick Step (G1); Poliquin Step Up (G1); Petersen Step Up (G1). **Or regress by:** Lower box, hand support, bodyweight.
- **Same level swaps:** DB Step Up; Goblet Step Up; Lateral Step Up
- **Cautions:** None specific. Knee friendly at lower heights. Use a low box and hand support for seniors and knee pain. Faster 'step ups' in BURN keep impact low.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8 (each leg)
- **Coach sources:** Boyle, Cosgrove, Gambetta

# 10. ROTATIONAL AND ANTI ROTATION

*Transverse plane, rotate and resist rotation*

**Grade ladder at a glance** (use this to slot every member into the same session at their level):

- **G1**: Pallof Press (Cable), Pallof Press (Band), Half Kneeling Pallof Press, Bird Dog, Tall Kneeling Pallof Press, Split Stance Pallof Press, Pallof Press with Overhead Reach, Pallof Hold Iso, Pallof Walkout, Pallof Press Lunge, Plate Halo, KB Halo, KB Around the World, Open Book (Side Lying), Suitcase Deadlift (Anti Lateral Flexion)
- **G2**: Plank Shoulder Tap, Plank Reach Out, Bear Plank Shoulder Tap, Side Plank Rotation (Thread the Needle), Cable Woodchop (High to Low), Cable Woodchop (Low to High), Half Kneeling Cable Chop, KB Windmill, Half Kneeling Cable Lift, Tall Kneeling Cable Chop, Band Woodchop, Cable Rotational Row, Cable Rotation (Horizontal), Rotational Press (Landmine), Standing Cable Rotation, Split Stance Cable Rotational Press, Landmine Rotation, T Rotation Press Up, Landmine Rainbow, Landmine 180, Quadruped Thoracic Rotation, Russian Twist (Plate), Seated Thoracic Rotation, Russian Twist (Med Ball), Bicycle Crunch, Seated Twist (Feet Down), Cross Body Mountain Climber, Med Ball Rotational Throw, Windscreen Wiper, Med Ball Scoop Toss, Supine Leg Lowering Twist, Med Ball Shot Put Throw, Med Ball Side Slam, Slam Ball Rotational Slam, Battle Rope Side to Side Waves, Rotational Lunge (Med Ball), Battle Rope Rainbows, Cable Lift with Step
- **G3**: Renegade Row (Anti Rotation), Bird Dog Row, Single Arm Plank, Single Arm KB Swing (Anti Rotation), Single Arm Cable Row with Rotation, Stir the Pot (Swiss Ball), Offset Front Rack Carry

✱ = not for group sessions (impact).

## Pallof Press (Cable)

`ROT-001 | G1 | Core: anti rotation (Pallof press) | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Cable machine
- **Why we use it:** The core's main job is to stop unwanted movement. The Pallof press resists the cable pulling you round, training the anti rotation strength that protects the back and transfers force in golf, tennis and lifting (McGill, Boyle, Cosgrove).
- **This variation:** Cable: constant tension through the whole range with smooth, joint friendly resistance.
- **Muscles:** Obliques, deep core, glutes
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Side on to the cable at chest height, brace. 2) Press the handle straight out from the chest and hold 2s. 3) Don't let the hands or hips rotate, return to the chest.
- **Common faults:** Rotating towards the cable; Leaning away; Holding the breath.
- **Progress to:** Band Woodchop (G2); Cable Lift with Step (G2); Half Kneeling Cable Chop (G2). **Or progress by:** Tall kneeling → half kneeling → split → standing → walkouts, add overhead reach, heavier.
- **Regress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or regress by:** Lighter band, closer to the anchor, iso hold.
- **Same level swaps:** Pallof Press; Pallof Walkout; Pallof Hold Iso
- **Cautions:** None specific. Excellent for back pain. Half kneeling reduces hip involvement and isolates the core.
- **Default prescription:** 2 to 3 sets x 6 to 10 reps each side (or 20 to 40s), slow and controlled
- **Coach sources:** McGill, Boyle, Cosgrove

## Plank Shoulder Tap

`ROT-002 | G2 | Core: anti extension (plank) | STRONG, HYBRID, BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Bodyweight
- **Why we use it:** The plank trains the core to resist extension. Useful foundation, part of the Optimal screen (30s kneeling → full plank → plank with full tension). Long lever and RKC versions dramatically increase difficulty without longer holds.
- **Muscles:** Abs, shoulders, glutes
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Elbows under shoulders, straight line head to heels. 2) Squeeze glutes, pull the ribs down, push the floor away. 3) Breathe, hold with full tension.
- **Common faults:** Sagging hips; Bum in the air; Holding for minutes with poor form.
- **Progress to:** Single Arm Plank (G3); Long Lever Plank (G3). **Or progress by:** Long lever, RKC plank, leg lift, body saw.
- **Regress to:** Dead Bug (G1); Plank on Knees (G1); Dead Bug Heel Taps (G1). **Or regress by:** Plank on knees, incline plank on a bench.
- **Same level swaps:** Plank Saw; RKC Plank; Front Plank
- **Cautions:** None specific. Shoulder or wrist pain: dead bug or Pallof press instead. Prefer 20 to 30s high tension holds over long sloppy ones.
- **Default prescription:** 3 sets x 20 to 40s (high tension)
- **Coach sources:** McGill, Boyle, Cosgrove

## Renegade Row (Anti Rotation)

`ROT-004 | G3 | Pull + core: plank row | HYBRID, BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Dumbbells (confirm)
- **Why we use it:** Rowing from a plank or bear position adds a strong anti rotation challenge: the core must stop the hips twisting. Great for HYBRID and BURN sessions.
- **Muscles:** Upper back, lats, core (anti rotation), shoulders
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Wide feet, strong plank or bear position. 2) Row one weight to the hip without the hips rotating. 3) Place it down with control, alternate.
- **Common faults:** Hips rotating; Feet too narrow; Rushing reps.
- **Progress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or progress by:** Narrower feet, heavier, add a push up.
- **Regress to:** Cross Body Mountain Climber (G2); KB Windmill (G2); Landmine 180 (G2). **Or regress by:** Knees down, bird dog row, chest supported row.
- **Same level swaps:** Renegade Row; Plank Row; Bird Dog Row
- **Cautions:** Shoulder. Wrist load: use hex DBs. Shoulder pain: use bird dog row or chest supported row instead.
- **Default prescription:** 2 to 3 sets x 6 to 10 reps each side (or 20 to 40s), slow and controlled
- **Coach sources:** Cosgrove, McGill (anti rotation)

## Half Kneeling Pallof Press

`ROT-005 | G1 | Core: anti rotation (Pallof press) | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Bodyweight
- **Why we use it:** The core's main job is to stop unwanted movement. The Pallof press resists the cable pulling you round, training the anti rotation strength that protects the back and transfers force in golf, tennis and lifting (McGill, Boyle, Cosgrove).
- **This variation:** Kneeling position locks the hips so the core has to control the trunk and stops the legs cheating.
- **Muscles:** Obliques, deep core, glutes

- **Progress to:** Band Woodchop (G2); Cable Lift with Step (G2); Half Kneeling Cable Chop (G2). **Or progress by:** Tall kneeling → half kneeling → split → standing → walkouts, add overhead reach, heavier.

## Bird Dog

`ROT-006 | G1 | Core: anti rotation / anti extension (bird dog) | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Bodyweight
- **Why we use it:** Part of the McGill Big 3. Reaching the opposite arm and leg while keeping the spine still trains the back extensors and anti rotation control with very low spinal load. A safe daily exercise for back pain and the foundation of Paul Chek's horse stance progressions.
- **Muscles:** Spinal extensors, glutes, deep core, shoulder stabilisers
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Hands under shoulders, knees under hips, neutral spine. 2) Reach the opposite arm and leg long (not high), hold 8 to 10s. 3) Sweep back under without the hips rotating.
- **Common faults:** Lifting the leg too high and arching; Hips rotating; Rushing.
- **Progress to:** KB Windmill (G2); Landmine 180 (G2); Band Woodchop (G2). **Or progress by:** Add a band, hold longer, bird dog row.
- **Regress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or regress by:** Arm only or leg only.
- **Same level swaps:** Bird Dog Hold
- **Cautions:** None specific. Back pain friendly. Wrist pain: use fists.
- **Default prescription:** Descending pyramid 6, 4, 2 each side with 8 to 10s holds, or 2 to 3 sets x 6 to 10 reps each side (or 20 to 40s), slow and controlled
- **Coach sources:** McGill, Paul Chek, Squat University
- **Also listed in:** Rehab: Lower Back, Mobility And Warm Up

## Tall Kneeling Pallof Press

`ROT-007 | G1 | Core: anti rotation (Pallof press) | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Bodyweight
- **Why we use it:** The core's main job is to stop unwanted movement. The Pallof press resists the cable pulling you round, training the anti rotation strength that protects the back and transfers force in golf, tennis and lifting (McGill, Boyle, Cosgrove).
- **This variation:** Kneeling position locks the hips so the core has to control the trunk and stops the legs cheating.
- **Muscles:** Obliques, deep core, glutes
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Side on to the cable at chest height, brace. 2) Press the handle straight out from the chest and hold 2s. 3) Don't let the hands or hips rotate, return to the chest.
- **Common faults:** Rotating towards the cable; Leaning away; Holding the breath.
- **Progress to:** Band Woodchop (G2); Cable Lift with Step (G2); Half Kneeling Cable Chop (G2). **Or progress by:** Tall kneeling → half kneeling → split → standing → walkouts, add overhead reach, heavier.
- **Regress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or regress by:** Lighter band, closer to the anchor, iso hold.
- **Same level swaps:** Pallof Press; Pallof Walkout; Pallof Hold Iso
- **Cautions:** None specific. Excellent for back pain. Half kneeling reduces hip involvement and isolates the core.

- **Coach sources:** McGill, Boyle, Cosgrove

## Bird Dog Row

`ROT-008 | G3 | Pull + core: plank row | HYBRID, BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Bodyweight
- **Why we use it:** Rowing from a plank or bear position adds a strong anti rotation challenge: the core must stop the hips twisting. Great for HYBRID and BURN sessions.
- **Muscles:** Upper back, lats, core (anti rotation), shoulders
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Wide feet, strong plank or bear position. 2) Row one weight to the hip without the hips rotating. 3) Place it down with control, alternate.
- **Common faults:** Hips rotating; Feet too narrow; Rushing reps.
- **Progress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or progress by:** Narrower feet, heavier, add a push up.
- **Regress to:** KB Windmill (G2); Landmine 180 (G2); Band Woodchop (G2). **Or regress by:** Knees down, bird dog row, chest supported row.
- **Same level swaps:** Plank Row; Renegade Row; Bear Plank Row
- **Cautions:** Shoulder. Wrist load: use hex DBs. Shoulder pain: use bird dog row or chest supported row instead.
- **Default prescription:** 2 to 3 sets x 6 to 10 reps each side (or 20 to 40s), slow and controlled
- **Coach sources:** Cosgrove, McGill (anti rotation)

## Plank Reach Out

`ROT-010 | G2 | Core: anti extension (plank) | STRONG, HYBRID, BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Bodyweight
- **Why we use it:** The plank trains the core to resist extension. Useful foundation, part of the Optimal screen (30s kneeling → full plank → plank with full tension). Long lever and RKC versions dramatically increase difficulty without longer holds.
- **Muscles:** Abs, shoulders, glutes
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Elbows under shoulders, straight line head to heels. 2) Squeeze glutes, pull the ribs down, push the floor away. 3) Breathe, hold with full tension.
- **Common faults:** Sagging hips; Bum in the air; Holding for minutes with poor form.
- **Progress to:** Single Arm Plank (G3); Long Lever Plank (G3). **Or progress by:** Long lever, RKC plank, leg lift, body saw.
- **Regress to:** Dead Bug (G1); Plank on Knees (G1); Dead Bug Heel Taps (G1). **Or regress by:** Plank on knees, incline plank on a bench.
- **Same level swaps:** Plank Saw; RKC Plank; Front Plank
- **Cautions:** None specific. Shoulder or wrist pain: dead bug or Pallof press instead. Prefer 20 to 30s high tension holds over long sloppy ones.
- **Default prescription:** 3 sets x 20 to 40s (high tension)
- **Coach sources:** McGill, Boyle, Cosgrove

## Side Plank Rotation (Thread the Needle)

`ROT-016 | G2 | Core: anti lateral flexion (side plank) | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Bodyweight
- **Why we use it:** Part of the McGill Big 3. Builds the side core that stabilises the spine when carrying or standing on one leg. Hip abduction versions also train the glute med.
- **Muscles:** Obliques, quadratus lumborum, glute med
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Elbow under the shoulder, body in a straight line. 2) Push the hips up and forward. 3) Breathe and hold.
- **Common faults:** Hips sagging or piking back; Rolling forward; Shoulder shrugging.
- **Progress to:** Adductor Slide (Slider) (G3); Uneven Front Rack Carry (G3); Copenhagen Plank (Long Lever) (G3). **Or progress by:** Feet stacked, add hip abduction, Copenhagen.
- **Regress to:** Side Plank (Knees) (G1); Copenhagen Plank (Short Lever) (G1). **Or regress by:** Knees bent side plank.
- **Same level swaps:** Side Plank; Side Plank Clam; Side Plank Hip Dips
- **Cautions:** None specific. Shoulder pain: kneeling version or suitcase carry instead.
- **Default prescription:** 3 sets x 15 to 45s each side (or 6/4/2 x 10s)
- **Coach sources:** McGill, Squat University

## Cable Woodchop (High to Low)

`ROT-018 | G2 | Rotation: chop and lift | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Cable machine
- **Why we use it:** Diagonal patterns that link the hips and shoulders through the core (Paul Chek's twist pattern, Gray Cook's chops and lifts). Train controlled rotation and are a staple of golf programmes.
- **This variation:** Cable: constant tension through the whole range with smooth, joint friendly resistance.
- **Muscles:** Obliques, core, hips, shoulders
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Feet stable, brace. 2) Pull the cable diagonally across the body, letting the hips and upper back turn together. 3) Control the return.
- **Common faults:** All arms; Twisting only at the low back; Too heavy and jerky.
- **Progress to:** Single Arm Cable Row with Rotation (G3); Bird Dog Row (G3); Single Arm Plank (G3). **Or progress by:** Standing, heavier, with a step, faster (power).
- **Regress to:** Pallof Press (Cable) (G1); Pallof Press (G1); Pallof Walkout (G1). **Or regress by:** Half/tall kneeling, lighter, smaller range.
- **Same level swaps:** Band Woodchop; Cable Lift with Step; Half Kneeling Cable Chop
- **Cautions:** None specific. Keep rotation through the hips and upper back, not the lumbar spine. Half kneeling is most back friendly.
- **Default prescription:** 2 to 3 sets x 6 to 10 reps each side (or 20 to 40s), slow and controlled
- **Coach sources:** Paul Chek, Gray Cook, Gambetta

## KB Halo

`ROT-019 | G1 | Shoulder / core: halo | HYBRID, STRONG | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Kettlebell
- **Why we use it:** Circling a weight around the head builds shoulder mobility and core control. Great warm up tool.
- **Muscles:** Shoulders, upper back, core
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Hold the bell upside down by the horns. 2) Circle it close around the head. 3) Keep ribs down, don't move the hips.
- **Common faults:** Arching the back; Bell too far from the head; Going too heavy.
- **Progress to:** KB Windmill (G2); Cross Body Mountain Climber (G2); Landmine 180 (G2). **Or progress by:** Heavier, half kneeling.
- **Regress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or regress by:** Lighter, plate.
- **Same level swaps:** Plate Halo; KB Around the World
- **Cautions:** None specific. Gentle for most shoulders.
- **Default prescription:** 2 sets x 5 to 8 each way
- **Coach sources:** Dan John

## Single Arm KB Swing (Anti Rotation)

`ROT-024 | G3 | Hinge: ballistic (power) | BURN, HYBRID, STRONG | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Kettlebell
- **Why we use it:** The king of hinge conditioning (Dan John, Pavel). Trains explosive hip extension (power) and heart rate at the same time with no impact on the knees. Excellent for fat loss, posture and glute strength. Dead stop versions teach control; single arm versions add anti rotation.
- **This variation:** One sided loading adds an anti rotation / anti lateral flexion core challenge and exposes left/right differences.
- **Muscles:** Glutes, hamstrings, core, grip, cardiovascular system
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Hike the bell back high between the thighs. 2) Snap the hips forward, squeeze the glutes, let the bell float to chest height. 3) Let it fall, hinge late, keep the spine neutral.
- **Common faults:** Squatting the swing instead of hinging; Lifting with the arms; Leaning back at the top.
- **Progress to:** Double KB Clean (G4); KB High Pull (Single Arm) (G4); Barbell Push Jerk (G4). **Or progress by:** Heavier bell, single arm, alternating, swings EMOM, heavier with fewer reps for power.
- **Regress to:** KB Swings (G2); KB Swing (Power) (G2); American KB Swing (G2). **Or regress by:** KB deadlift, dead stop swing, lighter bell, cable pull through.
- **Same level swaps:** Double KB Swing; Single Arm KB Swing; Single Arm KB Swing to Catch
- **Cautions:** Low back. Back friendly when the hinge is good. Teach the KB deadlift first. Not for acute low back pain. American (overhead) swings stress shoulders and low back: use hip height swings instead.
- **Default prescription:** 4 to 10 sets x 10 to 20 reps, or EMOM; 'hike, snap, float'
- **Coach sources:** Dan John, Pavel Tsatsouline, Cosgrove

- **Coaching cues:** 1) Feet stable, brace. 2) Pull the cable diagonally across the body, letting the hips and upper back turn together. 3) Control the return.
- **Common faults:** All arms; Twisting only at the low back; Too heavy and jerky.
- **Progress to:** Single Arm Cable Row with Rotation (G3); Bird Dog Row (G3); Single Arm Plank (G3). **Or progress by:** Standing, heavier, with a step, faster (power).
- **Regress to:** Pallof Press (Cable) (G1); Pallof Press (G1); Pallof Walkout (G1). **Or regress by:** Half/tall kneeling, lighter, smaller range.
- **Same level swaps:** Band Woodchop; Cable Lift with Step; Half Kneeling Cable Chop
- **Cautions:** None specific. Keep rotation through the hips and upper back, not the lumbar spine. Half kneeling is most back friendly.
- **Default prescription:** 2 to 3 sets x 6 to 10 reps each side (or 20 to 40s), slow and controlled
- **Coach sources:** Paul Chek, Gray Cook, Gambetta
- **Also listed in:** Rehab: Lower Back

## Single Arm Cable Row with Rotation

`ROT-026 | G3 | Horizontal pull: row | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Cable machine
- **Why we use it:** Rows build the upper back that holds posture upright and balances pressing. Chest supported rows remove the low back from the equation; single arm rows allow heavier loading and fix imbalances; bent over rows add hinge endurance. Aim for about 2 pulls for every push in desk based members.
- **This variation:** One sided loading adds an anti rotation / anti lateral flexion core challenge and exposes left/right differences. Cable: constant tension through the whole range with smooth, joint friendly resistance. Combination move: trains two qualities at once, efficient for HYBRID and BURN; keep technique of both parts clean before speeding up.
- **Muscles:** Upper back, lats, rear shoulders, biceps, grip
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Brace, shoulder blade pulls first, then the elbow. 2) Row towards the hip (lats) or lower ribs (upper back). 3) Pause, lower slowly to a full stretch.
- **Common faults:** Jerking and twisting the torso; Shrugging; Shortening the range.
- **Progress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or progress by:** Heavier, pause at the top, tempo, single arm, 1.5 reps.
- **Regress to:** Cable High Row (G2); Seated Cable Row (G2); Cable Squat to Row (G2). **Or regress by:** Chest supported row, cable row, TRX row.
- **Same level swaps:** Single Arm Cable Row; Split Stance Single Arm Cable Row; Single Arm DB Row
- **Cautions:** None specific. Chest supported and cable versions are the most back friendly. Bent over versions load the low back: avoid pairing with RDLs for 40+.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8
- **Coach sources:** DeFranco, Cressey, Poliquin, Boyle

## Cable Rotation (Horizontal)

`ROT-029 | G2 | Rotation: loaded rotation | HYBRID, STRONG | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Cable machine
- **Why we use it:** Controlled rotation through the hips and upper back with the landmine or cable. Builds rotational strength for golf and life (turning to reach, carrying).
- **This variation:** Cable: constant tension through the whole range with smooth, joint friendly resistance.
- **Muscles:** Obliques, hips, upper back
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Arms long, pivot the back foot. 2) Turn from the hips and upper back together. 3) Control the return through the middle.
- **Common faults:** Rotating only at the low back; Arms bending; Moving too fast.
- **Progress to:** Single Arm Cable Row with Rotation (G3); Bird Dog Row (G3); Single Arm Plank (G3). **Or progress by:** Heavier, faster, split stance.
- **Regress to:** Pallof Press (Cable) (G1); KB Halo (G1); Bird Dog (G1). **Or regress by:** Lighter, smaller range, anti rotation instead.
- **Same level swaps:** Standing Cable Rotation; Split Stance Cable Rotational Press; Landmine 180
- **Cautions:** None specific. Avoid fast loaded rotation with acute back pain.
- **Default prescription:** 2 to 3 sets x 6 to 10 reps each side (or 20 to 40s), slow and controlled
- **Coach sources:** Gambetta, Paul Chek

## Rotational Press (Landmine)

`ROT-030 | G2 | Push: landmine press | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Landmine (confirm)
- **Why we use it:** The landmine press moves on an arc between a horizontal and vertical press, letting the shoulder blade move freely. It is the most shoulder friendly way to press overhead and the go to for members who can't press straight overhead (Cressey). Half kneeling adds core and hip stability.
- **This variation:** Landmine: the arc path is shoulder and back friendly and very easy to learn.
- **Muscles:** Shoulders, chest, triceps, serratus, core
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Hold the end of the bar at the shoulder, ribs down, glutes tight. 2) Press up and forward, letting the shoulder blade reach around. 3) Lower with control back to the shoulder.
- **Common faults:** Arching the low back; Shrugging; Twisting the torso to press.
- **Progress to:** Single Arm Landmine Push Press (G3); Single Arm Landmine Press (Standing) (G3). **Or progress by:** Half kneeling → tall kneeling → split stance → standing → push press; add plates.
- **Regress to:** Landmine Press (Light) (G1); Seated DB Shoulder Press (G1). **Or regress by:** Lighter, two hands, half kneeling.
- **Same level swaps:** Landmine Press; Landmine Push Press; Landmine Chest Press
- **Cautions:** None specific. Best press for shoulder pain and limited overhead range.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8 (each arm)
- **Coach sources:** Cressey, Boyle, DeFranco

## T Rotation Press Up

`ROT-034 | G2 | Horizontal push: push up | STRONG, HYBRID, BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Bodyweight
- **Why we use it:** A moving plank: chest and arm strength plus core control. The shoulder blades move freely, which is healthier for shoulders than bench pressing. Easy to scale by hand height so every level in a group can do the same exercise. Push up plus adds serratus work for shoulder health.
- **Muscles:** Chest, shoulders, triceps, serratus, core (anti extension)
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Hands just outside shoulders, body in a straight line, glutes and abs tight. 2) Lower the chest between the hands, elbows about 45 degrees from the body. 3) Push the floor away until arms are straight and the upper back is spread.
- **Common faults:** Hips sagging; Elbows flaring to 90 degrees; Head poking forward / half reps.
- **Progress to:** Paused Press Up (G3); Archer Press Up (G3); Decline Press Up (G3). **Or progress by:** Lower the hand height (wall → bench → box → floor), tempo, pause, feet elevated, add a weighted vest/plate.
- **Regress to:** Box Press Up (G1); Wall Press Up (G1); Knee Press Up (G1). **Or regress by:** Higher incline (bench or wall), knee push up, shorter range.
- **Same level swaps:** Press Up; TRX Press Up; Wide Press Up
- **Cautions:** None specific. Wrist pain: use DB handles or fists. Shoulder pain: elevate the hands and keep elbows tucked.
- **Default prescription:** 3 sets x 6 to 15 reps (or total reps progression)
- **Coach sources:** Cosgrove, Boyle, Dan John

## Open Book (Side Lying)

`ROT-036 | G1 | Mobility: thoracic spine | STRONG, HYBRID, BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Bodyweight
- **Why we use it:** The upper back should move; the low back should be stable (joint by joint). Stiff upper backs cause rounded posture, shoulder pain and low back pain, and limit the golf swing. Daily T spine drills fix it.
- **Muscles:** Thoracic spine rotation and extension, lats, pecs
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Keep the hips still (knee pinned or in quadruped). 2) Rotate/extend through the upper back, follow the hand with the eyes. 3) Breathe out into the end range.
- **Common faults:** Rotating from the low back; Rushing; Forcing range.
- **Progress to:** KB Windmill (G2); Landmine 180 (G2); Band Woodchop (G2). **Or progress by:** Add a reach, hold end range longer.
- **Regress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or regress by:** Smaller range, seated version.
- **Same level swaps:** Open Book; Thread the Needle; Open Book Stretch
- **Cautions:** None specific. Very safe. Osteoporosis: avoid forced flexion; gentle rotation and extension are fine.
- **Default prescription:** 1 to 2 sets x 5 to 10 slow reps (or 30 to 60s), in warm up or cool down
- **Coach sources:** Squat University, Paul Chek, Cressey

## Russian Twist (Plate)

`ROT-039 | G2 | Core: rotation with flexion | BURN, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Plate
- **Why we use it:** Popular rotation exercises that combine spinal flexion and twisting. They do train the obliques, but the combination of flexion and rotation is the riskiest for discs.
- **Muscles:** Obliques, abs
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Sit tall, lean back slightly. 2) Rotate from the ribcage, not just the arms. 3) Control every rep.
- **Common faults:** Rounded slumped spine; Fast swinging; Heavy load.
- **Progress to:** Bird Dog Row (G3); Single Arm Plank (G3); Offset Front Rack Carry (G3). **Or progress by:** Feet up, heavier.
- **Regress to:** Plate Halo (G1); KB Halo (G1); Bird Dog (G1). **Or regress by:** Feet down, no load, Pallof press instead.
- **Same level swaps:** Bicycle Crunch; Windscreen Wiper; Seated Twist (Feet Down)
- **Cautions:** Low back, Osteoporosis/osteopenia. AVOID for back pain, disc history and osteoporosis (McGill). Prefer Pallof press and chops.
- **Default prescription:** 2 to 3 sets x 6 to 10 reps each side (or 20 to 40s), slow and controlled
- **Coach sources:** Paul Chek (ball versions), McGill (caution)

## Russian Twist (Med Ball)

`ROT-041 | G2 | Power: medicine ball throws and slams | HYBRID, BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Med ball / wall ball
- **Why we use it:** Med ball throws are the safest way to train power for 40+ members: no catching heavy loads, no landing impact, and you can throw as hard as possible. Rotational throws (scoop toss, shot put) are THE golf power exercise (Gambetta, Chek). Wall balls combine a squat with a throw for conditioning.
- **Muscles:** Whole body power, rotational core (rotational throws), shoulders
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Load the hips (or rotate back through the hips for rotational throws). 2) Explode from the ground up: legs, hips, then arms. 3) Throw with intent every rep, reset between reps.
- **Common faults:** Throwing with arms only; Rounding the back on slams; Doing so many reps that it becomes slow cardio.
- **Progress to:** DB Clean (G3); KB Clean (G3); DB Snatch (G3). **Or progress by:** Heavier ball, more distance/speed, step into the throw, single leg stance.
- **Regress to:** KB Halo (G1); Bird Dog (G1); Plate Halo (G1). **Or regress by:** Lighter ball, half kneeling throw, slower controlled chops.
- **Same level swaps:** Wall Balls; Med Ball Slam; Med Ball Side Slam
- **Cautions:** Osteoporosis/osteopenia. Low impact and joint friendly. Use a soft ball for slams. Rotational throws: avoid with acute back pain. Wall balls need shoulder overhead range.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 5 sets x 3 to 6 reps, full recovery (60 to 120s), stop when speed drops (each side for rotational)
- **Coach sources:** Gambetta, Cosgrove (power block), Paul Chek (twist)

## Cross Body Mountain Climber

`ROT-044 | G2 | Carry: suitcase / offset | STRONG, HYBRID, BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Dumbbells (confirm), Kettlebell
- **Why we use it:** One side loading turns a carry into an anti lateral flexion core exercise: you must stop the body leaning. McGill calls the suitcase carry one of the best core exercises.
- **Muscles:** Obliques, QL, grip, glute med
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Weight in one hand, stand tall, shoulders level. 2) Walk slowly without leaning towards or away from the weight. 3) Swap hands.
- **Common faults:** Leaning; Shrugging the loaded side; Rushing.
- **Progress to:** Uneven Front Rack Carry (G3); Offset Front Rack Carry (G3); Renegade Row (Anti Rotation) (G3). **Or progress by:** Heavier, march with high knees, longer.
- **Regress to:** Farmer's Carry (G1); Farmer's Carry March (G1); Farmer's Hold (Static) (G1). **Or regress by:** Lighter, static hold.
- **Same level swaps:** Suitcase Hold; Suitcase March; Suitcase Carry
- **Cautions:** None specific. Back pain friendly.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 5 x 20 to 40m (or 30 to 45s), rest 60 to 90s each side
- **Coach sources:** McGill, Dan John

- **Muscles:** Whole body power, rotational core (rotational throws), shoulders
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Load the hips (or rotate back through the hips for rotational throws). 2) Explode from the ground up: legs, hips, then arms. 3) Throw with intent every rep, reset between reps.
- **Common faults:** Throwing with arms only; Rounding the back on slams; Doing so many reps that it becomes slow cardio.
- **Progress to:** DB Clean (G3); KB Clean (G3); DB Snatch (G3). **Or progress by:** Heavier ball, more distance/speed, step into the throw, single leg stance.
- **Regress to:** KB Halo (G1); Bird Dog (G1); Plate Halo (G1). **Or regress by:** Lighter ball, half kneeling throw, slower controlled chops.
- **Same level swaps:** Wall Balls; Med Ball Slam; Med Ball Side Slam
- **Cautions:** None specific. Low impact and joint friendly. Use a soft ball for slams. Rotational throws: avoid with acute back pain. Wall balls need shoulder overhead range.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 5 sets x 3 to 6 reps, full recovery (60 to 120s), stop when speed drops (each side for rotational)
- **Coach sources:** Gambetta, Cosgrove (power block), Paul Chek (twist)
- **Also listed in:** Power And Plyometrics

## Windscreen Wiper

`ROT-046 | G2 | Core: rotation with flexion | BURN, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Bodyweight
- **Why we use it:** Popular rotation exercises that combine spinal flexion and twisting. They do train the obliques, but the combination of flexion and rotation is the riskiest for discs.
- **Muscles:** Obliques, abs
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Sit tall, lean back slightly. 2) Rotate from the ribcage, not just the arms. 3) Control every rep.
- **Common faults:** Rounded slumped spine; Fast swinging; Heavy load.
- **Progress to:** Bird Dog Row (G3); Single Arm Plank (G3); Offset Front Rack Carry (G3). **Or progress by:** Feet up, heavier.
- **Regress to:** KB Halo (G1); Bird Dog (G1); Plate Halo (G1). **Or regress by:** Feet down, no load, Pallof press instead.
- **Same level swaps:** Bicycle Crunch; Russian Twist (Plate); Seated Twist (Feet Down)
- **Cautions:** Low back, Osteoporosis/osteopenia. AVOID for back pain, disc history and osteoporosis (McGill). Prefer Pallof press and chops.
- **Default prescription:** 2 to 3 sets x 6 to 10 reps each side (or 20 to 40s), slow and controlled
- **Coach sources:** Paul Chek (ball versions), McGill (caution)

## Stir the Pot (Swiss Ball)

`ROT-050 | G3 | Core: anti extension + anti rotation (Swiss ball) | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Swiss ball (confirm)
- **Why we use it:** McGill's favourite advanced core drill: forearms on a Swiss ball making small circles while the body stays rigid.
- **This variation:** Swiss ball adds instability for core control (Paul Chek); keep loads modest.
- **Muscles:** Abs, obliques, shoulders
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Forearms on the ball, plank position. 2) Draw small circles with the elbows. 3) Keep the hips and back still.
- **Common faults:** Hips sagging; Big circles; Holding the breath.
- **Progress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or progress by:** Bigger circles, feet narrower.
- **Regress to:** KB Windmill (G2); Landmine 180 (G2); Band Woodchop (G2). **Or regress by:** Swiss ball plank hold.
- **Same level swaps:** Stir the Pot; Swiss Ball Stir the Pot
- **Cautions:** None specific. Safe for backs when form is held. Shoulder pain: reduce range.
- **Default prescription:** 2 to 3 x 5 to 10 circles each way
- **Coach sources:** McGill

## Suitcase Deadlift (Anti Lateral Flexion)

`ROT-052 | G1 | Hinge: deadlift (KB/DB/landmine) | STRONG, HYBRID, BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Bodyweight
- **Why we use it:** The safest way to teach lifting from the floor. Picking things up is a life skill (Primal Pattern 'bend'). Raising the bell on blocks reduces range for beginners and back pain; suitcase versions add anti lateral flexion.
- **This variation:** One sided loading adds an anti rotation / anti lateral flexion core challenge and exposes left/right differences.
- **Muscles:** Glutes, hamstrings, back, grip
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Bell between the feet (or beside for suitcase), hinge down with a flat back. 2) Grip, pull the shoulders down, brace. 3) Push the floor away and stand tall, squeeze the glutes.
- **Common faults:** Squatting down too low; Rounding to reach the bell; Leaning back at the top.
- **Progress to:** KB Swings (G2); Tempo DB RDL (G2); Trap Bar RDL (G2). **Or progress by:** Heavier bell, double KB, lower to the floor, progress to RDL, swing and trap bar.
- **Regress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or regress by:** Bell on a block/step, hinge drill.
- **Same level swaps:** KB Deadlift; DB Deadlift; Sumo KB Deadlift
- **Cautions:** None specific. Very back friendly. Elevate the bell on a step for limited hip mobility or back history.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8
- **Coach sources:** Dan John, McGill, Cosgrove

## Offset Front Rack Carry

`ROT-054 | G3 | Carry: front loaded | STRONG, HYBRID, BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Dumbbells (confirm), Kettlebell
- **Why we use it:** Holding the weight in front forces the core to resist being pulled forward and the upper back to stay upright. Great posture and core work.
- **This variation:** One sided loading adds an anti rotation / anti lateral flexion core challenge and exposes left/right differences.
- **Muscles:** Core (anti extension), upper back, legs
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Weight tight to the chest. 2) Stand tall, ribs down, walk slowly. 3) Breathe behind the brace.
- **Common faults:** Leaning back to counterbalance; Holding the breath; Elbows drifting.
- **Progress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or progress by:** Heavier, double KB, uneven.
- **Regress to:** Goblet Carry (G2); Duck Walk (KB Goblet) (G2); Front Rack Carry (Single KB) (G2). **Or regress by:** Lighter, goblet.
- **Same level swaps:** Front Rack Hold (Double KB); Front Rack Carry (Double KB); Zercher Carry (Barbell)
- **Cautions:** None specific. Generally safe. Duck walks are deep knee bending: knee pain caution.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 5 x 20 to 40m (or 30 to 45s), rest 60 to 90s
- **Coach sources:** Dan John, Cosgrove

## Battle Rope Side to Side Waves

`ROT-055 | G2 | Conditioning: battle ropes | BURN, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Battle ropes (confirm)
- **Why we use it:** Upper body conditioning with no impact. Great in BURN circuits and for members who can't run or jump.
- **Muscles:** Shoulders, arms, core, cardio
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Athletic stance, brace. 2) Drive the waves from the shoulders and hips. 3) Keep a steady rhythm.
- **Common faults:** Standing upright and stiff; Shrugging; Waves dying out.
- **Progress to:** Bird Dog Row (G3); Single Arm Plank (G3); Offset Front Rack Carry (G3). **Or progress by:** Longer, faster, heavier rope.
- **Regress to:** KB Halo (G1); Bird Dog (G1); Plate Halo (G1). **Or regress by:** Shorter intervals, kneeling.
- **Same level swaps:** Battle Rope Slams; Battle Rope Rainbows; Battle Rope Double Waves
- **Cautions:** None specific. Low impact. Rope jumping jacks involve jumping: swap to step jacks in groups.
- **Default prescription:** 6 to 10 x 20 to 30s / 30 to 60s rest
- **Coach sources:** Cosgrove (metabolic)

## Rotational Lunge (Med Ball)

`ROT-056 | G2 | Single leg: forward / walking lunge | BURN, HYBRID, STRONG | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Med ball / wall ball
- **Why we use it:** Forward and walking lunges add deceleration and balance: you have to control the body moving forward over the front leg. Very functional and very metabolic, so they suit BURN and HYBRID sessions. Loaded carry lunges add grip and core.
- **Muscles:** Quads, glutes, hamstrings, balance, grip when loaded
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Long step forward, land heel first. 2) Drop the back knee down, front knee over the middle of the foot. 3) Push through the front foot and step through to the next rep.
- **Common faults:** Short choppy steps that load the front knee; Front knee caving; Torso collapsing forward.
- **Progress to:** Barbell Walking Lunge (G3); Overhead Walking Lunge (KB) (G3); Overhead Walking Lunge (Plate) (G3). **Or progress by:** Add load (DB, KB rack, overhead), pulses, longer distance.
- **Regress to:** Split Squat (Supported) (G1); Split Squat (Bodyweight) (G1); TRX Assisted Split Squat (G1). **Or regress by:** Reverse lunge, split squat, hand support.
- **Same level swaps:** TRX Lunge; Lunge Pulses; Forward Lunge (DB)
- **Cautions:** Knee. More knee stress than reverse lunges. Swap to reverse lunges or split squats with knee pain. Needs space in groups.
- **Default prescription:** 3 sets x 8 to 12 reps, tempo 3-0-1-1, rest 60 to 90s, RPE 7 to 9 (each leg) or 20 to 30m
- **Coach sources:** Gambetta (lunge matrix), Cosgrove, Paul Chek (lunge pattern)

## Battle Rope Rainbows

- **Why we use it:** Upper body conditioning with no impact. Great in BURN circuits and for members who can't run or jump.

- **Regress to:** KB Halo (G1); Bird Dog (G1); Plate Halo (G1). **Or regress by:** Shorter intervals, kneeling.
- **Same level swaps:** Battle Rope Slams; Battle Rope Double Waves; Battle Rope Alternating Waves

## Cable Lift with Step

`ROT-058 | G2 | Rotation: chop and lift | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Cable machine
- **Why we use it:** Diagonal patterns that link the hips and shoulders through the core (Paul Chek's twist pattern, Gray Cook's chops and lifts). Train controlled rotation and are a staple of golf programmes.
- **This variation:** Cable: constant tension through the whole range with smooth, joint friendly resistance.
- **Muscles:** Obliques, core, hips, shoulders
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Feet stable, brace. 2) Pull the cable diagonally across the body, letting the hips and upper back turn together. 3) Control the return.
- **Common faults:** All arms; Twisting only at the low back; Too heavy and jerky.
- **Progress to:** Single Arm Cable Row with Rotation (G3); Bird Dog Row (G3); Single Arm Plank (G3). **Or progress by:** Standing, heavier, with a step, faster (power).
- **Regress to:** Pallof Press (Cable) (G1); Pallof Press (G1); Pallof Walkout (G1). **Or regress by:** Half/tall kneeling, lighter, smaller range.
- **Same level swaps:** Band Woodchop; Half Kneeling Cable Chop; Half Kneeling Cable Lift
- **Cautions:** None specific. Keep rotation through the hips and upper back, not the lumbar spine. Half kneeling is most back friendly.
- **Default prescription:** 2 to 3 sets x 6 to 10 reps each side (or 20 to 40s), slow and controlled
- **Coach sources:** Paul Chek, Gray Cook, Gambetta

# 11. CORE

*Brace, anti extension, flexion, stability*

**Grade ladder at a glance** (use this to slot every member into the same session at their level):

- **G1**: Dead Bug, Dead Bug (KB Pullover), Dead Bug Heel Taps, Plank on Knees, Side Plank (Knees), Bird Dog Hold, McGill Curl Up, Pelvic Tilt
- **G2**: Dead Bug (Band Resisted), Mountain Climber, Crunch, Reverse Crunch, Bench Reverse Crunch, Front Plank, Toe Touch Crunch, Plank with Leg Lift, Sit Up, Plank Up Down, Plank Saw, Cable Crunch (Kneeling), Plank Jacks, Hanging Knee Raise, RKC Plank, Hanging Leg Raise, Captain's Chair Knee Raise, Side Plank Hip Dips, Lying Leg Raise, Bear Plank Hold, Flutter Kicks, Bear Crawl, Scissor Kicks, Bear Crawl (Reverse), Heel Taps, Suitcase Hold, Suitcase March, Overhead March (KB), Side Bend (DB), Cable Side Bend, Copenhagen Side Plank, Single Leg Lowering, Crunch on Swiss Ball
- **G3**: TRX Knee Tuck, TRX Body Saw, Hollow Body Hold, Hollow Body Rock, V Up, Long Lever Plank, Tuck Up, Weighted Sit Up, Swiss Ball Stir the Pot, Ab Wheel Rollout (Kneeling), Slider Mountain Climber, TRX Fallout, TRX Pike
- **G4**: Swiss Ball Rollout, Swiss Ball Pike, Swiss Ball Jackknife, Barbell Rollout ✱, Slider Body Saw, Slider Pike

✱ = not for group sessions (impact).

## Dead Bug

`COR-001 | G1 | Core: anti extension (dead bug) | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Bodyweight
- **Why we use it:** Keeps the low back flat while the arms and legs move: anti extension control and coordination. Safe for almost everyone and the foundation of bracing (McGill, Chek).
- **Muscles:** Deep abs, hip flexors, coordination
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Back flat, ribs down, knees and arms up. 2) Slowly extend the opposite arm and leg while breathing out. 3) Return and swap without the back arching.
- **Common faults:** Low back lifting; Moving fast; Holding the breath.
- **Progress to:** Plank Saw (G2); RKC Plank (G2); Front Plank (G2). **Or progress by:** Straighter legs, band resisted, KB pullover, slower.
- **Regress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or regress by:** Heel taps, arms only.
- **Same level swaps:** Dead Bug Heel Taps; Dead Bug Bridge Hold; Dead Bug (Wall Press)
- **Cautions:** None specific. Back pain friendly. Pelvic floor friendly.
- **Default prescription:** 2 to 3 sets x 6 to 10 reps each side (or 20 to 40s), slow and controlled
- **Coach sources:** McGill, Paul Chek, Boyle
- **Also listed in:** Rehab: Lower Back, Mobility And Warm Up

## TRX Knee Tuck

`COR-002 | G3 | Core: dynamic flexion / pike | HYBRID, BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** TRX
- **Why we use it:** Dynamic core exercises that pull the knees or hips up from a plank or lying position. Good for conditioning and variety at higher levels.
- **Muscles:** Abs, hip flexors, shoulders
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Start in a strong plank. 2) Pull the knees or hips up with the abs. 3) Return with control.
- **Common faults:** Sagging plank; Using momentum; Shoulders drifting back.
- **Progress to:** Slider Pike (G4); Swiss Ball Pike (G4); Swiss Ball Jackknife (G4). **Or progress by:** Pike instead of tuck.
- **Regress to:** Crunch (G2); Sit Up (G2); Plank Saw (G2). **Or regress by:** Knee tuck, plank.
- **Same level swaps:** TRX Pike; V Up; Tuck Up
- **Cautions:** Low back, Osteoporosis/osteopenia, Pelvic floor. Lying V ups and tuck ups flex the spine: avoid for back pain and osteoporosis.
- **Default prescription:** 2 to 3 sets x 6 to 10 reps each side (or 20 to 40s), slow and controlled
- **Coach sources:** Boyle, Cosgrove

## Dead Bug (Band Resisted)

`COR-003 | G2 | Core: anti extension (dead bug) | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Resistance band (confirm)
- **Why we use it:** Keeps the low back flat while the arms and legs move: anti extension control and coordination. Safe for almost everyone and the foundation of bracing (McGill, Chek).
- **This variation:** Band resistance gets harder at the top (accommodating resistance) and can cue better positions such as knees out.
- **Muscles:** Deep abs, hip flexors, coordination
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Back flat, ribs down, knees and arms up. 2) Slowly extend the opposite arm and leg while breathing out. 3) Return and swap without the back arching.
- **Common faults:** Low back lifting; Moving fast; Holding the breath.
- **Progress to:** Single Arm Plank (G3); Long Lever Plank (G3); Hollow Body Hold (G3). **Or progress by:** Straighter legs, band resisted, KB pullover, slower.
- **Regress to:** Dead Bug (G1); Dead Bug Heel Taps (G1); Dead Bug Bridge Hold (G1). **Or regress by:** Heel taps, arms only.
- **Same level swaps:** Plank Saw; RKC Plank; Front Plank
- **Cautions:** None specific. Back pain friendly. Pelvic floor friendly.
- **Default prescription:** 2 to 3 sets x 6 to 10 reps each side (or 20 to 40s), slow and controlled
- **Coach sources:** McGill, Paul Chek, Boyle

## TRX Body Saw

`COR-004 | G3 | Core: anti extension (rollout) | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** TRX
- **Why we use it:** Rollouts and body saws are advanced anti extension: the further the arms reach, the harder the core works to stop the back arching.
- **Muscles:** Abs, lats, shoulders
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Kneeling or plank, ribs down, glutes tight. 2) Roll or slide out only as far as you can keep the back flat. 3) Pull back using the abs and lats.
- **Common faults:** Low back sagging; Hips piking first; Going too far too soon.
- **Progress to:** Barbell Rollout (G4); Slider Body Saw (G4); Swiss Ball Rollout (G4). **Or progress by:** Longer range, from feet.
- **Regress to:** Plank Saw (G2); RKC Plank (G2); Front Plank (G2). **Or regress by:** Swiss ball rollout short range, plank.
- **Same level swaps:** TRX Fallout; Ab Wheel Rollout (Kneeling); Swiss Ball Rollout (Short Range)
- **Cautions:** Low back. Can strain the low back if overreached. Shoulder pain: limit range.
- **Default prescription:** 2 to 3 sets x 6 to 10 reps each side (or 20 to 40s), slow and controlled
- **Coach sources:** McGill, Boyle, Cosgrove

`COR-005 | G1 | Core: anti extension (dead bug) | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

## Mountain Climber

`COR-006 | G2 | Core / conditioning: mountain climbers | BURN, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Bodyweight
- **Why we use it:** A plank with running legs. Good conditioning without jumping when done slowly; fast versions add impact through the wrists and shoulders.
- **Muscles:** Core, hip flexors, shoulders, cardio
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Strong plank, hands under shoulders. 2) Drive one knee towards the chest at a time. 3) Keep the hips level.
- **Common faults:** Hips bouncing high; Shoulders drifting behind the hands; Toe tapping without the knee driving.
- **Progress to:** V Up (G3); Tuck Up (G3); TRX Pike (G3). **Or progress by:** Faster, sliders, cross body.
- **Regress to:** Dead Bug (G1); Pelvic Tilt (G1); Bird Dog Hold (G1). **Or regress by:** Hands on a bench, slow.
- **Same level swaps:** Mountain Climbers; Mountain Climber Sprints
- **Cautions:** None specific. Wrist load. Slow and controlled versions are fine for groups; sprint versions are harder.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 6 x 20 to 30s
- **Coach sources:** DeFranco (Limber 11, slow), Cosgrove

## Dead Bug Heel Taps

`COR-007 | G1 | Core: anti extension (dead bug) | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Bodyweight
- **Why we use it:** Keeps the low back flat while the arms and legs move: anti extension control and coordination. Safe for almost everyone and the foundation of bracing (McGill, Chek).
- **Muscles:** Deep abs, hip flexors, coordination
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Back flat, ribs down, knees and arms up. 2) Slowly extend the opposite arm and leg while breathing out. 3) Return and swap without the back arching.
- **Common faults:** Low back lifting; Moving fast; Holding the breath.
- **Progress to:** Plank Saw (G2); RKC Plank (G2); Front Plank (G2). **Or progress by:** Straighter legs, band resisted, KB pullover, slower.
- **Regress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or regress by:** Heel taps, arms only.
- **Same level swaps:** Dead Bug; Dead Bug Bridge Hold; Dead Bug (Wall Press)
- **Cautions:** None specific. Back pain friendly. Pelvic floor friendly.
- **Default prescription:** 2 to 3 sets x 6 to 10 reps each side (or 20 to 40s), slow and controlled
- **Coach sources:** McGill, Paul Chek, Boyle

## Crunch

`COR-008 | G2 | Core: spinal flexion (crunch / sit up) | BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Bodyweight
- **Why we use it:** Classic ab exercises. They work the abs but repeated loaded spinal flexion is not ideal for discs, so they are low priority at Optimal compared with anti movement work.
- **Muscles:** Abs
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Ribs towards the hips. 2) Exhale as you curl. 3) Control the lowering.
- **Common faults:** Pulling on the neck; Using momentum; High reps fast.
- **Progress to:** V Up (G3); Tuck Up (G3); TRX Pike (G3). **Or progress by:** Weighted, cable.
- **Regress to:** Dead Bug (G1); Pelvic Tilt (G1); Bird Dog Hold (G1). **Or regress by:** McGill curl up, dead bug.
- **Same level swaps:** Sit Up; Reverse Crunch; Toe Touch Crunch
- **Cautions:** Low back, Osteoporosis/osteopenia. AVOID for back pain, disc history and osteoporosis. Use McGill curl up instead.
- **Default prescription:** 2 to 3 sets x 10 to 15 reps, tempo 2-1-1-1, rest 45 to 60s, RPE 8
- **Coach sources:** McGill (caution), Boyle (anti movement preference)

## Hollow Body Hold

`COR-009 | G3 | Core: anti extension (hollow body) | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Bodyweight
- **Why we use it:** A gymnastic anti extension hold. Harder than a dead bug.
- **This variation:** Isometric: builds strength and tendon tolerance in a fixed position with minimal joint irritation.
- **Muscles:** Abs, hip flexors
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Low back pressed down. 2) Arms and legs extended low. 3) Hold.
- **Common faults:** Back arching; Holding breath; Neck strain.
- **Progress to:** Slider Pike (G4); Swiss Ball Pike (G4); Barbell Rollout (G4). **Or progress by:** Longer levers, rocks.
- **Regress to:** Crunch (G2); Sit Up (G2); Plank Saw (G2). **Or regress by:** Tuck hold, dead bug.
- **Same level swaps:** Hollow Body Rock; Supine Hollow Hold (Tuck)
- **Cautions:** Low back, Osteoporosis/osteopenia, Pelvic floor. Can strain the low back if form is lost. Tuck the knees to regress.
- **Default prescription:** 3 x 15 to 30s
- **Coach sources:** Gymnastics, Boyle

## Front Plank

`COR-013 | G2 | Core: anti extension (plank) | STRONG, HYBRID, BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Bodyweight
- **Why we use it:** The plank trains the core to resist extension. Useful foundation, part of the Optimal screen (30s kneeling → full plank → plank with full tension). Long lever and RKC versions dramatically increase difficulty without longer holds.
- **Muscles:** Abs, shoulders, glutes
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Elbows under shoulders, straight line head to heels. 2) Squeeze glutes, pull the ribs down, push the floor away. 3) Breathe, hold with full tension.
- **Common faults:** Sagging hips; Bum in the air; Holding for minutes with poor form.
- **Progress to:** Single Arm Plank (G3); Long Lever Plank (G3). **Or progress by:** Long lever, RKC plank, leg lift, body saw.
- **Regress to:** Dead Bug (G1); Plank on Knees (G1); Dead Bug Heel Taps (G1). **Or regress by:** Plank on knees, incline plank on a bench.
- **Same level swaps:** Plank Saw; RKC Plank; Plank Jacks
- **Cautions:** None specific. Shoulder or wrist pain: dead bug or Pallof press instead. Prefer 20 to 30s high tension holds over long sloppy ones.
- **Default prescription:** 3 sets x 20 to 40s (high tension)
- **Coach sources:** McGill, Boyle, Cosgrove

## V Up

`COR-016 | G3 | Core: dynamic flexion / pike | HYBRID, BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Bodyweight
- **Why we use it:** Dynamic core exercises that pull the knees or hips up from a plank or lying position. Good for conditioning and variety at higher levels.
- **Muscles:** Abs, hip flexors, shoulders
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Start in a strong plank. 2) Pull the knees or hips up with the abs. 3) Return with control.
- **Common faults:** Sagging plank; Using momentum; Shoulders drifting back.
- **Progress to:** Slider Pike (G4); Swiss Ball Pike (G4); Swiss Ball Jackknife (G4). **Or progress by:** Pike instead of tuck.
- **Regress to:** Crunch (G2); Sit Up (G2); Plank Saw (G2). **Or regress by:** Knee tuck, plank.
- **Same level swaps:** Tuck Up; TRX Pike; TRX Knee Tuck
- **Cautions:** Low back, Osteoporosis/osteopenia, Pelvic floor. Lying V ups and tuck ups flex the spine: avoid for back pain and osteoporosis.
- **Default prescription:** 2 to 3 sets x 6 to 10 reps each side (or 20 to 40s), slow and controlled
- **Coach sources:** Boyle, Cosgrove

## Hanging Knee Raise

`COR-026 | G2 | Core: lower abs / hip flexors | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Rig / pull up bar
- **Why we use it:** Lowering and raising the legs while keeping the low back down trains lower abdominal control. Hanging versions add grip and are advanced.
- **Muscles:** Abs, hip flexors
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Low back pressed down. 2) Lower the legs only as far as the back stays flat. 3) Exhale as you lift.
- **Common faults:** Back arching off the floor; Swinging; Rushing.
- **Progress to:** V Up (G3); Tuck Up (G3); TRX Pike (G3). **Or progress by:** Straighter legs, hanging.
- **Regress to:** Dead Bug (G1); Pelvic Tilt (G1); Bird Dog Hold (G1). **Or regress by:** Bent knee heel taps, dead bug.
- **Same level swaps:** Hanging Leg Raise; Captain's Chair Knee Raise; Heel Taps
- **Cautions:** None specific. Back pain: keep the knees bent and range short. Hanging versions need healthy shoulders.
- **Default prescription:** 2 to 3 sets x 6 to 10 reps each side (or 20 to 40s), slow and controlled
- **Coach sources:** Boyle, Paul Chek

- **Cautions:** None specific. Back pain: keep the knees bent and range short. Hanging versions need healthy shoulders.

## Bear Plank Hold

`COR-033 | G2 | Core: anti extension (plank) | STRONG, HYBRID, BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Bodyweight
- **Why we use it:** The plank trains the core to resist extension. Useful foundation, part of the Optimal screen (30s kneeling → full plank → plank with full tension). Long lever and RKC versions dramatically increase difficulty without longer holds.
- **This variation:** Isometric: builds strength and tendon tolerance in a fixed position with minimal joint irritation.
- **Muscles:** Abs, shoulders, glutes
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Elbows under shoulders, straight line head to heels. 2) Squeeze glutes, pull the ribs down, push the floor away. 3) Breathe, hold with full tension.
- **Common faults:** Sagging hips; Bum in the air; Holding for minutes with poor form.
- **Progress to:** Single Arm Plank (G3); Long Lever Plank (G3). **Or progress by:** Long lever, RKC plank, leg lift, body saw.
- **Regress to:** Dead Bug (G1); Plank on Knees (G1); Dead Bug Heel Taps (G1). **Or regress by:** Plank on knees, incline plank on a bench.
- **Same level swaps:** Plank Saw; RKC Plank; Front Plank
- **Cautions:** None specific. Shoulder or wrist pain: dead bug or Pallof press instead. Prefer 20 to 30s high tension holds over long sloppy ones.
- **Default prescription:** 3 sets x 20 to 40s (high tension)
- **Coach sources:** McGill, Boyle, Cosgrove
- **Also listed in:** Rehab: Lower Back

## Bear Crawl

`COR-035 | G2 | Core: quadruped (bear hold / crawl) | HYBRID, BURN, STRONG | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Bodyweight
- **Why we use it:** Bear holds and crawls train the core and shoulders together and build coordination (Gambetta, Chek). Getting down to and moving on the floor is also a longevity skill.
- **Muscles:** Core, shoulders, quads, coordination
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Hands under shoulders, knees under hips, knees hover 2 to 3cm. 2) Back flat, move opposite hand and foot together. 3) Small steps, keep the hips still.
- **Common faults:** Hips high; Back rounding; Moving too fast.
- **Progress to:** V Up (G3); Tuck Up (G3); TRX Pike (G3). **Or progress by:** Longer, add drag/load, reverse and lateral.
- **Regress to:** Dead Bug (G1); Pelvic Tilt (G1); Bird Dog Hold (G1). **Or regress by:** Static bear hold, knees down.
- **Same level swaps:** Crab Walk; Lateral Bear Crawl; KB Bear Crawl Drag
- **Cautions:** None specific. Wrist pain: use fists or DB handles.
- **Default prescription:** 3 x 20 to 40s or 10 to 20m
- **Coach sources:** Gambetta, Paul Chek
- **Also listed in:** Conditioning, Mobility And Warm Up

## Swiss Ball Rollout

`COR-039 | G4 | Core: anti extension (rollout) | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Swiss ball (confirm)
- **Why we use it:** Rollouts and body saws are advanced anti extension: the further the arms reach, the harder the core works to stop the back arching.
- **This variation:** Swiss ball adds instability for core control (Paul Chek); keep loads modest.
- **Muscles:** Abs, lats, shoulders
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Kneeling or plank, ribs down, glutes tight. 2) Roll or slide out only as far as you can keep the back flat. 3) Pull back using the abs and lats.
- **Common faults:** Low back sagging; Hips piking first; Going too far too soon.
- **Progress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or progress by:** Longer range, from feet.
- **Regress to:** Swiss Ball Rollout (Short Range) (G3); TRX Fallout (G3); TRX Body Saw (G3). **Or regress by:** Swiss ball rollout short range, plank.
- **Same level swaps:** Barbell Rollout; Slider Body Saw
- **Cautions:** Low back. Can strain the low back if overreached. Shoulder pain: limit range.
- **Default prescription:** 2 to 3 sets x 6 to 10 reps each side (or 20 to 40s), slow and controlled
- **Coach sources:** McGill, Boyle, Cosgrove

## Suitcase Hold

`COR-040 | G2 | Carry: suitcase / offset | STRONG, HYBRID, BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Dumbbells (confirm), Kettlebell
- **Why we use it:** One side loading turns a carry into an anti lateral flexion core exercise: you must stop the body leaning. McGill calls the suitcase carry one of the best core exercises.
- **This variation:** One sided loading adds an anti rotation / anti lateral flexion core challenge and exposes left/right differences. Isometric: builds strength and tendon tolerance in a fixed position with minimal joint irritation.
- **Muscles:** Obliques, QL, grip, glute med
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Weight in one hand, stand tall, shoulders level. 2) Walk slowly without leaning towards or away from the weight. 3) Swap hands.
- **Common faults:** Leaning; Shrugging the loaded side; Rushing.
- **Progress to:** Uneven Front Rack Carry (G3); V Up (G3); Tuck Up (G3). **Or progress by:** Heavier, march with high knees, longer.
- **Regress to:** Farmer's Carry (G1); Farmer's Carry March (G1); Farmer's Hold (Static) (G1). **Or regress by:** Lighter, static hold.
- **Same level swaps:** Suitcase March; Suitcase Carry; Cross Body Carry
- **Cautions:** None specific. Back pain friendly.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 5 x 20 to 40m (or 30 to 45s), rest 60 to 90s each side
- **Coach sources:** McGill, Dan John

## Swiss Ball Stir the Pot

`COR-041 | G3 | Core: anti extension + anti rotation (Swiss ball) | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Swiss ball (confirm)
- **Why we use it:** McGill's favourite advanced core drill: forearms on a Swiss ball making small circles while the body stays rigid.
- **This variation:** Swiss ball adds instability for core control (Paul Chek); keep loads modest.
- **Muscles:** Abs, obliques, shoulders
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Forearms on the ball, plank position. 2) Draw small circles with the elbows. 3) Keep the hips and back still.
- **Common faults:** Hips sagging; Big circles; Holding the breath.
- **Progress to:** Swiss Ball Pike (G4); Swiss Ball Rollout (G4); Swiss Ball Jackknife (G4). **Or progress by:** Bigger circles, feet narrower.
- **Regress to:** Crunch on Swiss Ball (G2); Crunch (G2); Sit Up (G2). **Or regress by:** Swiss ball plank hold.
- **Same level swaps:** Stir the Pot; Stir the Pot (Swiss Ball)
- **Cautions:** None specific. Safe for backs when form is held. Shoulder pain: reduce range.
- **Default prescription:** 2 to 3 x 5 to 10 circles each way
- **Coach sources:** McGill

## Swiss Ball Pike

`COR-043 | G4 | Core: dynamic flexion / pike | HYBRID, BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Swiss ball (confirm)
- **Why we use it:** Dynamic core exercises that pull the knees or hips up from a plank or lying position. Good for conditioning and variety at higher levels.
- **This variation:** Swiss ball adds instability for core control (Paul Chek); keep loads modest.
- **Muscles:** Abs, hip flexors, shoulders
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Start in a strong plank. 2) Pull the knees or hips up with the abs. 3) Return with control.
- **Common faults:** Sagging plank; Using momentum; Shoulders drifting back.
- **Progress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or progress by:** Pike instead of tuck.
- **Regress to:** V Up (G3); Tuck Up (G3); TRX Pike (G3). **Or regress by:** Knee tuck, plank.
- **Same level swaps:** Swiss Ball Jackknife; Slider Pike
- **Cautions:** Low back, Osteoporosis/osteopenia, Pelvic floor. Lying V ups and tuck ups flex the spine: avoid for back pain and osteoporosis.
- **Default prescription:** 2 to 3 sets x 6 to 10 reps each side (or 20 to 40s), slow and controlled
- **Coach sources:** Boyle, Cosgrove

## Overhead March (KB)

`COR-044 | G2 | Carry: overhead / waiter | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Kettlebell
- **Why we use it:** Holding weight overhead while walking trains shoulder stability and core in one. Bottoms up holds make the rotator cuff work hard with light weight: brilliant for shoulder rehab.
- **Muscles:** Shoulder stability, rotator cuff, core
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Arm locked, biceps by the ear, shoulder packed. 2) Ribs down, walk slowly. 3) Keep the weight stacked over the shoulder.
- **Common faults:** Arching the back; Arm drifting forward; Going too heavy.
- **Progress to:** Bottoms Up KB Carry (G3); Overhead Carry (Double KB) (G3); Bottoms Up KB Carry Overhead (G3). **Or progress by:** Heavier, double, bottoms up.
- **Regress to:** Waiter's Carry (Light) (G1); Dead Bug (KB Pullover) (G1); Dead Bug (G1). **Or regress by:** Waiter's carry, lighter, static hold.
- **Same level swaps:** Bottoms Up KB Hold; Overhead Hold (KB); Waiter's Carry (KB)
- **Cautions:** Shoulder. Needs pain free overhead range. Waiter's carry (arm at 90 degrees) is an easier option.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 5 x 20 to 40m (or 30 to 45s), rest 60 to 90s
- **Coach sources:** Dan John, Cressey

## Bird Dog Hold

`COR-046 | G1 | Core: anti rotation / anti extension (bird dog) | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Bodyweight
- **Why we use it:** Part of the McGill Big 3. Reaching the opposite arm and leg while keeping the spine still trains the back extensors and anti rotation control with very low spinal load. A safe daily exercise for back pain and the foundation of Paul Chek's horse stance progressions.
- **This variation:** Isometric: builds strength and tendon tolerance in a fixed position with minimal joint irritation.
- **Muscles:** Spinal extensors, glutes, deep core, shoulder stabilisers
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Hands under shoulders, knees under hips, neutral spine. 2) Reach the opposite arm and leg long (not high), hold 8 to 10s. 3) Sweep back under without the hips rotating.
- **Common faults:** Lifting the leg too high and arching; Hips rotating; Rushing.
- **Progress to:** Crunch (G2); Sit Up (G2); Plank Saw (G2). **Or progress by:** Add a band, hold longer, bird dog row.
- **Regress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or regress by:** Arm only or leg only.
- **Same level swaps:** Bird Dog
- **Cautions:** None specific. Back pain friendly. Wrist pain: use fists.
- **Default prescription:** Descending pyramid 6, 4, 2 each side with 8 to 10s holds, or 2 to 3 sets x 6 to 10 reps each side (or 20 to 40s), slow and controlled
- **Coach sources:** McGill, Paul Chek, Squat University
- **Also listed in:** Rehab: Lower Back

## McGill Curl Up

`COR-048 | G1 | Core: McGill curl up | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Bodyweight
- **Why we use it:** Part of the McGill Big 3: trains the front abs while keeping the low back in neutral. Safer than sit ups and crunches for anyone with back history.
- **Muscles:** Rectus abdominis (without spinal flexion)
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Lie on your back, one knee bent, hands under the low back. 2) Brace and lift the head and shoulders slightly as one unit. 3) Hold 8 to 10s, lower.
- **Common faults:** Tucking the chin; Flattening the low back; Curling up too high.
- **Progress to:** Crunch (G2); Sit Up (G2); Plank Saw (G2). **Or progress by:** Raise elbows off the floor, longer holds.
- **Regress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or regress by:** Shorter holds.
- **Same level swaps:** McGill Big 3 (Curl Up, Side Plank, Bird Dog)
- **Cautions:** None specific. Back pain friendly. Part of the Big 3.
- **Default prescription:** Descending pyramid: 6, 4, 2 reps with 8 to 10s holds
- **Coach sources:** McGill, Squat University
- **Also listed in:** Rehab: Lower Back

## Side Bend (DB)

`COR-050 | G2 | Core: lateral flexion | STRONG | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Dumbbells (confirm)
- **Why we use it:** Side bends train the obliques through range. Suitcase holds/carries train the same muscles isometrically and are usually a better choice.
- **Muscles:** Obliques, QL
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Stand tall, weight in one hand. 2) Bend to the side slowly, then pull back up with the other side. 3) No twisting.
- **Common faults:** Twisting; Going heavy; Leaning forward.
- **Progress to:** V Up (G3); Tuck Up (G3); TRX Pike (G3). **Or progress by:** Heavier, cable.
- **Regress to:** Dead Bug (G1); Pelvic Tilt (G1); Bird Dog Hold (G1). **Or regress by:** Suitcase hold.
- **Same level swaps:** Cable Side Bend
- **Cautions:** None specific. Light only for back pain.
- **Default prescription:** 2 to 3 sets x 10 to 15 reps, tempo 2-1-1-1, rest 45 to 60s, RPE 8
- **Coach sources:** Poliquin

## Slider Body Saw

`COR-051 | G4 | Core: anti extension (rollout) | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Sliders (confirm)
- **Why we use it:** Rollouts and body saws are advanced anti extension: the further the arms reach, the harder the core works to stop the back arching.
- **This variation:** Sliders add a friction based eccentric control challenge.
- **Muscles:** Abs, lats, shoulders
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Kneeling or plank, ribs down, glutes tight. 2) Roll or slide out only as far as you can keep the back flat. 3) Pull back using the abs and lats.
- **Common faults:** Low back sagging; Hips piking first; Going too far too soon.
- **Progress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or progress by:** Longer range, from feet.
- **Regress to:** TRX Fallout (G3); TRX Body Saw (G3); Ab Wheel Rollout (Kneeling) (G3). **Or regress by:** Swiss ball rollout short range, plank.
- **Same level swaps:** Barbell Rollout; Swiss Ball Rollout
- **Cautions:** Low back. Can strain the low back if overreached. Shoulder pain: limit range.
- **Default prescription:** 2 to 3 sets x 6 to 10 reps each side (or 20 to 40s), slow and controlled
- **Coach sources:** McGill, Boyle, Cosgrove

## Cable Side Bend

`COR-052 | G2 | Core: lateral flexion | STRONG | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Cable machine
- **Why we use it:** Side bends train the obliques through range. Suitcase holds/carries train the same muscles isometrically and are usually a better choice.
- **This variation:** Cable: constant tension through the whole range with smooth, joint friendly resistance.
- **Muscles:** Obliques, QL
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Stand tall, weight in one hand. 2) Bend to the side slowly, then pull back up with the other side. 3) No twisting.
- **Common faults:** Twisting; Going heavy; Leaning forward.
- **Progress to:** V Up (G3); Tuck Up (G3); TRX Pike (G3). **Or progress by:** Heavier, cable.
- **Regress to:** Dead Bug (G1); Pelvic Tilt (G1); Bird Dog Hold (G1). **Or regress by:** Suitcase hold.
- **Same level swaps:** Side Bend (DB)
- **Cautions:** None specific. Light only for back pain.
- **Default prescription:** 2 to 3 sets x 10 to 15 reps, tempo 2-1-1-1, rest 45 to 60s, RPE 8
- **Coach sources:** Poliquin

## Slider Pike

`COR-053 | G4 | Core: dynamic flexion / pike | HYBRID, BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Sliders (confirm)
- **Why we use it:** Dynamic core exercises that pull the knees or hips up from a plank or lying position. Good for conditioning and variety at higher levels.
- **This variation:** Sliders add a friction based eccentric control challenge.
- **Muscles:** Abs, hip flexors, shoulders
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Start in a strong plank. 2) Pull the knees or hips up with the abs. 3) Return with control.
- **Common faults:** Sagging plank; Using momentum; Shoulders drifting back.
- **Progress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or progress by:** Pike instead of tuck.
- **Regress to:** V Up (G3); Tuck Up (G3); TRX Pike (G3). **Or regress by:** Knee tuck, plank.
- **Same level swaps:** Swiss Ball Pike; Swiss Ball Jackknife
- **Cautions:** Low back, Osteoporosis/osteopenia, Pelvic floor. Lying V ups and tuck ups flex the spine: avoid for back pain and osteoporosis.
- **Default prescription:** 2 to 3 sets x 6 to 10 reps each side (or 20 to 40s), slow and controlled
- **Coach sources:** Boyle, Cosgrove

## Copenhagen Side Plank

`COR-054 | G2 | Hip: adductor strength | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Bodyweight
- **Why we use it:** Copenhagen planks are among the best researched ways to prevent groin injury, and adductor strength supports knee and hip health. Ball squeezes are a gentle entry point.
- **Muscles:** Adductors (inner thigh), core
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Side plank with the top leg on a bench (inside of the knee for short lever, ankle for long lever). 2) Lift the hips into a straight line by squeezing the top leg down. 3) Hold or lift and lower.
- **Common faults:** Hips sagging; Rolling forward; Starting with the long lever.
- **Progress to:** Adductor Slide (Slider) (G3); Copenhagen Plank (Long Lever) (G3). **Or progress by:** Short → long lever, add leg raises.
- **Regress to:** Dead Bug (G1); Pelvic Tilt (G1); Bird Dog Hold (G1). **Or regress by:** Ball squeeze, side lying adduction.
- **Same level swaps:** Adductor Squeeze (Ball); Side Lying Hip Adduction; Standing Cable Hip Adduction
- **Cautions:** None specific. Short lever first. Groin pain: ball squeeze isometrics.
- **Default prescription:** 2 to 3 sets x 15 to 30s each side
- **Coach sources:** Research (groin injury prevention), Boyle

## Slider Mountain Climber

`COR-055 | G3 | Core / conditioning: mountain climbers | BURN, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Sliders (confirm)
- **Why we use it:** A plank with running legs. Good conditioning without jumping when done slowly; fast versions add impact through the wrists and shoulders.
- **This variation:** Sliders add a friction based eccentric control challenge.
- **Muscles:** Core, hip flexors, shoulders, cardio
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Strong plank, hands under shoulders. 2) Drive one knee towards the chest at a time. 3) Keep the hips level.
- **Common faults:** Hips bouncing high; Shoulders drifting behind the hands; Toe tapping without the knee driving.
- **Progress to:** Slider Pike (G4); Slider Body Saw (G4); Swiss Ball Pike (G4). **Or progress by:** Faster, sliders, cross body.
- **Regress to:** Mountain Climber (G2); Mountain Climbers (G2); Mountain Climber Sprints (G2). **Or regress by:** Hands on a bench, slow.
- **Cautions:** None specific. Wrist load. Slow and controlled versions are fine for groups; sprint versions are harder.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 6 x 20 to 30s
- **Coach sources:** DeFranco (Limber 11, slow), Cosgrove

## Pelvic Tilt

`COR-056 | G1 | Core: breathing and pelvic control | STRONG, HYBRID, BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Bodyweight
- **Why we use it:** Breathing is the foundation of bracing (Chek: breathing first). Crocodile and 90/90 breathing teach 360 degree breathing, calm the nervous system and help back pain and pelvic floor function.
- **Muscles:** Diaphragm, deep core, pelvic floor
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Lie in position, hands on the lower ribs. 2) Breathe in through the nose expanding 360 degrees (belly, sides, back). 3) Exhale slowly fully, feeling the ribs drop.
- **Common faults:** Chest and shoulder breathing; Arching the back; Rushing.
- **Progress to:** Crunch (G2); Sit Up (G2); Plank Saw (G2). **Or progress by:** Add movement (dead bug with breathing).
- **Regress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or regress by:** Shorter sets.
- **Same level swaps:** 90/90 Breathing; Pelvic Tilt (Supine); 4 Point TVA Draw In (Chek)
- **Cautions:** None specific. Universally safe. Great on RED readiness days.
- **Default prescription:** 5 to 10 slow breaths
- **Coach sources:** Paul Chek, McGill, Squat University
- **Also listed in:** Rehab: Lower Back

## TRX Fallout

`COR-057 | G3 | Core: anti extension (rollout) | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** TRX
- **Why we use it:** Rollouts and body saws are advanced anti extension: the further the arms reach, the harder the core works to stop the back arching.

- **Regress to:** Plank Saw (G2); RKC Plank (G2); Front Plank (G2). **Or regress by:** Swiss ball rollout short range, plank.
- **Same level swaps:** TRX Body Saw; Ab Wheel Rollout (Kneeling); Swiss Ball Rollout (Short Range)
- **Cautions:** Low back. Can strain the low back if overreached. Shoulder pain: limit range.
- **Default prescription:** 2 to 3 sets x 6 to 10 reps each side (or 20 to 40s), slow and controlled

## Single Leg Lowering

`COR-058 | G2 | Core: lower abs / hip flexors | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Bodyweight
- **Why we use it:** Lowering and raising the legs while keeping the low back down trains lower abdominal control. Hanging versions add grip and are advanced.
- **Muscles:** Abs, hip flexors
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Low back pressed down. 2) Lower the legs only as far as the back stays flat. 3) Exhale as you lift.
- **Common faults:** Back arching off the floor; Swinging; Rushing.
- **Progress to:** V Up (G3); Tuck Up (G3); TRX Pike (G3). **Or progress by:** Straighter legs, hanging.
- **Regress to:** Dead Bug (G1); Pelvic Tilt (G1); Bird Dog Hold (G1). **Or regress by:** Bent knee heel taps, dead bug.
- **Same level swaps:** Heel Taps; Flutter Kicks; Scissor Kicks
- **Cautions:** None specific. Back pain: keep the knees bent and range short. Hanging versions need healthy shoulders.
- **Default prescription:** 2 to 3 sets x 6 to 10 reps each side (or 20 to 40s), slow and controlled
- **Coach sources:** Boyle, Paul Chek

## TRX Pike

`COR-059 | G3 | Core: dynamic flexion / pike | HYBRID, BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** TRX
- **Why we use it:** Dynamic core exercises that pull the knees or hips up from a plank or lying position. Good for conditioning and variety at higher levels.
