- **Progress to:** Slider Pike (G4); Swiss Ball Pike (G4); Swiss Ball Jackknife (G4). **Or progress by:** Pike instead of tuck.
- **Regress to:** Crunch (G2); Sit Up (G2); Plank Saw (G2). **Or regress by:** Knee tuck, plank.
- **Same level swaps:** TRX Knee Tuck; V Up; Tuck Up
- **Cautions:** Low back, Osteoporosis/osteopenia, Pelvic floor. Lying V ups and tuck ups flex the spine: avoid for back pain and osteoporosis.

## Crunch on Swiss Ball

`COR-060 | G2 | Core: spinal flexion (crunch / sit up) | BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Swiss ball (confirm)
- **Why we use it:** Classic ab exercises. They work the abs but repeated loaded spinal flexion is not ideal for discs, so they are low priority at Optimal compared with anti movement work.
- **This variation:** Swiss ball adds instability for core control (Paul Chek); keep loads modest.
- **Muscles:** Abs
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Ribs towards the hips. 2) Exhale as you curl. 3) Control the lowering.
- **Common faults:** Pulling on the neck; Using momentum; High reps fast.
- **Progress to:** Swiss Ball Stir the Pot (G3); V Up (G3); Tuck Up (G3). **Or progress by:** Weighted, cable.
- **Regress to:** Dead Bug (G1); Pelvic Tilt (G1); Bird Dog Hold (G1). **Or regress by:** McGill curl up, dead bug.
- **Same level swaps:** Crunch; Sit Up; Reverse Crunch
- **Cautions:** Low back, Osteoporosis/osteopenia. AVOID for back pain, disc history and osteoporosis. Use McGill curl up instead.
- **Default prescription:** 2 to 3 sets x 10 to 15 reps, tempo 2-1-1-1, rest 45 to 60s, RPE 8
- **Coach sources:** McGill (caution), Boyle (anti movement preference)

# 12. LOADED CARRIES

*Grip, posture, trunk and shoulder stability*

**Grade ladder at a glance** (use this to slot every member into the same session at their level):

- **G1**: Farmer's Carry (DB), Farmer's Carry (KB), Farmer's Carry (Trap Bar), Fat Grip Farmer's Carry, Sled Push, Sled Pull (Rope), Sled Drag (Backwards), Sled Drag (Forwards Harness), Sled Lateral Drag, Sled Push (Low Handles), Sled Push (High Handles), Plate Drag (Bear Crawl), Farmer's Hold (Static), Farmer's Carry March, Farmer's Carry on Toes, Farmer's Carry Shuttle, Lateral Farmer's Carry, Backwards Farmer's Carry
- **G2**: Farmer's Carry Up and Down Step, Towel Grip Carry, Suitcase Carry (DB), Cross Body Carry, Suitcase Carry (KB), Offset Carry (Heavy and Light), Front Rack Carry (Single KB), Goblet Carry, Waiter's Carry (KB), Waiter's Carry (DB), Slam Ball Bear Hug Carry, Mixed Carry (Rack and Suitcase), Mixed Carry (Overhead and Suitcase), KB Bear Crawl Drag, Plate Pinch Carry, Plate Hug Carry, Suitcase Hold (Static), Trap Bar Hold (Static), Landmine Carry, Bottoms Up KB Hold, Suitcase Carry March, Plate Pinch Hold, Overhead Hold (KB), Farmer's Walk Lunge, Suitcase Lunge Carry, Front Rack Walking Lunge, Carry Medley (Farmer, Rack, Overhead), Duck Walk (KB Goblet), Farmer's Carry Step Over
- **G3**: Front Rack Carry (Double KB), Bottoms Up KB Carry, Overhead Carry (Double KB), Overhead Carry (Plate), Slam Ball Overhead Carry, Zercher Carry (Barbell), Barbell Overhead Carry, Dead Hang (Grip), Front Rack Hold (Double KB), Overhead Walking Lunge (KB), Single Arm Farmer's Carry Turn, Uneven Front Rack Carry
- **G4**: Single Arm Overhead Carry (DB)

✱ = not for group sessions (impact).

## Farmer's Carry (DB)

`CAR-001 | G1 | Carry: farmer's carry | STRONG, HYBRID, BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Dumbbells (confirm)
- **Why we use it:** Dan John says loaded carries change lives. Picking up heavy things and walking trains grip (a strong longevity predictor), posture, core and conditioning all at once, with low technical demand and low injury risk. Every member, every week.
- **Muscles:** Grip, traps, core, glutes, posture
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Deadlift the weights up properly. 2) Stand tall, shoulders down, walk with short controlled steps. 3) Breathe and keep the ribs down.
- **Common faults:** Shrugging; Leaning forward or side to side; Fast sloppy steps.
- **Progress to:** Suitcase Hold (G2); Suitcase March (G2); Suitcase Carry (G2). **Or progress by:** Heavier, longer, on the toes, with steps/obstacles; Dan John standard: bodyweight total for men.
- **Regress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or regress by:** Lighter, shorter, static hold.
- **Same level swaps:** Farmer's Carry; Farmer's Carry March; Farmer's Hold (Static)
- **Cautions:** None specific. Very safe. Pick up and put down with a good hinge. Grip limited members: straps are fine to train the rest.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 5 x 20 to 40m (or 30 to 45s), rest 60 to 90s
- **Coach sources:** Dan John, Attia (grip), Cosgrove

## Farmer's Carry Up and Down Step

`CAR-002 | G2 | Carry: complex / medley | HYBRID, BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Dumbbells (confirm), Kettlebell
- **Why we use it:** Combining positions, directions and obstacles adds variety and real world challenge.
- **Muscles:** Whole body, grip, core
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Change positions with control. 2) Stand tall through every position. 3) Short controlled steps.
- **Common faults:** Rushing transitions; Losing posture; Too heavy.
- **Progress to:** Uneven Front Rack Carry (G3); Single Arm Farmer's Carry Turn (G3); Bottoms Up KB Carry (G3). **Or progress by:** Heavier, longer.
- **Regress to:** Farmer's Carry March (G1); Farmer's Hold (Static) (G1); Farmer's Carry on Toes (G1). **Or regress by:** Lighter, single position.
- **Same level swaps:** Farmer's Carry Step Over; Mixed Carry (Rack and Suitcase); Mixed Carry (Overhead and Suitcase)
- **Cautions:** None specific. Generally safe.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 5 x 20 to 40m (or 30 to 45s), rest 60 to 90s
- **Coach sources:** Dan John, Gambetta

## Towel Grip Carry

`CAR-004 | G2 | Carry: grip strength | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Dumbbells (confirm), Kettlebell
- **Why we use it:** Grip strength is one of the strongest predictors of healthy ageing and all cause mortality (Attia). Easy to train at the end of sessions.
- **Muscles:** Forearms, hands, shoulders
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Crush the handle/plate. 2) Shoulders down and back. 3) Hold for time.
- **Common faults:** Shrugging; Holding the breath; Bent wrists.
- **Progress to:** Uneven Front Rack Carry (G3); Single Arm Farmer's Carry Turn (G3); Bottoms Up KB Carry (G3). **Or progress by:** Heavier, thicker grip, longer.
- **Regress to:** Farmer's Carry March (G1); Farmer's Hold (Static) (G1); Farmer's Carry on Toes (G1). **Or regress by:** Lighter, shorter.
- **Same level swaps:** Plate Pinch Hold; Plate Pinch Carry; Trap Bar Hold (Static)
- **Cautions:** None specific. Elbow pain: reduce load.
- **Default prescription:** 3 x 20 to 45s
- **Coach sources:** Attia, Dan John

## Suitcase Carry (DB)

`CAR-007 | G2 | Carry: suitcase / offset | STRONG, HYBRID, BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Dumbbells (confirm)
- **Why we use it:** One side loading turns a carry into an anti lateral flexion core exercise: you must stop the body leaning. McGill calls the suitcase carry one of the best core exercises.
- **This variation:** One sided loading adds an anti rotation / anti lateral flexion core challenge and exposes left/right differences.
- **Muscles:** Obliques, QL, grip, glute med
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Weight in one hand, stand tall, shoulders level. 2) Walk slowly without leaning towards or away from the weight. 3) Swap hands.
- **Common faults:** Leaning; Shrugging the loaded side; Rushing.
- **Progress to:** Uneven Front Rack Carry (G3); Single Arm Farmer's Carry Turn (G3); Dead Hang (Grip) (G3). **Or progress by:** Heavier, march with high knees, longer.
- **Regress to:** Farmer's Carry (G1); Farmer's Carry (DB) (G1); Farmer's Carry March (G1). **Or regress by:** Lighter, static hold.
- **Same level swaps:** Suitcase Hold; Suitcase March; Suitcase Carry
- **Cautions:** None specific. Back pain friendly.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 5 x 20 to 40m (or 30 to 45s), rest 60 to 90s each side
- **Coach sources:** McGill, Dan John

- **Common faults:** Leaning; Shrugging the loaded side; Rushing.
- **Progress to:** Uneven Front Rack Carry (G3); Single Arm Farmer's Carry Turn (G3); Bottoms Up KB Carry (G3). **Or progress by:** Heavier, march with high knees, longer.
- **Regress to:** Farmer's Carry (G1); Farmer's Carry March (G1); Farmer's Hold (Static) (G1). **Or regress by:** Lighter, static hold.
- **Same level swaps:** Suitcase Hold; Suitcase March; Suitcase Carry
- **Cautions:** None specific. Back pain friendly.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 5 x 20 to 40m (or 30 to 45s), rest 60 to 90s each side
- **Coach sources:** McGill, Dan John

## Front Rack Carry (Single KB)

`CAR-011 | G2 | Carry: front loaded | STRONG, HYBRID, BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Kettlebell
- **Why we use it:** Holding the weight in front forces the core to resist being pulled forward and the upper back to stay upright. Great posture and core work.
- **Muscles:** Core (anti extension), upper back, legs
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Weight tight to the chest. 2) Stand tall, ribs down, walk slowly. 3) Breathe behind the brace.
- **Common faults:** Leaning back to counterbalance; Holding the breath; Elbows drifting.
- **Progress to:** Offset Front Rack Carry (G3); Front Rack Hold (Double KB) (G3); Front Rack Carry (Double KB) (G3). **Or progress by:** Heavier, double KB, uneven.
- **Regress to:** Farmer's Carry (KB) (G1); Farmer's Carry March (G1); Farmer's Hold (Static) (G1). **Or regress by:** Lighter, goblet.
- **Same level swaps:** Goblet Carry; Duck Walk (KB Goblet); Landmine Carry
- **Cautions:** None specific. Generally safe. Duck walks are deep knee bending: knee pain caution.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 5 x 20 to 40m (or 30 to 45s), rest 60 to 90s
- **Coach sources:** Dan John, Cosgrove

## Sled Push

`CAR-012 | G1 | Carry / gait: sled push, pull and drag | BURN, HYBRID, STRONG | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Sled
- **Why we use it:** The sled is the most joint friendly strength and conditioning tool in the gym: concentric only, so almost no soreness, no impact and no technique to fail. Ben Patrick uses backward drags for knee health; DeFranco uses pushes for conditioning. Every member at every level can use it.
- **Muscles:** Quads, glutes, calves, whole body conditioning
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Push: arms extended or bent, body at 45 degrees, drive through the balls of the feet. 2) Drag backward: lean back, small steps, push through the front of the foot (knees over toes). 3) Keep steady steps and a neutral spine.
- **Common faults:** Hips too high or too low; Rounding the back; Taking huge steps that slow the sled.
- **Progress to:** Prowler Push (G3); Sled Sprint (Push) (G3); Sled Sprint (Pull) (G3). **Or progress by:** More weight, faster (sprints), longer distance, less rest.
- **Regress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or regress by:** Lighter, slower, shorter distance.
- **Same level swaps:** Sled Pull; Sled Row (Rope); Sled Pull (Rope)
- **Cautions:** None specific. Almost universally safe. Backward drag is a knee pain staple. Heavy pushes raise blood pressure: keep breathing.
- **Default prescription:** 6 to 10 x 15 to 25m, walk back recovery; or 3 to 5 min backward drag in warm up
- **Coach sources:** Ben Patrick (ATG), DeFranco, Boyle
- **Also listed in:** Conditioning

## Sled Drag (Backwards)

`CAR-016 | G1 | Knee: backward walking / sled | STRONG, HYBRID, BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Sled
- **Why we use it:** Ben Patrick's number one knee tool: walking backwards loads the quads with the knee travelling over the toes, floods the knee with blood and is nearly impossible to overdo.
- **Muscles:** Quads (VMO), knee tendons
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Lean back slightly against the sled (or hold the treadmill rails). 2) Small steps, push through the front of the foot. 3) Knees travel over the toes.
- **Common faults:** Big steps; Standing tall; Too heavy.
- **Progress to:** Goblet Carry (G2); Landmine Carry (G2); Plate Hug Carry (G2). **Or progress by:** Heavier, longer.
- **Regress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or regress by:** Lighter, treadmill flat.
- **Same level swaps:** Reverse Sled Drag; Sled Drag Backwards; Backwards Walking (Treadmill Incline)
- **Cautions:** None specific. Knee pain staple. Very safe.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 5 min warm up, or 4 to 6 x 20m
- **Coach sources:** Ben Patrick (ATG)

## Bottoms Up KB Carry

`CAR-017 | G3 | Carry: overhead / waiter | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Kettlebell
- **Why we use it:** Holding weight overhead while walking trains shoulder stability and core in one. Bottoms up holds make the rotator cuff work hard with light weight: brilliant for shoulder rehab.
- **This variation:** Bottoms up kettlebell forces the grip and rotator cuff to stabilise; a brilliant (light) shoulder rehab tool.
- **Muscles:** Shoulder stability, rotator cuff, core
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Arm locked, biceps by the ear, shoulder packed. 2) Ribs down, walk slowly. 3) Keep the weight stacked over the shoulder.
- **Common faults:** Arching the back; Arm drifting forward; Going too heavy.
- **Progress to:** Single Arm Overhead Carry (DB) (G4). **Or progress by:** Heavier, double, bottoms up.
- **Regress to:** Bottoms Up KB Hold (G2); Overhead Hold (KB) (G2); Overhead March (KB) (G2). **Or regress by:** Waiter's carry, lighter, static hold.
- **Same level swaps:** Overhead Carry (Double KB); Bottoms Up KB Carry Overhead; Overhead Carry (Plate)
- **Cautions:** Shoulder. Needs pain free overhead range. Waiter's carry (arm at 90 degrees) is an easier option.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 5 x 20 to 40m (or 30 to 45s), rest 60 to 90s
- **Coach sources:** Dan John, Cressey
- **Also listed in:** Rehab: Shoulder

## Slam Ball Bear Hug Carry

`CAR-025 | G2 | Core: quadruped (bear hold / crawl) | HYBRID, BURN, STRONG | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Slam ball (confirm)
- **Why we use it:** Bear holds and crawls train the core and shoulders together and build coordination (Gambetta, Chek). Getting down to and moving on the floor is also a longevity skill.
- **Muscles:** Core, shoulders, quads, coordination
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Hands under shoulders, knees under hips, knees hover 2 to 3cm. 2) Back flat, move opposite hand and foot together. 3) Small steps, keep the hips still.
- **Common faults:** Hips high; Back rounding; Moving too fast.
- **Progress to:** Slam Ball Overhead Carry (G3); Dead Hang (Grip) (G3); Bottoms Up KB Carry (G3). **Or progress by:** Longer, add drag/load, reverse and lateral.
- **Regress to:** Sled Push (G1); Sled Pull (Rope) (G1); Sled Lateral Drag (G1). **Or regress by:** Static bear hold, knees down.
- **Same level swaps:** Crab Walk; Bear Crawl; Lateral Bear Crawl
- **Cautions:** None specific. Wrist pain: use fists or DB handles.
- **Default prescription:** 3 x 20 to 40s or 10 to 20m
- **Coach sources:** Gambetta, Paul Chek

## Mixed Carry (Rack and Suitcase)

`CAR-026 | G2 | Carry: complex / medley | HYBRID, BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Dumbbells (confirm), Kettlebell
- **Why we use it:** Combining positions, directions and obstacles adds variety and real world challenge.
- **This variation:** One sided loading adds an anti rotation / anti lateral flexion core challenge and exposes left/right differences.
- **Muscles:** Whole body, grip, core
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Change positions with control. 2) Stand tall through every position. 3) Short controlled steps.
- **Common faults:** Rushing transitions; Losing posture; Too heavy.
- **Progress to:** Uneven Front Rack Carry (G3); Single Arm Farmer's Carry Turn (G3); Bottoms Up KB Carry (G3). **Or progress by:** Heavier, longer.
- **Regress to:** Farmer's Carry March (G1); Farmer's Hold (Static) (G1); Farmer's Carry on Toes (G1). **Or regress by:** Lighter, single position.
- **Same level swaps:** Farmer's Carry Step Over; Farmer's Carry Up and Down Step; Mixed Carry (Overhead and Suitcase)
- **Cautions:** None specific. Generally safe.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 5 x 20 to 40m (or 30 to 45s), rest 60 to 90s
- **Coach sources:** Dan John, Gambetta

## Plate Pinch Carry

`CAR-030 | G2 | Carry: grip strength | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Plate
- **Why we use it:** Grip strength is one of the strongest predictors of healthy ageing and all cause mortality (Attia). Easy to train at the end of sessions.
- **Muscles:** Forearms, hands, shoulders
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Crush the handle/plate. 2) Shoulders down and back. 3) Hold for time.
- **Common faults:** Shrugging; Holding the breath; Bent wrists.
- **Progress to:** Overhead Carry (Plate) (G3); Dead Hang (Grip) (G3); Bottoms Up KB Carry (G3). **Or progress by:** Heavier, thicker grip, longer.
- **Regress to:** Plate Drag (Bear Crawl) (G1); Sled Push (G1); Sled Pull (Rope) (G1). **Or regress by:** Lighter, shorter.
- **Same level swaps:** Plate Pinch Hold; Towel Grip Carry; Trap Bar Hold (Static)
- **Cautions:** None specific. Elbow pain: reduce load.
- **Default prescription:** 3 x 20 to 45s
- **Coach sources:** Attia, Dan John

## Plate Drag (Bear Crawl)

`CAR-031 | G1 | Carry / gait: sled push, pull and drag | BURN, HYBRID, STRONG | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Plate
- **Why we use it:** The sled is the most joint friendly strength and conditioning tool in the gym: concentric only, so almost no soreness, no impact and no technique to fail. Ben Patrick uses backward drags for knee health; DeFranco uses pushes for conditioning. Every member at every level can use it.
- **Muscles:** Quads, glutes, calves, whole body conditioning
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Push: arms extended or bent, body at 45 degrees, drive through the balls of the feet. 2) Drag backward: lean back, small steps, push through the front of the foot (knees over toes). 3) Keep steady steps and a neutral spine.
- **Common faults:** Hips too high or too low; Rounding the back; Taking huge steps that slow the sled.
- **Progress to:** Prowler Push (G3); Sled Sprint (Push) (G3); Sled Sprint (Pull) (G3). **Or progress by:** More weight, faster (sprints), longer distance, less rest.
- **Regress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or regress by:** Lighter, slower, shorter distance.
- **Same level swaps:** Sled Push; Sled Pull; Sled Row (Rope)
- **Cautions:** None specific. Almost universally safe. Backward drag is a knee pain staple. Heavy pushes raise blood pressure: keep breathing.
- **Default prescription:** 6 to 10 x 15 to 25m, walk back recovery; or 3 to 5 min backward drag in warm up
- **Coach sources:** Ben Patrick (ATG), DeFranco, Boyle

## Plate Hug Carry

`CAR-032 | G2 | Carry: front loaded | STRONG, HYBRID, BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Plate
- **Why we use it:** Holding the weight in front forces the core to resist being pulled forward and the upper back to stay upright. Great posture and core work.
- **Muscles:** Core (anti extension), upper back, legs
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Weight tight to the chest. 2) Stand tall, ribs down, walk slowly. 3) Breathe behind the brace.
- **Common faults:** Leaning back to counterbalance; Holding the breath; Elbows drifting.
- **Progress to:** Offset Front Rack Carry (G3); Zercher Carry (Barbell) (G3); Front Rack Hold (Double KB) (G3). **Or progress by:** Heavier, double KB, uneven.
- **Regress to:** Plate Drag (Bear Crawl) (G1); Sled Push (G1); Sled Pull (Rope) (G1). **Or regress by:** Lighter, goblet.
- **Same level swaps:** Goblet Carry; Landmine Carry; Duck Walk (KB Goblet)
- **Cautions:** None specific. Generally safe. Duck walks are deep knee bending: knee pain caution.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 5 x 20 to 40m (or 30 to 45s), rest 60 to 90s
- **Coach sources:** Dan John, Cosgrove

## Farmer's Hold (Static)

`CAR-033 | G1 | Carry: farmer's carry | STRONG, HYBRID, BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Dumbbells (confirm), Kettlebell
- **Why we use it:** Dan John says loaded carries change lives. Picking up heavy things and walking trains grip (a strong longevity predictor), posture, core and conditioning all at once, with low technical demand and low injury risk. Every member, every week.
- **Muscles:** Grip, traps, core, glutes, posture
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Deadlift the weights up properly. 2) Stand tall, shoulders down, walk with short controlled steps. 3) Breathe and keep the ribs down.
- **Common faults:** Shrugging; Leaning forward or side to side; Fast sloppy steps.
- **Progress to:** Suitcase Hold (G2); Suitcase March (G2); Suitcase Carry (G2). **Or progress by:** Heavier, longer, on the toes, with steps/obstacles; Dan John standard: bodyweight total for men.
- **Regress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or regress by:** Lighter, shorter, static hold.
- **Same level swaps:** Farmer's Carry; Farmer's Carry March; Farmer's Carry on Toes
- **Cautions:** None specific. Very safe. Pick up and put down with a good hinge. Grip limited members: straps are fine to train the rest.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 5 x 20 to 40m (or 30 to 45s), rest 60 to 90s
- **Coach sources:** Dan John, Attia (grip), Cosgrove

## Suitcase Hold (Static)

`CAR-035 | G2 | Carry: suitcase / offset | STRONG, HYBRID, BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Dumbbells (confirm), Kettlebell
- **Why we use it:** One side loading turns a carry into an anti lateral flexion core exercise: you must stop the body leaning. McGill calls the suitcase carry one of the best core exercises.
- **This variation:** One sided loading adds an anti rotation / anti lateral flexion core challenge and exposes left/right differences.
- **Muscles:** Obliques, QL, grip, glute med
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Weight in one hand, stand tall, shoulders level. 2) Walk slowly without leaning towards or away from the weight. 3) Swap hands.
- **Common faults:** Leaning; Shrugging the loaded side; Rushing.
- **Progress to:** Uneven Front Rack Carry (G3); Single Arm Farmer's Carry Turn (G3); Bottoms Up KB Carry (G3). **Or progress by:** Heavier, march with high knees, longer.
- **Regress to:** Farmer's Carry (G1); Farmer's Carry March (G1); Farmer's Hold (Static) (G1). **Or regress by:** Lighter, static hold.
- **Same level swaps:** Suitcase Hold; Suitcase March; Suitcase Carry
- **Cautions:** None specific. Back pain friendly.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 5 x 20 to 40m (or 30 to 45s), rest 60 to 90s each side
- **Coach sources:** McGill, Dan John

## Barbell Overhead Carry

`CAR-036 | G3 | Carry: overhead / waiter | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Barbell
- **Why we use it:** Holding weight overhead while walking trains shoulder stability and core in one. Bottoms up holds make the rotator cuff work hard with light weight: brilliant for shoulder rehab.
- **This variation:** Barbell: allows the heaviest loading for maximum strength and bone stimulus; earn it with technique (usually G3 to G4, Teams).
- **Muscles:** Shoulder stability, rotator cuff, core
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Arm locked, biceps by the ear, shoulder packed. 2) Ribs down, walk slowly. 3) Keep the weight stacked over the shoulder.
- **Common faults:** Arching the back; Arm drifting forward; Going too heavy.
- **Progress to:** Single Arm Overhead Carry (DB) (G4). **Or progress by:** Heavier, double, bottoms up.
- **Regress to:** Overhead Hold (DB) (G2); Bottoms Up KB Hold (G2); Overhead Hold (KB) (G2). **Or regress by:** Waiter's carry, lighter, static hold.
- **Same level swaps:** Bottoms Up KB Carry; Overhead Carry (Plate); Slam Ball Overhead Carry
- **Cautions:** Shoulder. Needs pain free overhead range. Waiter's carry (arm at 90 degrees) is an easier option.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 5 x 20 to 40m (or 30 to 45s), rest 60 to 90s
- **Coach sources:** Dan John, Cressey

## Trap Bar Hold (Static)

`CAR-037 | G2 | Carry: grip strength | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Trap bar (confirm)
- **Why we use it:** Grip strength is one of the strongest predictors of healthy ageing and all cause mortality (Attia). Easy to train at the end of sessions.
- **Muscles:** Forearms, hands, shoulders
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Crush the handle/plate. 2) Shoulders down and back. 3) Hold for time.
- **Common faults:** Shrugging; Holding the breath; Bent wrists.
- **Progress to:** Dead Hang (Grip) (G3); Bottoms Up KB Carry (G3); Overhead Carry (Plate) (G3). **Or progress by:** Heavier, thicker grip, longer.
- **Regress to:** Farmer's Carry (Trap Bar) (G1); Sled Push (G1); Sled Pull (Rope) (G1). **Or regress by:** Lighter, shorter.
- **Same level swaps:** Towel Grip Carry; Plate Pinch Hold; Plate Pinch Carry
- **Cautions:** None specific. Elbow pain: reduce load.
- **Default prescription:** 3 x 20 to 45s
- **Coach sources:** Attia, Dan John

## Dead Hang (Grip)

`CAR-039 | G3 | Vertical pull: pull up / chin up / hangs | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Rig / pull up bar
- **Why we use it:** The ultimate upper body bodyweight strength test. Hangs build grip (a strong predictor of longevity) and decompress the spine; negatives and isometrics build strength for the first pull up. LIFTMOR used jumping chin ups with drop landings for bone.
- **Muscles:** Lats, upper back, biceps, grip, core
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Grip slightly wider than shoulders (chin up: palms facing you). 2) Pull the shoulder blades down first, then drive the elbows to the ribs. 3) Chin over the bar, lower slowly to straight arms.
- **Common faults:** Kipping or swinging; Half reps; Shrugging at the bottom.
- **Progress to:** Weighted Pull Up (G4); Weighted Chin Up (G4); Commando Pull Up (G4). **Or progress by:** Band assisted → negatives → bodyweight → weighted.
- **Regress to:** Hanging (Supported) (G2); TRX Assisted Pull Up (G2); Band Assisted Pull Up (G2). **Or regress by:** Lat pulldown, TRX assisted pull up, scapula pull up, dead hang.
- **Same level swaps:** Pull Up; Chin Up; Dead Hang
- **Cautions:** Shoulder. Shoulder pain: neutral grip, band assistance. Hanging can irritate some shoulders: build up gradually.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8 or total reps
- **Coach sources:** DeFranco, Dan John, Attia (grip), Boyle

## Farmer's Walk Lunge

`CAR-046 | G2 | Single leg: forward / walking lunge | BURN, HYBRID, STRONG | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Bodyweight
- **Why we use it:** Forward and walking lunges add deceleration and balance: you have to control the body moving forward over the front leg. Very functional and very metabolic, so they suit BURN and HYBRID sessions. Loaded carry lunges add grip and core.
- **Muscles:** Quads, glutes, hamstrings, balance, grip when loaded
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Long step forward, land heel first. 2) Drop the back knee down, front knee over the middle of the foot. 3) Push through the front foot and step through to the next rep.
- **Common faults:** Short choppy steps that load the front knee; Front knee caving; Torso collapsing forward.
- **Progress to:** Barbell Walking Lunge (G3); Overhead Walking Lunge (KB) (G3); Overhead Walking Lunge (Plate) (G3). **Or progress by:** Add load (DB, KB rack, overhead), pulses, longer distance.
- **Regress to:** Split Squat (Supported) (G1); Split Squat (Bodyweight) (G1); TRX Assisted Split Squat (G1). **Or regress by:** Reverse lunge, split squat, hand support.
- **Same level swaps:** TRX Lunge; Lunge Pulses; Forward Lunge (DB)
- **Cautions:** Knee. More knee stress than reverse lunges. Swap to reverse lunges or split squats with knee pain. Needs space in groups.
- **Default prescription:** 3 sets x 8 to 12 reps, tempo 3-0-1-1, rest 60 to 90s, RPE 7 to 9 (each leg) or 20 to 30m
- **Coach sources:** Gambetta (lunge matrix), Cosgrove, Paul Chek (lunge pattern)

- **Cautions:** Knee. More knee stress than reverse lunges. Swap to reverse lunges or split squats with knee pain. Needs space in groups.
- **Default prescription:** 3 sets x 8 to 12 reps, tempo 3-0-1-1, rest 60 to 90s, RPE 7 to 9 (each leg) or 20 to 30m
- **Coach sources:** Gambetta (lunge matrix), Cosgrove, Paul Chek (lunge pattern)

## Carry Medley (Farmer, Rack, Overhead)

`CAR-051 | G2 | Carry: complex / medley | HYBRID, BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Dumbbells (confirm), Kettlebell
- **Why we use it:** Combining positions, directions and obstacles adds variety and real world challenge.
- **Muscles:** Whole body, grip, core
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Change positions with control. 2) Stand tall through every position. 3) Short controlled steps.
- **Common faults:** Rushing transitions; Losing posture; Too heavy.
- **Progress to:** Uneven Front Rack Carry (G3); Single Arm Farmer's Carry Turn (G3); Bottoms Up KB Carry (G3). **Or progress by:** Heavier, longer.
- **Regress to:** Farmer's Carry March (G1); Farmer's Hold (Static) (G1); Farmer's Carry on Toes (G1). **Or regress by:** Lighter, single position.
- **Same level swaps:** Farmer's Carry Step Over; Farmer's Carry Up and Down Step; Mixed Carry (Rack and Suitcase)
- **Cautions:** Shoulder. Generally safe.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 5 x 20 to 40m (or 30 to 45s), rest 60 to 90s
- **Coach sources:** Dan John, Gambetta

## Overhead Walking Lunge (KB)

`CAR-052 | G3 | Single leg: forward / walking lunge | BURN, HYBRID, STRONG | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Kettlebell
- **Why we use it:** Forward and walking lunges add deceleration and balance: you have to control the body moving forward over the front leg. Very functional and very metabolic, so they suit BURN and HYBRID sessions. Loaded carry lunges add grip and core.
- **Muscles:** Quads, glutes, hamstrings, balance, grip when loaded
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Long step forward, land heel first. 2) Drop the back knee down, front knee over the middle of the foot. 3) Push through the front foot and step through to the next rep.
- **Common faults:** Short choppy steps that load the front knee; Front knee caving; Torso collapsing forward.
- **Progress to:** Single Arm Overhead Carry (DB) (G4). **Or progress by:** Add load (DB, KB rack, overhead), pulses, longer distance.
- **Regress to:** Suitcase Lunge Carry (G2); Walking Lunge Front Rack (KB) (G2); TRX Lunge (G2). **Or regress by:** Reverse lunge, split squat, hand support.
- **Same level swaps:** Barbell Walking Lunge; Overhead Walking Lunge (Plate)
- **Cautions:** Knee, Shoulder. More knee stress than reverse lunges. Swap to reverse lunges or split squats with knee pain. Needs space in groups.
- **Default prescription:** 3 sets x 8 to 12 reps, tempo 3-0-1-1, rest 60 to 90s, RPE 7 to 9 (each leg) or 20 to 30m
- **Coach sources:** Gambetta (lunge matrix), Cosgrove, Paul Chek (lunge pattern)

`CAR-053 | G3 | Carry: complex / medley | HYBRID, BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Dumbbells (confirm), Kettlebell
- **Why we use it:** Combining positions, directions and obstacles adds variety and real world challenge.
- **This variation:** One sided loading adds an anti rotation / anti lateral flexion core challenge and exposes left/right differences.
- **Muscles:** Whole body, grip, core
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Change positions with control. 2) Stand tall through every position. 3) Short controlled steps.
- **Common faults:** Rushing transitions; Losing posture; Too heavy.
- **Progress to:** Single Arm Overhead Carry (DB) (G4). **Or progress by:** Heavier, longer.
- **Regress to:** Farmer's Carry Step Over (G2); Farmer's Carry Up and Down Step (G2); Mixed Carry (Rack and Suitcase) (G2). **Or regress by:** Lighter, single position.
- **Cautions:** None specific. Generally safe.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 5 x 20 to 40m (or 30 to 45s), rest 60 to 90s
- **Coach sources:** Dan John, Gambetta

## Lateral Farmer's Carry

`CAR-054 | G1 | Carry: farmer's carry | STRONG, HYBRID, BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Dumbbells (confirm), Kettlebell
- **Why we use it:** Dan John says loaded carries change lives. Picking up heavy things and walking trains grip (a strong longevity predictor), posture, core and conditioning all at once, with low technical demand and low injury risk. Every member, every week.
- **Muscles:** Grip, traps, core, glutes, posture
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Deadlift the weights up properly. 2) Stand tall, shoulders down, walk with short controlled steps. 3) Breathe and keep the ribs down.
- **Common faults:** Shrugging; Leaning forward or side to side; Fast sloppy steps.
- **Progress to:** Suitcase Hold (G2); Suitcase March (G2); Suitcase Carry (G2). **Or progress by:** Heavier, longer, on the toes, with steps/obstacles; Dan John standard: bodyweight total for men.
- **Regress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or regress by:** Lighter, shorter, static hold.
- **Same level swaps:** Farmer's Carry; Farmer's Carry March; Farmer's Hold (Static)
- **Cautions:** None specific. Very safe. Pick up and put down with a good hinge. Grip limited members: straps are fine to train the rest.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 5 x 20 to 40m (or 30 to 45s), rest 60 to 90s
- **Coach sources:** Dan John, Attia (grip), Cosgrove

## Duck Walk (KB Goblet)

`CAR-055 | G2 | Carry: front loaded | STRONG, HYBRID, BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Kettlebell
- **Why we use it:** Holding the weight in front forces the core to resist being pulled forward and the upper back to stay upright. Great posture and core work.
- **Muscles:** Core (anti extension), upper back, legs
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Weight tight to the chest. 2) Stand tall, ribs down, walk slowly. 3) Breathe behind the brace.
- **Common faults:** Leaning back to counterbalance; Holding the breath; Elbows drifting.
- **Progress to:** Offset Front Rack Carry (G3); Front Rack Hold (Double KB) (G3); Front Rack Carry (Double KB) (G3). **Or progress by:** Heavier, double KB, uneven.
- **Regress to:** Farmer's Carry (KB) (G1); Farmer's Carry March (G1); Farmer's Hold (Static) (G1). **Or regress by:** Lighter, goblet.
- **Same level swaps:** Goblet Carry; Front Rack Carry (Single KB); Landmine Carry
- **Cautions:** Knee. Generally safe. Duck walks are deep knee bending: knee pain caution.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 5 x 20 to 40m (or 30 to 45s), rest 60 to 90s
- **Coach sources:** Dan John, Cosgrove

## Uneven Front Rack Carry

`CAR-057 | G3 | Carry: suitcase / offset | STRONG, HYBRID, BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Dumbbells (confirm), Kettlebell
- **Why we use it:** One side loading turns a carry into an anti lateral flexion core exercise: you must stop the body leaning. McGill calls the suitcase carry one of the best core exercises.
- **This variation:** One sided loading adds an anti rotation / anti lateral flexion core challenge and exposes left/right differences.
- **Muscles:** Obliques, QL, grip, glute med
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Weight in one hand, stand tall, shoulders level. 2) Walk slowly without leaning towards or away from the weight. 3) Swap hands.
- **Common faults:** Leaning; Shrugging the loaded side; Rushing.
- **Progress to:** Single Arm Overhead Carry (DB) (G4). **Or progress by:** Heavier, march with high knees, longer.
- **Regress to:** Suitcase Hold (G2); Suitcase March (G2); Suitcase Carry (G2). **Or regress by:** Lighter, static hold.
- **Cautions:** None specific. Back pain friendly.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 5 x 20 to 40m (or 30 to 45s), rest 60 to 90s each side
- **Coach sources:** McGill, Dan John

## Farmer's Carry Step Over

`CAR-058 | G2 | Carry: complex / medley | HYBRID, BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Dumbbells (confirm), Kettlebell

## Single Arm Overhead Carry (DB)

`CAR-059 | G4 | Carry: overhead / waiter | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Dumbbells (confirm)
- **Why we use it:** Holding weight overhead while walking trains shoulder stability and core in one. Bottoms up holds make the rotator cuff work hard with light weight: brilliant for shoulder rehab.
- **This variation:** One sided loading adds an anti rotation / anti lateral flexion core challenge and exposes left/right differences.
- **Muscles:** Shoulder stability, rotator cuff, core
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Arm locked, biceps by the ear, shoulder packed. 2) Ribs down, walk slowly. 3) Keep the weight stacked over the shoulder.
- **Common faults:** Arching the back; Arm drifting forward; Going too heavy.
- **Progress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or progress by:** Heavier, double, bottoms up.
- **Regress to:** Bottoms Up KB Carry (G3); Overhead Carry (Plate) (G3); Barbell Overhead Carry (G3). **Or regress by:** Waiter's carry, lighter, static hold.
- **Cautions:** Shoulder. Needs pain free overhead range. Waiter's carry (arm at 90 degrees) is an easier option.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 5 x 20 to 40m (or 30 to 45s), rest 60 to 90s
- **Coach sources:** Dan John, Cressey

# 13. POWER AND PLYOMETRICS

*Jumps, throws, explosive lifts*

**Grade ladder at a glance** (use this to slot every member into the same session at their level):

- **G2**: Snap Downs, Drop Squat, Step Down from Box, Med Ball Chest Pass, Med Ball Overhead Throw, Med Ball Slam, Slam Ball Slam, Med Ball Rotational Throw, Med Ball Scoop Throw, Med Ball Backwards Throw, Med Ball Wall Ball, Skipping (Rope) ✱, Explosive Band Row, Mountain Climber Sprints, KB Swing (Power)
- **G3**: Pogo Hops ✱, Hang Power Clean, Power Clean, Squat Jump ✱, Hang Power Snatch, Squat Jump and Stick ✱, Barbell Push Press, Box Jump ✱, Box Jump (Seated Start) ✱, DB Snatch, DB Clean, Broad Jump ✱, DB Hang Clean, Broad Jump and Stick ✱, Landmine Clean, Tuck Jump ✱, Landmine Squat to Press (Power), Split Squat Jump ✱, Single Leg Hop ✱, Single Leg Hop and Stick ✱, Lateral Bound ✱, Hurdle Hops ✱, Line Hops (Forwards and Back) ✱, Depth Drop ✱, Depth Jump ✱, A Skip ✱, Sled Sprint (Push), Power Skip ✱, Sled Sprint (Pull), Bounding ✱, Prowler Push, Trap Bar Jump ✱, Sprint Start (Falling Start) ✱, DB Squat Jump ✱, Kneeling Jump ✱, KB Snatch, Seated Box Jump ✱, KB Clean, Hip Thrust Jump (Banded) ✱
- **G4**: Double KB Clean, Barbell Push Jerk ✱, Alternating Lunge Jump ✱, Single Leg Box Jump ✱, Plyo Press Up ✱, Clap Press Up ✱

✱ = not for group sessions (impact).

## Pogo Hops

`PWR-001 | G3 | Power: jumps, hops and landings (plyometric) | HYBRID | Group: No | Impact: high | Teams only: Yes | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Bodyweight
- **Why we use it:** Jumps and hops train power, tendon stiffness and bone (impact is a key bone stimulus in LIFTMOR). Landings (snap downs, drop squats, jump and stick) teach the body to absorb force, the foundation of injury prevention. Progress carefully: landing before jumping, low before high, two legs before one.
- **Muscles:** Whole lower body, tendons, nervous system
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Land softly and quietly, hips back, knees over toes. 2) Stick the landing for a second before the next rep. 3) Quality over quantity: stop when height or control drops.
- **Common faults:** Landing stiff legged or with knees caving; Too many reps (plyos are not cardio); Progressing too fast.
- **Progress to:** Single Leg Box Jump (G4); Alternating Lunge Jump (G4). **Or progress by:** Landings → small jumps → box jumps → broad jumps → single leg hops → depth jumps.
- **Regress to:** Snap Downs (G2); Drop Squat (G2); Pogo Hops (Low) (G2). **Or regress by:** Snap downs/drop squat and stick, step ups, sled push, med ball throws.
- **Same level swaps:** A Skip; Box Jump; Bounding
- **Cautions:** Knee, Low back, Osteoporosis/osteopenia, Pelvic floor. IMPACT: excluded from Optimal GROUP sessions (no jumping rule). Teams only after screening. Avoid with pelvic floor symptoms, osteoporosis with fracture history, joint replacements, acute knee/Achilles pain.
- **Group swap:** Group swap (no jumping): sled push, fast step ups, med ball chest pass or slam, KB swing, fast sit to stand
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 5 sets x 3 to 6 reps, full recovery (60 to 120s), stop when speed drops; 2 to 3 sessions/week max, low total contacts (20 to 60)
- **Coach sources:** Gambetta, DeFranco (dynamic effort), LIFTMOR research (impact for bone)

## Double KB Clean

`PWR-002 | G4 | Power: Olympic lift / derivative | HYBRID, STRONG | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Kettlebell
- **Why we use it:** Explosive triple extension (ankles, knees, hips) trains power and rate of force development. Power declines faster than strength with age, so it must be trained, but the skill demand is high. DB, KB and landmine versions are far easier to learn and safer for groups than barbell versions.
- **This variation:** Double KB: heavier total load plus a front rack or bilateral grip demand.
- **Muscles:** Whole body: glutes, quads, hamstrings, traps, shoulders
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Start in a strong hinge with the weight close. 2) Explode up through the legs and hips, shrug and pull the elbows high. 3) Catch softly in a strong rack position (or overhead), stand tall.
- **Common faults:** Pulling early with the arms; Weight swinging away from the body; Catching with the back arched.
- **Progress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or progress by:** Pull → hang version → from the floor; DB → KB → barbell.
- **Regress to:** KB Clean (G3); KB Snatch (G3); KB High Pull (G3). **Or regress by:** Pull only (no catch), KB swing, med ball scoop toss, landmine clean.
- **Same level swaps:** KB High Pull (Single Arm); Barbell Push Jerk; Clean Pull (Barbell)
- **Cautions:** Low back, Osteoporosis/osteopenia, Shoulder. Wrists, shoulders and low back need to be healthy. Barbell versions: Teams G4 only. Not for osteoporosis without careful progression.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 5 sets x 3 to 6 reps, full recovery (60 to 120s), stop when speed drops
- **Coach sources:** DeFranco, Cosgrove (power block), Gambetta

## Barbell Push Jerk

`PWR-011 | G4 | Power: Olympic lift / derivative | HYBRID, STRONG | Group: No | Impact: none | Teams only: Yes | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Barbell
- **Why we use it:** Explosive triple extension (ankles, knees, hips) trains power and rate of force development. Power declines faster than strength with age, so it must be trained, but the skill demand is high. DB, KB and landmine versions are far easier to learn and safer for groups than barbell versions.
- **This variation:** Barbell: allows the heaviest loading for maximum strength and bone stimulus; earn it with technique (usually G3 to G4, Teams).
- **Muscles:** Whole body: glutes, quads, hamstrings, traps, shoulders
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Start in a strong hinge with the weight close. 2) Explode up through the legs and hips, shrug and pull the elbows high. 3) Catch softly in a strong rack position (or overhead), stand tall.
- **Common faults:** Pulling early with the arms; Weight swinging away from the body; Catching with the back arched.
- **Progress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or progress by:** Pull → hang version → from the floor; DB → KB → barbell.
- **Regress to:** Power Clean (G3); Hang Clean Pull (G3); Hang Power Clean (G3). **Or regress by:** Pull only (no catch), KB swing, med ball scoop toss, landmine clean.
- **Same level swaps:** Clean Pull (Barbell); Double KB Clean; KB High Pull (Single Arm)
- **Cautions:** Low back, Osteoporosis/osteopenia, Shoulder. Wrists, shoulders and low back need to be healthy. Barbell versions: Teams G4 only. Not for osteoporosis without careful progression.
- **Group swap:** Teams only (heavy or high skill): in groups use a G3 regression from the Regress to list
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 5 sets x 3 to 6 reps, full recovery (60 to 120s), stop when speed drops
- **Coach sources:** DeFranco, Cosgrove (power block), Gambetta

## Step Down from Box

`PWR-014 | G2 | Single leg: eccentric step down | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: low | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Box / bench / step
- **Why we use it:** Controlled lowering from a step builds knee control and eccentric quad strength, the exact quality needed for walking downstairs. Also a key screening test for knee valgus and hip control.
- **Muscles:** Quads, glutes, hip stabilisers
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Stand on a box, other leg hanging off the front or side. 2) Lower slowly by bending the standing knee, hips back slightly. 3) Tap the heel lightly and return without pushing off the floor.
- **Common faults:** Knee diving in; Hip dropping on the free side; Crashing down to the floor.
- **Progress to:** Pistol Squat (G3); Skater Squat (G3); Shrimp Squat (G3). **Or progress by:** Higher box, hold weight, slower lowering.
- **Regress to:** Patrick Step (G1); Poliquin Step Up (G1); Petersen Step Up (G1). **Or regress by:** Lower box, hand support, Poliquin step up.
- **Same level swaps:** Low Box Step Down; Lateral Step Down; Forward Step Down
- **Cautions:** None specific. Excellent for knee rehab when the box is low. Raise the height as control improves.
- **Default prescription:** 2 to 3 sets x 8 to 12 each leg, 3s lowering
- **Coach sources:** Squat University, Poliquin, Boyle

## Landmine Squat to Press (Power)

`PWR-021 | G3 | Squat + vertical push (combination) | BURN, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Landmine (confirm)
- **Why we use it:** Links a squat and an overhead press into one total body movement. Very metabolic, great for BURN and HYBRID sessions, and the legs help drive the weight overhead so people can press more.
- **This variation:** Landmine: the arc path is shoulder and back friendly and very easy to learn. Combination move: trains two qualities at once, efficient for HYBRID and BURN; keep technique of both parts clean before speeding up. Fast/power version: move with intent, stop when speed drops.
- **Muscles:** Quads, glutes, shoulders, triceps, core
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Squat with the weight in the rack. 2) Drive up hard and use that momentum to press overhead. 3) Lock out with biceps by the ears, ribs down, then lower back to the rack.
- **Common faults:** Pressing before the legs finish the drive; Arching the low back at the top; Losing the rack position and squatting with the elbows dropped.
- **Progress to:** Barbell Thruster (G4); Double KB Front Squat to Press (G4); Barbell Front Rack Squat to Press (G4). **Or progress by:** Add load, double KBs, barbell, more rounds or density.
- **Regress to:** Med Ball Slam (G2); Slam Ball Slam (G2); KB Swing (Power) (G2). **Or regress by:** Goblet squat to press, landmine squat to press, split into separate squat and press.
- **Same level swaps:** Landmine Squat to Press; DB Thruster; KB Thruster
- **Cautions:** Shoulder. Needs pain free overhead range. With shoulder pain swap to squat to landmine press. Watch technique as fatigue builds in circuits.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 4 sets x 8 to 12 reps, or 30 to 40s in circuits
- **Coach sources:** Cosgrove (MRT), DeFranco

## Med Ball Chest Pass

`PWR-023 | G2 | Power: medicine ball throws and slams | HYBRID, BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Med ball / wall ball
- **Why we use it:** Med ball throws are the safest way to train power for 40+ members: no catching heavy loads, no landing impact, and you can throw as hard as possible. Rotational throws (scoop toss, shot put) are THE golf power exercise (Gambetta, Chek). Wall balls combine a squat with a throw for conditioning.
- **Muscles:** Whole body power, rotational core (rotational throws), shoulders
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Load the hips (or rotate back through the hips for rotational throws). 2) Explode from the ground up: legs, hips, then arms. 3) Throw with intent every rep, reset between reps.
- **Common faults:** Throwing with arms only; Rounding the back on slams; Doing so many reps that it becomes slow cardio.
- **Progress to:** DB Clean (G3); KB Clean (G3); DB Snatch (G3). **Or progress by:** Heavier ball, more distance/speed, step into the throw, single leg stance.
- **Regress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or regress by:** Lighter ball, half kneeling throw, slower controlled chops.
- **Same level swaps:** Wall Balls; Med Ball Slam; Med Ball Side Slam
- **Cautions:** None specific. Low impact and joint friendly. Use a soft ball for slams. Rotational throws: avoid with acute back pain. Wall balls need shoulder overhead range.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 5 sets x 3 to 6 reps, full recovery (60 to 120s), stop when speed drops (each side for rotational)
- **Coach sources:** Gambetta, Cosgrove (power block), Paul Chek (twist)

- **Common faults:** Throwing with arms only; Rounding the back on slams; Doing so many reps that it becomes slow cardio.
- **Progress to:** DB Clean (G3); KB Clean (G3); DB Snatch (G3). **Or progress by:** Heavier ball, more distance/speed, step into the throw, single leg stance.
- **Regress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or regress by:** Lighter ball, half kneeling throw, slower controlled chops.
- **Same level swaps:** Wall Balls; Med Ball Slam; Med Ball Side Slam
- **Cautions:** Shoulder. Low impact and joint friendly. Use a soft ball for slams. Rotational throws: avoid with acute back pain. Wall balls need shoulder overhead range.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 5 sets x 3 to 6 reps, full recovery (60 to 120s), stop when speed drops (each side for rotational)
- **Coach sources:** Gambetta, Cosgrove (power block), Paul Chek (twist)

## Clap Press Up

`PWR-038 | G4 | Power: upper body plyometric | HYBRID | Group: No | Impact: high | Teams only: Yes | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Bodyweight
- **Why we use it:** Explosive push ups train upper body power. Advanced and higher joint stress, so Teams only for members with healthy wrists and shoulders.
- **Muscles:** Chest, shoulders, triceps
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Lower under control, push explosively so the hands leave the floor. 2) Land softly with bent elbows. 3) Reset each rep.
- **Common faults:** Sagging hips; Landing on locked elbows; Doing them fatigued.
- **Progress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or progress by:** Higher, then clap.
- **Regress to:** DB Clean (G3); KB Clean (G3); DB Snatch (G3). **Or regress by:** Incline plyo push up, med ball chest pass.
- **Same level swaps:** Plyo Press Up
- **Cautions:** Pelvic floor, Shoulder. Wrist and shoulder stress. Not for groups or anyone with shoulder pain. Med ball chest pass is the safer option.
- **Group swap:** Group swap: med ball chest pass or explosive band press
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 5 sets x 3 to 6 reps, full recovery (60 to 120s), stop when speed drops
- **Coach sources:** DeFranco, Gambetta

## Explosive Band Row

`PWR-040 | G2 | Horizontal pull: row | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Resistance band (confirm)
- **Why we use it:** Rows build the upper back that holds posture upright and balances pressing. Chest supported rows remove the low back from the equation; single arm rows allow heavier loading and fix imbalances; bent over rows add hinge endurance. Aim for about 2 pulls for every push in desk based members.
- **Muscles:** Upper back, lats, rear shoulders, biceps, grip
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Brace, shoulder blade pulls first, then the elbow. 2) Row towards the hip (lats) or lower ribs (upper back). 3) Pause, lower slowly to a full stretch.
- **Common faults:** Jerking and twisting the torso; Shrugging; Shortening the range.
- **Progress to:** Single Arm DB Row (G3); Single Arm KB Row (G3); Seal Row (Barbell) (G3). **Or progress by:** Heavier, pause at the top, tempo, single arm, 1.5 reps.
- **Regress to:** Chest Supported DB Row (G1); Chest Supported DB Row (Neutral) (G1). **Or regress by:** Chest supported row, cable row, TRX row.
- **Same level swaps:** Band Row; Kroc Row; Pendlay Row
- **Cautions:** None specific. Chest supported and cable versions are the most back friendly. Bent over versions load the low back: avoid pairing with RDLs for 40+.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8
- **Coach sources:** DeFranco, Cressey, Poliquin, Boyle

## Sled Sprint (Push)

`PWR-042 | G3 | Carry / gait: sled push, pull and drag | BURN, HYBRID, STRONG | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Sled
- **Why we use it:** The sled is the most joint friendly strength and conditioning tool in the gym: concentric only, so almost no soreness, no impact and no technique to fail. Ben Patrick uses backward drags for knee health; DeFranco uses pushes for conditioning. Every member at every level can use it.
- **This variation:** Fast/power version: move with intent, stop when speed drops.
- **Muscles:** Quads, glutes, calves, whole body conditioning
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Push: arms extended or bent, body at 45 degrees, drive through the balls of the feet. 2) Drag backward: lean back, small steps, push through the front of the foot (knees over toes). 3) Keep steady steps and a neutral spine.
- **Common faults:** Hips too high or too low; Rounding the back; Taking huge steps that slow the sled.
- **Progress to:** Double KB Clean (G4); Barbell Push Jerk (G4). **Or progress by:** More weight, faster (sprints), longer distance, less rest.
- **Regress to:** Sled Push (G1); Sled Pull (G1); Sled Row (Rope) (G1). **Or regress by:** Lighter, slower, shorter distance.
- **Same level swaps:** Prowler Push; Sled Sprint (Pull)
- **Cautions:** None specific. Almost universally safe. Backward drag is a knee pain staple. Heavy pushes raise blood pressure: keep breathing.
- **Default prescription:** 6 to 10 x 15 to 25m, walk back recovery; or 3 to 5 min backward drag in warm up
- **Coach sources:** Ben Patrick (ATG), DeFranco, Boyle

`PWR-043 | G3 | Power: jumps, hops and landings (plyometric) | HYBRID | Group: No | Impact: high | Teams only: Yes | Seniors: Check`

## Mountain Climber Sprints

`PWR-050 | G2 | Core / conditioning: mountain climbers | BURN, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Bodyweight
- **Why we use it:** A plank with running legs. Good conditioning without jumping when done slowly; fast versions add impact through the wrists and shoulders.
- **This variation:** Fast/power version: move with intent, stop when speed drops.
- **Muscles:** Core, hip flexors, shoulders, cardio
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Strong plank, hands under shoulders. 2) Drive one knee towards the chest at a time. 3) Keep the hips level.
- **Common faults:** Hips bouncing high; Shoulders drifting behind the hands; Toe tapping without the knee driving.
- **Progress to:** DB Clean (G3); KB Clean (G3); DB Snatch (G3). **Or progress by:** Faster, sliders, cross body.
- **Regress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or regress by:** Hands on a bench, slow.
- **Same level swaps:** Mountain Climber; Mountain Climbers
- **Cautions:** None specific. Wrist load. Slow and controlled versions are fine for groups; sprint versions are harder.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 6 x 20 to 30s
- **Coach sources:** DeFranco (Limber 11, slow), Cosgrove

## KB Swing (Power)

`PWR-051 | G2 | Hinge: ballistic (power) | BURN, HYBRID, STRONG | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Kettlebell
- **Why we use it:** The king of hinge conditioning (Dan John, Pavel). Trains explosive hip extension (power) and heart rate at the same time with no impact on the knees. Excellent for fat loss, posture and glute strength. Dead stop versions teach control; single arm versions add anti rotation.
- **This variation:** Fast/power version: move with intent, stop when speed drops.
- **Muscles:** Glutes, hamstrings, core, grip, cardiovascular system
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Hike the bell back high between the thighs. 2) Snap the hips forward, squeeze the glutes, let the bell float to chest height. 3) Let it fall, hinge late, keep the spine neutral.
- **Common faults:** Squatting the swing instead of hinging; Lifting with the arms; Leaning back at the top.
- **Progress to:** Double KB Swing (G3); Single Arm KB Swing (G3); Single Arm KB Swing to Catch (G3). **Or progress by:** Heavier bell, single arm, alternating, swings EMOM, heavier with fewer reps for power.
- **Regress to:** KB Deadlift (G1); Sumo KB Deadlift (G1); Elevated KB Deadlift (G1). **Or regress by:** KB deadlift, dead stop swing, lighter bell, cable pull through.
- **Same level swaps:** KB Swings; American KB Swing; KB Dead Stop Swing
- **Cautions:** Low back. Back friendly when the hinge is good. Teach the KB deadlift first. Not for acute low back pain. American (overhead) swings stress shoulders and low back: use hip height swings instead.
- **Default prescription:** 4 to 10 sets x 10 to 20 reps, or EMOM; 'hike, snap, float'
- **Coach sources:** Dan John, Pavel Tsatsouline, Cosgrove

## KB Snatch

`PWR-053 | G3 | Power: Olympic lift / derivative | HYBRID, STRONG | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Kettlebell
- **Why we use it:** Explosive triple extension (ankles, knees, hips) trains power and rate of force development. Power declines faster than strength with age, so it must be trained, but the skill demand is high. DB, KB and landmine versions are far easier to learn and safer for groups than barbell versions.
- **Muscles:** Whole body: glutes, quads, hamstrings, traps, shoulders
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Start in a strong hinge with the weight close. 2) Explode up through the legs and hips, shrug and pull the elbows high. 3) Catch softly in a strong rack position (or overhead), stand tall.
- **Common faults:** Pulling early with the arms; Weight swinging away from the body; Catching with the back arched.
- **Progress to:** Double KB Clean (G4); KB High Pull (Single Arm) (G4); Barbell Push Jerk (G4). **Or progress by:** Pull → hang version → from the floor; DB → KB → barbell.
- **Regress to:** KB Swing (Power) (G2); Med Ball Slam (G2); Slam Ball Slam (G2). **Or regress by:** Pull only (no catch), KB swing, med ball scoop toss, landmine clean.
- **Same level swaps:** KB Clean; KB High Pull; KB Clean and Press
- **Cautions:** Low back, Osteoporosis/osteopenia, Shoulder. Wrists, shoulders and low back need to be healthy. Barbell versions: Teams G4 only. Not for osteoporosis without careful progression.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 5 sets x 3 to 6 reps, full recovery (60 to 120s), stop when speed drops
- **Coach sources:** DeFranco, Cosgrove (power block), Gambetta
- **Also listed in:** Conditioning

# 14. CONDITIONING

*Engine, finishers, intervals*

**Grade ladder at a glance** (use this to slot every member into the same session at their level):

- **G1**: Assault Bike Sprint, Assault Bike Steady State, Bike Erg Intervals, Rower Intervals, Rower 500m, Rower Steady State, Ski Erg Intervals, Ski Erg 250m, Treadmill Incline Walk, Sled Push, Sled Pull, Farmer's Carry Shuttle, Sled Drag Backwards, Shadow Boxing, Partner Rower Relay, Tabata Bike, Rower and Ski Ladder, Sled Push and Bike Couplet
- **G2**: Mountain Climbers, Jumping Jacks ✱, Star Jumps ✱, Skipping ✱, Double Unders ✱, Bear Crawl, Crab Walk, Box Step Ups (Fast), Battle Rope Alternating Waves, Battle Rope Double Waves, Battle Rope Slams, Battle Rope Jumping Jacks ✱, Slam Ball Slams, Plank Jacks, Wall Balls, KB Swings, TRX Row (Fast Tempo), KB Complex, DB Complex, EMOM (Mixed), AMRAP Circuit, Every Minute Carry and Swing
- **G3**: Sprawls ✱, High Knees ✱, Butt Kicks ✱, Treadmill Sprint ✱, Shuttle Runs ✱, Jump Squats ✱, Lunge Jumps ✱, Skater Jumps ✱, Tuck Jumps ✱, Devil's Press ✱, TRX Squat Jump ✱, KB Snatch, KB Clean and Press, Bike and Burpee Ladder ✱, Barbell Complex, Man Makers ✱, DB Thrusters, Burpees ✱, Burpee Over Bar ✱, Burpee Box Jump Over ✱

✱ = not for group sessions (impact).

## Assault Bike Sprint

`CON-001 | G1 | Conditioning: erg / walking | BURN, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Assault bike / bike
- **Why we use it:** The bike, rower and ski erg give big conditioning with no impact, and every level can work at their own intensity. Zone 2 builds the aerobic base (Attia); short sprints suit menopause and fat loss (Sims, Cosgrove hierarchy). Backward walking (treadmill or sled) is Ben Patrick's knee warm up.
- **This variation:** Fast/power version: move with intent, stop when speed drops.
- **Muscles:** Heart and lungs, legs (bike/rower), upper body (ski/rower)
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Bike: push and pull with arms and legs, steady cadence. 2) Rower: legs, body, arms; then arms, body, legs. 3) Ski: hinge and pull down, drive the hips.

- **Progress to:** Crab Walk (G2); KB Swings (G2); Bear Crawl (G2). **Or progress by:** Longer work, shorter rest, higher watts/calories, more rounds.
- **Regress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or regress by:** Easier pace, shorter intervals, more rest.
- **Same level swaps:** Tabata Bike; Bike (Easy); Bike Erg Intervals
- **Cautions:** None specific. Low impact. Rower and ski: watch low back flexion. Treadmill sprints involve impact.

## Sprawls

`CON-002 | G3 | Conditioning: total body (burpee family) | BURN, HYBRID | Group: No | Impact: high | Teams only: Yes | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Bodyweight
- **Why we use it:** Ground to standing conditioning drills. Huge metabolic demand, but the jump and drop to the floor add impact and wrist/shoulder stress.
- **Muscles:** Whole body
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Hands down, step or jump back to plank. 2) Chest down (if required), back to feet. 3) Stand tall (jump only if allowed).
- **Common faults:** Sagging plank; Crashing to the floor; Sloppy as fatigue builds.
- **Progress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or progress by:** Add a press, push up or jump.
- **Regress to:** Crab Walk (G2); KB Swings (G2); Bear Crawl (G2). **Or regress by:** Step back burpee, incline burpee onto a bench.
- **Same level swaps:** Step Back Burpee (No Jump); Squat Thrust to Bench (No Jump); Burpees
- **Cautions:** Low back, Osteoporosis/osteopenia, Pelvic floor. IMPACT when jumping: group sessions use the no jump version (step back, step in, stand). Devil's press and man makers: DB hinge skill required.
- **Group swap:** Group swap: step back burpee (no jump), squat thrust to a bench, wall ball
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 6 x 20 to 40s
- **Coach sources:** Cosgrove (metabolic)

## Mountain Climbers

`CON-004 | G2 | Core / conditioning: mountain climbers | BURN, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Bodyweight
- **Why we use it:** A plank with running legs. Good conditioning without jumping when done slowly; fast versions add impact through the wrists and shoulders.
- **Muscles:** Core, hip flexors, shoulders, cardio
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Strong plank, hands under shoulders. 2) Drive one knee towards the chest at a time. 3) Keep the hips level.
- **Common faults:** Hips bouncing high; Shoulders drifting behind the hands; Toe tapping without the knee driving.
- **Progress to:** KB Snatch (G3); DB Thrusters (G3); Barbell Complex (G3). **Or progress by:** Faster, sliders, cross body.
- **Regress to:** Sled Push (G1); Sled Pull (G1); Rower 500m (G1). **Or regress by:** Hands on a bench, slow.
- **Same level swaps:** Mountain Climber; Mountain Climber Sprints
- **Cautions:** None specific. Wrist load. Slow and controlled versions are fine for groups; sprint versions are harder.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 6 x 20 to 30s
- **Coach sources:** DeFranco (Limber 11, slow), Cosgrove

## Crab Walk

`CON-019 | G2 | Core: quadruped (bear hold / crawl) | HYBRID, BURN, STRONG | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Bodyweight
- **Why we use it:** Bear holds and crawls train the core and shoulders together and build coordination (Gambetta, Chek). Getting down to and moving on the floor is also a longevity skill.
- **Muscles:** Core, shoulders, quads, coordination
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Hands under shoulders, knees under hips, knees hover 2 to 3cm. 2) Back flat, move opposite hand and foot together. 3) Small steps, keep the hips still.
- **Common faults:** Hips high; Back rounding; Moving too fast.
- **Progress to:** KB Snatch (G3); DB Thrusters (G3); Barbell Complex (G3). **Or progress by:** Longer, add drag/load, reverse and lateral.
- **Regress to:** Sled Push (G1); Sled Pull (G1); Rower 500m (G1). **Or regress by:** Static bear hold, knees down.
- **Same level swaps:** Bear Crawl; Lateral Bear Crawl; KB Bear Crawl Drag
- **Cautions:** None specific. Wrist pain: use fists or DB handles.
- **Default prescription:** 3 x 20 to 40s or 10 to 20m
- **Coach sources:** Gambetta, Paul Chek

**Sled Push** (G1): full entry under Loaded Carries, ID CAR-012.

## Sled Pull

`CON-021 | G1 | Carry / gait: sled push, pull and drag | BURN, HYBRID, STRONG | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Sled
- **Why we use it:** The sled is the most joint friendly strength and conditioning tool in the gym: concentric only, so almost no soreness, no impact and no technique to fail. Ben Patrick uses backward drags for knee health; DeFranco uses pushes for conditioning. Every member at every level can use it.
- **Muscles:** Quads, glutes, calves, whole body conditioning
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Push: arms extended or bent, body at 45 degrees, drive through the balls of the feet. 2) Drag backward: lean back, small steps, push through the front of the foot (knees over toes). 3) Keep steady steps and a neutral spine.
- **Common faults:** Hips too high or too low; Rounding the back; Taking huge steps that slow the sled.
- **Progress to:** Prowler Push (G3); Sled Sprint (Push) (G3); Sled Sprint (Pull) (G3). **Or progress by:** More weight, faster (sprints), longer distance, less rest.
- **Regress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or regress by:** Lighter, slower, shorter distance.
- **Same level swaps:** Sled Push; Sled Row (Rope); Sled Pull (Rope)
- **Cautions:** None specific. Almost universally safe. Backward drag is a knee pain staple. Heavy pushes raise blood pressure: keep breathing.
- **Default prescription:** 6 to 10 x 15 to 25m, walk back recovery; or 3 to 5 min backward drag in warm up
- **Coach sources:** Ben Patrick (ATG), DeFranco, Boyle

**Farmer's Carry Shuttle** (G1): full entry under Loaded Carries, ID CAR-049.

## Sled Drag Backwards

`CON-022 | G1 | Knee: backward walking / sled | STRONG, HYBRID, BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Sled
- **Why we use it:** Ben Patrick's number one knee tool: walking backwards loads the quads with the knee travelling over the toes, floods the knee with blood and is nearly impossible to overdo.
- **Muscles:** Quads (VMO), knee tendons
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Lean back slightly against the sled (or hold the treadmill rails). 2) Small steps, push through the front of the foot. 3) Knees travel over the toes.
- **Common faults:** Big steps; Standing tall; Too heavy.
- **Progress to:** Crab Walk (G2); KB Swings (G2); Bear Crawl (G2). **Or progress by:** Heavier, longer.
- **Regress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or regress by:** Lighter, treadmill flat.
- **Same level swaps:** Reverse Sled Drag; Sled Drag (Backwards); Backwards Walking (Treadmill Incline)
- **Cautions:** None specific. Knee pain staple. Very safe.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 5 min warm up, or 4 to 6 x 20m
- **Coach sources:** Ben Patrick (ATG)

## Box Step Ups (Fast)

`CON-023 | G2 | Single leg: step up | STRONG, HYBRID, BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Box / bench / step
- **Why we use it:** A real life movement (stairs, kerbs, climbing). Very back friendly, easy to scale by box height, and the concentric emphasis means little soreness. Knee drive and crossover versions add balance and hip work.
- **This variation:** Fast/power version: move with intent, stop when speed drops.
- **Muscles:** Quads, glutes, hamstrings, balance
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Whole foot on the box, knee over the middle of the foot. 2) Lean forward slightly and drive through the box leg to stand tall. 3) Step down with control, don't push off the bottom leg.
- **Common faults:** Pushing off the floor leg; Knee caving as you stand; Box too high so the hip hikes.
- **Progress to:** Barbell Step Up (G3); Step Up to Single Leg RDL (G3). **Or progress by:** Higher box, add DBs/goblet/barbell, add a knee drive, slower lowering.
- **Regress to:** Patrick Step (G1); Poliquin Step Up (G1); Petersen Step Up (G1). **Or regress by:** Lower box, hand support, bodyweight.
- **Same level swaps:** DB Step Up; Goblet Step Up; Lateral Step Up
- **Cautions:** None specific. Knee friendly at lower heights. Use a low box and hand support for seniors and knee pain. Faster 'step ups' in BURN keep impact low.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8 (each leg)
- **Coach sources:** Boyle, Cosgrove, Gambetta

## Battle Rope Alternating Waves

`CON-024 | G2 | Conditioning: battle ropes | BURN, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Battle ropes (confirm)
- **Why we use it:** Upper body conditioning with no impact. Great in BURN circuits and for members who can't run or jump.
- **Muscles:** Shoulders, arms, core, cardio
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Athletic stance, brace. 2) Drive the waves from the shoulders and hips. 3) Keep a steady rhythm.
- **Common faults:** Standing upright and stiff; Shrugging; Waves dying out.
- **Progress to:** KB Snatch (G3); DB Thrusters (G3); Barbell Complex (G3). **Or progress by:** Longer, faster, heavier rope.
- **Regress to:** Sled Push (G1); Sled Pull (G1); Rower 500m (G1). **Or regress by:** Shorter intervals, kneeling.
- **Same level swaps:** Battle Rope Slams; Battle Rope Rainbows; Battle Rope Double Waves
- **Cautions:** None specific. Low impact. Rope jumping jacks involve jumping: swap to step jacks in groups.
- **Default prescription:** 6 to 10 x 20 to 30s / 30 to 60s rest
- **Coach sources:** Cosgrove (metabolic)

## Jump Squats

`CON-025 | G3 | Power: jumps, hops and landings (plyometric) | HYBRID | Group: No | Impact: high | Teams only: Yes | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Bodyweight
- **Why we use it:** Jumps and hops train power, tendon stiffness and bone (impact is a key bone stimulus in LIFTMOR). Landings (snap downs, drop squats, jump and stick) teach the body to absorb force, the foundation of injury prevention. Progress carefully: landing before jumping, low before high, two legs before one.
- **Muscles:** Whole lower body, tendons, nervous system
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Land softly and quietly, hips back, knees over toes. 2) Stick the landing for a second before the next rep. 3) Quality over quantity: stop when height or control drops.
- **Common faults:** Landing stiff legged or with knees caving; Too many reps (plyos are not cardio); Progressing too fast.
- **Progress to:** Single Leg Box Jump (G4); Alternating Lunge Jump (G4). **Or progress by:** Landings → small jumps → box jumps → broad jumps → single leg hops → depth jumps.
- **Regress to:** Snap Downs (G2); Drop Squat (G2); Pogo Hops (Low) (G2). **Or regress by:** Snap downs/drop squat and stick, step ups, sled push, med ball throws.
- **Same level swaps:** A Skip; Box Jump; Bounding
- **Cautions:** Knee, Low back, Osteoporosis/osteopenia, Pelvic floor. IMPACT: excluded from Optimal GROUP sessions (no jumping rule). Teams only after screening. Avoid with pelvic floor symptoms, osteoporosis with fracture history, joint replacements, acute knee/Achilles pain.
- **Group swap:** Group swap (no jumping): sled push, fast step ups, med ball chest pass or slam, KB swing, fast sit to stand
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 5 sets x 3 to 6 reps, full recovery (60 to 120s), stop when speed drops; 2 to 3 sessions/week max, low total contacts (20 to 60)
- **Coach sources:** Gambetta, DeFranco (dynamic effort), LIFTMOR research (impact for bone)

## Slam Ball Slams

`CON-031 | G2 | Power: medicine ball throws and slams | HYBRID, BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Slam ball (confirm)
- **Why we use it:** Med ball throws are the safest way to train power for 40+ members: no catching heavy loads, no landing impact, and you can throw as hard as possible. Rotational throws (scoop toss, shot put) are THE golf power exercise (Gambetta, Chek). Wall balls combine a squat with a throw for conditioning.
- **Muscles:** Whole body power, rotational core (rotational throws), shoulders
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Load the hips (or rotate back through the hips for rotational throws). 2) Explode from the ground up: legs, hips, then arms. 3) Throw with intent every rep, reset between reps.
- **Common faults:** Throwing with arms only; Rounding the back on slams; Doing so many reps that it becomes slow cardio.
- **Progress to:** DB Clean (G3); KB Clean (G3); DB Snatch (G3). **Or progress by:** Heavier ball, more distance/speed, step into the throw, single leg stance.
- **Regress to:** Sled Push (G1); Sled Pull (G1); Rower 500m (G1). **Or regress by:** Lighter ball, half kneeling throw, slower controlled chops.
- **Same level swaps:** Med Ball Slam; Slam Ball Slam; Med Ball Side Slam
- **Cautions:** None specific. Low impact and joint friendly. Use a soft ball for slams. Rotational throws: avoid with acute back pain. Wall balls need shoulder overhead range.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 5 sets x 3 to 6 reps, full recovery (60 to 120s), stop when speed drops (each side for rotational)
- **Coach sources:** Gambetta, Cosgrove (power block), Paul Chek (twist)

**Plank Jacks** (G2): full entry under Core, ID COR-025.

## Devil's Press

`CON-033 | G3 | Conditioning: total body (burpee family) | BURN, HYBRID | Group: No | Impact: high | Teams only: Yes | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Bodyweight
- **Why we use it:** Ground to standing conditioning drills. Huge metabolic demand, but the jump and drop to the floor add impact and wrist/shoulder stress.
- **Muscles:** Whole body
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Hands down, step or jump back to plank. 2) Chest down (if required), back to feet. 3) Stand tall (jump only if allowed).
- **Common faults:** Sagging plank; Crashing to the floor; Sloppy as fatigue builds.
- **Progress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or progress by:** Add a press, push up or jump.
- **Regress to:** Crab Walk (G2); KB Swings (G2); Bear Crawl (G2). **Or regress by:** Step back burpee, incline burpee onto a bench.
- **Same level swaps:** Step Back Burpee (No Jump); Squat Thrust to Bench (No Jump); Sprawls
- **Cautions:** Low back, Osteoporosis/osteopenia, Pelvic floor. IMPACT when jumping: group sessions use the no jump version (step back, step in, stand). Devil's press and man makers: DB hinge skill required.
- **Group swap:** Group swap: step back burpee (no jump), squat thrust to a bench, wall ball
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 6 x 20 to 40s
- **Coach sources:** Cosgrove (metabolic)

## KB Swings

`CON-034 | G2 | Hinge: ballistic (power) | BURN, HYBRID, STRONG | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Kettlebell
- **Why we use it:** The king of hinge conditioning (Dan John, Pavel). Trains explosive hip extension (power) and heart rate at the same time with no impact on the knees. Excellent for fat loss, posture and glute strength. Dead stop versions teach control; single arm versions add anti rotation.
- **Muscles:** Glutes, hamstrings, core, grip, cardiovascular system
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Hike the bell back high between the thighs. 2) Snap the hips forward, squeeze the glutes, let the bell float to chest height. 3) Let it fall, hinge late, keep the spine neutral.
- **Common faults:** Squatting the swing instead of hinging; Lifting with the arms; Leaning back at the top.
- **Progress to:** Double KB Swing (G3); Single Arm KB Swing (G3); Single Arm KB Swing to Catch (G3). **Or progress by:** Heavier bell, single arm, alternating, swings EMOM, heavier with fewer reps for power.
- **Regress to:** KB Deadlift (G1); Sumo KB Deadlift (G1); Elevated KB Deadlift (G1). **Or regress by:** KB deadlift, dead stop swing, lighter bell, cable pull through.
- **Same level swaps:** KB Swing (Power); American KB Swing; KB Dead Stop Swing
- **Cautions:** Low back. Back friendly when the hinge is good. Teach the KB deadlift first. Not for acute low back pain. American (overhead) swings stress shoulders and low back: use hip height swings instead.
- **Default prescription:** 4 to 10 sets x 10 to 20 reps, or EMOM; 'hike, snap, float'
- **Coach sources:** Dan John, Pavel Tsatsouline, Cosgrove

## TRX Row (Fast Tempo)

`CON-036 | G2 | Horizontal pull: inverted / suspension row | STRONG, HYBRID, BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** TRX
- **Why we use it:** Pulling your own bodyweight in a plank position. The angle sets the difficulty, so it scales from total beginner (standing upright) to advanced (feet elevated) in the same station. A core Optimal group exercise and part of Ed's screening (TRX row at 45 degrees).
- **This variation:** Tempo version: a slow 3 to 5 second lowering builds control, tendon strength and muscle at lighter loads (Poliquin), ideal for joint sensitive members. Fast/power version: move with intent, stop when speed drops.
- **Muscles:** Upper back, lats, rear shoulders, biceps, core
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Body in a straight line, heels down. 2) Pull the chest to the handles, shoulder blades back and down. 3) Lower slowly to straight arms.
- **Common faults:** Hips sagging; Shrugging or poking the chin forward; Half reps.
- **Progress to:** Single Arm TRX Row (G3); TRX Row (Feet Elevated) (G3); Band Resisted Inverted Row (G3). **Or progress by:** Walk the feet forward (more horizontal), feet elevated, single arm, pause/tempo.
- **Regress to:** Chest Supported DB Row (G1); Chest Supported DB Row (Neutral) (G1). **Or regress by:** Stand more upright, step back, scapular retraction only (G1 of the Optimal screen).
- **Same level swaps:** TRX Row; Isometric Row Hold (TRX); Inverted Row to Pull Up Progression
- **Cautions:** None specific. Shoulder friendly. Neutral grip TRX handles are easiest on elbows.
- **Default prescription:** 3 sets x 8 to 15 reps (or total reps progression), pause at the top
- **Coach sources:** Cosgrove, Boyle, Dan John

**KB Clean and Press** (G3): full entry under Vertical Push, ID VPU-059.

## Shadow Boxing

`CON-037 | G1 | Conditioning: shadow boxing | BURN, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Bodyweight
