## Scorpion (Prone)

`MOB-017 | G1 | Mobility: spinal / back care | STRONG, HYBRID, BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Bodyweight
- **Why we use it:** Gentle spinal mobility for back care and warm ups. Extension drills (prone lying, McKenzie press ups) often ease disc type back pain; flexion drills (knee to chest, child's pose) often ease stiffness and stenosis type pain. Find the direction that helps the individual (McGill: find the pain triggers) and use it.
- **Muscles:** Spine, hips
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Move slowly through comfortable range. 2) Breathe out into the end range. 3) Stop if symptoms travel down a leg.
- **Common faults:** Forcing range; Holding the breath; Bouncing.
- **Progress to:** Bear Crawl (G2); Quadruped Thoracic Rotation (G2); Spiderman Lunge with Rotation (G2). **Or progress by:** Bigger range, add breathing holds.
- **Regress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or regress by:** Smaller range.
- **Same level swaps:** Cat Cow; Child's Pose; Supine Twist
- **Cautions:** None specific. Generally very safe. Osteoporosis: avoid repeated or loaded spinal flexion. Pain spreading into a leg: stop and refer.
- **Default prescription:** 1 to 2 sets x 5 to 10 slow reps (or 30 to 60s), in warm up or cool down
- **Coach sources:** McGill, Squat University, McKenzie method (physio)

## Shin Box Get Up

`MOB-020 | G1 | Hip: rotation mobility | STRONG, HYBRID, BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Kettlebell, Box / bench / step
- **Why we use it:** Hip internal and external rotation are often the first ranges lost with age and are critical for the golf swing, squat depth and low back health (joint by joint).
- **Muscles:** Hip rotators, capsule
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Sit tall in 90/90 or lie in position. 2) Rotate through the hips, keep the chest tall. 3) Move slowly, hold the end range.
- **Common faults:** Rounding the back; Forcing; Using hands to cheat.
- **Progress to:** Bear Crawl (G2); Quadruped Thoracic Rotation (G2); Spiderman Lunge with Rotation (G2). **Or progress by:** Hands free, hip lifts, longer holds.
- **Regress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or regress by:** Hands support.
- **Same level swaps:** Shin Box; 90/90 Hip Lift; 90/90 Hip Switch
- **Cautions:** None specific. Hip pain: reduce range.
- **Default prescription:** 1 to 2 sets x 5 to 10 slow reps (or 30 to 60s), in warm up or cool down
- **Coach sources:** Squat University, Gambetta (golf)

## Mini Band Lateral Walk

`MOB-021 | G1 | Hip: abduction / glute med | STRONG, HYBRID, BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Mini band (confirm)
- **Why we use it:** The side glutes stop the knee caving and the pelvis dropping when on one leg. Weak glute meds are linked to knee pain, hip pain and back pain. Simple band work fixes it and works brilliantly as a warm up (Squat University, Boyle).
- **This variation:** The mini band cues the knees out and switches on the glute med.
- **Muscles:** Glute medius and minimus, hip stabilisers
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Athletic stance, band around the knees or ankles. 2) Push the knees out, step sideways (or lift the leg) leading with the heel. 3) Stay low and keep the pelvis level.
- **Common faults:** Rocking the torso side to side; Feet turning out; Letting the band pull the knees in.
- **Progress to:** Single Leg Glute Bridge (Mini Band) (G2); Cossack Squat (G2); Paused Hip Thrust (G2). **Or progress by:** Heavier band, band lower on the leg, side plank abduction.
- **Regress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or regress by:** Side lying with no band, smaller range.
- **Same level swaps:** Monster Walk; Lateral Band Walk; Crab Walk (Mini Band)
- **Cautions:** None specific. Very joint friendly, ideal for hip and knee rehab.
- **Default prescription:** 2 to 3 sets x 10 to 20 each side
- **Coach sources:** Squat University, Boyle, Paul Chek

## Ankle Rocks (Knee to Wall)

`MOB-027 | G1 | Mobility: ankle dorsiflexion | STRONG, HYBRID, BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Bodyweight
- **Why we use it:** Stiff ankles cause heels lifting, knees caving and forward lean in squats, and pain further up the chain (joint by joint). The knee to wall test is the screen; rocks and banded mobs are the fix (Squat University).
- **Muscles:** Ankle joint, calves
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Half kneeling, foot about 10cm from the wall. 2) Drive the knee forward over the toes keeping the heel down. 3) Rock in and out.
- **Common faults:** Heel lifting; Knee caving inward; Forcing.
- **Progress to:** Bear Crawl (G2); Quadruped Thoracic Rotation (G2); Spiderman Lunge with Rotation (G2). **Or progress by:** Further from the wall, band, load.
- **Regress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or regress by:** Closer to the wall.
- **Same level swaps:** Banded Ankle Mobility; Knee to Wall Ankle Mobility
- **Cautions:** None specific. Universally safe.
- **Default prescription:** 2 x 10 to 15 rocks each side
- **Coach sources:** Squat University, Ben Patrick

## Calf Stretch (Wall)

`MOB-029 | G1 | Mobility: stretch / spinal mobility | STRONG, HYBRID, BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Bodyweight
- **Why we use it:** Static and gentle mobility work restores range lost from sitting and ageing. Best used where a screen shows a restriction (Squat University: screen, correct, retest), and to cool down. McKenzie press ups and extension work often relieve disc type back pain; flexion stretches often suit stenosis type pain: individualise.
- **Muscles:** Target muscles and joints vary (named in the exercise)
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Get into position slowly. 2) Breathe out to relax into range, no bouncing. 3) Hold 30 to 60s or do slow reps.
- **Common faults:** Forcing painful range; Holding the breath; Stretching instead of strengthening when stability is the issue.
- **Progress to:** Bear Crawl (G2); Quadruped Thoracic Rotation (G2); Spiderman Lunge with Rotation (G2). **Or progress by:** Longer holds, deeper range, add loaded stretching.
- **Regress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or regress by:** Smaller range, supported versions.
- **Same level swaps:** Frog Stretch; Couch Stretch; Elephant Walk
- **Cautions:** None specific. Gentle and safe. Stop if symptoms travel down the leg. Osteoporosis: avoid loaded flexion stretches.
- **Default prescription:** 1 to 2 sets x 5 to 10 slow reps (or 30 to 60s), in warm up or cool down
- **Coach sources:** Squat University, DeFranco (Limber 11), Ben Patrick (couch stretch), McGill

## Hip CARs

`MOB-032 | G1 | Mobility: controlled articular rotations (CARs) | STRONG, HYBRID, BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Bodyweight
- **Why we use it:** Slow, full range joint circles under tension. Maintains each joint's usable range and gives a daily joint health check.
- **Muscles:** Joint capsule, end range control
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Brace everything else. 2) Move the joint through its biggest circle slowly. 3) Keep tension the whole way.
- **Common faults:** Compensating with other joints; Rushing; Forcing painful range.
- **Progress to:** Bear Crawl (G2); Quadruped Thoracic Rotation (G2); Spiderman Lunge with Rotation (G2). **Or progress by:** Bigger circle, more tension.
- **Regress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or regress by:** Smaller circle.
- **Same level swaps:** Neck CARs; Shoulder CARs; Standing Hip CARs
- **Cautions:** None specific. Universally safe.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 5 slow reps each direction
- **Coach sources:** FRC style mobility, Dean Somerset

## Light Jog

`MOB-034 | G3 | Conditioning: running based | HYBRID | Group: No | Impact: high | Teams only: Yes | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Bodyweight
- **Why we use it:** Running based conditioning. Effective but impact based.
- **This variation:** Reduced range/load version: used for rehab, beginners, warm ups or flare up days.
- **Muscles:** Legs, heart and lungs
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Tall posture. 2) Quick light steps. 3) Arms drive.
- **Common faults:** Overstriding; Heavy landing; Too much volume.
- **Progress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or progress by:** Faster, longer.
- **Regress to:** Bear Crawl (G2); Quadruped Thoracic Rotation (G2); Spiderman Lunge with Rotation (G2). **Or regress by:** Walk, incline walk, bike.
- **Same level swaps:** High Knees; Butt Kicks; Shuttle Runs
- **Cautions:** Knee, Osteoporosis/osteopenia, Pelvic floor. IMPACT: excluded from group sessions. Swap to bike/ski/rower/sled.
- **Group swap:** Group swap: assault bike, ski erg, rower, sled push, marching high knees
- **Default prescription:** Intervals: e.g. 6 to 10 x 15 to 30s hard / 60 to 90s easy, or 20 to 40 min steady (zone 2)
- **Coach sources:** Gambetta

- **Default prescription:** 1 to 2 x 5 to 10 each side (or 20 to 30m)
- **Coach sources:** DeFranco (Limber 11, Simple 6), Gambetta, Squat University

## Rower (Easy 2 Minutes)

`MOB-036 | G1 | Conditioning: erg / walking | BURN, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Rower
- **Why we use it:** The bike, rower and ski erg give big conditioning with no impact, and every level can work at their own intensity. Zone 2 builds the aerobic base (Attia); short sprints suit menopause and fat loss (Sims, Cosgrove hierarchy). Backward walking (treadmill or sled) is Ben Patrick's knee warm up.
- **Muscles:** Heart and lungs, legs (bike/rower), upper body (ski/rower)
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Bike: push and pull with arms and legs, steady cadence. 2) Rower: legs, body, arms; then arms, body, legs. 3) Ski: hinge and pull down, drive the hips.
- **Common faults:** Rowing with the arms first; Hunched posture; Going out too hard in intervals.
- **Progress to:** Bear Crawl (G2); Quadruped Thoracic Rotation (G2); Spiderman Lunge with Rotation (G2). **Or progress by:** Longer work, shorter rest, higher watts/calories, more rounds.
- **Regress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or regress by:** Easier pace, shorter intervals, more rest.
- **Same level swaps:** Rower 500m; Rower Intervals; Rower Steady State
- **Cautions:** None specific. Low impact. Rower and ski: watch low back flexion. Treadmill sprints involve impact.
- **Default prescription:** Intervals: e.g. 6 to 10 x 15 to 30s hard / 60 to 90s easy, or 20 to 40 min steady (zone 2)
- **Coach sources:** Attia (zone 2, VO2), Cosgrove (intervals), Stacy Sims (sprints), Ben Patrick (backward walking)

## Arm Circles

`MOB-037 | G1 | Warm up: dynamic mobility | STRONG, HYBRID, BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Bodyweight
- **Why we use it:** Dynamic drills raise temperature, take joints through range and rehearse patterns (RAMP warm up). The World's Greatest Stretch hits hip flexors, hamstrings, adductors and T spine in one move. 40+ members need a full 8 to 10 minute warm up every session.
- **Muscles:** Whole body
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Move through big comfortable ranges. 2) Increase range each rep. 3) Breathe and stay controlled.
- **Common faults:** Rushing; Bouncing into range; Skipping the warm up.
- **Progress to:** Bear Crawl (G2); Quadruped Thoracic Rotation (G2); Spiderman Lunge with Rotation (G2). **Or progress by:** Bigger range, add reaches.
- **Regress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or regress by:** Smaller range, hand support.
- **Same level swaps:** A March; Inchworm; Crab Reach
- **Cautions:** None specific. Safe for almost everyone.
- **Default prescription:** 1 to 2 x 5 to 10 each side (or 20 to 30m)
- **Coach sources:** DeFranco (Limber 11, Simple 6), Gambetta, Squat University

# 20. OPTIMAL BRAIN ADDITIONS (COACH RESEARCH)

*Signature exercises from the coach research not already in the movement library*

**Grade ladder at a glance** (use this to slot every member into the same session at their level):

- **G1**: Patrick Step, Front Foot Elevated ATG Split Squat (Assisted), KOT Calf Raise, Tib Bar Tibialis Raise, Elephant Walk, Lunge Matrix (Forward, Lateral, Rotational, Reverse), Limber 11 (DeFranco Lower Body Routine), Simple 6 (DeFranco Upper Body Routine), McGill Big 3 (Curl Up, Side Plank, Bird Dog), 4 Point TVA Draw In (Chek), Fast Sit to Stand (Power), Tandem Stance Balance, Heel to Toe Walk, Clock Reach (Single Leg Balance), Heel Drops (Bone Loading), Marching High Knees, Zone 2 Steady State (Bike, Rower or Ski), VO2 Max Intervals (4 x 4 min), Sprint Intervals 10 to 20s (Bike or Ski), Banded Hip Distraction
- **G2**: ATG Split Squat, Reverse Nordic (Assisted), Slant Board Goblet Squat, SSB Split Squat, SSB Reverse Lunge, SSB Good Morning, Prone Cobra (Chek), Swiss Ball Supine Lateral Ball Roll (Chek), Floor to Stand Transfer, Half Kneeling to Stand, Step Jacks (No Jump)
- **G3**: SSB Squat, SSB Box Squat, Jumping Chin Up with Drop Landing (LIFTMOR) ✱, Step Back Burpee (No Jump), Squat Thrust to Bench (No Jump), Trap Bar Deadlift (Low Handles), Nordic Curl (Full)
- **G4**: SSB Pause Squat

✱ = not for group sessions (impact).

## Patrick Step

`ADD-001 | G1 | Single leg: knee over toes step (VMO) | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Box / bench / step
- **Why we use it:** Ben Patrick's entry level knee builder from ATG Zero: standing on a low step on the ball of the foot, the knee travels forward over the toes as the other heel lowers to tap the floor. It teaches the quads, not the joint, to own the knees over toes position and is the first step towards the ATG split squat.
- **Muscles:** Quads (VMO emphasis), knee tendons, ankle
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Stand on a low step, working heel raised on a small plate or wedge (Poliquin) or on the toes (Patrick). 2) Slowly lower the other heel towards the floor by bending the working knee forward over the toes. 3) Lightly tap and drive back up through the front of the foot, keeping the knee in line.
- **Common faults:** Hips shifting back instead of the knee travelling forward; Knee caving inward; Dropping fast instead of controlling the lowering.
- **Progress to:** ATG Split Squat (G2); SSB Split Squat (G2); Split Squat (DB) (G2). **Or progress by:** Higher step, slower tempo, hold DBs, progress to step downs and front foot elevated split squats.
- **Regress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or regress by:** Lower step, hand on the rig, partial range.
- **Same level swaps:** Poliquin Step Up; Petersen Step Up
- **Cautions:** None specific. Knee friendly when kept pain free. Start with a very low step (5 to 10cm) and hand support. Ideal in every knee pain programme.
- **Default prescription:** 2 to 3 sets x 10 to 20 each leg, slow lowering (3s)
- **Coach sources:** Poliquin, Ben Patrick (ATG), Squat University

## ATG Split Squat

`ADD-002 | G2 | Single leg: split squat | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Bodyweight
- **Why we use it:** Ben Patrick's signature exercise: a long split squat where the front knee travels well past the toes with the heel staying down and the back knee lowers to the floor, giving a deep hip flexor stretch on the back leg. It builds strength in the deepest knee position and hip flexor flexibility at the same time. Start with the front foot elevated and hand support, hold the bottom for time (e.g. 30s), then add reps and load.
- **Muscles:** Quads, glutes, adductors
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Long split stance, both feet pointing forward, hip width apart. 2) Lower the back knee straight down towards the floor. 3) Push through the front foot to stand, keep the torso tall.
- **Common faults:** Stance too narrow (tightrope), losing balance; Front heel lifting; Lunging forward instead of dropping down.
- **Progress to:** Barbell Split Squat (G3); Band Resisted Split Squat (G3); Offset Single Arm Split Squat (G3). **Or progress by:** Add load, elevate the front foot (ATG style), then elevate the back foot (RFESS).
- **Regress to:** Split Squat (Supported) (G1); Split Squat (Bodyweight) (G1); TRX Assisted Split Squat (G1). **Or regress by:** TRX or rig assisted split squat, shorter range, isometric split squat hold.
- **Same level swaps:** SSB Split Squat; Split Squat (DB); Cable Split Squat
- **Cautions:** None specific. Knee friendly when depth is controlled. Use a pad under the back knee. Hold a support for balance in seniors.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8 (each leg)
- **Coach sources:** Boyle, Squat University, Ben Patrick (front foot elevated)

## Front Foot Elevated ATG Split Squat (Assisted)

`ADD-003 | G1 | Single leg: split squat | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Box / bench / step
- **Why we use it:** The regression Ben Patrick uses before the floor level ATG split squat: front foot on a step and hands on a support so the knee can travel over the toes in a pain free range.
- **This variation:** Assisted version: support lets members practise the full pattern safely while strength builds (Cosgrove: regress to progress).
- **Muscles:** Quads, glutes, adductors
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Long split stance, both feet pointing forward, hip width apart. 2) Lower the back knee straight down towards the floor. 3) Push through the front foot to stand, keep the torso tall.
- **Common faults:** Stance too narrow (tightrope), losing balance; Front heel lifting; Lunging forward instead of dropping down.
- **Progress to:** ATG Split Squat (G2); SSB Split Squat (G2); Split Squat (DB) (G2). **Or progress by:** Add load, elevate the front foot (ATG style), then elevate the back foot (RFESS).
- **Regress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or regress by:** TRX or rig assisted split squat, shorter range, isometric split squat hold.
- **Same level swaps:** Split Squat (Supported); Split Squat (Bodyweight); TRX Assisted Split Squat
- **Cautions:** None specific. Knee friendly when depth is controlled. Use a pad under the back knee. Hold a support for balance in seniors.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8 (each leg)
- **Coach sources:** Boyle, Squat University, Ben Patrick (front foot elevated)

## Reverse Nordic (Assisted)

`ADD-004 | G2 | Squat: knee dominant (quad lengthening) | STRONG | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Bodyweight
- **Why we use it:** Kneeling, the body leans back as one line from knee to head, lengthening and strengthening the quads (especially rectus femoris) through a range most people never train. Ben Patrick uses it for knee resilience and hip flexor length. Use a band or partner for assistance and short range first.
- **This variation:** Assisted version: support lets members practise the full pattern safely while strength builds (Cosgrove: regress to progress).
- **Muscles:** Quads (rectus femoris in a lengthened position), hip flexors
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Hold a post or TRX for support. 2) Rise onto the toes, push the knees forward and lean the body back as one straight line from knee to shoulder. 3) Lower only as far as pain free, drive back up through the quads.
- **Common faults:** Bending at the hips (turns it into a normal squat); Dropping too deep too early; Letting go of the support before ready.
- **Progress to:** SSB Squat (G3); SSB Box Squat (G3); Nordic Curl (Full) (G3). **Or progress by:** Increase range, reduce hand assistance, add a plate at the chest, progress towards reverse Nordic.
- **Regress to:** Patrick Step (G1); Elephant Walk (G1); KOT Calf Raise (G1). **Or regress by:** Short range only, more hand support, swap to Spanish squat or heels elevated goblet squat.
- **Same level swaps:** Sissy Squat (Assisted); Sissy Squat (Assisted, Short Range)
- **Cautions:** Knee. Earn it. Start short range with hand support. Avoid with acute knee pain, recent knee surgery or knee replacements unless cleared.
- **Default prescription:** 2 to 3 sets x 6 to 12 reps, slow lowering, hand support
- **Coach sources:** Ben Patrick (ATG), Poliquin (VMO work)

## KOT Calf Raise

`ADD-005 | G1 | Lower leg: calf | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Bodyweight
- **Why we use it:** Knees over toes calf raise (Ben Patrick): the knee is pushed forward over the toes during the raise, training the calf and Achilles in the bent knee position used in walking downhill, stairs and squatting.
- **Muscles:** Calves (gastrocnemius straight knee, soleus bent knee), Achilles
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Full stretch at the bottom. 2) Rise to the highest point on the big toe. 3) Pause, lower slowly (3s).
- **Common faults:** Bouncing; Rolling to the outside of the foot; Partial range.
- **Progress to:** ATG Split Squat (G2); SSB Split Squat (G2); SSB Good Morning (G2). **Or progress by:** Single leg, off a step, add load.
- **Regress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or regress by:** Two legs, hand support, flat floor.
- **Same level swaps:** Single Leg Calf Raise; Calf Raise (Straight Knee); Seated Calf Raise (Bent Knee)
- **Cautions:** None specific. Achilles pain: slow heavy calf raises are rehab gold.
- **Default prescription:** 3 x 12 to 20 (slow)
- **Coach sources:** Ben Patrick (ATG), Rehab research (Achilles)

## Tib Bar Tibialis Raise

`ADD-006 | G1 | Lower leg: tibialis raise | STRONG, HYBRID, BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Tib bar (confirm)
- **Why we use it:** Loaded tibialis raise using a tib bar or a plate/KB over the feet while seated. Ben Patrick's advanced standard is around 25% bodyweight for 5 x 5. Strong shins protect the knees and ankles and balance the calves.
- **Muscles:** Tibialis anterior (shin), ankle
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Back against a wall, heels 30 to 50cm away. 2) Lift the toes up as high as possible. 3) Lower slowly.
- **Common faults:** Bending the knees; Rushing; Partial range.
- **Progress to:** ATG Split Squat (G2); SSB Split Squat (G2); SSB Good Morning (G2). **Or progress by:** Feet further from the wall, single leg, tib bar load.
- **Regress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or regress by:** Closer to the wall.
- **Same level swaps:** Tibialis Raise
- **Cautions:** None specific. Universally safe.
- **Default prescription:** 2 to 3 x 20 to 25
- **Coach sources:** Ben Patrick (ATG)

## Slant Board Goblet Squat

`ADD-007 | G2 | Squat: knee dominant bilateral | STRONG, HYBRID, BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Kettlebell, Slant board (confirm)
- **Why we use it:** Squatting with the heels on a slant board lets the knees travel well forward with the torso upright, loading the quads and VMO with less ankle demand. A Ben Patrick and Squat University tool for knee health and quad strength.
- **Muscles:** Quads, glutes, adductors, upper back, core
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Hold the bell tight to the chest, elbows pointing down. 2) Push the knees out and sit between the hips, chest proud. 3) Drive up through the whole foot, squeeze the glutes at the top.
- **Common faults:** Rounding the upper back and letting the weight pull you forward; Heels lifting; Knees caving inward on the way up.
- **Progress to:** Paused Goblet Squat (G3); 1.5 Rep Goblet Squat (G3). **Or progress by:** Add load, tempo (4-1-1-0), pause at the bottom, 1.5 reps, move to double KB front squat or SSB squat.
- **Regress to:** Goblet Box Squat (G1); Box Squat (G1); TRX Assisted Squat (G1). **Or regress by:** Goblet squat to a box, TRX assisted squat, lighter bell.
- **Same level swaps:** Goblet Squat (KB); Goblet Squat (DB); Tempo Goblet Squat
- **Cautions:** None specific. Knee and back friendly. Heels elevated version helps stiff ankles. Use a box for depth control with knee pain. Upper back can fatigue first as loads get heavy.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8
- **Coach sources:** Dan John, Squat University, Cosgrove, Boyle

## Elephant Walk

`ADD-008 | G1 | Mobility: stretch / spinal mobility | STRONG, HYBRID, BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Bodyweight
- **Why we use it:** ATG hamstring mobility drill: hands on the floor (or blocks), alternate bending and straightening each knee to walk the hamstrings into length. Loaded or unloaded, used in Ben Patrick's ATG Zero.
- **Muscles:** Target muscles and joints vary (named in the exercise)
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Get into position slowly. 2) Breathe out to relax into range, no bouncing. 3) Hold 30 to 60s or do slow reps.
- **Common faults:** Forcing painful range; Holding the breath; Stretching instead of strengthening when stability is the issue.
- **Progress to:** ATG Split Squat (G2); SSB Split Squat (G2); SSB Good Morning (G2). **Or progress by:** Longer holds, deeper range, add loaded stretching.
- **Regress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or regress by:** Smaller range, supported versions.
- **Same level swaps:** Frog Stretch; Couch Stretch; Pigeon Stretch
- **Cautions:** None specific. Gentle and safe. Stop if symptoms travel down the leg. Osteoporosis: avoid loaded flexion stretches.
- **Default prescription:** 1 to 2 sets x 5 to 10 slow reps (or 30 to 60s), in warm up or cool down
- **Coach sources:** Squat University, DeFranco (Limber 11), Ben Patrick (couch stretch), McGill

## SSB Squat

`ADD-009 | G3 | Squat: knee dominant bilateral (loaded) | STRONG | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Safety squat bar
- **Why we use it:** The safety squat bar lets members back squat heavy without needing shoulder mobility to hold a straight bar, and its forward pitch keeps the torso upright. It is Optimal's main heavy squat tool for 40+ members with cranky shoulders, elbows or wrists. DeFranco built his reputation using it.
- **This variation:** Safety squat bar: heavy loading without needing shoulder mobility to hold a straight bar; DeFranco's go to for cranky shoulders.
- **Muscles:** Quads, glutes, adductors, upper back
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Handles in front, pads on the upper back, brace 360 degrees before descending. 2) Push knees out over the middle of the foot, sit between the hips. 3) Drive up with the chest leading, don't let the bar tip you forward.
- **Common faults:** Letting the bar pull the chest forward and rounding the upper back; Losing the brace at the bottom; Cutting depth as the weight goes up.
- **Progress to:** SSB Pause Squat (G4); Anderson Squat (G4); Tempo Back Squat (G4). **Or progress by:** Add load (double progression), pause squats, tempo 4-1-X-0, SSB split squats, rep maxes on rotating variations (Teams G4).
- **Regress to:** Barbell Box Squat (G2); Banded Barbell Box Squat (G2). **Or regress by:** SSB box squat to a higher box, goblet squat, front loaded DB squat.
- **Same level swaps:** SSB Box Squat; Zercher Squat; DB Front Squat
- **Cautions:** None specific. Shoulder and wrist friendly. Still a spinal load: check back history. For knee pain use a box to control depth.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8
- **Coach sources:** DeFranco, Squat University, Cosgrove

- **Same level swaps:** Anderson Squat; Tempo Back Squat; Paused Back Squat
- **Cautions:** None specific. Shoulder and wrist friendly. Still a spinal load: check back history. For knee pain use a box to control depth.

- **Equipment:** Safety squat bar
- **Why we use it:** Split squat with the safety squat bar: allows heavier single leg loading than dumbbells without grip limiting, and keeps the shoulders comfortable.

## SSB Reverse Lunge

`ADD-013 | G2 | Single leg: reverse lunge | STRONG, HYBRID, BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Safety squat bar
- **Why we use it:** Reverse lunge loaded with the safety squat bar for heavy single leg strength without grip or shoulder limitations.
- **This variation:** Safety squat bar: heavy loading without needing shoulder mobility to hold a straight bar; DeFranco's go to for cranky shoulders.
- **Muscles:** Quads, glutes, hamstrings
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Stand tall, step one foot back. 2) Drop the back knee towards the floor, front shin fairly vertical. 3) Drive through the front heel to stand back up.
- **Common faults:** Stepping too short; Front knee collapsing; Leaning forward and rounding.
- **Progress to:** Slider Reverse Lunge (G3); Deficit Reverse Lunge (G3); Barbell Reverse Lunge (G3). **Or progress by:** Add load, deficit (front foot on a plate), knee drive at the top, barbell/landmine.
- **Regress to:** Split Squat (Supported) (G1); Split Squat (Bodyweight) (G1); TRX Assisted Split Squat (G1). **Or regress by:** Split squat (static), hand support, shorter range.
- **Same level swaps:** Reverse Lunge (DB); Cable Reverse Lunge; Goblet Reverse Lunge
- **Cautions:** None specific. Most knee friendly lunge. Use a pad and hand support for beginners.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8 (each leg)
- **Coach sources:** Boyle, Cosgrove, Squat University

## SSB Good Morning

`ADD-014 | G2 | Hinge: good morning | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Safety squat bar, Barbell
- **Why we use it:** Good morning with the safety squat bar: the handles and padding make it more comfortable and safer to learn than a straight bar good morning. Builds hamstrings and back extensors. Teams G3 to G4 only and not for low back pain.
- **This variation:** Safety squat bar: heavy loading without needing shoulder mobility to hold a straight bar; DeFranco's go to for cranky shoulders.
- **Muscles:** Hamstrings, glutes, spinal erectors
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Soft knees, brace, push the hips back. 2) Keep the spine long and neutral. 3) Stand up by driving the hips forward.
- **Common faults:** Rounding the spine; Bending the knees too much; Going deeper than hamstring length allows.
- **Progress to:** Barbell Good Morning (G3); Barbell Romanian Deadlift (G3); Paused DB RDL (G3). **Or progress by:** Band → light barbell → SSB good morning, tempo, pause.
- **Regress to:** Bodyweight Good Morning (G1); Hip Hinge to Wall (G1); Hip Hinge Dowel Drill (G1). **Or regress by:** Bodyweight, dowel hinge drill.
- **Same level swaps:** Seated Good Morning; Banded Good Morning; Single Leg Good Morning
- **Cautions:** Low back. Loaded good mornings are not for low back pain. Keep loads light and range controlled for 40+.
- **Default prescription:** 3 sets x 8 to 12 reps, tempo 3-0-1-1, rest 60 to 90s, RPE 7 to 9
- **Coach sources:** Westside/DeFranco, Ben Patrick (seated), Poliquin

## Lunge Matrix (Forward, Lateral, Rotational, Reverse)

`ADD-015 | G1 | Warm up: dynamic mobility | STRONG, HYBRID, BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Bodyweight
- **Why we use it:** Vern Gambetta's multi directional lunge sequence: a lunge forward, to the side, rotational (turning 135 degrees) and backward on each leg. It warms up the hips in all three planes and builds balance and multi plane strength. Ideal warm up for golf and 40+ hips.
- **Muscles:** Whole body
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Move through big comfortable ranges. 2) Increase range each rep. 3) Breathe and stay controlled.
- **Common faults:** Rushing; Bouncing into range; Skipping the warm up.
- **Progress to:** ATG Split Squat (G2); SSB Split Squat (G2); SSB Good Morning (G2). **Or progress by:** Bigger range, add reaches.
- **Regress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or regress by:** Smaller range, hand support.
- **Same level swaps:** A March; Inchworm; Crab Reach
- **Cautions:** None specific. Safe for almost everyone.
- **Default prescription:** 1 to 2 x 5 to 10 each side (or 20 to 30m)
- **Coach sources:** DeFranco (Limber 11, Simple 6), Gambetta, Squat University

## McGill Big 3 (Curl Up, Side Plank, Bird Dog)

`ADD-018 | G1 | Core: McGill curl up | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Bodyweight
- **Why we use it:** Professor Stuart McGill's daily core routine for back health: modified curl up, side plank and bird dog, each held 8 to 10 seconds in a descending pyramid (e.g. 6, 4, 2 reps). Builds core endurance and stiffness without stressing the discs. Default warm up for any member with back history.
- **Muscles:** Rectus abdominis (without spinal flexion)
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Lie on your back, one knee bent, hands under the low back. 2) Brace and lift the head and shoulders slightly as one unit. 3) Hold 8 to 10s, lower.
- **Common faults:** Tucking the chin; Flattening the low back; Curling up too high.
- **Progress to:** ATG Split Squat (G2); SSB Split Squat (G2); SSB Good Morning (G2). **Or progress by:** Raise elbows off the floor, longer holds.
- **Regress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or regress by:** Shorter holds.
- **Same level swaps:** McGill Curl Up
- **Cautions:** None specific. Back pain friendly. Part of the Big 3.
- **Default prescription:** Descending pyramid: 6, 4, 2 reps with 8 to 10s holds
- **Coach sources:** McGill, Squat University

## 4 Point TVA Draw In (Chek)

`ADD-019 | G1 | Core: breathing and pelvic control | STRONG, HYBRID, BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Bodyweight
- **Why we use it:** Paul Chek's inner unit drill: on hands and knees, let the belly relax then draw the belly button gently towards the spine without moving the spine, hold and breathe. Teaches deep core activation before loading (stabilisers before prime movers).
- **Muscles:** Diaphragm, deep core, pelvic floor
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Lie in position, hands on the lower ribs. 2) Breathe in through the nose expanding 360 degrees (belly, sides, back). 3) Exhale slowly fully, feeling the ribs drop.
- **Common faults:** Chest and shoulder breathing; Arching the back; Rushing.
- **Progress to:** ATG Split Squat (G2); SSB Split Squat (G2); SSB Good Morning (G2). **Or progress by:** Add movement (dead bug with breathing).
- **Regress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or regress by:** Shorter sets.
- **Same level swaps:** Pelvic Tilt; 90/90 Breathing; Pelvic Tilt (Supine)
- **Cautions:** None specific. Universally safe. Great on RED readiness days.
- **Default prescription:** 5 to 10 slow breaths
- **Coach sources:** Paul Chek, McGill, Squat University

## Prone Cobra (Chek)

`ADD-020 | G2 | Hinge: back extension | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Bodyweight
- **Why we use it:** Paul Chek's postural endurance exercise: lying face down, lift the chest slightly and rotate the thumbs out to squeeze the shoulder blades, hold. Strengthens the upper back and spinal extensors that hold upright posture.
- **Muscles:** Spinal erectors, glutes, hamstrings
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Hinge at the hips, keep the spine long. 2) Lift to a straight line from head to heels using the glutes. 3) Lower with control.
- **Common faults:** Hyperextending at the top; Swinging/using momentum; Rounding heavily at the bottom under load.
- **Progress to:** SSB Squat (G3); SSB Box Squat (G3); Nordic Curl (Full) (G3). **Or progress by:** Hold a plate, single leg, pause at the top.
- **Regress to:** Reverse Hyper (Bench, Light) (G1); 45 Degree Back Extension (Bodyweight) (G1). **Or regress by:** Superman, bird dog, shorter range.
- **Same level swaps:** Reverse Hyper (Bench); Superman (Alternating); 45 Degree Back Extension
- **Cautions:** None specific. Good for most back pain when kept to neutral. Avoid loaded flexion at the bottom for osteoporosis.
- **Default prescription:** 2 to 3 sets x 10 to 15 reps, tempo 2-1-1-1, rest 45 to 60s, RPE 8
- **Coach sources:** DeFranco (reverse hyper), McGill, Paul Chek (prone cobra)

## Swiss Ball Supine Lateral Ball Roll (Chek)

`ADD-021 | G2 | Rotation: loaded rotation | HYBRID, STRONG | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Swiss ball (confirm)
- **Why we use it:** Paul Chek's twist pattern exercise: lying with the shoulders on a Swiss ball and hips up, arms out holding a light weight, shuffle sideways across the ball keeping the body level. Trains rotational stability of the trunk and hips.
- **This variation:** Swiss ball adds instability for core control (Paul Chek); keep loads modest.
- **Muscles:** Obliques, hips, upper back
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Arms long, pivot the back foot. 2) Turn from the hips and upper back together. 3) Control the return through the middle.
- **Common faults:** Rotating only at the low back; Arms bending; Moving too fast.
- **Progress to:** SSB Squat (G3); SSB Box Squat (G3); Nordic Curl (Full) (G3). **Or progress by:** Heavier, faster, split stance.
- **Regress to:** Patrick Step (G1); Elephant Walk (G1); KOT Calf Raise (G1). **Or regress by:** Lighter, smaller range, anti rotation instead.
- **Same level swaps:** Landmine 180; Landmine Rainbow; Landmine Rotation
- **Cautions:** None specific. Avoid fast loaded rotation with acute back pain.
- **Default prescription:** 2 to 3 sets x 6 to 10 reps each side (or 20 to 40s), slow and controlled
- **Coach sources:** Gambetta, Paul Chek

## Floor to Stand Transfer

`ADD-022 | G2 | Total body: Turkish get up / windmill | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Bodyweight
- **Why we use it:** Getting down to the floor and back up with as little support as possible. A key longevity skill (Attia, Dan John) and part of the Optimal screen. Progress from using a chair to hands only to no hands.
- **Muscles:** Shoulder stability, core, hips, whole body
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Eyes on the bell, arm locked. 2) Move through each step slowly: roll to elbow, hand, high bridge, sweep the leg, kneel, stand. 3) Reverse every step with control.
- **Common faults:** Rushing; Bent arm; Losing sight of the bell.
- **Progress to:** SSB Squat (G3); SSB Box Squat (G3); Nordic Curl (Full) (G3). **Or progress by:** Heavier bell, full get up.
- **Regress to:** Half Turkish Get Up (G1); Turkish Get Up (Light) (G1). **Or regress by:** Half get up, shoe on the fist, no weight.
- **Same level swaps:** KB Windmill; Arm Bar (KB); Turkish Get Up
- **Cautions:** Shoulder. Learn with a shoe or no weight first. Shoulder pain: half get up with no load only.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 5 reps each side, slow
- **Coach sources:** Dan John, Pavel Tsatsouline, Gray Cook

## Half Kneeling to Stand

`ADD-023 | G2 | Total body: Turkish get up / windmill | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Bodyweight
- **Why we use it:** From half kneeling, stand up without using the hands (then lower back down). Builds the strength and balance needed to get off the floor, and is a stepping stone to the Turkish get up.
- **This variation:** Kneeling position locks the hips so the core has to control the trunk and stops the legs cheating.
- **Muscles:** Shoulder stability, core, hips, whole body
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Eyes on the bell, arm locked. 2) Move through each step slowly: roll to elbow, hand, high bridge, sweep the leg, kneel, stand. 3) Reverse every step with control.
- **Common faults:** Rushing; Bent arm; Losing sight of the bell.
- **Progress to:** SSB Squat (G3); SSB Box Squat (G3); Nordic Curl (Full) (G3). **Or progress by:** Heavier bell, full get up.
- **Regress to:** Half Turkish Get Up (G1); Turkish Get Up (Light) (G1). **Or regress by:** Half get up, shoe on the fist, no weight.
- **Same level swaps:** KB Windmill; Arm Bar (KB); Turkish Get Up
- **Cautions:** Shoulder. Learn with a shoe or no weight first. Shoulder pain: half get up with no load only.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 5 reps each side, slow
- **Coach sources:** Dan John, Pavel Tsatsouline, Gray Cook

## Fast Sit to Stand (Power)

`ADD-024 | G1 | Squat: functional (sit to stand) | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Box / bench / step
- **Why we use it:** Stand up from a chair as fast as possible, sit down slowly. Trains power, which declines faster than strength with age, using the safest possible movement. Seniors programme staple.
- **This variation:** Fast/power version: move with intent, stop when speed drops.
- **Muscles:** Quads, glutes, balance
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Sit tall on a box or chair, feet slightly back under the knees. 2) Lean the chest forward, push the floor away and stand up tall. 3) Sit back down slowly with control, don't flop.
- **Common faults:** Using the hands to push off; Feet too far forward; Collapsing back down onto the seat.
- **Progress to:** ATG Split Squat (G2); SSB Split Squat (G2); SSB Good Morning (G2). **Or progress by:** Lower the box, hold a weight at the chest, stand up as fast as possible (power), single leg sit to stand.
- **Regress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or regress by:** Raise the seat, use hands on thighs or a TRX for help, reduce reps.
- **Same level swaps:** Sit to Stand (Chair); Squat to Box Stand Up (Bodyweight)
- **Cautions:** None specific. Suitable for almost everyone. Raise the seat height for painful knees or hips. Single leg version needs good knee control.
- **Default prescription:** 3 sets x 8 to 12 reps (or max reps in 30s for testing), stand up fast, lower slowly
- **Coach sources:** Seniors research (functional testing), Gambetta (fundamental movement), Attia (centenarian decathlon)

## Tandem Stance Balance

`ADD-025 | G1 | Balance and proprioception | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Bodyweight
- **Why we use it:** Standing heel to toe (one foot directly in front of the other) near a support. A falls prevention staple and seniors programme warm up.
- **Muscles:** Foot, ankle, hip stabilisers, nervous system
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Stand tall near a support. 2) Grip the floor with the foot, soft knee. 3) Hold or reach while keeping the hips level.
- **Common faults:** Locking the knee; Holding the breath; Doing it far from support.
- **Progress to:** ATG Split Squat (G2); SSB Split Squat (G2); SSB Good Morning (G2). **Or progress by:** Eyes closed, cushion, reach, catch a ball.
- **Regress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or regress by:** Hand on support, tandem stance.
- **Same level swaps:** Heel to Toe Walk; Single Leg Balance; Star Excursion Balance
- **Cautions:** None specific. Always near a rail or rig for seniors.
- **Default prescription:** 3 x 20 to 30s each leg
- **Coach sources:** Gambetta, Falls prevention research

- **Why we use it:** Walking in a straight line placing the heel directly in front of the toes. Trains dynamic balance and gait (Gambetta: postural alignment and dynamic balance are the foundation).

## Clock Reach (Single Leg Balance)

`ADD-027 | G1 | Balance and proprioception | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Bodyweight
- **Why we use it:** Standing on one leg and reaching the other foot to points on an imaginary clock. Builds balance, ankle and hip control.

## Jumping Chin Up with Drop Landing (LIFTMOR)

`ADD-028 | G3 | Vertical pull: pull up / chin up / hangs | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: No | Impact: high | Teams only: Yes | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Rig / pull up bar
- **Why we use it:** Used in the LIFTMOR trial for postmenopausal bone health: jump to the top of a chin up, lower slowly, then drop and land firmly on both feet. The landing impact loads the hips and spine. Supervised Teams only, screened, no pelvic floor symptoms.
- **Muscles:** Lats, upper back, biceps, grip, core
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Grip slightly wider than shoulders (chin up: palms facing you). 2) Pull the shoulder blades down first, then drive the elbows to the ribs. 3) Chin over the bar, lower slowly to straight arms.
- **Common faults:** Kipping or swinging; Half reps; Shrugging at the bottom.
- **Progress to:** Weighted Pull Up (G4); Weighted Chin Up (G4); Commando Pull Up (G4). **Or progress by:** Band assisted → negatives → bodyweight → weighted.
- **Regress to:** Hanging (Supported) (G2); TRX Assisted Pull Up (G2); Band Assisted Pull Up (G2). **Or regress by:** Lat pulldown, TRX assisted pull up, scapula pull up, dead hang.
- **Same level swaps:** Pull Up; Chin Up; Dead Hang
- **Cautions:** Pelvic floor, Shoulder. Shoulder pain: neutral grip, band assistance. Hanging can irritate some shoulders: build up gradually.
- **Group swap:** Use a no impact exercise from the same pattern
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8 or total reps
- **Coach sources:** DeFranco, Dan John, Attia (grip), Boyle

## Heel Drops (Bone Loading)

`ADD-029 | G1 | Lower leg: calf | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: low | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Bodyweight
- **Why we use it:** Rise onto the toes and drop firmly onto the heels. A low level impact progression used to load bone in members not yet ready for jumps. No flight phase, so it can be used in groups if comfortable.
- **Muscles:** Calves (gastrocnemius straight knee, soleus bent knee), Achilles
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Full stretch at the bottom. 2) Rise to the highest point on the big toe. 3) Pause, lower slowly (3s).
- **Common faults:** Bouncing; Rolling to the outside of the foot; Partial range.
- **Progress to:** ATG Split Squat (G2); SSB Split Squat (G2); SSB Good Morning (G2). **Or progress by:** Single leg, off a step, add load.
- **Regress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or regress by:** Two legs, hand support, flat floor.
- **Same level swaps:** KOT Calf Raise; Single Leg Calf Raise; Calf Raise (Straight Knee)
- **Cautions:** None specific. Achilles pain: slow heavy calf raises are rehab gold.
- **Default prescription:** 3 x 12 to 20 (slow)
- **Coach sources:** Ben Patrick (ATG), Rehab research (Achilles)

## Step Back Burpee (No Jump)

`ADD-030 | G3 | Conditioning: total body (burpee family) | BURN, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Bodyweight
- **Why we use it:** The Optimal group burpee: hands down, step back to plank, step in, stand tall. All of the metabolic benefit with no jumping or landing.
- **Muscles:** Whole body
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Hands down, step or jump back to plank. 2) Chest down (if required), back to feet. 3) Stand tall (jump only if allowed).
- **Common faults:** Sagging plank; Crashing to the floor; Sloppy as fatigue builds.
- **Progress to:** SSB Pause Squat (G4). **Or progress by:** Add a press, push up or jump.
- **Regress to:** ATG Split Squat (G2); SSB Split Squat (G2); SSB Good Morning (G2). **Or regress by:** Step back burpee, incline burpee onto a bench.
- **Same level swaps:** Squat Thrust to Bench (No Jump); Sprawls; Burpees
- **Cautions:** Low back, Osteoporosis/osteopenia, Pelvic floor. IMPACT when jumping: group sessions use the no jump version (step back, step in, stand). Devil's press and man makers: DB hinge skill required.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 6 x 20 to 40s
- **Coach sources:** Cosgrove (metabolic)

## Step Jacks (No Jump)

`ADD-032 | G2 | Conditioning: jumping cardio | BURN | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Bodyweight
- **Why we use it:** Step one foot out to the side as the arms rise overhead, alternate sides. Low impact jumping jack alternative for groups.

- **Same level swaps:** Skipping; Star Jumps; Jumping Jacks

- **Equipment:** Bodyweight
- **Why we use it:** Driving the knees up in a fast march with no hop. A no impact swap for high knees in group warm ups and finishers.
- **Muscles:** Whole body

- **Common faults:** Rushing; Bouncing into range; Skipping the warm up.
- **Progress to:** ATG Split Squat (G2); SSB Split Squat (G2); SSB Good Morning (G2). **Or progress by:** Bigger range, add reaches.

## Zone 2 Steady State (Bike, Rower or Ski)

`ADD-034 | G1 | Conditioning: erg / walking | BURN, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Assault bike / bike, Rower, Ski erg
- **Why we use it:** 20 to 45 minutes at a pace where you can just hold a conversation (RPE 3 to 4). Builds the aerobic base, mitochondrial health and fat burning capacity; Peter Attia's longevity foundation. Usually done outside group sessions (walks, cycling) or as recovery.
- **Muscles:** Heart and lungs, legs (bike/rower), upper body (ski/rower)
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Bike: push and pull with arms and legs, steady cadence. 2) Rower: legs, body, arms; then arms, body, legs. 3) Ski: hinge and pull down, drive the hips.
- **Common faults:** Rowing with the arms first; Hunched posture; Going out too hard in intervals.
- **Progress to:** ATG Split Squat (G2); SSB Split Squat (G2); SSB Good Morning (G2). **Or progress by:** Longer work, shorter rest, higher watts/calories, more rounds.
- **Regress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or regress by:** Easier pace, shorter intervals, more rest.
- **Same level swaps:** Rower and Ski Ladder; Sprint Intervals 10 to 20s (Bike or Ski); Rower 500m
- **Cautions:** None specific. Low impact. Rower and ski: watch low back flexion. Treadmill sprints involve impact.
- **Default prescription:** Intervals: e.g. 6 to 10 x 15 to 30s hard / 60 to 90s easy, or 20 to 40 min steady (zone 2)
- **Coach sources:** Attia (zone 2, VO2), Cosgrove (intervals), Stacy Sims (sprints), Ben Patrick (backward walking)

## VO2 Max Intervals (4 x 4 min)

`ADD-035 | G1 | Conditioning: erg / walking | BURN, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Bodyweight
- **Why we use it:** 4 to 5 intervals of 3 to 4 minutes hard (RPE 8 to 9) with equal easy recovery on the bike, rower or ski. Improves peak aerobic capacity, one of the strongest predictors of longevity (Attia). Teams, once per week maximum.
- **Muscles:** Heart and lungs, legs (bike/rower), upper body (ski/rower)
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Bike: push and pull with arms and legs, steady cadence. 2) Rower: legs, body, arms; then arms, body, legs. 3) Ski: hinge and pull down, drive the hips.
- **Common faults:** Rowing with the arms first; Hunched posture; Going out too hard in intervals.
- **Progress to:** ATG Split Squat (G2); SSB Split Squat (G2); SSB Good Morning (G2). **Or progress by:** Longer work, shorter rest, higher watts/calories, more rounds.
- **Regress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or regress by:** Easier pace, shorter intervals, more rest.
- **Same level swaps:** Rower 500m; Tabata Bike; Bike (Easy)
- **Cautions:** None specific. Low impact. Rower and ski: watch low back flexion. Treadmill sprints involve impact.
- **Default prescription:** Intervals: e.g. 6 to 10 x 15 to 30s hard / 60 to 90s easy, or 20 to 40 min steady (zone 2)
- **Coach sources:** Attia (zone 2, VO2), Cosgrove (intervals), Stacy Sims (sprints), Ben Patrick (backward walking)

## Sprint Intervals 10 to 20s (Bike or Ski)

`ADD-036 | G1 | Conditioning: erg / walking | BURN, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Yes`

- **Equipment:** Assault bike / bike, Ski erg
- **Why we use it:** 6 to 10 all out efforts of 10 to 20 seconds with 1 to 2 minutes easy. Stacy Sims recommends this short, sharp style for peri and post menopausal women; Cosgrove ranks intervals above steady cardio for fat loss. Zero impact on the bike or ski erg.
- **This variation:** Fast/power version: move with intent, stop when speed drops.
- **Muscles:** Heart and lungs, legs (bike/rower), upper body (ski/rower)
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Bike: push and pull with arms and legs, steady cadence. 2) Rower: legs, body, arms; then arms, body, legs. 3) Ski: hinge and pull down, drive the hips.
- **Common faults:** Rowing with the arms first; Hunched posture; Going out too hard in intervals.
- **Progress to:** ATG Split Squat (G2); SSB Split Squat (G2); SSB Good Morning (G2). **Or progress by:** Longer work, shorter rest, higher watts/calories, more rounds.
- **Regress to:** None named, use the levers. **Or regress by:** Easier pace, shorter intervals, more rest.
- **Same level swaps:** Zone 2 Steady State (Bike, Rower or Ski); Tabata Bike; Bike (Easy)
- **Cautions:** None specific. Low impact. Rower and ski: watch low back flexion. Treadmill sprints involve impact.
- **Default prescription:** Intervals: e.g. 6 to 10 x 15 to 30s hard / 60 to 90s easy, or 20 to 40 min steady (zone 2)
- **Coach sources:** Attia (zone 2, VO2), Cosgrove (intervals), Stacy Sims (sprints), Ben Patrick (backward walking)

## Trap Bar Deadlift (Low Handles)

`ADD-037 | G3 | Hinge: trap bar deadlift | STRONG | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Trap bar (confirm)
- **Why we use it:** The trap bar lets people stand inside the weight with neutral grip, so the load sits in line with the body. Far less low back stress than a straight bar and much easier to learn. DeFranco and Cosgrove's go to heavy lift and Optimal's default heavy deadlift for 40+ (bone density, strength, grip).
- **Muscles:** Glutes, quads, hamstrings, back, grip
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Stand in the middle, hinge down and grip the handles. 2) Chest proud, take the slack out of the bar, brace. 3) Push the floor away, stand tall, lower with control.
- **Common faults:** Hips shooting up first; Rounding the back off the floor; Jerking the bar off the floor.
- **Progress to:** Rack Pull (G4); Block Pull (G4); Sumo Deadlift (G4). **Or progress by:** Add load, low handles, pause just off the floor, rep max progressions (Teams G4).
- **Regress to:** Trap Bar RDL (G2); Trap Bar Deadlift (High Handles) (G2); Tempo DB RDL (G2). **Or regress by:** High handles, KB deadlift from blocks, lighter load.
- **Same level swaps:** Trap Bar Deadlift; Paused DB RDL; Barbell Romanian Deadlift
- **Cautions:** None specific. The most joint friendly heavy lift. High handles reduce range for tall members or stiff hips/backs.
- **Default prescription:** 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8
- **Coach sources:** DeFranco, Cosgrove, LIFTMOR research

## Nordic Curl (Full)

`ADD-038 | G3 | Hinge: knee flexion (hamstring curl) | STRONG, HYBRID | Group: Yes | Impact: none | Teams only: No | Seniors: Check`

- **Equipment:** Bodyweight
- **Why we use it:** Hamstrings both extend the hip and bend the knee; curls train the knee bending role that RDLs miss. Strong hamstrings protect knees and reduce hamstring strain risk. Nordic curls are among the best researched injury prevention exercises.
- **Muscles:** Hamstrings (knee flexion function), glutes
- **Coaching cues:** 1) Lie on your back, heels on the ball/sliders/TRX, lift the hips. 2) Curl the heels towards the bum keeping the hips high. 3) Extend slowly back out (control is the exercise).
- **Common faults:** Hips dropping during the curl; Rushing the lowering; Cramping (start with fewer reps).
- **Progress to:** SSB Pause Squat (G4); Single Leg Slider Curl (G4). **Or progress by:** Hips stay up throughout, single leg, slower lowering, Nordic progression.
- **Regress to:** TRX Hamstring Curl (G2); Swiss Ball Hamstring Curl (G2); Hamstring Curl (Swiss Ball) (G2). **Or regress by:** Hips on the floor curl, eccentric only, double leg.
- **Same level swaps:** Slider Hamstring Curl; Hamstring Curl (Slider); Single Leg Swiss Ball Curl
- **Cautions:** None specific. Knee friendly. Nordics are demanding: use band assistance and partial range, expect soreness at first.
- **Default prescription:** 3 sets x 8 to 12 reps, tempo 3-0-1-1, rest 60 to 90s, RPE 7 to 9
- **Coach sources:** Squat University, Ben Patrick (Nordic), Poliquin
